To step down alternating voltage amplitude
qs.e: The reservoir capacitor charges during voltage peaks and discharges during troughs, smoothing out pulsating AC ripples into a smooth DC output voltage.

qs.q: How must a semiconductor p-n junction diode be connected to a DC power source to operate in forward-bias mode?
o: Anode (p-type) to negative terminal, Cathode (n-type) to positive terminal
Anode (p-type) to positive terminal, Cathode (n-type) to negative terminal
Both terminals connected to negative supply
Both terminals connected to positive supply
qs.e: Forward bias requires connecting p-type anode to positive potential and n-type cathode to negative potential, reducing the depletion layer width and permitting current flow.

qs.q: In a common-emitter npn bipolar junction transistor amplifier circuit, collector current is Ic = 4.8 mA (0.0048 A) and base current is Ib = 40 µA (0.000040 A). What is the DC current gain (beta β) of the transistor?
qs.e: DC current gain β = Collector current Ic / Base current Ib = 4.8 mA / 0.040 mA = 120.0.

qs.q: A logic circuit consists of a two-input NAND gate immediately followed by a NOT gate (inverter). What single logic gate produces the exact same truth table output?
qs.e: A NOT gate inverts the output of a NAND gate. Inverting NOT(NAND) cancels the negation, yielding an AND gate.

qs.q: In a digital logic circuit, inputs A and B feed into an OR gate. The output of the OR gate and input A feed into an AND gate. What is the Boolean expression for the output Y?
qs.e: Boolean expression Y = A AND (A OR B). By absorption law of Boolean algebra: A · (A + B) = A. The output Y is identical to input A.

qs.q: When a 50 Hz sinusoidal alternating current mains supply is connected to a full-wave bridge rectifier, what is the fundamental ripple frequency of the output DC voltage?
qs.e: Full-wave rectifiers rectify both positive and negative half-cycles of the AC input, doubling the output pulse frequency to 2 × 50 Hz = 100 Hz.

qs.q: What key operational characteristic makes a Zener diode suitable for use as a voltage regulator in electronic power supply circuits?
o: It acts as a variable resistor whose resistance decreases with light intensity
It allows current to flow freely only in the forward biased direction
It maintains a constant voltage drop across its terminals when operated in reverse breakdown region
It amplifies weak AC signals with high voltage gain
qs.e: When reverse biased beyond its breakdown threshold voltage (V_z), a Zener diode maintains a nearly constant voltage drop across a wide range of reverse currents.

qs.q: According to energy band theory of solids, what are the typical energy band gaps (E_g) for conductors, semiconductors (e.g. Silicon), and insulators respectively?
o: Zero gap in conductors, ~1.1 eV in Silicon, and >5.0 eV in insulators
~1.1 eV in conductors, zero gap in Silicon, and >5.0 eV in insulators
>5.0 eV in conductors, ~1.1 eV in Silicon, and zero gap in insulators
Zero gap in conductors, >5.0 eV in Silicon, and ~1.1 eV in insulators
qs.e: Conductors have overlapping valence and conduction bands (zero gap), semiconductors have a small energy gap (~1.1 eV for Si), and insulators have a large forbidden energy gap (>5.0 eV).

qs.q: A common-emitter BJT transistor amplifier has a transistor current gain β = 80, input resistance R_in = 1.0 kΩ (1000 Ω), and load resistance R_load = 5.0 kΩ (5000 Ω). What is the small-signal voltage gain A_v of the amplifier?

A vernier caliper with negative zero error (-0.03 mm) gives a main scale reading of 12.0 mm and the 7th vernier scale division aligns with a main scale line. If least count is 0.01 mm, what is the corrected measurement?
qs.e: Observed reading = Main scale + (vernier division × least count) = 12.0 + (7 × 0.01) = 12.07 mm. Corrected reading = Observed reading - Zero error = 12.07 - (-0.03) = 12.10 mm.

qs.q: A 5.0 kg wooden block on a 37° rough incline (sin 37° = 0.60, cos 37° = 0.80) is pulled up the incline by a cable tension of 50.0 N. Taking coefficient of kinetic friction µ_k = 0.25 and g = 10 m/s², what is the acceleration of the block up the incline?
qs.e: Normal force N = m g cos(37°) = 5.0 × 10 × 0.80 = 40.0 N. Frictional force f_k = µ_k N = 0.25 × 40.0 = 10.0 N. Gravity component down incline = m g sin(37°) = 5.0 × 10 × 0.60 = 30.0 N. Net force up incline = 50.0 - (30.0 + 10.0) = 10.0 N. Acceleration a = Net force / mass = 10.0 / 5.0 = 2.00 m/s².

qs.q: On a frictionless linear air track, Glider A (mass 1.5 kg, speed 4.0 m/s East) collides head-on with Glider B (mass 2.5 kg, speed 2.0 m/s West) and they latch together. What total kinetic energy is lost in the collision?
A differential wheel and axle has a wheel radius of 30 cm and axle radii of 12 cm and 8 cm. If efficiency of the machine is 80%, what effort is required to raise a 600 N load?
qs.e: Velocity ratio VR = 2 R / (r1 - r2) = (2 × 30) / (12 - 8) = 60 / 4 = 15.0. MA = Efficiency × VR = 0.80 × 15.0 = 12.0. Effort = Load / MA = 600 N / 12.0 = 50.0 N.

qs.q: Two wires A and B of the same metallic material have lengths in the ratio L_A / L_B = 2.0 and radii in the ratio r_A / r_B = 0.50. When equal tensile forces F are applied, what is the ratio of their extensions e_A / e_B?
qs.e: Extension e = (F × L) / (A × Y) = (F × L) / (π × r² × Y) ∝ L / r². Ratio e_A / e_B = (L_A / L_B) × (r_B / r_A)² = 2.0 × (1.0 / 0.50)² = 2.0 × 4.0 = 8.0.

qs.q: A glass beaker of height 30 cm filled with water (density 1000 kg/m³, g = 10 m/s²) has a tiny hole at depth h = 20 cm below the surface. Taking speed of efflux v = √(2 g h), at what horizontal distance from the base does the emerging water stream strike the table?
qs.e: Efflux velocity v = √(2 × 10 × 0.20 m) = √4.0 = 2.0 m/s. Height of fall H = 0.30 - 0.20 = 0.10 m. Time of fall t = √(2 H / g) = √(2 × 0.10 / 10) = √0.02 ≈ 0.1414 s. Horizontal range x = v × t = 2.0 m/s × 0.1414 s = 0.2828 m = 28.28 cm.

qs.q: Which of the following physical quantities is correctly paired with its SI base unit?
qs.e: Formula/Reasoning: Among the choices, the Ampere (A) is an SI base unit. Newton (N), Joule (J), and Pascal (Pa) are derived units expressed in terms of base units (kg, m, s, A).

qs.q: A commuter minibus in Ibadan travels 90 km in 1.5 hours. What is its average speed in meters per second?
qs.e: Formula: Speed = distance / time. Distance = 90,000 m, Time = 1.5 × 3600 = 5400 s. Substitution: v = 90000 / 5400 = 16.67 m/s. Physical reasoning: Converting km to meters and hours to seconds yields 16.67 m/s.

qs.q: The property of a body to remain in its state of rest or uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force is known as
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Inertia is Newton's First Law concept representing resistance to change in state of motion. Mass is the quantitative measure of inertia.

qs.q: Calculate the momentum of a 1200 kg delivery van moving along a straight road at a constant velocity of 20 m/s.
qs.e: Formula: p = m × v. Substitution: p = 1200 kg × 20 m/s = 24,000 kg·m/s. Physical reasoning: Linear momentum is the product of mass and velocity.

qs.q: A carpenter exerts a constant horizontal force of 45 N to push a wooden box through a distance of 6 m across a smooth floor. How much work is done by the carpenter?
qs.e: Formula: W = F × d. Substitution: W = 45 N × 6 m = 270 J. Physical reasoning: Work done equals force multiplied by displacement in the direction of the force.

qs.q: To eliminate parallax error when reading a liquid level on a graduated measuring cylinder, the observer's line of sight must be
o: Horizontal and aligned with the bottom of the meniscus
At an angle of 45° above the meniscus
Aligned with the top edge of the liquid meniscus
At an angle of 30° below the meniscus
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Parallax error is avoided by looking perpendicularly (horizontally) at the scale, aligned with the bottom of a concave meniscus for transparent liquids.

qs.q: A racing car accelerates uniformly from rest to a speed of 35 m/s in 7.0 seconds. Determine the magnitude of its acceleration.
qs.e: Formula: a = (v - u) / t. Substitution: a = (35 - 0) / 7.0 = 5.0 m/s². Physical reasoning: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.

qs.q: A body accelerates uniformly from an initial velocity of 12 m/s to a final velocity of 28 m/s in 4.0 seconds. Calculate the total distance covered during this time.
qs.e: Formula: s = ((u + v) / 2) × t. Substitution: s = ((12 + 28) / 2) × 4.0 = 20 × 4.0 = 80 m. Physical reasoning: Distance is average velocity multiplied by time interval.

qs.q: Calculate the force required to pull a 6.0 kg crate up a smooth plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal with an acceleration of 1.5 m/s². (Take g = 10 m/s²)
qs.e: Formula: F - m·g·sin(θ) = m·a => F = m·g·sin(θ) + m·a. Substitution: F = 6 × 10 × sin(30°) + 6 × 1.5 = 6 × 10 × 0.5 + 9 = 30 + 9 = 39 N.

qs.q: A trolley of mass 3.0 kg moving at 8.0 m/s on a smooth track collides with and sticks to a stationary trolley of mass 5.0 kg. Find their common velocity after the collision.
An electric pump at Kainji dam lifts 500 kg of water through a vertical height of 18 m in 10 seconds. If g = 10 m/s², what is the useful output power of the pump?
qs.e: Formula: P = (m·g·h) / t. Substitution: P = (500 × 10 × 18) / 10 = 90,000 / 10 = 9,000 W (9 kW). Physical reasoning: Power is the rate of doing gravitational work.

qs.q: The main scale of a vernier calliper reads 4.2 cm, and the 7th vernier division coincides with a main scale mark. If the calliper has a positive zero error of 0.03 cm, what is the corrected reading?
qs.e: Formula: Uncorrected reading = 4.2 + 0.07 = 4.27 cm. Corrected reading = Uncorrected reading - Zero error. Substitution: 4.27 - 0.03 = 4.24 cm.

qs.q: A stone is thrown vertically upwards from the ground with an initial speed of 30 m/s. Assuming g = 10 m/s² and neglecting air resistance, calculate the maximum height reached.
qs.e: Formula: v² = u² - 2gh. At max height v = 0 => h = u² / (2g). Substitution: h = (30)² / (2 × 10) = 900 / 20 = 45 m.

qs.q: Two blocks of masses 4 kg and 6 kg resting on a frictionless horizontal table are connected by a light string. A horizontal force of 20 N pulls the 6 kg block. Find the tension in the connecting string.
qs.e: Formula: Acceleration a = F / (m1 + m2) = 20 / (4 + 6) = 2.0 m/s². Tension T pulling 4 kg mass = m1 × a = 4 × 2.0 = 8 N.

qs.q: A rifle of mass 4.5 kg fires a bullet of mass 0.015 kg at a muzzle velocity of 600 m/s. Calculate the recoil velocity of the rifle.
qs.e: Formula: Conservation of momentum: m_r · v_r + m_b · v_b = 0 => v_r = -(m_b · v_b) / m_r. Substitution: v_r = (0.015 × 600) / 4.5 = 9.0 / 4.5 = 2.0 m/s in opposite direction.

qs.q: A 0.4 kg coconut falls from a palm tree from a height of 15 m above the ground. Compute its kinetic energy just before hitting the ground. (g = 10 m/s²)
qs.e: Formula: Potential energy converted to kinetic energy: KE = m·g·h. Substitution: KE = 0.4 × 10 × 15 = 60 J.

qs.q: Which of the following combinations represents the dimensions of dynamic viscosity?
qs.e: Formula: Dynamic viscosity η = Force / (Area × velocity gradient) = [M L T⁻²] / ([L²] × [T⁻¹]) = [M L⁻¹ T⁻¹].

qs.q: A motorcycle starts from rest and accelerates at a constant rate of 2.5 m/s² along a straight stretch of the Lagos-Ibadan expressway. How long will it take to cover 125 meters?
A person of mass 70 kg stands on a weighing balance inside an elevator descending with a uniform downward acceleration of 2.0 m/s². What reading does the balance display? (g = 10 m/s²)
qs.e: Formula: Apparent weight N = m(g - a). Substitution: N = 70 × (10 - 2.0) = 70 × 8 = 560 N.

qs.q: A stationary explosive charge of mass 8.0 kg detonates into two fragments of masses 3.0 kg and 5.0 kg. If the 3.0 kg fragment moves off at 20 m/s, calculate the kinetic energy of the 5.0 kg fragment.
qs.e: Formula: Conservation of momentum: m1·v1 = m2·v2 => 3 × 20 = 5 × v2 => v2 = 12 m/s. Kinetic energy KE2 = 0.5 × m2 × v2² = 0.5 × 5 × (12)² = 0.5 × 5 × 144 = 360 J.

qs.q: An electric motor with an efficiency of 75% is used to lift a load of 300 kg vertically at a constant speed of 2.0 m/s. Calculate the electrical power input to the motor. (g = 10 m/s²)
qs.e: Formula: Useful output power P_out = F × v = m·g·v = 300 × 10 × 2.0 = 6,000 W. Efficiency η = P_out / P_in => P_in = 6,000 / 0.75 = 8,000 W.

qs.q: A projectile is launched from ground level with an initial speed of 50 m/s at an angle of 30° above the horizontal. Calculate its horizontal range. (Take g = 10 m/s² and √3 ≈ 1.732)
A 12 kg wooden crate is pulled horizontally across a concrete floor at a constant speed by a force of 48 N. What is the coefficient of kinetic friction between the crate and the floor? (g = 10 m/s²)
qs.e: Formula: At constant speed, pulling force F = frictional force f_k = µ_k · N. Normal reaction N = m·g = 12 × 10 = 120 N. Thus µ_k = F / N = 48 / 120 = 0.40.

qs.q: A 0.2 kg steel ball moving at 10 m/s collides head-on elastically with an identical stationary steel ball. What are the velocities of the first and second balls respectively after collision?
qs.e: Formula: For head-on elastic collision of equal masses (m1 = m2), the bodies exchange their velocities completely. v1 = 0 m/s, v2 = 10 m/s.

qs.q: A horizontal spring of stiffness constant k = 500 N/m is compressed by 0.12 m from its relaxed length. What is the elastic potential energy stored in the spring?
The radius of a solid sphere is measured as r = (5.00 ± 0.10) cm. Calculate the percentage uncertainty in the calculated volume of the sphere.
qs.e: Formula: Volume V = (4/3)πr³. Fractional uncertainty ΔV / V = 3 × (Δr / r). Fractional error in r = 0.10 / 5.00 = 0.02 (2%). Percentage uncertainty in V = 3 × 2% = 6.0%.

qs.q: A stone is dropped from rest from the top of the Niger River bridge at Lokoja, 45 meters above the water surface. How long does it take to hit the water? (g = 10 m/s²)
In an Atwood machine, two masses of 3.0 kg and 5.0 kg are connected over a frictionless light pulley. Find the magnitude of the acceleration of the system. (g = 10 m/s²)
A 0.15 kg tennis ball traveling horizontally at 20 m/s is struck back by a racket, leaving at 30 m/s in the opposite direction. What is the magnitude of the impulse imparted to the ball?
qs.e: Formula: Impulse J = Δp = m(v - u). Taking initial direction positive, u = +20, v = -30. Substitution: J = 0.15 × (-30 - 20) = 0.15 × (-50) = -7.5 N·s. Magnitude = 7.5 N·s.

qs.q: A variable force F acts on an object such that F increases linearly from 0 N to 40 N over a distance of 6 m, and then remains constant at 40 N for another 4 m. What is the total work done?
qs.e: Formula: Total work = Area under F-x graph. Area = Triangle area + Rectangle area = (0.5 × 6 × 40) + (4 × 40) = 120 + 160 = 280 J.

qs.q: A car of mass 1000 kg rounds a flat circular curve of radius 40 m at a constant speed of 20 m/s. Determine the required centripetal force.
A block of mass 5.0 kg rests on a rough plane inclined at 37° to the horizontal. If the block is on the verge of sliding down the incline, what is the coefficient of static friction? (tan 37° ≈ 0.75)
qs.e: Formula: At the angle of repose θ, µ_s = tan(θ). Substitution: µ_s = tan(37°) = 0.75.

qs.q: An engine delivers 50 kW of mechanical power to drive a speed-boat at a constant speed of 25 m/s against water resistance. What is the magnitude of the total resistive force acting on the boat?
qs.e: Formula: P = F × v => F = P / v. Substitution: F = 50,000 W / 25 m/s = 2,000 N.

qs.q: A projectile is launched from ground level with speed u at 60° above horizontal. At the highest point of its trajectory, its speed is 15 m/s. What was the initial launch speed u?
qs.e: Formula: At maximum height, vertical velocity is zero, so velocity is purely horizontal: v_top = u · cos(θ). Substitution: 15 = u · cos(60°) => 15 = u × 0.5 => u = 30 m/s.

qs.q: A 8.0 kg mass resting on a 30° smooth inclined plane is connected by a light cord passing over a smooth pulley at the top to a hanging mass m. If the system stays in static equilibrium, what is mass m?
qs.e: Formula: For equilibrium, tension T = m·g = M·g·sin(30°). Substitution: m = M · sin(30°) = 8.0 × 0.5 = 4.0 kg.

qs.q: A 1200 kg car travelling east at 15 m/s collides with a 800 kg car travelling north at 20 m/s. If they lock together after impact, calculate the magnitude of their common velocity immediately after collision.
qs.e: Formula: px = m1·v1 = 1200 × 15 = 18000 kg·m/s. py = m2·v2 = 800 × 20 = 16000 kg·m/s. Total momentum p_tot = √(18000² + 16000²) = √(324M + 256M) = √580M = 24,083 kg·m/s. Total mass M_tot = 2000 kg. Common velocity v = p_tot / M_tot = 24083 / 2000 = 12.04 ≈ 12.0 m/s.

qs.q: A 1000 kg car travelling at 20 m/s collides head-on with a stationary 1500 kg truck and sticks to it. How much kinetic energy is transformed into thermal energy and deformation during the impact?
The density of a cylindrical brass rod of mass m = (200 ± 2) g, length L = (10.0 ± 0.1) cm, and radius r = (1.00 ± 0.02) cm is calculated. What is the percentage error in the density?
qs.e: Formula: Volume V = π r² L => Density ρ = m / (π r² L). Fractional error Δρ/ρ = Δm/m + 2(Δr/r) + ΔL/L. Substitution: Δm/m = 2/200 = 1%, Δr/r = 0.02/1.00 = 2%, ΔL/L = 0.1/10.0 = 1%. Total percentage error = 1% + 2(2%) + 1% = 6.0%.

qs.q: Two cars A and B start from the same point. Car A travels due East at 40 km/h, while Car B travels at 40 km/h in a direction 60° North of East. What is the magnitude of the relative velocity of B with respect to A?
A spring balance inside a lift supporting a 5.0 kg mass shows a reading of 57.5 N. If g = 10 m/s², describe the motion of the lift.
o: Moving downwards at constant speed of 1.5 m/s
Moving upwards at constant speed of 1.5 m/s
qs.e: Formula: Apparent weight N = m(g + a) => 57.5 = 5.0 × (10 + a) => 11.5 = 10 + a => a = +1.5 m/s². Positive acceleration means accelerating upwards.

qs.q: A horizontal hose shoots a stream of water of cross-sectional area 4.0 cm² against a vertical wall at a velocity of 15 m/s. If the water stops dead on impact without bouncing back, what force is exerted on the wall? (Density of water = 1000 kg/m³)
qs.e: Formula: Mass flow rate dm/dt = ρ · A · v. Area A = 4.0 × 10⁻⁴ m². dm/dt = 1000 × 4.0×10⁻⁴ × 15 = 6.0 kg/s. Force F = (dm/dt) × v = 6.0 × 15 = 90 N.

qs.q: A small block slides down a frictionless track that loops in a vertical circle of radius R = 4.0 m. What is the minimum height H above the bottom of the loop from which the block must be released from rest to complete the loop without leaving the track?
qs.e: Formula: Minimum release height H above bottom of loop to complete loop-the-loop is H = 2.5 × R. Substitution: H = 2.5 × 4.0 m = 10.0 m.

qs.q: The velocity of a particle moving along a straight line is given by v(t) = 3t² - 6t + 2 (in m/s). What is its displacement between t = 0 s and t = 3 s?
qs.e: Formula: s = ∫₀³ (3t² - 6t + 2) dt = [t³ - 3t² + 2t]₀³. Substitution: s = (3³ - 3(3)² + 2(3)) - 0 = (27 - 27 + 6) = 6 m.

qs.q: What is the maximum speed at which an unbanked curve of radius 90 m can be safely negotiated by a car if the coefficient of static friction between tyres and road is 0.40? (g = 10 m/s²)
qs.e: Formula: v_max = √(µ_s · g · r). Substitution: v_max = √(0.40 × 10 × 90) = √360 ≈ 18.97 m/s.

qs.q: A solid uniform cylinder of mass M and radius R rolls down an inclined plane of height h without slipping. Starting from rest at the top, what is its linear velocity at the bottom of the incline? (g = 10 m/s²)
qs.e: Formula: Total KE = Translational KE + Rotational KE = 0.5 M v² + 0.5 I ω². For solid cylinder I = 0.5 M R² and ω = v/R. Total KE = 0.5 M v² + 0.25 M v² = 0.75 M v². Setting mgh = 0.75 M v² => v² = (4/3)gh => v = √(4gh / 3).

qs.q: A rescue canister is launched from a cliff of height 40 m above sea level with an initial velocity of 20 m/s at an angle of 30° above the horizontal. Calculate the total time taken for the canister to hit the water below. (g = 10 m/s²)
qs.e: Formula: Vertical component of initial velocity u_y = 20 · sin(30°) = 10 m/s. Taking downwards as negative, displacement y = -40 m. Equation: -40 = 10t - 5t² => 5t² - 10t - 40 = 0 => t² - 2t - 8 = 0 => (t - 4)(t + 2) = 0 => t = 4.0 s.

qs.q: Three blocks of masses m1 = 2 kg, m2 = 3 kg, and m3 = 5 kg are placed in contact on a rough horizontal surface with coefficient of friction µ = 0.2. A horizontal pushing force F = 40 N is applied to m1. Find the contact force between m2 and m3. (g = 10 m/s²)
qs.e: Formula: Total friction f_tot = µ(m1+m2+m3)g = 0.2 × 10 × 10 = 20 N. Net pushing force F_net = F - f_tot = 40 - 20 = 20 N. Acceleration a = F_net / M_tot = 20 / 10 = 2.0 m/s². The contact force N23 between m2 and m3 accelerates block m3 against its friction: N23 - µ·m3·g = m3·a => N23 - 0.2×5×10 = 5 × 2.0 => N23 - 10 = 10 => N23 = 20 N.

qs.q: A rocket hovering in mid-air near the Earth's surface consumes fuel and ejects hot exhaust gas vertically downwards at a relative speed of 1200 m/s. If the total mass of the rocket is 3000 kg, at what rate must fuel be burned to keep it hovering? (g = 10 m/s²)
qs.e: Formula: Thrust T = (dm/dt) · v_rel. For hovering, T = m·g => (dm/dt) · v_rel = m·g => dm/dt = (m·g) / v_rel. Substitution: dm/dt = (3000 × 10) / 1200 = 30,000 / 1200 = 25.0 kg/s.

qs.q: A hydroelectric plant at Kainji receives water from a reservoir at a volume flow rate of 150 m³/s through a penstock with an effective vertical head of 40 m. If the overall efficiency of the station (turbine + generator) is 85%, compute the electrical power output. (Density of water = 1000 kg/m³, g = 10 m/s²)
qs.e: Formula: Water mass flow rate dm/dt = Q × ρ = 150 × 1000 = 150,000 kg/s. Input potential energy power P_in = (dm/dt) × g × h = 150,000 × 10 × 40 = 60,000,000 W = 60 MW. Output power P_out = η × P_in = 0.85 × 60 MW = 51.0 MW.

qs.q: For an ideal block and tackle pulley system consisting of 5 pulleys, what is its velocity ratio?
qs.e: Physical reasoning: For a block and tackle pulley system, the velocity ratio (VR) equals the total number of pulleys in the system, which is 5.

qs.q: Hooke's law states that within the elastic limit, the extension of an elastic material is directly proportional to the
qs.e: Formula: F = k · x. Physical reasoning: Hooke's law establishes that applied force F is directly proportional to extension x up to the elastic limit.

qs.q: Which of the following units is equivalent to one Pascal (Pa)?
qs.e: Formula: Pressure P = Force / Area => 1 Pa = 1 N / 1 m² = 1 N/m².

qs.q: Archimedes' principle states that when an object is wholly or partially immersed in a fluid, it experiences an upthrust equal to the
o: Weight of the object in air
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Upthrust on an immersed body equals the weight of the fluid displaced by the submerged portion.

qs.q: How does an increase in temperature affect the viscosity of liquids and gases respectively?
o: Liquid viscosity decreases; gas viscosity increases
Liquid viscosity increases; gas viscosity decreases
Both liquid and gas viscosity increase
Both liquid and gas viscosity decrease
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Heating a liquid reduces cohesive intermolecular forces (decreasing viscosity), while heating a gas increases molecular collision rates (increasing viscosity).

qs.q: The mechanical advantage (MA) of a machine is defined as the ratio of
o: Distance moved by effort to distance moved by load
qs.e: Formula: MA = Load (L) / Effort (E). Physical reasoning: Mechanical advantage measures force multiplication by a machine.

qs.q: The standard atmospheric pressure at sea level is approximately equal to
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Standard atmospheric pressure at sea level is 760 mmHg = 1.013 × 10⁵ N/m² (Pa).

qs.q: An inclined plane of length 12 m is used to raise a heavy generator to a height of 3 m. If an effort of 200 N is required to push a 600 N generator up the plane, what is the efficiency of the plane?
qs.e: Formula: Velocity Ratio VR = Length / Height = 12 / 3 = 4. Mechanical Advantage MA = Load / Effort = 600 / 200 = 3. Efficiency η = (MA / VR) × 100% = (3 / 4) × 100% = 75%.

qs.q: A force of 15 N produces an extension of 3.0 cm in a spiral spring. Assuming Hooke's law holds, what force will produce an extension of 7.0 cm in the same spring?
qs.e: Formula: F = k · x => k = F1 / x1 = 15 / 3.0 = 5.0 N/cm. Force F2 = k × x2 = 5.0 N/cm × 7.0 cm = 35 N.

qs.q: Calculate the hydrostatic pressure exerted at the bottom of a water storage tank filled to a depth of 8.0 m. (Density of water = 1000 kg/m³, g = 10 m/s²)
qs.e: Formula: Hydrostatic pressure P = ρ · g · h. Substitution: P = 1000 kg/m³ × 10 m/s² × 8.0 m = 80,000 Pa (80 kPa).

qs.q: A solid wooden block of density 750 kg/m³ floats in fresh water of density 1000 kg/m³. What fraction of the block's total volume is submerged?
qs.e: Formula: For a floating body, Fraction submerged V_sub / V_total = ρ_body / ρ_fluid. Substitution: V_sub / V_total = 750 / 1000 = 0.75.

qs.q: Capillary rise of liquid in a narrow glass tube is caused by surface tension. If the radius of the tube is halved, how does the height of the liquid column change?
qs.e: Formula: Jurin's law h = (2 T cos θ) / (r ρ g). Since height h is inversely proportional to radius r (h ∝ 1/r), halving r doubles the height h.

qs.q: A wheel and axle system has a wheel radius of 24 cm and an axle radius of 4 cm. Determine the velocity ratio of the machine.
qs.e: Formula: Velocity ratio VR = Radius of wheel (R) / Radius of axle (r). Substitution: VR = 24 / 4 = 6.0.

qs.q: A spring of force constant 300 N/m is stretched through a distance of 0.06 m. Calculate the work done in stretching the spring.
qs.e: Formula: Work done W = 0.5 × k × x². Substitution: W = 0.5 × 300 N/m × (0.06 m)² = 150 × 0.0036 = 0.54 J.

qs.q: In a hydraulic press, a force of 40 N applied to a small piston of cross-sectional area 0.02 m² produces a force F2 on a large piston of area 0.50 m². Calculate F2.
qs.e: Formula: Pascal's principle F1 / A1 = F2 / A2 => F2 = F1 × (A2 / A1). Substitution: F2 = 40 × (0.50 / 0.02) = 40 × 25 = 1000 N.

qs.q: A hydrometer sinks deeper into liquid A than into liquid B. This observation indicates that
o: Liquid A is less dense than Liquid B
Liquid A is denser than Liquid B
Liquid A has higher surface tension than Liquid B
Liquid A has higher viscosity than Liquid B
qs.e: Physical reasoning: By Archimedes' principle, a hydrometer must displace a greater volume of a less dense liquid to balance its fixed weight, so it sinks deeper in less dense liquids.

qs.q: Small spherical rain drops reach a constant terminal velocity while falling through calm air. At terminal velocity, the net force acting on a drop is
o: Equal to the viscous drag force
qs.e: Physical reasoning: At terminal velocity, acceleration is zero, so the net force acting on the object is exactly zero (downward weight = upward drag + buoyancy).

qs.q: A steel wire of diameter 2.0 mm supports a load of 314 N. What tensile stress is developed in the wire? (Take π ≈ 3.14)
qs.e: Formula: Radius r = 1.0 mm = 1.0 × 10⁻³ m. Area A = π · r² = 3.14 × (10⁻³)² = 3.14 × 10⁻⁶ m². Tensile stress = Force / Area = 314 / (3.14 × 10⁻⁶) = 1.0 × 10⁸ Pa.

qs.q: A screw jack has a pitch of 0.5 cm and a tommy bar (lever arm) of length 35 cm. Calculate the velocity ratio of the screw jack. (Take π ≈ 22/7)
qs.e: Formula: VR = 2 · π · L / pitch. Substitution: VR = (2 × (22/7) × 35 cm) / 0.5 cm = (220 cm) / 0.5 cm = 440.

qs.q: The figure below shows a block and tackle pulley system. <svg width="180" height="200" viewBox="0 0 180 200" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="#ffffff"/><line x1="30" y1="15" x2="150" y2="15" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="4"/><circle cx="70" cy="45" r="18" fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="110" cy="45" r="18" fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="55" y="115" width="70" height="18" fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="70" cy="100" r="14" fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="110" cy="100" r="14" fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="75" y="145" width="30" height="25" fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2"/><text x="90" y="162" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle">LOAD</text></svg> If an effort of 200 N is required to raise a load of 600 N, calculate the efficiency of the system.
qs.e: Formula: The 4-pulley system has VR = 4. Mechanical Advantage MA = Load / Effort = 600 / 200 = 3. Efficiency η = (MA / VR) × 100% = (3 / 4) × 100% = 75%.

qs.q: A metallic wire of length 2.5 m and cross-sectional area 1.2 mm² elongates by 1.5 mm when subjected to a tension of 180 N. Calculate Young's Modulus for the wire material.
A barometer uses cooking oil of density 800 kg/m³ instead of mercury. If atmospheric pressure is 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa and g = 10 m/s², what is the height of the oil column in the barometer?
A piece of alloy weighs 60 N in air and 45 N when completely immersed in water. Calculate the density of the alloy. (Density of water = 1000 kg/m³, g = 10 m/s²)
qs.e: Formula: Upthrust U = Weight in air - Weight in water = 60 - 45 = 15 N. Relative Density RD = Weight in air / Upthrust = 60 / 15 = 4.0. Density = RD × ρ_water = 4.0 × 1000 = 4000 kg/m³.

qs.q: A clean razor blade of length 4.0 cm floats horizontally on water. If the surface tension of water is 0.072 N/m, calculate the maximum downward force due to surface tension supporting the blade.
qs.e: Formula: Since liquid touches both sides of the blade along its length, total perimeter length = 2 × L = 2 × 0.04 m = 0.08 m. Force F = T × 2L = 0.072 × 0.08 = 0.00576 N = 5.76 × 10⁻³ N.

qs.q: A gear system consists of a driving gear with 16 teeth meshed with a driven gear with 64 teeth. Determine the velocity ratio of the gear system.
qs.e: Formula: Velocity ratio VR = Number of teeth on driven gear / Number of teeth on driving gear = 64 / 16 = 4.0.

qs.q: A uniform wire is stretched within its elastic limit such that the tensile strain produced is 0.002. If Young's modulus of the wire is 2.0 × 10¹¹ Pa, calculate the energy stored per unit volume.
qs.e: Formula: Energy per unit volume u = 0.5 × Stress × Strain = 0.5 × (E × Strain) × Strain = 0.5 × E × (Strain)². Substitution: u = 0.5 × (2.0 × 10¹¹) × (0.002)² = 1.0 × 10¹¹ × 4.0 × 10⁻⁶ = 4.0 × 10⁵ J/m³.

qs.q: Calculate the total pressure at the bottom of a swimming pool filled with fresh water to a depth of 5.0 m, given atmospheric pressure = 1.01 × 10⁵ Pa, water density = 1000 kg/m³, and g = 10 m/s².
qs.e: Formula: P_total = P_atm + ρ · g · h. Substitution: P_total = 1.01 × 10⁵ + (1000 × 10 × 5.0) = 101,000 + 50,000 = 151,000 Pa = 1.51 × 10⁵ Pa.

qs.q: An iceberg of density 920 kg/m³ floats in seawater of density 1025 kg/m³. What percentage of the iceberg's total volume remains exposed above the water surface?
qs.e: Formula: Fraction submerged = ρ_ice / ρ_water = 920 / 1025 = 0.8975 (89.75%). Fraction exposed above water = 1 - 0.8975 = 0.1025 (10.25%).

qs.q: Two spherical raindrops of radii r and 2r fall through calm air at their respective terminal velocities v1 and v2. Assuming Stokes' law applies, calculate the ratio v1 / v2.
qs.e: Formula: Terminal velocity v_t = (2 r² (ρ - σ) g) / (9 η) => v_t ∝ r². Ratio v1 / v2 = (r / 2r)² = (1/2)² = 1/4.

qs.q: An effort of 120 N applied to a machine moves through a distance of 15 m to lift a load of 450 N through a vertical height of 3 m. Calculate the work lost against friction in the machine.
qs.e: Formula: Work Input = Effort × distance = 120 × 15 = 1800 J. Work Output = Load × height = 450 × 3 = 1350 J. Work lost = Input - Output = 1800 - 1350 = 450 J.

qs.q: Two identical springs each of stiffness constant k = 400 N/m are connected in parallel to support a weight. What is the effective spring constant of the parallel combination?
qs.e: Formula: For springs in parallel, effective stiffness k_eff = k1 + k2. Substitution: k_eff = 400 + 400 = 800 N/m.

qs.q: A U-tube open at both ends contains mercury (density = 13,600 kg/m³). Water (density = 1000 kg/m³) is poured into one arm until it forms a column of height 27.2 cm. Calculate the difference in mercury levels between the two arms.
qs.e: Formula: At equilibrium, pressure of water column = pressure of mercury column => ρ_w · g · h_w = ρ_m · g · h_m => h_m = (ρ_w · h_w) / ρ_m. Substitution: h_m = (1000 × 27.2) / 13600 = 27200 / 13600 = 2.0 cm.

qs.q: A solid lead sphere of mass 2.26 kg and density 11,300 kg/m³ is submerged in ethanol of density 800 kg/m³. Compute the apparent weight of the lead sphere in ethanol. (g = 10 m/s²)
qs.e: Formula: True weight W = m · g = 2.26 × 10 = 22.6 N. Volume V = m / ρ_lead = 2.26 / 11300 = 2.0 × 10⁻⁴ m³. Upthrust U = ρ_eth · V · g = 800 × 2.0×10⁻⁴ × 10 = 1.6 N. Apparent weight = W - U = 22.6 - 1.6 = 21.0 N.

qs.q: When a clean glass capillary tube is dipped vertically into mercury, the mercury level inside the tube depresses below the external surface because
o: Cohesive forces between mercury molecules exceed adhesive forces between glass and mercury
Adhesive forces between glass and mercury exceed cohesive forces
Mercury wets the glass surface completely
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Capillary depression occurs when cohesion within the liquid is greater than adhesion between liquid and container, resulting in an obtuse contact angle and depressed meniscus.

qs.q: A lifting machine with a velocity ratio of 8 requires an effort of 150 N to raise a load of 960 N. What force is required to overcome internal friction in the machine?
qs.e: Formula: Ideal effort E_ideal = Load / VR = 960 / 8 = 120 N. Actual effort E_actual = 150 N. Frictional effort E_friction = E_actual - E_ideal = 150 - 120 = 30 N.

qs.q: A copper wire of original length 2.000 m and diameter 1.0 mm is stretched by an applied force that increases uniformly from 0 N to 157 N. If Young's modulus for copper is 1.0 × 10¹¹ Pa, calculate the work done in stretching the wire. (Take π ≈ 3.14)

A mercury barometer reads 760 mmHg at sea level where atmospheric pressure is 1.013 × 10⁵ Pa. At the top of Aso Rock in Abuja, the barometer reading drops to 710 mmHg. Assuming uniform air density of 1.20 kg/m³ and g = 9.8 m/s², estimate the height of Aso Rock.
qs.e: Formula: Pressure drop ΔP = ρ_hg · g · Δh_hg = 13600 × 9.8 × (0.050 m) = 6664 Pa. Air pressure column ΔP = ρ_air · g · H_rock => H_rock = ΔP / (ρ_air · g) = 6664 / (1.20 × 9.8) = 6664 / 11.76 = 566.7 ≈ 566 m.

qs.q: A hot-air balloon has a volume of 800 m³. The density of surrounding cool air is 1.25 kg/m³, while the density of hot air inside the balloon is 0.85 kg/m³. What is the maximum total payload (including basket and envelope) the balloon can carry? (g = 10 m/s²)
qs.e: Formula: Upthrust U = ρ_cool · V · g = 1.25 × 800 × 10 = 10,000 N. Weight of hot air W_hot = ρ_hot · V · g = 0.85 × 800 × 10 = 6,800 N. Net buoyant force = U - W_hot = 10,000 - 6,800 = 3,200 N. Maximum payload mass = 3,200 / 10 = 320 kg.

qs.q: Two identical spherical water droplets of radius r = 1.0 mm merge to form a single larger drop. If the surface tension of water is 0.072 N/m, calculate the energy released during coalescence. (Take π ≈ 3.142)
A combined machine consists of an inclined plane of angle 30° driving a wheel and axle with wheel radius 20 cm and axle radius 5 cm. What is the total velocity ratio of this combined machine?
qs.e: Formula: VR of inclined plane = 1 / sin(30°) = 2.0. VR of wheel and axle = R / r = 20 / 5 = 4.0. Total VR of compound machine = VR1 × VR2 = 2.0 × 4.0 = 8.0.

qs.q: A steel cable of Young's Modulus E = 2.0 × 10¹¹ Pa and cross-sectional area 2.0 cm² supports an elevator. If the maximum permissible tensile strain is 0.15%, what is the maximum safe load that can be suspended?
qs.e: Formula: Area A = 2.0 cm² = 2.0 × 10⁻⁴ m². Strain ε = 0.15% = 0.0015. Stress σ = E × ε = 2.0 × 10¹¹ × 0.0015 = 3.0 × 10⁸ Pa. Max Load F = σ × A = 3.0 × 10⁸ × 2.0 × 10⁻⁴ = 60,000 N.

qs.q: An air bubble of volume 2.0 cm³ at the bottom of Lake Chad where the total pressure is 3.0 atm rises to the surface where pressure is 1.0 atm. Assuming temperature remains constant, what is the volume of the bubble just before reaching the surface?
qs.e: Formula: Boyle's law P1 · V1 = P2 · V2. Substitution: 3.0 atm × 2.0 cm³ = 1.0 atm × V2 => V2 = 6.0 cm³.

qs.q: A hollow wooden cube of side length 20 cm and mass 4.8 kg floats in water. How much additional load must be placed on top of the cube so that its upper surface is level with the water surface? (Density of water = 1000 kg/m³)
qs.e: Formula: Total volume of cube V = (0.20 m)³ = 0.008 m³. Total upthrust when fully submerged U = ρ_w · V · g = 1000 × 0.008 × 10 = 80 N = 8.0 kg weight. Total mass required to submerge = 8.0 kg. Additional load = 8.0 kg - 4.8 kg = 3.2 kg.

qs.q: The excess pressure inside a spherical soap bubble of radius r1 is ΔP1. If the radius is doubled to r2 = 2 r1, how does the excess pressure ΔP2 compare to ΔP1?
qs.e: Formula: Excess pressure inside a soap bubble ΔP = 4T / r. Since ΔP is inversely proportional to radius r (ΔP ∝ 1/r), doubling the radius halves the excess pressure: ΔP2 = 0.5 ΔP1.

qs.q: The radius of a circular pipe carrying water narrows from R1 = 4 cm to R2 = 2 cm. According to Poiseuille's law for laminar viscous flow, by what factor does the volume flow rate decrease if the pressure gradient remains unchanged?
qs.e: Formula: Poiseuille's equation volume flow rate Q = (π r⁴ ΔP) / (8 η L) => Q ∝ r⁴. Ratio Q1 / Q2 = (R1 / R2)⁴ = (4 / 2)⁴ = 2⁴ = 16.

qs.q: A uniform heavy wire of mass m, length L, Young's modulus E, and cross-sectional area A hangs vertically from a rigid ceiling under its own weight. What is the total elongation of the wire?
qs.e: Formula: Tension at height y from bottom is T(y) = (m/L) y g. Extension d(ΔL) = T(y) dy / (A E). Integrating from 0 to L: ΔL = ∫₀ᴸ (m g y / (L A E)) dy = (m g L) / (2 A E).

qs.q: A differential wheel and axle has wheel radius R = 30 cm, and axle radii R1 = 12 cm and R2 = 8 cm. Calculate the velocity ratio of this machine.
qs.e: Formula: Velocity ratio of differential wheel and axle VR = 2 R / (R1 - R2). Substitution: VR = 2 × 30 / (12 - 8) = 60 / 4 = 15.0.

qs.q: A U-tube filled with liquid of density ρ rotates about one of its vertical limbs at a constant angular velocity ω. If the distance between the two vertical limbs is d, calculate the difference in liquid heights h between the two limbs. (g = acceleration due to gravity)
qs.e: Formula: Centrifugal pressure gradient dp/dr = ρ ω² r => ΔP = 0.5 ρ ω² d². Hydrostatic height difference ΔP = ρ g h => ρ g h = 0.5 ρ ω² d² => h = (ω² d²) / (2g).

qs.q: A hollow spherical copper shell of outer radius R = 10 cm and inner radius r = 8 cm floats completely submerged in oil of density 800 kg/m³. Calculate the density of the copper material.
qs.e: Formula: Submerged buoyancy force = Weight of shell => ρ_oil × (4/3)π R³ × g = ρ_cu × (4/3)π (R³ - r³) × g => ρ_cu = ρ_oil × R³ / (R³ - r³). Substitution: R³ = 1000, r³ = 512, R³ - r³ = 488. ρ_cu = 800 × 1000 / 488 = 800,000 / 488 ≈ 1639.3 kg/m³.

qs.q: A small metal sphere of radius r and density ρ falling in oil of density σ and viscosity η reaches terminal velocity v1. A second sphere of radius 2r made of the same metal falls in the same oil. What is its terminal velocity v2 in terms of v1?
qs.e: Formula: Stokes' terminal velocity v_t = (2 r² (ρ - σ) g) / (9 η) => v_t ∝ r². Since radius is doubled (2r), terminal velocity increases by factor of 2² = 4. Thus v2 = 4 v1.

qs.q: Which mode of heat transfer requires no material medium and can take place across a vacuum?
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Thermal radiation transfers heat via electromagnetic waves, requiring no intervening material medium.

qs.q: In a transverse wave, the particles of the medium vibrate in a direction that is
o: Perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation
Parallel to the direction of wave propagation
At an angle of 45° to wave propagation
In circular loops along wave propagation
qs.e: Physical reasoning: By definition, transverse wave oscillations occur perpendicular to the direction of wave energy transport.

qs.q: The persistence of sound due to multiple reflections from walls or obstacle surfaces in a large hall is called
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Reverberation is the prolonged sound caused by repeated reflections off enclosed room surfaces.

qs.q: Which of the following electromagnetic waves has the highest frequency in the electromagnetic spectrum?
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Order of increasing frequency: Radio < Microwave < Infrared < Visible < UV < X-ray < Gamma rays.

qs.q: What is the standard SI unit of specific heat capacity?
qs.e: Formula: c = Q / (m · ΔT) => Units = Joules / (kilograms × Kelvin) = J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹.

qs.q: In all ideal gas law calculations, temperatures must be expressed in which temperature scale?
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Absolute temperature in Kelvin represents true molecular thermal kinetic energy, where 0 K is absolute zero.

qs.q: A continuous steel rail on the Third Mainland Bridge in Lagos has a length of 40 m at 20°C. If the temperature rises to 45°C during peak afternoon heat, calculate the expansion in length. (Linear expansivity of steel = 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹)
A quantity of oxygen gas occupies 250 cm³ at 27°C. What volume will it occupy at 87°C under constant pressure?
qs.e: Formula: Charles' law V1 / T1 = V2 / T2. Temperatures in K: T1 = 27 + 273 = 300 K, T2 = 87 + 273 = 360 K. Substitution: 250 / 300 = V2 / 360 => V2 = 250 × (360 / 300) = 300 cm³.

qs.q: A radio station in Abuja broadcasts at a frequency of 100 MHz. Calculate the wavelength of the radio waves. (Speed of light c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)
qs.e: Formula: c = f · λ => λ = c / f. Substitution: f = 100 × 10⁶ Hz = 1.0 × 10⁸ Hz. λ = 3.0 × 10⁸ / 1.0 × 10⁸ = 3.0 m.

qs.q: A boy stands 170 m away from a tall cliff and claps his hands. If the speed of sound in air is 340 m/s, how long after clapping does he hear the echo?
qs.e: Formula: Echo distance 2d = v · t => t = 2d / v. Substitution: t = (2 × 170) / 340 = 340 / 340 = 1.0 s.

qs.q: Light of wavelength 600 nm travels from air into glass. What is the frequency of this light in glass? (Speed of light in air = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)
qs.e: Formula: Frequency f = c / λ remains invariant when light enters a new medium. Substitution: f = 3.0 × 10⁸ / (600 × 10⁻⁹) = 3.0 × 10⁸ / 6.0 × 10⁻⁷ = 5.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz.

qs.q: In a mixture experiment, 0.3 kg of water at 80°C is mixed with 0.2 kg of water at 20°C in a well-lagged container. Compute the final equilibrium temperature.
qs.e: Formula: Heat lost = Heat gained => m1 · c · (T1 - Tf) = m2 · c · (Tf - T2). Substitution: 0.3 × (80 - Tf) = 0.2 × (Tf - 20) => 24 - 0.3 Tf = 0.2 Tf - 4 => 28 = 0.5 Tf => Tf = 56°C.

qs.q: A sealed rigid steel cylinder contains air at a pressure of 2.0 atm at 27°C. If the cylinder is heated to 177°C, calculate the new internal pressure.
qs.e: Formula: Pressure law P1 / T1 = P2 / T2 (constant volume). T1 = 27 + 273 = 300 K, T2 = 177 + 273 = 450 K. Substitution: 2.0 / 300 = P2 / 450 => P2 = 2.0 × (450 / 300) = 3.0 atm.

qs.q: Two points on a progressive wave are separated by a distance equal to three-quarters of a wavelength (3λ/4). What is the phase difference between these two points?
qs.e: Formula: Phase difference Δϕ = (2π / λ) × Δx. Substitution: Δϕ = (2π / λ) × (3λ / 4) = 3π/2 rad = 270°.

qs.q: A stretched sonometer wire of length 0.5 m vibrates in its fundamental mode. If the speed of transverse waves on the wire is 200 m/s, find its fundamental frequency.
qs.e: Formula: Fundamental wavelength λ = 2 L = 2 × 0.5 = 1.0 m. Frequency f = v / λ = 200 / 1.0 = 200 Hz.

qs.q: Light waves can be polarized, whereas sound waves cannot. This difference proves that sound waves are
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Polarization is unique to transverse waves where oscillations occur in planes perpendicular to propagation. Longitudinal waves cannot be polarized.

qs.q: How much heat energy is required to completely melt 0.40 kg of ice at 0°C into water at 0°C? (Specific latent heat of fusion of ice = 3.36 × 10⁵ J/kg)
qs.e: Formula: Q = m · L_f. Substitution: Q = 0.40 kg × 3.36 × 10⁵ J/kg = 1.344 × 10⁵ J (134.4 kJ).

qs.q: The ideal gas equation is written as PV = nRT. What does 'n' represent in this equation?
qs.e: Physical reasoning: In PV = nRT, 'n' represents the amount of substance in moles.

qs.q: An electric immersion heater rated at 100 W is immersed in 0.25 kg of a liquid inside a well-lagged calorimeter. The temperature of the liquid rises from 25°C to 45°C in 5.0 minutes. Calculate the specific heat capacity of the liquid (neglecting calorimeter heat capacity).
A gas occupies a volume of 400 cm³ at a pressure of 1.0 atm and temperature of 27°C. If the pressure is increased to 2.0 atm and the temperature rises to 127°C, calculate the new volume of the gas.
A stationary wave setup on a stretched string of length 1.2 m forms 3 antinodes (3rd harmonic). If the frequency of vibration is 150 Hz, compute the wave propagation speed on the string.
qs.e: Formula: For 3rd harmonic, L = 3 (λ/2) => λ = 2L / 3 = (2 × 1.2) / 3 = 0.8 m. Wave speed v = f · λ = 150 × 0.8 = 120 m/s.

qs.q: In a resonance tube experiment, the first two resonance lengths are obtained at L1 = 18.0 cm and L2 = 54.0 cm using a tuning fork of frequency 425 Hz. Determine the speed of sound in air.
How much heat energy is needed to convert 0.10 kg of ice at -10°C into steam at 100°C? (c_ice = 2100 J/kg·K, c_water = 4200 J/kg·K, L_f = 3.36×10⁵ J/kg, L_v = 2.26×10⁶ J/kg)
According to kinetic theory, the absolute temperature of an ideal gas is directly proportional to the average
o: Translational kinetic energy of its molecules
qs.e: Formula: Average KE = (3/2) k_B T. Physical reasoning: Temperature is a direct macroscopic measure of mean molecular kinetic energy.

qs.q: Two coherent light sources produce interference. Destructive interference (dark fringe) occurs at a point where the path difference between the two interfering waves is
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Destructive interference occurs when waves arrive completely out of phase (180° phase difference), corresponding to path difference of half-integral wavelengths (m + 0.5) λ.

qs.q: Two tuning forks of frequencies 512 Hz and 516 Hz are sounded together. How many beats are heard in a duration of 3.0 seconds?
qs.e: Formula: Beat frequency f_beat = |f1 - f2| = 516 - 512 = 4 Hz (4 beats per second). In 3.0 s, Total beats = 4 × 3.0 = 12 beats.

qs.q: A diffraction grating has 500 lines per millimeter. What is the highest order spectrum m that can be observed for yellow light of wavelength 600 nm?
qs.e: Formula: Grating spacing d = 1 / 500 mm = 1/500,000 m = 2.0 × 10⁻⁶ m = 2000 nm. For max order m, sin θ ≤ 1 => m · λ ≤ d => m ≤ d / λ = 2000 / 600 = 3.33 => Highest integer m = 3.

qs.q: The apparent cubic expansivity of a liquid measured in a glass vessel is 1.5 × 10⁻⁴ K⁻¹. If the linear expansivity of glass is 1.0 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹, compute the real (absolute) cubic expansivity of the liquid.
qs.e: Formula: γ_real = γ_apparent + γ_container. Container cubic expansivity γ_vessel = 3 × α_glass = 3 × 1.0 × 10⁻⁵ = 0.3 × 10⁻⁴ K⁻¹. γ_real = 1.5 × 10⁻⁴ + 0.3 × 10⁻⁴ = 1.8 × 10⁻⁴ K⁻¹.

qs.q: A vessel contains a mixture of 2 moles of Nitrogen and 3 moles of Oxygen gas at a total pressure of 5.0 atm. What is the partial pressure exerted by Nitrogen gas?
qs.e: Formula: Mole fraction χ_N2 = 2 / (2 + 3) = 0.4. Partial pressure P_N2 = χ_N2 × P_total = 0.4 × 5.0 = 2.0 atm.

qs.q: A water wave has a speed of 2.4 m/s and a frequency of 6.0 Hz. What is the distance between two consecutive wave crests?
qs.e: Formula: Distance between consecutive crests = wavelength λ = v / f = 2.4 / 6.0 = 0.4 m.

qs.q: An open organ pipe of length L1 has the same fundamental frequency as a closed organ pipe of length L2. Determine the ratio L1 / L2.
qs.e: Formula: Open pipe fundamental f_open = v / (2 L1). Closed pipe fundamental f_closed = v / (4 L2). Since f_open = f_closed => v / (2 L1) = v / (4 L2) => 2 L1 = 4 L2 => L1 / L2 = 2.

qs.q: Unpolarized light is incident on a polished glass plate of refractive index n = 1.50. Calculate Brewster's polarizing angle of incidence. (Take tan⁻¹(1.50) ≈ 56.3°)
qs.e: Formula: Brewster's law tan(θ_B) = n => θ_B = tan⁻¹(1.50) = 56.3°.

qs.q: A solar collector panel of area 3.0 m² receives solar radiation at a rate of 800 W/m². If its efficiency in heating water is 50%, how long will it take to raise the temperature of 20 kg of water by 30°C? (c_water = 4200 J/kg·K)
qs.e: Formula: Total incident solar power = 800 × 3.0 = 2400 W. Useful power P = 0.50 × 2400 = 1200 W. Required heat Q = m · c · ΔT = 20 × 4200 × 30 = 2,520,000 J. Time t = Q / P = 2,520,000 / 1200 = 2100 seconds (35.0 minutes).

qs.q: A compressed gas cylinder fitted with a safety valve designed to open at a pressure of 12.0 atm contains gas at 8.0 atm at 27°C. To what maximum temperature can the cylinder be safely heated before the valve opens?

A guitar string of fixed length L and mass per unit length µ is under tension T. If the tension in the string is quadrupled while all other parameters remain constant, how does the fundamental frequency change?
qs.e: Formula: f = (1 / 2L) √(T / µ) => f ∝ √T. Replacing T with 4T gives f_new = √(4) · f = 2 f.

qs.q: An ambulance siren produces sound of frequency 680 Hz. If the ambulance approaches a stationary pedestrian at a speed of 20 m/s on a windless day, calculate the frequency heard by the pedestrian. (Speed of sound in air = 340 m/s)
qs.e: Formula: Doppler shift for approaching source f' = f × (v / (v - u_source)). Substitution: f' = 680 × (340 / (340 - 20)) = 680 × (340 / 320) = 680 × 1.0625 = 722.5 Hz.

qs.q: Monochromatic light of wavelength 600 nm passes through a single narrow slit of width 0.12 mm. Find the angular half-width (angle from central maximum to first minimum) of the central diffraction peak.
qs.e: Formula: Single slit first minimum condition a · sin θ = λ => sin θ ≈ θ = λ / a. Substitution: θ = 600 × 10⁻⁹ / (0.12 × 10⁻³) = 6.0 × 10⁻⁷ / 1.2 × 10⁻⁴ = 0.005 rad (0.286°).

qs.q: A composite wall consists of an inner layer of brick (thickness L1 = 0.10 m, thermal conductivity K1 = 0.6 W/m·K) and an outer insulation layer (thickness L2 = 0.05 m, K2 = 0.05 W/m·K). If inner temperature is 25°C and outer temperature is 5°C, find the steady-state temperature at the interface.
qs.e: Formula: Thermal resistance R = L / K. R1 = 0.10 / 0.6 = 0.1667 K/W, R2 = 0.05 / 0.05 = 1.0 K/W. At steady state, (25 - T_int) / 0.1667 = (T_int - 5) / 1.0 => 6(25 - T_int) = T_int - 5 => 150 - 6 T_int = T_int - 5 => 155 = 7 T_int => T_int = 22.14°C.

qs.q: The pressure exerted by an ideal gas of density ρ and root-mean-square velocity v_rms is given by kinetic theory as
qs.e: Formula: P = (1/3) ρ v_rms², derived from kinetic momentum transfer of N gas molecules colliding with container walls.

qs.q: When a progressive wave pulse on a light string reflects from a rigid fixed boundary, it undergoes a phase shift of
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Reflection at a fixed rigid end undergoes a 180° phase inversion due to Newton's third law reaction force exerted by the support.

qs.q: A sonometer wire of length 0.8 m and mass per unit length 2.0 × 10⁻³ kg/m is kept under a tension of 160 N. Calculate the fundamental frequency of the wire.

To reduce reflections from a glass lens surface (n = 1.50), an anti-reflection thin film coating of magnesium fluoride (n = 1.38) is applied. What is the minimum non-zero thickness of the coating required for destructive interference of reflected yellow light (λ = 552 nm in air)?
qs.e: Formula: For destructive reflection in anti-reflection coating (phase shift at both interfaces), minimum coating thickness t = λ_air / (4 n_film) = 552 nm / (4 × 1.38) = 552 / 5.52 = 100 nm.

qs.q: A blackbody sphere of radius R1 at temperature T1 = 300 K radiates thermal power P1. If its temperature is raised to T2 = 600 K while its radius remains unchanged, what is the new radiated power P2 in terms of P1?
qs.e: Formula: Stefan-Boltzmann law P = ε σ A T⁴ => P ∝ T⁴. P2 / P1 = (T2 / T1)⁴ = (600 / 300)⁴ = 2⁴ = 16. Thus P2 = 16 P1.

qs.q: The Van der Waals equation of state for one mole of a real gas is written as (P + a/V²)(V - b) = RT. What physical effect does the term 'a/V²' account for?
o: Attractive intermolecular forces reducing measured pressure
Finite volume occupied by gas molecules
Loss of kinetic energy during inelastic collisions
Rotational degree of freedom of real gas molecules
qs.e: Physical reasoning: The term a/V² accounts for cohesive attractive forces between real gas molecules which reduce the impact force against container walls compared to ideal gases.

qs.q: A spherical star radiates heat into space. If its radius doubles and its absolute surface temperature is halved, how does its total radiated power change according to Stefan-Boltzmann law?
o: It decreases by factor of 4 (P_new = P / 4)
qs.e: Formula: Radiated power P = 4π R² σ T⁴. P_new = 4π (2R)² σ (T/2)⁴ = 4π (4 R²) σ (T⁴ / 16) = (4/16) P = P / 4.

qs.q: The equation of a transverse progressive wave travelling along a string is given by y(x,t) = 0.04 sin(200π t - 0.5π x), where x and y are in meters and t is in seconds. Determine the speed and direction of propagation of the wave.
qs.e: Formula: General form y = A sin(ω t - k x). Here ω = 200π rad/s, k = 0.5π rad/m. Wave speed v = ω / k = (200π) / (0.5π) = 400 m/s. The minus sign in (ω t - k x) indicates propagation in the positive x-direction.

qs.q: If the sound intensity level in an auditorium increases by 20 decibels (dB), by what factor has the physical sound intensity I increased?

According to Rayleigh's criterion, two point light sources of wavelength λ = 550 nm are just resolved by a circular telescope aperture of diameter D = 0.22 m. Compute the minimum angular separation θ between the two point sources.
qs.e: Formula: Rayleigh criterion θ_min = (1.22 · λ) / D. Substitution: θ_min = (1.22 × 550 × 10⁻⁹ m) / 0.22 m = (6.71 × 10⁻7) / 0.22 = 3.05 × 10⁻⁶ rad.

qs.q: Snell's law of refraction relates the angle of incidence i and angle of refraction r for light passing between two media as
qs.e: Formula: sin i / sin r = n (refractive index). Physical reasoning: Snell's law governs directional bending of light rays at media interfaces.

qs.q: Which type of curved mirror is used as a side wing rear-view mirror on motor vehicles because it produces an erect and wide field of view?
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Convex mirrors always form virtual, erect, and diminished images, offering a wider field of view for drivers.

qs.q: What is the SI unit of electric charge?
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Electric charge is measured in Coulombs, where 1 Coulomb = 1 Ampere-second.

qs.q: The electrical resistance of a uniform metallic conductor is inversely proportional to its
qs.e: Formula: R = ρ · L / A. Resistance is inversely proportional to cross-sectional area A.

qs.q: At the magnetic equator of the Earth, what is the value of the angle of dip (inclination)?
qs.e: Physical reasoning: At the magnetic equator, the Earth's magnetic field lines lie completely horizontal, so angle of dip θ = 0°.

qs.q: The critical angle of a medium is defined as the angle of incidence in the optically denser medium for which the angle of refraction in the rarer medium is
qs.e: Physical reasoning: By definition, at the critical angle of incidence θ_c, the refracted ray grazes the interface at r = 90°.

qs.q: An ammeter is an instrument used to measure electric current. How must an ammeter be connected in an electric circuit?
o: In series-parallel across the power source
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Ammeters have near-zero resistance and must be connected in series so that the full circuit current flows through them.

qs.q: The diagram below illustrates a light ray incident on a rectangular glass block of refractive index n = 1.50. <svg width="180" height="140" viewBox="0 0 180 140" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="40" y="35" width="100" height="70" fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="90" y1="15" x2="90" y2="125" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="3,3"/><line x1="30" y1="10" x2="90" y2="35" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="90" y1="35" x2="105" y2="105" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="105" y1="105" x2="165" y2="130" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2"/><text x="25" y="25" font-size="10">Incident Ray</text></svg> If the angle of incidence in air is 30.0°, calculate the angle of refraction r inside the glass block.
A concave mirror has a focal length of 15 cm. An object is placed 30 cm in front of the mirror on its principal axis. Calculate the distance of the image from the mirror.
qs.e: Formula: 1/f = 1/u + 1/v => 1/15 = 1/30 + 1/v => 1/v = 1/15 - 1/30 = 1/30 => v = 30 cm. Image is real, inverted, and located at 2f.

qs.q: Two positive point charges q1 = +2.0 µC and q2 = +4.0 µC are separated by a distance of 0.30 m in vacuum. Calculate the electrostatic repulsive force between them. (k = 1/(4πε0) = 9.0 × 10⁹ N·m²/C²)

Consider the electrical circuit shown below. <svg width="180" height="120" viewBox="0 0 180 120" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="25" y="25" width="130" height="70" fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="60" y="15" width="40" height="20" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2"/><text x="80" y="29" font-size="9" text-anchor="middle">R1=6Ω</text><line x1="115" y1="25" x2="115" y2="95" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="95" y="50" width="40" height="20" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2"/><text x="115" y="64" font-size="9" text-anchor="middle">R2=12Ω</text><rect x="50" y="85" width="30" height="20" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2"/><text x="65" y="99" font-size="9" text-anchor="middle">12V</text></svg> Resistor R1 = 6 Ω is connected in series with a parallel branch of two 12 Ω resistors across a 12 V DC supply. What total current flows from the battery?
qs.e: Formula: R_parallel = (12 × 12) / (12 + 12) = 6 Ω. Total equivalent resistance R_eq = R1 + R_parallel = 6 + 6 = 12 Ω. Total current I = V / R_eq = 12 V / 12 Ω = 1.0 A.

qs.q: A straight wire of length 0.50 m carrying a current of 4.0 A is positioned at right angles to a uniform magnetic field of flux density 0.20 T. Calculate the magnetic force exerted on the wire.
qs.e: Formula: F = B · I · L · sin(θ). Substitution: F = 0.20 T × 4.0 A × 0.50 m × sin(90°) = 0.40 N.

qs.q: A swimming pool appears to be 3.0 m deep when viewed vertically from above. If the refractive index of water is 1.33 (4/3), calculate the real depth of the pool.
qs.e: Formula: Refractive index n = Real depth / Apparent depth => Real depth = n × Apparent depth. Substitution: Real depth = (4/3) × 3.0 m = 4.0 m.

qs.q: A convex lens has a focal length of 20 cm. If an object is placed 10 cm in front of the lens, describe the image formed.
o: Virtual, erect, and located 20 cm in front of the lens
Real, inverted, and located 20 cm behind the lens
Virtual, inverted, and located 10 cm in front of the lens
Real, erect, and located 40 cm behind the lens
qs.e: Formula: 1/f = 1/u + 1/v => 1/20 = 1/10 + 1/v => 1/v = 1/20 - 1/10 = -1/20 => v = -20 cm. Negative sign indicates virtual, erect image located on object side.

qs.q: Calculate the electric potential at a distance of 0.50 m from a point charge of +5.0 µC in free space. (k = 9.0 × 10⁹ N·m²/C²)
qs.e: Formula: Electric potential V = k · Q / r. Substitution: V = (9.0 × 10⁹ × 5.0 × 10⁻⁶) / 0.50 = (4.5 × 10⁴) / 0.50 = 9.0 × 10⁴ V (90 kV).

qs.q: An electric light bulb is marked '220 V, 100 W'. Calculate the electrical resistance of the filament when operated at its rated voltage.
qs.e: Formula: Power P = V² / R => Resistance R = V² / P. Substitution: R = (220)² / 100 = 48,400 / 100 = 484 Ω.

qs.q: Bar magnets attract iron filings most strongly at their pole ends. The region around a magnet where magnetic force is detectable is called the
qs.e: Physical reasoning: A magnetic field is the space around a magnet or current-carrying conductor where magnetic forces act on magnetic materials or charges.

qs.q: The speed of light in vacuum is 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s. Calculate the speed of light in a diamond crystal having a refractive index of 2.42.
qs.e: Formula: Refractive index n = c / v => v = c / n. Substitution: v = 3.0 × 10⁸ / 2.42 = 1.2396 × 10⁸ ≈ 1.24 × 10⁸ m/s.

qs.q: A household in Enugu operates a 1.5 kW air conditioner for 8 hours daily. Calculate the cost of running this appliance for 30 days if PHCN charges ₦50 per kilowatt-hour (kWh).
qs.e: Formula: Energy consumed in kWh = Power (kW) × Time (hours) = 1.5 kW × (8 h/day × 30 days) = 1.5 × 240 = 360 kWh. Total cost = 360 kWh × ₦50/kWh = ₦18,000.

qs.q: Determine the critical angle for total internal reflection when light passes from a dense crown glass prism (n = 2.00) into air.
qs.e: Formula: sin(θ_c) = 1 / n. Substitution: sin(θ_c) = 1 / 2.00 = 0.500 => θ_c = sin⁻¹(0.500) = 30.0°.

qs.q: A compound microscope has an objective lens of magnifying power 10 and an eyepiece of magnifying power 15. Determine the total magnification produced by the microscope.
qs.e: Formula: Total magnification M_total = M_objective × M_eyepiece. Substitution: M_total = 10 × 15 = 150.

qs.q: A parallel-plate air capacitor has a capacitance of 12 µF. If the space between its plates is completely filled with a dielectric material of dielectric constant K = 5.0, what is its new capacitance?
qs.e: Formula: C_dielectric = K · C_air. Substitution: C = 5.0 × 12 µF = 60 µF.

qs.q: A dry cell of electromotive force (e.m.f.) 2.0 V and internal resistance r is connected across an external resistor of 3.8 Ω. If the terminal potential difference across the cell is 1.9 V, compute r.
qs.e: Formula: Current I = V / R = 1.9 / 3.8 = 0.50 A. Cell equation E = V + I · r => 2.0 = 1.9 + 0.50 r => 0.10 = 0.50 r => r = 0.20 Ω.

qs.q: The total magnetic field of the Earth at a location in Northern Nigeria is 4.0 × 10⁻⁵ T, and the angle of dip is 60°. Calculate the magnitude of the horizontal component of the Earth's magnetic field B_H.
qs.e: Formula: B_H = B_total · cos(θ). Substitution: B_H = 4.0 × 10⁻⁵ T × cos(60°) = 4.0 × 10⁻⁵ × 0.50 = 2.0 × 10⁻⁵ T.

qs.q: A light ray passes symmetrically through an equilateral triangular glass prism (angle of prism A = 60°) at minimum deviation. If the angle of minimum deviation is 30°, compute the refractive index of the glass.
When a thin converging convex lens of refractive index n = 1.5 is immersed in clean water (n = 1.33), its focal length
qs.e: Formula: Lens maker's formula 1/f = (n_lens / n_medium - 1) × (1/R1 - 1/R2). Immersing in water lowers relative refractive index from 1.5 to (1.5/1.33 = 1.128), reducing power and increasing focal length f.

qs.q: Calculate the electrical energy stored in a 20 µF capacitor charged to a potential difference of 200 V.
qs.e: Formula: E = 0.5 · C · V². Substitution: E = 0.5 × (20 × 10⁻⁶ F) × (200 V)² = 10⁻⁵ × 40,000 = 0.40 J.

qs.q: Four resistors arranged in a Wheatstone bridge network are R1 = 10 Ω, R2 = 20 Ω, R3 = 15 Ω, and R4. If the bridge is balanced so no current flows through the central galvanometer, calculate R4.
qs.e: Formula: For balance R1 / R2 = R3 / R4 => 10 / 20 = 15 / R4 => 0.5 = 15 / R4 => R4 = 30 Ω.

qs.q: An electron of charge 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C moving at a speed of 5.0 × 10⁶ m/s enters perpendicularly into a uniform magnetic field of 0.20 T. Compute the magnetic force acting on the electron.
qs.e: Formula: F = q · v · B · sin(90°). Substitution: F = (1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) × (5.0 × 10⁶ m/s) × (0.20 T) = 1.6 × 10⁻¹³ N.

qs.q: A parallel-sided glass slab of thickness 6.0 cm and refractive index 1.50 is placed over a printed mark on paper. By what distance does the mark appear raised when viewed normally?
qs.e: Formula: Apparent displacement d = t · (1 - 1/n). Substitution: d = 6.0 cm × (1 - 1/1.50) = 6.0 × (1 - 0.6667) = 6.0 × (1/3) = 2.0 cm.

qs.q: Two thin lenses of focal lengths +20 cm and -50 cm are placed in thin contact. Calculate the focal length of the lens combination.
qs.e: Formula: Power P_total = P1 + P2 = (1/f1) + (1/f2) in meters = (1/0.20) + (1/-0.50) = +5.0 - 2.0 = +3.0 Dioptres. F_total = 1 / P_total = 1 / 3.0 m = +0.333 m = +33.3 cm.

qs.q: Two large parallel metal plates separated by a distance of 0.05 m in air are connected across a 250 V DC supply. Compute the electric field intensity between the plates.
qs.e: Formula: Electric field E = V / d. Substitution: E = 250 V / 0.05 m = 5000 V/m (N/C).

qs.q: How does the electrical resistance of pure metals and intrinsic semiconductors change as temperature increases?
o: Metal resistance increases; semiconductor resistance decreases
Metal resistance decreases; semiconductor resistance increases
Both metal and semiconductor resistance increase
Both metal and semiconductor resistance decrease
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Heating metals increases lattice vibration scattering (increasing resistance), while heating semiconductors liberates electron-hole pairs (decreasing resistance).

qs.q: Materials that possess small positive magnetic susceptibility and are weakly attracted into a magnetic field are classified as
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Paramagnetic substances (e.g. aluminum) have small positive magnetic susceptibility and are weakly attracted by magnets.

qs.q: In a potentiometer experiment, a standard cell of e.m.f. 1.50 V gives a balance length of 60.0 cm along the uniform slide wire. An unknown cell gives a balance length of 80.0 cm. What is the e.m.f. of the unknown cell?

A light ray in air enters a liquid layer of refractive index 1.33 floating on a glass block of refractive index 1.50. If the ray enters the liquid at 45°, calculate the angle of refraction inside the glass block.
qs.e: Formula: Snell's law across parallel layers: n_air · sin(i) = n_glass · sin(r_glass) => 1.0 × sin(45°) = 1.50 × sin(r_glass) => sin(r_glass) = 0.7071 / 1.50 = 0.4714 => r_glass = sin⁻¹(0.4714) = 28.1°.

qs.q: Using the displacement method, a convex lens placed at two positions separated by d = 20 cm produces sharp images of an object on a screen separated from the object by D = 100 cm. Compute the focal length of the lens.
qs.e: Formula: Focal length f = (D² - d²) / (4D). Substitution: f = (100² - 20²) / (4 × 100) = (10000 - 400) / 400 = 9600 / 400 = 24.0 cm.

qs.q: A hollow conducting metal sphere of radius R = 0.20 m carries a net static charge Q = +4.0 µC. Calculate the electric field intensity E at a point located 0.10 m from the center inside the sphere.
qs.e: Formula: According to Gauss's law, all electrostatic charge resides on the outer surface of a conductor. The interior electric field E = 0 everywhere inside a hollow conductor.

qs.q: A galvanometer has a coil resistance Rg = 50 Ω and gives full-scale deflection for a current Ig = 2.0 mA. What shunt resistance S must be connected in parallel to convert it into an ammeter reading up to 5.0 A?
qs.e: Formula: Shunt S = (Ig · Rg) / (I - Ig). Substitution: S = (0.002 A × 50 Ω) / (5.0 A - 0.002 A) = 0.10 / 4.998 ≈ 0.020 Ω.

qs.q: A rectangular wire coil of 100 turns, area A = 0.02 m², carrying a current of 3.0 A is placed in a uniform magnetic field B = 0.50 T. What is the maximum magnetic torque exerted on the coil?
qs.e: Formula: Max torque τ_max = N · I · A · B. Substitution: τ_max = 100 × 3.0 A × 0.02 m² × 0.50 T = 3.0 N·m.

qs.q: An optical fiber core has refractive index n1 = 1.60 surrounded by cladding of n2 = 1.44. Calculate the critical angle at the core-cladding interface for guiding light through total internal reflection.
qs.e: Formula: sin(θ_c) = n2 / n1. Substitution: sin(θ_c) = 1.44 / 1.60 = 0.900 => θ_c = sin⁻¹(0.900) = 64.16° ≈ 64.2°.

qs.q: Spherical aberration in thick spherical mirrors can be eliminated or minimized by replacing them with
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Parabolic mirrors bring all parallel incoming rays (both marginal and axial) to a single sharp focal point, eliminating spherical aberration.

qs.q: Two capacitors C1 = 4.0 µF and C2 = 6.0 µF are connected in series across a 100 V DC source. Calculate the electric charge on each capacitor and potential difference across C1.
o: Charge = 240 µC; Voltage across C1 = 60 V
Charge = 400 µC; Voltage across C1 = 40 V
Charge = 240 µC; Voltage across C1 = 40 V
Charge = 100 µC; Voltage across C1 = 50 V
qs.e: Formula: Equivalent series capacitance C_eq = (4 × 6) / (4 + 6) = 2.4 µF. Total charge Q = C_eq × V = 2.4 µF × 100 V = 240 µC (same on both capacitors). Voltage across C1: V1 = Q / C1 = 240 µC / 4.0 µF = 60 V.

qs.q: A galvanometer of resistance Rg = 100 Ω full-scale deflection Ig = 1.0 mA is to be converted into a voltmeter reading up to 10.0 V. Calculate the resistance R of the multiplier resistor required in series.
qs.e: Formula: Multiplier resistance R = (V / Ig) - Rg. Substitution: R = (10.0 V / 0.001 A) - 100 Ω = 10,000 - 100 = 9,900 Ω.

qs.q: A proton of mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg and charge 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C moves in a circular orbit of radius r = 0.20 m in a uniform magnetic field B = 0.50 T. Calculate the orbital speed of the proton.
qs.e: Formula: Magnetic centripetal equilibrium q · v · B = (m · v²) / r => v = (q · B · r) / m. Substitution: v = (1.6×10⁻¹⁹ × 0.50 × 0.20) / (1.67×10⁻²⁷) = (1.6 × 10⁻²⁰) / (1.67 × 10⁻²⁷) = 9.58 × 10⁶ m/s.

qs.q: According to the Maximum Power Transfer Theorem, a DC source of electromotive force E and internal resistance r delivers maximum electrical power to an external load resistor R when R equals
qs.e: Formula: P_load = I² R = (E / (R + r))² R. Differentiating dP/dR = 0 yields R = r for maximum power dissipation in load.

qs.q: A parallel-plate capacitor connected to a constant voltage supply V has plate separation d and initial force of attraction F1 between plates. If the separation is doubled to 2d while remaining connected to V, what is the new attractive force F2?
qs.e: Formula: Force F = 0.5 · ε0 · A · (V / d)². Since voltage V is constant, force F is inversely proportional to d² (F ∝ 1/d²). Doubling d reduces force by factor of 2² = 4 => F2 = 0.25 F1.

qs.q: White light passes through a glass prism. The dispersion of color components occurs primarily because
o: The refractive index of glass varies inversely with wavelength, bending violet more than red
Red light travels faster in vacuum than violet light
Violet light has higher velocity inside glass than red light
Red light undergoes total internal reflection inside the prism
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Glass dispersion happens because refractive index n decreases with increasing wavelength (n_violet > n_red), causing violet light to refract through larger angles than red light.

qs.q: Two long straight parallel conductors separated by distance d = 0.10 m carry currents I1 = 10 A and I2 = 20 A in the same direction. Calculate the magnetic force per unit length acting between them. (µ0 = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A)
qs.e: Formula: Force per unit length F/L = (µ0 · I1 · I2) / (2π · d). Currents in same direction attract. Substitution: F/L = (4π × 10⁻⁷ × 10 × 20) / (2π × 0.10) = 2 × 10⁻⁷ × 2000 = 4.0 × 10⁻⁴ N/m (attractive).

qs.q: A thin convex glass lens exhibits chromatic aberration. If blue light and red light focus at distances f_blue and f_red from the lens center respectively, which relation is correct?
qs.e: Formula: Since n_blue > n_red, power P_blue > P_red, meaning the lens bends blue light more strongly. Thus focal length for blue is shorter than red: f_red > f_blue.

qs.q: Lenz's law of electromagnetic induction states that the direction of an induced electromotive force (e.m.f.) is always such that it
o: Opposes the change in magnetic flux producing it
Reinforces the magnetic flux producing it
Is perpendicular to the velocity vector
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Lenz's law is a consequence of conservation of energy; induced current flows to oppose the change in magnetic flux that creates it.

qs.q: In the photoelectric effect, the minimum frequency of incident light required to cause the emission of photoelectrons from a metal surface is called the
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Threshold frequency f0 is the minimum photon frequency needed to overcome the binding energy (work function) of electrons in a metal.

qs.q: An alpha particle emitted during radioactive nuclear decay is identical to a
qs.e: Physical reasoning: An alpha particle consists of two protons and two neutrons, which is identical to a helium-4 nucleus.

qs.q: The process of adding minute controlled quantities of specific impurities to an intrinsic semiconductor to increase its electrical conductivity is known as
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Doping introduces donor or acceptor atoms into intrinsic silicon/germanium to create N-type or P-type semiconductors.

qs.q: For an ideal transformer, the ratio of secondary voltage Vs to primary voltage Vp is equal to the ratio of
o: Secondary turns Ns to primary turns Np
Primary turns Np to secondary turns Ns
Primary current Ip to secondary current Is
Secondary resistance Rs to primary resistance Rp
qs.e: Formula: Vs / Vp = Ns / Np = Ip / Is. Physical reasoning: Induced EMF per turn is identical in both primary and secondary windings.

qs.q: What is the SI unit of activity of a radioactive source?
qs.e: Physical reasoning: One Becquerel (Bq) is defined as one nuclear decay per second (1 decay/s).

qs.q: Which digital logic gate produces a HIGH output (1) ONLY when all of its inputs are HIGH (1)?
qs.e: Physical reasoning: The AND logic operation requires every input to be logic 1 for the output to evaluate to logic 1.

qs.q: An ideal step-down transformer used in a mobile phone charger converts a 220 V AC mains voltage to 11 V AC. If the primary winding has 1000 turns, how many turns are in the secondary winding?
qs.e: Formula: Vs / Vp = Ns / Np => Ns = Np × (Vs / Vp). Substitution: Ns = 1000 × (11 / 220) = 1000 × (1/20) = 50 turns.

qs.q: Calculate the energy of a photon of yellow light having a frequency of 5.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz. (Planck's constant h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s)
qs.e: Formula: E = h · f. Substitution: E = (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s) × (5.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz) = 3.315 × 10⁻¹⁹ J.

qs.q: A radioactive isotope has a half-life of 4.0 days. If a sample initially contains 80 g of the isotope, what mass of the isotope remains un-decayed after 12.0 days?
qs.e: Formula: Number of half-lives n = total time / T1/2 = 12.0 / 4.0 = 3 half-lives. Fraction remaining = (1/2)³ = 1/8. Remaining mass = 80 g / 8 = 10 g.

qs.q: A P-N junction diode allows electric current to flow easily when it is
qs.e: Physical reasoning: In forward bias (p-type connected to positive, n-type to negative), the internal depletion layer narrows, permitting major carrier flow.

qs.q: The root-mean-square (r.m.s.) voltage of the PHCN domestic AC electricity supply in Nigeria is 220 V. Calculate the peak voltage of this supply. (Take √2 ≈ 1.414)
qs.e: Formula: V_peak = V_rms × √2. Substitution: V_peak = 220 V × 1.414 = 311.08 ≈ 311 V.

qs.q: Calculate the de Broglie wavelength of an electron moving at a speed of 2.0 × 10⁶ m/s. (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s, mass of electron m_e = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg)
In the nuclear reaction ₂₃₈₉₂U -> ₂₃₄₉₀Th + X, identify the emitted particle X.
qs.e: Formula: Mass balance: 238 = 234 + A => A = 4. Atomic number balance: 92 = 90 + Z => Z = 2. Particle ₄²X is a Helium nucleus (alpha particle).

qs.q: In a full-wave bridge rectifier circuit, how many semiconductor diodes are connected together in a bridge network?
qs.e: Physical reasoning: A full-wave bridge rectifier utilizes 4 diodes to rectify both positive and negative half-cycles of AC input.

qs.q: A straight copper rod of length 0.40 m moves at a constant velocity of 10.0 m/s perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of flux density 0.50 T. Compute the induced e.m.f. across the rod.
qs.e: Formula: E = B · L · v · sin(90°). Substitution: E = 0.50 T × 0.40 m × 10.0 m/s = 2.0 V.

qs.q: In a Coolidge X-ray tube, high-speed electrons strike a heavy tungsten target. What energy transformation occurs at the target?
o: Kinetic energy of electrons is converted into X-rays and thermal energy
Nuclear energy is converted into electromagnetic radiation
Chemical energy is converted into electrical energy
X-ray photon energy is converted into kinetic energy of target ions
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Rapid deceleration of high-speed electrons striking the heavy metal target produces continuous and characteristic X-rays along with significant heat.

qs.q: During beta-minus (β⁻) radioactive decay, what change occurs within the parent nucleus?
o: A neutron transforms into a proton, emitting an electron and antineutrino
A proton transforms into a neutron, emitting a positron
Two protons and two neutrons are ejected together
The nucleus loses excess excitation energy without changing nucleon numbers
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Beta-minus decay converts a neutron into a proton plus an electron (β⁻ particle) and an antineutrino, increasing atomic number Z by 1 while mass number A remains constant.

qs.q: For an NPN bipolar junction transistor operating as an amplifier in the active region, the bias conditions must be
o: Base-emitter junction forward biased; collector-base junction reverse biased
Both base-emitter and collector-base junctions forward biased
Both base-emitter and collector-base junctions reverse biased
Base-emitter junction reverse biased; collector-base junction forward biased
qs.e: Physical reasoning: Active region operation requires forward-biasing the input (base-emitter) junction and reverse-biasing the output (collector-base) junction.

qs.q: An inductor of self-inductance L = 0.20 H carries a current that decreases uniformly from 5.0 A to 1.0 A in a time interval of 0.05 seconds. Calculate the magnitude of the self-induced e.m.f.
Light of frequency 8.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz shines on a potassium metal surface having a work function of 2.0 eV. Calculate the maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons in eV. (h = 4.14 × 10⁻¹⁵ eV·s)
qs.e: Formula: Photon energy E = h · f = (4.14 × 10⁻¹⁵ eV·s) × (8.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz) = 3.312 eV. Max KE = E - W0 = 3.312 - 2.0 = 1.312 ≈ 1.31 eV.

qs.q: The mass defect for a Helium nucleus (₄²He) is measured to be 0.0304 atomic mass units (u). Compute the nuclear binding energy of the Helium nucleus. (1 u = 931.5 MeV)
qs.e: Formula: Binding energy BE = Δm · 931.5 MeV. Substitution: BE = 0.0304 u × 931.5 MeV/u = 28.3176 ≈ 28.32 MeV.

qs.q: In a common-emitter transistor amplifier circuit, a base current change of ΔIb = 40 µA produces a collector current change of ΔIc = 3.2 mA. Calculate the small-signal current gain β of the transistor.
qs.e: Formula: Current gain β = ΔIc / ΔIb. Substitution: ΔIb = 40 × 10⁻⁶ A = 0.04 mA. β = 3.2 mA / 0.04 mA = 80.

qs.q: A transformer connected to a 220 V AC supply draws a primary current of 2.0 A. If it delivers a secondary current of 36 A at a voltage of 11 V, calculate the operational efficiency of the transformer.
qs.e: Formula: Power input P_in = Vp · Ip = 220 V × 2.0 A = 440 W. Power output P_out = Vs · Is = 11 V × 36 A = 396 W. Efficiency η = (P_out / P_in) × 100% = (396 / 440) × 100% = 90%.

qs.q: According to the Bohr model of the hydrogen atom, an electron transitions from energy level n = 3 (E3 = -1.51 eV) to level n = 2 (E2 = -3.40 eV). What is the energy of the photon emitted?
qs.e: Formula: Photon energy ΔE = E3 - E2 = -1.51 eV - (-3.40 eV) = -1.51 + 3.40 = 1.89 eV.

qs.q: The half-life of Radon-222 is 3.8 days. Calculate the decay constant λ of Radon-222 in units of day⁻¹.
qs.e: Formula: Decay constant λ = ln(2) / T1/2 = 0.69315 / 3.8 days = 0.1824 ≈ 0.182 day⁻¹.

qs.q: Identify the logic gate whose truth table output is logic 1 ONLY when both inputs A and B are logic 0.
