qs.q: Industrial synthesis of sulfur trioxide: 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g) (ΔH = -198 kJ/mol). According to Le Chatelier's principle, which operational conditions maximize the equilibrium yield of SO₃?
qs.e: Forward reaction reduces gas moles (3 moles reactant -> 2 moles product) and is exothermic. Thus, high pressure (favors fewer moles) and low temperature (favors exothermic direction) maximize SO₃ yield.

qs.q: In a standard Daniell electrochemical cell Zn(s) | Zn²⁺(aq) || Cu²⁺(aq) | Cu(s), which electrode serves as the anode and what primary reaction occurs there?
o: Zinc electrode, where oxidation Zn(s) -> Zn²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ occurs
Copper electrode, where oxidation Cu(s) -> Cu²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ occurs
Zinc electrode, where reduction Zn²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ -> Zn(s) occurs
Copper electrode, where reduction Cu²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ -> Cu(s) occurs
qs.e: In a galvanic cell, oxidation occurs at the negative anode. Zinc is more reactive than copper, so the zinc electrode acts as the anode where Zn undergoes oxidation to Zn²⁺.

qs.q: Titration of 25.0 cm³ of a 0.050 mol/dm³ sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃) solution required 20.0 cm³ of hydrochloric acid (HCl) for complete neutralization using methyl orange indicator. Calculate the concentration of the HCl solution in mol/dm³.
qs.e: Reaction: Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl -> 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂ (n_b = 1, n_a = 2). Formula: (C_a x V_a) / (C_b x V_b) = 2 / 1 -> C_a = (2 x C_b x V_b) / V_a = (2 x 0.050 x 25.0) / 20.0 = 2.5 / 20.0 = 0.125 mol/dm³.

qs.q: How many Coulombs of electricity are required to deposit 0.54 g of aluminium metal at the cathode during the electrolysis of molten alumina? (Al = 27.0, Faraday constant F = 96,500 C/mol)
qs.e: Cathode reaction: Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ -> Al. Moles of Al = 0.54 g / 27.0 g/mol = 0.020 mol. Moles of e⁻ needed = 3 x 0.020 = 0.060 mol. Charge Q = n x F = 0.060 mol x 96,500 C/mol = 5790 C.

qs.q: What type of structural isomerism is illustrated by the pair of alkenes 1-butene and 2-butene?
qs.e: 1-butene (CH₂=CH-CH₂-CH₃) and 2-butene (CH₃-CH=CH-CH₃) have the same carbon skeleton and functional group, but differ in the position of the C=C double bond, making them position isomers.

qs.q: When ethanol (C₂H₅OH) is heated at 170 °C with excess concentrated sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄), what primary gaseous organic product is obtained?
qs.e: Dehydration of ethanol at 170 °C with conc. H₂SO₄ yields ethene: C₂H₅OH -> C₂H₄ + H₂O. (At lower temperature ~140 °C with excess ethanol, ethoxyethane is formed).

qs.q: Which condensation synthetic polymer is produced by reacting hexamethylenediamine with hexane-1,6-dioic acid (adipic acid)?
qs.e: Hexamethylenediamine (6 carbons) and adipic acid (6 carbons) undergo condensation polymerization with elimination of water to form the polyamide Nylon-6,6.

qs.q: Which major metallic element is commercially extracted from bauxite ore via purified alumina?
qs.e: Bauxite (hydrated aluminium oxide, Al₂O₃·xH₂O) is the principal ore used for the industrial extraction of aluminium metal.

qs.q: Which acidic gas is evolved when solid sodium chloride reacts with concentrated sulfuric acid upon gentle warming?
qs.e: Reaction: NaCl(s) + H₂SO₄(l) -> NaHSO₄(s) + HCl(g). Conc. H₂SO₄ is not strong enough to oxidize Cl⁻ to Cl₂, so misty fumes of HCl gas are evolved.

qs.q: Which atmospheric pollutants cause depletion of the stratospheric ozone layer through catalytic destruction cycles?
qs.e: CFCs released into the stratosphere undergo photolysis by UV light to form chlorine free radicals (Cl·), which catalytically destroy ozone molecules (O₃).

qs.q: In qualitative inorganic analysis, what reagents are used to carry out the 'brown ring test' for nitrate ions (NO₃⁻)?
o: Freshly prepared iron(II) sulfate solution and concentrated H₂SO₄
Barium nitrate solution and dilute nitric acid
Silver nitrate solution and aqueous ammonia
Sodium hydroxide solution and aluminium foil
qs.e: Mixing NO₃⁻ solution with fresh FeSO₄ solution and carefully layering conc. H₂SO₄ down the side of the test tube forms a brown ring of [Fe(H₂O)₅(NO)]²⁺ at the liquid interface.

qs.q: Why does diamond possess an extraordinarily high melting point (~3550 °C) and extreme mechanical hardness?
o: It forms a 3D giant covalent lattice with strong sp³ C-C bonds throughout
It consists of close-packed carbon cations surrounded by delocalized electrons
Strong van der Waals forces bind its heavy carbon macromolecular rings
It contains ionic bonds between alternating carbon isotopes
qs.e: Each carbon in diamond is tetrahedrally bonded to 4 other carbon atoms by strong covalent bonds in a continuous 3D network lattice, requiring immense thermal energy to break.

qs.q: What is the ground-state valence electron configuration of an iron(III) ion, Fe³⁺? (Iron atomic number Z = 26)
qs.e: Neutral iron atom Fe: [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s². Upon losing 3 electrons to form Fe³⁺, the two 4s electrons are removed first, followed by one 3d electron, leaving [Ar] 3d⁵.

qs.q: A sample of 2.50 g of a hydrated metal sulfate MSO₄·xH₂O was heated strongly, driving off water and leaving 1.60 g of anhydrous MSO₄. Given the relative atomic mass of M is 64.0, determine x. (S = 32.0, O = 16.0, H = 1.0)

Using Graham's law: Gas A diffuses through a porous plug in 40 seconds, whereas an equal volume of oxygen gas (O₂) diffuses under identical conditions in 20 seconds. Calculate the molar mass of gas A. (O = 16.0)
qs.e: Time is inversely proportional to rate: t_A / t_O₂ = √(M_A / M_O₂). M_O₂ = 32 g/mol. (40 s / 20 s) = √(M_A / 32) -> 2 = √(M_A / 32) -> 4 = M_A / 32 -> M_A = 128 g/mol.

qs.q: The equilibrium constant K_c for A(g) + 2B(g) ⇌ C(g) is 4.0 dm⁶/mol² at a given temperature. If the equilibrium concentrations of A and C are both 0.50 mol/dm³, calculate the equilibrium concentration of B.

Complete combustion of 0.80 g of methanol (CH₃OH) in a bomb calorimeter raised the temperature of 200 g of water by 24.0 °C. Calculate the standard enthalpy of combustion per mole of methanol. (C = 12.0, H = 1.0, O = 16.0, c = 4.2 J/g·°C)
qs.e: Q = m x c x ΔT = 200 g x 4.2 J/g·°C x 24.0 °C = 20,160 J = 20.16 kJ. Molar mass CH₃OH = 32.0 g/mol. Moles burned = 0.80 g / 32.0 g/mol = 0.025 mol. ΔH_c = -Q / moles = -20.16 kJ / 0.025 mol = -806.4 kJ/mol.

qs.q: What mass of pure solid sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is required to prepare 500 cm³ of an aqueous solution having a pH of 13.0 at 25 °C? (Na = 23.0, O = 16.0, H = 1.0)
qs.e: pH = 13.0 -> pOH = 14.0 - 13.0 = 1.0 -> [OH⁻] = 10⁻¹ = 0.10 mol/dm³. Volume = 0.50 dm³. Moles NaOH = 0.10 mol/dm³ x 0.50 dm³ = 0.050 mol. Molar mass NaOH = 40.0 g/mol. Mass = 0.050 mol x 40.0 g/mol = 2.00 g.

qs.q: In the electrolysis of aqueous copper(II) sulfate using copper electrodes, a current of 2.00 A flows for 4825 seconds. What is the mass change of the copper anode?
qs.e: At anode, copper dissolves: Cu(s) -> Cu²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻. Q = 2.00 A x 4825 s = 9650 C. Moles e⁻ = 9650 / 96500 = 0.10 mol. Moles Cu dissolved = 0.10 / 2 = 0.050 mol. Mass decrease = 0.050 mol x 63.5 g/mol = 3.175 g ≈ 3.18 g decrease.

qs.q: What volume of 0.020 mol/dm³ potassium permanganate (KMnO₄) solution in acidic medium is required to oxidize completely 25.0 cm³ of 0.10 mol/dm³ iron(II) sulfate (FeSO₄) solution?
qs.e: Ionic equation: MnO₄⁻ + 5Fe²⁺ + 8H⁺ -> Mn²⁺ + 5Fe³⁺ + 4H₂O (n_a = 1, n_b = 5). Formula: (C_a x V_a) / (C_b x V_b) = 1 / 5 -> V_a = (C_b x V_b) / (5 x C_a) = (0.10 x 25.0) / (5 x 0.020) = 2.5 / 0.10 = 25.0 cm³.

qs.q: What two organic compounds are formed when ethyl propanoate (CH₃CH₂COOCH₂CH₃) undergoes alkaline hydrolysis with aqueous sodium hydroxide solution?
qs.e: Saponification: CH₃CH₂COOCH₂CH₃ + NaOH -> CH₃CH₂COONa (sodium propanoate) + CH₃CH₂OH (ethanol).

qs.q: In the Solvay process for manufacturing sodium carbonate, what gaseous compound is recovered when ammonium chloride solution is treated with calcium hydroxide Ca(OH)₂?
qs.e: In the ammonia recovery tower: 2NH₄Cl + Ca(OH)₂ -> CaCl₂ + 2H₂O + 2NH₃(g). The liberated ammonia gas is recycled back into the process.

qs.q: When 2.46 g of hydrated magnesium sulfate (MgSO₄·xH₂O) was heated to constant mass, 1.20 g of anhydrous MgSO₄ remained. Determine x. (Mg = 24.3, S = 32.0, O = 16.0, H = 1.0)
In the van der Waals equation for real gases, (P + a/V²)(V - b) = RT, what physical property does the correction term 'a/V²' account for?
o: Intermolecular attractive forces between gas particles
The finite volume occupied by gas molecules
Inelastic collisions between gas particles and container walls
Dissociation of gas molecules into atoms
qs.e: The constant 'a' corrects for intermolecular attractive forces that reduce observed pressure compared to an ideal gas. Constant 'b' corrects for actual volume occupied by gas molecules.

qs.q: A 1.50 g mixture of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) and magnesium carbonate (MgCO₃) was heated strongly to constant mass, leaving a residue of 0.76 g of mixed oxides (CaO and MgO). Calculate the mass of CaCO₃ present in the original mixture. (Ca = 40.0, Mg = 24.3, C = 12.0, O = 16.0)
qs.e: Let x = mass CaCO₃, so (1.50 - x) = mass MgCO₃. M(CaCO₃) = 100.0 g/mol, M(CaO) = 56.0 g/mol. Residue from x g CaCO₃ = 0.56x. M(MgCO₃) = 84.3 g/mol, M(MgO) = 40.3 g/mol. Residue from MgCO₃ = (40.3/84.3)(1.50 - x) = 0.478(1.50 - x) = 0.717 - 0.478x. Total residue = 0.56x + 0.717 - 0.478x = 0.76 -> 0.082x = 0.043 -> x = 0.524 g ≈ 0.52 g.

qs.q: Calculate the lattice enthalpy of crystalline sodium chloride, NaCl(s), given the Born-Haber data: ΔH_f°(NaCl) = -411 kJ/mol, ΔH_sub(Na) = +107 kJ/mol, IE₁(Na) = +496 kJ/mol, ½ D(Cl₂) = +122 kJ/mol, EA₁(Cl) = -349 kJ/mol.
qs.e: Born-Haber cycle equation: ΔH_f° = ΔH_sub + IE₁ + ½ D + EA₁ + U. -411 = 107 + 496 + 122 - 349 + U -> -411 = +376 + U -> U = -411 - 376 = -787 kJ/mol.

qs.q: Calculate the standard cell potential E°cell for the spontaneous redox reaction 3Zn(s) + 2Cr³⁺(aq) -> 3Zn²⁺(aq) + 2Cr(s) given E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = -0.76 V and E°(Cr³⁺/Cr) = -0.74 V.
qs.e: Anode (oxidation): Zn -> Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻ (E° = -0.76 V). Cathode (reduction): Cr³⁺ + 3e⁻ -> Cr (E° = -0.74 V). E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = -0.74 V - (-0.76 V) = +0.02 V.

qs.q: Calculate the pH of a solution prepared by mixing 40.0 cm³ of 0.10 mol/dm³ HCl with 60.0 cm³ of 0.10 mol/dm³ NaOH solution at 25 °C.
qs.e: Moles H⁺ = 0.0400 dm³ x 0.10 mol/dm³ = 0.0040 mol. Moles OH⁻ = 0.0600 dm³ x 0.10 mol/dm³ = 0.0060 mol. Neutralization leaves excess OH⁻ = 0.0060 - 0.0040 = 0.0020 mol in total volume = 100 cm³ = 0.100 dm³. [OH⁻] = 0.0020 / 0.100 = 0.020 mol/dm³. pOH = -log₁₀(0.020) = 1.699. pH = 14.00 - 1.699 = 12.301 ≈ 12.30.

qs.q: A reaction rate constant quadruples from k₁ to k₂ = 4.0 k₁ when the reaction temperature is increased from 300 K to 320 K. Calculate the activation energy Ea for this reaction in kJ/mol. (Gas constant R = 8.314 J/mol·K)
Isotopes of the same chemical element possess the same number of protons but differ in their number of:
qs.e: Isotopes have identical atomic numbers (protons) but different mass numbers due to varying numbers of uncharged neutrons in their nuclei.

qs.q: Which group of chemical elements in the Periodic Table consists of unreactive monoatomic gases with stable outer electron octets?
qs.e: Noble gases (Group 18 / Group 0) have complete valence electron shells (ns² np⁶), rendering them chemically inert under standard conditions.

qs.q: According to VSEPR theory, what molecular geometry is possessed by a water molecule (H₂O)?
qs.e: Water has 2 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs on the central oxygen atom. Repulsion between lone pairs distorts the shape into a V-shaped (bent) geometry with bond angle ~104.5°.

qs.q: What name is given to the physical phase transition in which a solid changes directly into a gas without melting into a liquid?
qs.e: Sublimation is the direct phase change from solid to gas upon heating (e.g., iodine, dry ice, ammonium chloride).

qs.q: What is the pH value of pure neutral water at a temperature of 25 °C?
qs.e: At 25 °C, auto-ionization of water yields [H⁺] = [OH⁻] = 1.0 x 10⁻⁷ mol/dm³, so pH = -log₁₀(1.0 x 10⁻⁷) = 7.0.

qs.q: Which non-metallic element is added to natural rubber during vulcanization to form cross-links and improve elasticity?
qs.e: Vulcanization involves heating natural rubber with elemental sulfur to create disulfide cross-links between polymer chains, increasing toughness and elasticity.

qs.q: Which atmospheric pollutants react in sunlight to generate ground-level ozone and photochemical smog in urban areas?
o: Nitrogen oxides (NOx) and volatile organic compounds
qs.e: Photochemical smog is formed when nitrogen oxides (NOx) and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) undergo photochemical reactions in sunlight.

qs.q: Calculate the relative molar mass of calcium nitrate, Ca(NO₃)₂. (Ca = 40.0, N = 14.0, O = 16.0)
According to Charles's law, for a fixed mass of an ideal gas at constant pressure, the volume is directly proportional to the:
qs.e: Charles's law states V ∝ T (where T is absolute temperature in Kelvin) when mass and pressure remain constant.

qs.q: In the balanced chemical equation C₂H₅OH(l) + 3O₂(g) -> 2CO₂(g) + 3H₂O(g), what is the mole ratio of oxygen to ethanol?
qs.e: The stoichiometric coefficients show that 1 mole of ethanol reacts with 3 moles of oxygen gas, giving a ratio of 3 : 1.

qs.q: What is the physical appearance/color of anhydrous copper(II) sulfate powder, CuSO₄?
qs.e: Anhydrous copper(II) sulfate (CuSO₄) is a white powder. It turns blue when hydrated to form CuSO₄·5H₂O.

qs.q: Why does raising the temperature of a reaction mixture significantly increase the rate of reaction?
o: A greater fraction of colliding molecules possess kinetic energy greater than or equal to activation energy
The activation energy barrier of the reaction is lowered
The overall enthalpy change ΔH of the reaction becomes more exothermic
The concentration of reactants increases automatically
qs.e: Increasing temperature shifts the Boltzmann energy distribution curve, exponentially increasing the proportion of molecules with E ≥ Ea.

qs.q: What term describes the minimum kinetic energy required by colliding reactant molecules to undergo a successful reaction?
qs.e: Activation energy (Ea) is the energy threshold colliding particles must overcome to break existing bonds and form the transition state.

qs.q: Which solid zinc salt decomposes upon heating to leave a oxide residue that is yellow when hot and white when cold?
qs.e: ZnCO₃(s) -> ZnO(s) + CO₂(g). Zinc oxide (ZnO) exhibits thermochromism: it is yellow when hot and turns white upon cooling.

qs.q: In the reduction reaction CuO(s) + H₂(g) -> Cu(s) + H₂O(l), which substance acts as the reducing agent?
qs.e: Hydrogen (H₂) removes oxygen from CuO and undergoes oxidation (oxidation state increases from 0 to +1), so H₂ is the reducing agent.

qs.q: Which gas is evolved at the cathode during the electrolysis of dilute aqueous sulfuric acid using platinum electrodes?
qs.e: At the cathode (negative electrode), hydrogen ions (H⁺) are discharged in preference to water: 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ -> H₂(g).

qs.q: When ethene gas is bubbled into bromine water in the dark, what reaction occurs and what visual change is observed?
o: Addition reaction occurs and reddish-brown bromine water turns colorless
Substitution reaction occurs and a white precipitate forms
Oxidation reaction occurs and solution turns deep purple
No reaction takes place in the dark
qs.e: Ethene undergoes electrophilic addition across C=C to form 1,2-dibromoethane (CH₂Br-CH₂Br), rapidly decolorizing reddish-brown bromine water.

qs.q: Which class of organic compounds is formed when an alkanoic acid reacts with an alkanol in the presence of concentrated sulfuric acid catalyst?
qs.e: Esterification: R-COOH + R'-OH ⇌ R-COO-R' + H₂O. The products are esters (alkanoates) which possess sweet fruity aromas.

qs.q: Which chemical reagent forms a bright silver mirror on the inner wall of a clean test tube when warmed with an alkanal (aldehyde)?
qs.e: Tollens' reagent contains [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺. Aldehydes reduce Ag⁺ to metallic silver (silver mirror) while being oxidized to carboxylate ions.

qs.q: An organic compound contains 52.2% carbon, 13.0% hydrogen, and 34.8% oxygen by mass. Its molar mass is 46.0 g/mol. Determine its molecular formula. (C = 12.0, H = 1.0, O = 16.0)
qs.e: Moles C = 52.2 / 12.0 = 4.35; H = 13.0 / 1.0 = 13.0; O = 34.8 / 16.0 = 2.175. Divide by 2.175: C = 2, H = 6, O = 1. Empirical formula C₂H₆O (mass = 46.0 g/mol). Molecular formula = C₂H₆O.

qs.q: A gas sample occupies 250 cm³ at 20 °C and 1.0 atm pressure. Calculate its volume at 100 °C under the same constant pressure.
qs.e: Using Charles's law: V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂. T₁ = 20 + 273 = 293 K; T₂ = 100 + 273 = 373 K. V₂ = (250 cm³ x 373 K) / 293 K = 93250 / 293 = 318.26 cm³ ≈ 318 cm³.

qs.q: In the industrial synthesis of ammonia N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) (ΔH = -92 kJ/mol), what effect does introducing an iron catalyst have on the equilibrium constant K_c?
o: It has no effect on the value of K_c or the equilibrium position
It increases K_c by favoring the forward reaction
It decreases K_c by accelerating the reverse reaction
It doubles the equilibrium yield of ammonia
qs.e: A catalyst increases the rates of both forward and reverse reactions equally. It speeds up the attainment of equilibrium but does NOT alter K_c or equilibrium position.

qs.q: Calculate the standard e.m.f. of the cell Fe(s) | Fe²⁺(aq) || Cu²⁺(aq) | Cu(s) given E°(Fe²⁺/Fe) = -0.44 V and E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V.
qs.e: E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) - E°(Fe²⁺/Fe) = +0.34 V - (-0.44 V) = +0.78 V.

qs.q: What mass of anhydrous sodium carbonate, Na₂CO₃, is needed to prepare 250 cm³ of a 0.10 mol/dm³ standard solution? (Na = 23.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0)
qs.e: Molar mass Na₂CO₃ = 2(23) + 12 + 3(16) = 106.0 g/mol. Volume = 0.250 dm³. Moles required = 0.10 mol/dm³ x 0.250 dm³ = 0.025 mol. Mass = 0.025 mol x 106.0 g/mol = 2.65 g.

qs.q: Calculate the time required in seconds to deposit 1.08 g of silver metal at the cathode during electrolysis of AgNO₃ solution using a steady current of 0.50 A. (Ag = 108.0, F = 96,500 C/mol)
qs.e: Cathode: Ag⁺ + e⁻ -> Ag. Moles Ag = 1.08 g / 108.0 g/mol = 0.010 mol. Charge Q = moles e⁻ x F = 0.010 mol x 96,500 C/mol = 965 C. Time t = Q / I = 965 C / 0.50 A = 1930 s.

qs.q: Complete combustion of 20.0 cm³ of a gaseous alkane required 100.0 cm³ of oxygen gas at s.t.p. Determine the molecular formula of the alkane.
qs.e: Combustion of alkane C_n H_{2n+2} + [(3n+1)/2] O₂ -> n CO₂ + (n+1) H₂O. Volume ratio O₂ / alkane = 100.0 / 20.0 = 5. (3n+1)/2 = 5 -> 3n + 1 = 10 -> 3n = 9 -> n = 3. Alkane is C₃H₈ (propane).

qs.q: What organic product is obtained from the controlled oxidation of propan-2-ol using acidified potassium dichromate (VI)?
qs.e: Propan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol. Mild oxidation of secondary alcohols yields ketones (propanone, CH₃COCH₃), which resist further oxidation.

qs.q: Which monomer unit is polymerized to manufacture the addition plastic polyethene?
qs.e: Polyethene is synthesized by addition polymerization of the monomer ethene (CH₂=CH₂) under pressure in the presence of a catalyst.

qs.q: In the extraction of zinc from zinc blende ore (ZnS), what preliminary chemical treatment converts the sulfide ore into zinc oxide?
o: Roasting the ore in excess air
Thermal reduction with coke in a furnace
qs.e: Zinc blende (ZnS) is roasted in excess air at ~900 °C: 2ZnS(s) + 3O₂(g) -> 2ZnO(s) + 2SO₂(g) to convert sulfide into oxide prior to reduction.

qs.q: In the Haber process for manufacturing ammonia gas, what catalyst and promoter combination is operating at ~450 °C and 200 atm?
o: Finely divided iron catalyst with aluminium oxide promoter
Vanadium(V) oxide catalyst with silica promoter
qs.e: The Haber process uses finely divided iron as catalyst with promoters such as Al₂O₃ and K₂O to optimize rate and catalyst longevity.

qs.q: Which greenhouse gas is emitted into the atmosphere by ruminant livestock digestion, waterlogged rice paddies, and anaerobic decomposition in landfills?
qs.e: Methane (CH₄) is produced by methanogenic archaea during anaerobic fermentation in livestock rumen, rice paddies, and landfills.

qs.q: Which qualitative test confirms the presence of ammonium ions (NH₄⁺) in an unknown inorganic salt?
o: Warming the salt with aqueous NaOH liberates a gas that turns damp red litmus paper blue
Adding dilute HCl liberates a gas that turns lime water milky
Adding AgNO₃ solution produces a yellow precipitate
Adding BaCl₂ solution produces a white precipitate
qs.e: NH₄⁺ + OH⁻ -> NH₃(g) + H₂O. Ammonia gas (NH₃) is alkaline, turning moist red litmus paper blue and forming dense white fumes of NH₄Cl with conc. HCl.

qs.q: Which species contains a coordinate (dative covalent) bond formed by donation of a lone pair from oxygen to a hydrogen ion?
qs.e: In H₃O⁺, oxygen donates its unshared lone pair of electrons to an electron-deficient H⁺ ion to form a dative covalent bond: H₂O: + H⁺ -> H₃O⁺.

qs.q: Calculate the actual mass in grams of a single atom of carbon-12 (¹²C). (Avogadro constant N_A = 6.02 x 10²³ mol⁻¹)
qs.e: Mass of 1 atom = molar mass / N_A = 12.0 g/mol / (6.02 x 10²³ mol⁻¹) = 1.993 x 10⁻²³ g ≈ 1.99 x 10⁻²³ g.

qs.q: A 2.00 g sample of impure iron ore was dissolved in acid to form Fe²⁺ and titrated with 0.020 mol/dm³ KMnO₄ solution in acidic medium. It required 35.0 cm³ of KMnO₄ for complete reaction. Calculate the percentage purity of iron in the sample. (Fe = 55.85)
qs.e: 5Fe²⁺ + MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ -> 5Fe³⁺ + Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O. Moles MnO₄⁻ = 0.0350 dm³ x 0.020 mol/dm³ = 0.00070 mol. Moles Fe²⁺ = 5 x 0.00070 = 0.00350 mol. Mass pure Fe = 0.00350 mol x 55.85 g/mol = 0.19548 g. Percentage purity = (0.19548 g / 2.00 g) x 100 = 9.77% ≈ 9.8%.

qs.q: A 5.00 dm³ rigid gas container holds 14.0 g of nitrogen gas (N₂) at 27 °C. Calculate the pressure of the gas in kilopascals (kPa). (N = 14.0, R = 8.314 J/mol·K)
For the gaseous equilibrium reaction A(g) + B(g) ⇌ 2C(g), 1.0 mol of A and 1.0 mol of B were mixed in a 1.0 dm³ vessel. At equilibrium, 1.2 mol of C was present. Calculate K_c.
qs.e: Formation of 1.2 mol C consumes 0.6 mol A and 0.6 mol B. Equilibrium concs: [A] = 1.0 - 0.6 = 0.4 M; [B] = 0.4 M; [C] = 1.2 M. K_c = [C]² / ([A][B]) = (1.2)² / (0.4 x 0.4) = 1.44 / 0.16 = 9.0.

qs.q: Using Hess's Law, calculate ΔH° for the synthesis reaction C(s) + 2H₂(g) -> CH₄(g) given standard enthalpies of combustion: ΔH_c°(C) = -393.5 kJ/mol, ΔH_c°(H₂) = -285.8 kJ/mol, and ΔH_c°(CH₄) = -890.4 kJ/mol.
Calculate the pH of a 0.020 mol/dm³ solution of barium hydroxide, Ba(OH)₂, assuming complete ionization in water.

What volume of chlorine gas measured at s.t.p. is liberated at the anode during the electrolysis of molten NaCl when a current of 5.00 A flows for 1930 seconds? (Faraday constant F = 96,500 C/mol, Molar volume at s.t.p. = 22.4 dm³/mol)
qs.e: Q = I x t = 5.00 A x 1930 s = 9650 C. Moles e⁻ = 9650 / 96500 = 0.10 mol. Anode: 2Cl⁻ -> Cl₂ + 2e⁻. Moles Cl₂ = 0.10 / 2 = 0.050 mol. Volume Cl₂ at s.t.p. = 0.050 mol x 22.4 dm³/mol = 1.12 dm³.

qs.q: When ethanol is warmed with acidified potassium dichromate(VI) solution, what distinct color change is observed?
qs.e: Orange dichromate ions (Cr₂O₇²⁻, Cr in +6 state) oxidize ethanol to ethanal/ethanoic acid and are reduced to green chromium(III) ions (Cr³⁺).

qs.q: Which functional group is produced when a primary alcohol is fully oxidized under reflux with excess acidified potassium dichromate(VI)?
qs.e: Full oxidation of a primary alcohol (R-CH₂OH) under reflux yields a carboxylic acid (R-COOH) with a carboxyl group.

qs.q: In the industrial Contact process for manufacturing sulfuric acid, what catalyst is utilized for the oxidation of SO₂ to SO₃ at ~450 °C?
qs.e: Vanadium(V) oxide (V₂O₅) catalyzes 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g) efficiently at optimum temperatures of 400-450 °C.

qs.q: Heating 3.82 g of hydrated sodium borate (borax, Na₂B₄O₇·xH₂O) leaves a residue of 2.02 g of anhydrous Na₂B₄O₇. Calculate x. (Na = 23.0, B = 10.8, O = 16.0, H = 1.0)
Calculate the relative rate of diffusion of hydrogen gas (H₂) compared to oxygen gas (O₂) under identical conditions of temperature and pressure. (H = 1.0, O = 16.0)
qs.e: Graham's Law: Rate_H₂ / Rate_O₂ = √(M_O₂ / M_H₂) = √(32.0 / 2.0) = √16.0 = 4.0. Hydrogen gas diffuses 4.0 times faster than oxygen.

qs.q: An organic compound containing carbon, hydrogen, and chlorine consists of 24.24% C and 4.04% H by mass. Its relative vapor density is 49.5. Determine its molecular formula. (C = 12.0, H = 1.0, Cl = 35.5)
qs.e: % Cl = 100 - (24.24 + 4.04) = 71.72%. Moles C = 24.24/12 = 2.02; H = 4.04/1 = 4.04; Cl = 71.72/35.5 = 2.02. Ratio C:H:Cl = 1:2:1 -> Empirical formula CH₂Cl (mass = 49.5 g/mol). Molar mass = 2 x vapor density = 2 x 49.5 = 99.0 g/mol. Molecular formula = (CH₂Cl)₂ = C₂H₄Cl₂.

qs.q: Calculate the lattice enthalpy of magnesium oxide, MgO(s), from Born-Haber data: ΔH_f°(MgO) = -602 kJ/mol, ΔH_sub(Mg) = +148 kJ/mol, IE₁ + IE₂(Mg) = +2188 kJ/mol, ½ D(O₂) = +249 kJ/mol, EA₁ + EA₂(O) = +657 kJ/mol.
Calculate the equilibrium constant K_eq at 298 K for the cell reaction Zn(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) ⇌ Zn²⁺(aq) + Cu(s) given E°cell = +1.10 V. (Use 2.303 RT/F = 0.0591 V)
Calculate the pH of a 0.10 mol/dm³ solution of a weak monoprotic acid HA with ionization constant K_a = 1.0 x 10⁻⁵ mol/dm³.
qs.e: For weak acid HA: [H⁺] = √(K_a x C) = √(1.0 x 10⁻⁵ x 0.10) = √(1.0 x 10⁻⁶) = 1.0 x 10⁻³ mol/dm³. pH = -log₁₀(1.0 x 10⁻³) = 3.00.

qs.q: A first-order chemical reaction A -> Products has a half-life of 20.0 minutes. What percentage of the initial concentration of reactant A remains unreacted after 80.0 minutes?
qs.e: Number of elapsed half-lives n = total time / t_1/2 = 80.0 min / 20.0 min = 4. Fraction remaining = (1/2)⁴ = 1/16 = 0.0625. Percentage remaining = 0.0625 x 100 = 6.25%.

qs.q: What is the maximum number of electrons that can occupy all atomic orbitals in the 2p subshell?
qs.e: The 2p subshell contains 3 p-orbitals (2p_x, 2p_y, 2p_z), each holding a maximum of 2 electrons with paired spins, giving a total of 6 electrons.

qs.q: Which element in Period 3 of the Periodic Table possesses the highest electronegativity value?
qs.e: Electronegativity increases across Period 3 from left to right. Excluded noble gas argon, chlorine has the highest electronegativity (3.16 on Pauling scale).

qs.q: Which type of chemical bonding exists in a solid crystal of metallic sodium?
qs.e: Metallic bonding consists of an array of positive metal ions (Na⁺) surrounded by a sea of delocalized valence electrons.

qs.q: What process describes the spontaneous spreading and mixing of gas molecules through space due to random thermal motion?
qs.e: Diffusion is the movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to lower concentration until evenly distributed.

qs.q: According to the Arrhenius theory, a base is defined as a chemical substance that dissociates in water to yield:
qs.e: Arrhenius defined a base as a compound that increases the concentration of OH⁻ ions when dissolved in water.

qs.q: Which halogen gas is dissolved in municipal water supplies as a disinfectant to destroy pathogenic microorganisms?
qs.e: Chlorination of drinking water destroys harmful bacteria and viruses by forming hypochlorous acid (HOCl).

qs.q: Which triatomic atmospheric gas absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation in the stratosphere, protecting life on Earth?
qs.e: Stratospheric ozone (O₃) filters out high-energy UV-B and UV-C solar radiation.

qs.q: Calculate the mass of 0.25 moles of pure sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄. (H = 1.0, S = 32.0, O = 16.0)
qs.e: Molar mass H₂SO₄ = 2(1.0) + 32.0 + 4(16.0) = 98.0 g/mol. Mass = moles x molar mass = 0.25 mol x 98.0 g/mol = 24.5 g.

qs.q: Standard temperature and pressure (s.t.p.) conditions in gas calculations correspond to which values?
qs.e: Standard temperature is defined as 273.15 K (0 °C) and standard pressure is 1.0 atm (101.3 kPa or 760 mmHg).

qs.q: In the balanced stoichiometric combustion of butane: 2C₄H₁₀(g) + 13O₂(g) -> 8CO₂(g) + 10H₂O(g), what is the mole ratio of oxygen to butane?
qs.e: The balanced equation shows 13 moles of O₂ react with 2 moles of C₄H₁₀, giving a mole ratio of 13 : 2.

qs.q: What chemical formula represents crystalline cobalt(II) chloride hexahydrate?
qs.e: Cobalt(II) chloride forms pink hexahydrate crystals with formula CoCl₂·6H₂O.

qs.q: How does crushing a large solid reactant into a fine powder influence the rate of a heterogeneous reaction?
o: It increases reaction rate by expanding total exposed surface area
It decreases reaction rate by reducing molecular kinetic energy
It lowers activation energy threshold of the reaction
It shifts equilibrium position toward reactant side
qs.e: Powdering a solid drastically increases exposed surface area per unit mass, allowing more collisions per second between reactants.

qs.q: Which property correctly characterizes an endothermic chemical process?
o: Heat energy is absorbed from surroundings and ΔH is positive
Heat energy is released to surroundings and ΔH is negative
System temperature rises spontaneously without heating
Enthalpy of products is lower than enthalpy of reactants
qs.e: Endothermic reactions absorb heat (H_products > H_reactants), resulting in a positive enthalpy change (ΔH > 0).

qs.q: What is the commercial chemical name for washing soda crystals?
qs.e: Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O.

qs.q: In the reaction Zn(s) + 2HCl(aq) -> ZnCl₂(aq) + H₂(g), what change in oxidation state occurs for zinc metal?
qs.e: Elemental zinc (0) loses 2 electrons to form Zn²⁺ (+2) in ZnCl₂, undergoing oxidation.

qs.q: During the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride in a Downs cell, at which electrode is chlorine gas evolved?
qs.e: Chloride ions (Cl⁻) migrate to the positive anode where they lose electrons (oxidation) to form Cl₂ gas: 2Cl⁻ -> Cl₂ + 2e⁻.

qs.q: What is the systematic IUPAC name for CH₃-CH₂-CH(CH₃)-CH₂-CH₃?
qs.e: The longest continuous carbon chain has 5 carbons (pentane). A methyl group is attached to C3, giving 3-methylpentane.

qs.q: Which IUPAC naming suffix identifies members of the alkanal (aldehyde) homologous series?
qs.e: Alkanals carry the IUPAC suffix '-al' (e.g. methanal, ethanal, propanal).

qs.q: What is the correct protocol for preparing a dilute sulfuric acid solution from concentrated sulfuric acid in the laboratory?
o: Slowly add concentrated acid to water with continuous stirring
Slowly add water to concentrated acid with continuous stirring
Mix equal volumes rapidly in a closed flask
Pour water directly into heated concentrated acid
qs.e: Dilution of conc. H₂SO₄ is highly exothermic. Adding acid slowly to water allows water's high heat capacity to absorb heat safely, preventing localized boiling and acid splattering.

qs.q: Calculate the percentage by mass of water of crystallization in washing soda crystals, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O. (Na = 23.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0, H = 1.0)
Calculate the volume occupied by 2.00 moles of an ideal gas at 300 K and 2.00 atm pressure. (R = 0.0821 dm³·atm/mol·K)
For the equilibrium system 2NO₂(g) [reddish-brown] ⇌ N₂O₄(g) [colorless] (ΔH = -57 kJ/mol), what visual change occurs when a sealed gas tube is immersed in ice water?
o: The brown color fades, turning nearly colorless
Solid black precipitate forms on tube walls
qs.e: Cooling in ice water shifts the equilibrium in the exothermic forward direction to form more colorless N₂O₄ gas, causing the brown NO₂ color to fade.

qs.q: What primary essential function is served by a salt bridge in a electrochemical galvanic cell?
o: Maintains electrical neutrality in both half-cell solutions by allowing ion migration
Transfers electrons directly between cathode and anode compartments
Increases standard cell potential E°cell above standard values
Prevents metallic oxidation at the anode
qs.e: The salt bridge completes the circuit and maintains electrical neutrality by allowing cations and anions to migrate between half-cells without mixing the solutions.

qs.q: Calculate the pH of a 0.050 mol/dm³ solution of hydrochloric acid (HCl), assuming complete ionization.
What mass of zinc metal is deposited at the cathode when a constant current of 4.00 A is passed through aqueous zinc sulfate for 1930 seconds? (Zn = 65.4, Faraday constant F = 96,500 C/mol)
What type of reaction occurs when propene gas reacts with hydrogen gas in the presence of a nickel catalyst at 150 °C?
qs.e: CH₃-CH=CH₂ + H₂ -> CH₃-CH₂-CH₃ (propane) via catalytic addition of hydrogen across the C=C double bond.

qs.q: Which reaction conditions convert ethanol into ethanoic acid in high yield?
o: Refluxing ethanol with excess acidified potassium dichromate(VI)
Distilling ethanol with concentrated H₂SO₄ at 140 °C
Reacting ethanol with sodium hydroxide solution at room temperature
Passing ethanol vapor over heated alumina catalyst
qs.e: Full oxidation of ethanol (primary alcohol) to ethanoic acid requires refluxing with excess oxidizing agent (acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ or KMnO₄).

qs.q: Which synthetic polymer is classified as a polyester formed by condensation of benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid and ethane-1,2-diol?
qs.e: Terylene (Dacron) is a polyester formed by step-growth condensation polymerization of terephthalic acid and ethylene glycol.

qs.q: In the blast furnace, which chemical gas acts as the primary reducing agent that reduces iron oxides to metallic molten iron?
qs.e: In the blast furnace, carbon monoxide (CO formed from reaction of coke with CO₂) reduces Fe₂O₃: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO -> 2Fe + 3CO₂.

qs.q: What acid solution is formed when sulfur dioxide gas dissolves in water?
qs.e: SO₂(g) + H₂O(l) ⇌ H₂SO₃(aq) forms weak sulfurous acid.

qs.q: Which toxic gas inhaled into human lungs combines irreversibly with hemoglobin to form carboxyhemoglobin, preventing oxygen transport?
qs.e: CO binds to hemoglobin with an affinity ~200 times greater than oxygen, forming stable carboxyhemoglobin and causing cellular hypoxia.

qs.q: Which chemical test is used to distinguish between unsaturated alkenes and saturated alkanes?
o: Shaking with bromine water; alkene rapidly decolorizes it while alkane does not in the dark
Testing with damp red litmus paper
qs.e: Alkenes undergo rapid electrophilic addition with reddish-brown bromine water, turning it colorless. Alkanes do not react in the dark.

qs.q: Why does sodium chloride (NaCl) possess a high melting point of 801 °C?
o: Strong ionic electrostatic forces extend throughout its 3D giant crystal lattice
Covalent bonds bind all individual NaCl molecules into macromolecules
Heavy molecular weight creates strong intermolecular van der Waals forces
Metallic bonding between sodium cations creates high stability
qs.e: NaCl exists as a giant ionic lattice where Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions are held by strong 3D electrostatic attractions, requiring vast thermal energy to disrupt.

qs.q: What is the ground-state electronic configuration of a copper atom (Cu, atomic number Z = 29)?
qs.e: Copper exhibits an anomalous electron configuration [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹ because a completely filled 3d subshell offers extra thermodynamic stability compared to [Ar] 3d⁹ 4s².

qs.q: A sample of 1.20 g of a divalent metal M reacted completely with excess dilute HCl to produce 448 cm³ of hydrogen gas at s.t.p. Calculate the relative atomic mass of metal M. (Molar volume at s.t.p. = 22.4 dm³/mol)
qs.e: M(s) + 2HCl(aq) -> MCl₂(aq) + H₂(g). Moles H₂ = 0.448 dm³ / 22.4 dm³/mol = 0.020 mol. Moles M = 0.020 mol. Relative atomic mass = mass / moles = 1.20 g / 0.020 mol = 60.0 g/mol.

qs.q: Using Graham's law of diffusion: Unknown gas X diffuses through a porous membrane at half the rate of methane gas (CH₄). Calculate the molar mass of gas X. (C = 12.0, H = 1.0)
Write the correct equilibrium constant expression K_c for the reversible gaseous reaction 4NH₃(g) + 5O₂(g) ⇌ 4NO(g) + 6H₂O(g).
qs.e: K_c is the ratio of product concentrations raised to their stoichiometric coefficients over reactant concentrations raised to theirs: [NO]⁴[H₂O]⁶ / ([NH₃]⁴[O₂]⁵).

qs.q: Given average bond enthalpies: N≡N = 945 kJ/mol, H-H = 436 kJ/mol, and N-H = 391 kJ/mol, calculate the standard enthalpy change ΔH for the synthesis reaction N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) -> 2NH₃(g).
qs.e: Bonds broken = D(N≡N) + 3 D(H-H) = 945 + 3(436) = 945 + 1308 = +2253 kJ/mol. Bonds formed = 6 D(N-H) = 6(391) = 2346 kJ/mol. ΔH = 2253 - 2346 = -93 kJ/mol.

qs.q: What volume of 0.20 mol/dm³ NaOH solution is required to neutralize completely 50.0 cm³ of 0.10 mol/dm³ sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄)?
qs.e: H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH -> Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O (n_a = 1, n_b = 2). Formula: (C_a x V_a) / (C_b x V_b) = 1 / 2 -> V_b = (2 x C_a x V_a) / C_b = (2 x 0.10 x 50.0) / 0.20 = 10.0 / 0.20 = 50.0 cm³.

qs.q: Calculate the volume of oxygen gas measured at s.t.p. liberated at the anode when a current of 2.00 A flows through dilute sodium hydroxide solution for 9650 seconds. (Faraday constant F = 96,500 C/mol, Molar volume at s.t.p. = 22.4 dm³/mol)
qs.e: Q = I x t = 2.00 A x 9650 s = 19,300 C. Moles e⁻ = 19,300 / 96500 = 0.20 mol. Reaction: 4OH⁻ -> 2H₂O + O₂ + 4e⁻. Moles O₂ = 0.20 / 4 = 0.050 mol. Volume = 0.050 mol x 22.4 dm³/mol = 1.12 dm³.

qs.q: Determine the oxidation state of sulfur in sodium metabisulfite (sodium pyrosulfite), Na₂S₂O₅.
Which organic ester is synthesized when propanoic acid is heated with methanol in the presence of concentrated sulfuric acid catalyst?
qs.e: CH₃CH₂COOH + CH₃OH ⇌ CH₃CH₂COOCH₃ (methyl propanoate) + H₂O.

qs.q: Which process is employed industrially to refine crude blister copper to 99.99% purity for high-conductivity electrical wires?
o: Electrolytic refining using crude copper anode and pure copper cathode
Smelting in a reverberatory furnace with silica flux
qs.e: In electrolytic refining, impure copper is made the anode and pure copper sheet the cathode in aqueous CuSO₄/H₂SO₄. Copper dissolves from anode and deposits cleanly on cathode.

qs.q: A sample of 1.43 g of hydrated sodium carbonate Na₂CO₃·xH₂O required 20.0 cm³ of 0.50 mol/dm³ HCl for complete neutralization. Calculate x. (Na = 23.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0, H = 1.0)
qs.e: Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl -> 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂. Moles HCl = 0.020 dm³ x 0.50 mol/dm³ = 0.010 mol. Moles Na₂CO₃ = 0.010 / 2 = 0.0050 mol. Mass anhydrous Na₂CO₃ = 0.0050 mol x 106.0 g/mol = 0.53 g. Mass H₂O = 1.43 - 0.53 = 0.90 g. Moles H₂O = 0.90 / 18.0 = 0.050 mol. Ratio x = 0.050 / 0.0050 = 10.

qs.q: Calculate the density of carbon dioxide gas (CO₂) in g/dm³ at s.t.p. (C = 12.0, O = 16.0, Molar volume at s.t.p. = 22.4 dm³/mol)
qs.e: Molar mass CO₂ = 12.0 + 2(16.0) = 44.0 g/mol. Density at s.t.p. = Molar mass / Molar volume = 44.0 g/mol / 22.4 dm³/mol = 1.964 g/dm³ ≈ 1.96 g/dm³.

qs.q: Complete combustion of 1.16 g of a pure hydrocarbon produced 3.52 g of CO₂ and 1.80 g of H₂O. Given its relative vapor density is 29.0, determine its molecular formula. (C = 12.0, H = 1.0)
qs.e: Moles C = 3.52 / 44.0 = 0.080 mol; Moles H = 2 x (1.80 / 18.0) = 0.200 mol. Ratio C : H = 0.080 : 0.200 = 2 : 5 -> Empirical formula C₂H₅ (mass = 29.0 g/mol). Molar mass = 2 x 29.0 = 58.0 g/mol. Molecular formula = (C₂H₅)₂ = C₄H₁₀.

qs.q: Calculate the lattice enthalpy of calcium fluoride, CaF₂(s), from Born-Haber cycle data: ΔH_f°(CaF₂) = -1220 kJ/mol, ΔH_sub(Ca) = +178 kJ/mol, IE₁ + IE₂(Ca) = +1735 kJ/mol, D(F₂) = +159 kJ/mol, 2 x EA₁(F) = -656 kJ/mol.
Calculate the cell potential E_cell at 298 K for Zn(s) | Zn²⁺(0.10 M) || Cu²⁺(1.00 M) | Cu(s) given E°cell = +1.10 V. (Nernst equation constant 2.303 RT/nF = 0.0591/n V)
Calculate the pH of a 0.050 mol/dm³ solution of weak base ammonia (NH₃) in water at 25 °C given K_b = 1.80 x 10⁻⁵ mol/dm³.
For a first-order thermal decomposition reaction A -> B + C, the rate constant k at 500 K is 2.303 x 10⁻³ s⁻¹. How many seconds are required for 90.0% of reactant A to decompose?
qs.e: For a first-order reaction: t = (2.303 / k) x log₁₀([A]₀ / [A]_t). 90.0% decomposition leaves 10.0% remaining ([A]₀ / [A]_t = 100 / 10 = 10). log₁₀(10) = 1.0. t = (2.303 / 2.303 x 10⁻³ s⁻¹) x 1.0 = 1000 seconds.

qs.q: The principal quantum number n = 1 designates which atomic electron shell?
qs.e: Principal quantum number n = 1 corresponds to the innermost electron shell, designated as the K shell.

qs.q: Which halogen element exists as a dense reddish-brown volatile liquid at room temperature and pressure?
qs.e: Bromine is the only non-metallic element that exists as a liquid under ambient conditions.

qs.q: Which type of chemical bonding involves sharing pair(s) of electrons between non-metal atoms?
qs.e: Covalent bonding involves overlap of atomic orbitals sharing electron pairs between non-metal atoms.

qs.q: In kinetic molecular theory, what macro-property measures the average kinetic energy of constituent particles?
qs.e: Temperature is directly proportional to the average translational kinetic energy of molecules in a system.

qs.q: What is the pH of a neutral aqueous solution of pure sodium chloride (NaCl) at 25 °C?
qs.e: NaCl is a salt formed from strong acid (HCl) and strong base (NaOH), forming a neutral solution with pH = 7.0.

qs.q: Which noble gas is filled into incandescent light bulbs to prevent tungsten filament oxidation?
qs.e: Argon is an abundant, unreactive noble gas used to provide an inert atmosphere in light bulbs.

qs.q: Which atmospheric gas produced by anaerobic decay of organic material in landfills acts as a greenhouse gas?
qs.e: Methane (CH₄) is generated during anaerobic bacterial decomposition of organic waste.

qs.q: Calculate the number of moles contained in 9.0 g of pure water, H₂O. (H = 1.0, O = 16.0)
qs.e: Molar mass H₂O = 2(1.0) + 16.0 = 18.0 g/mol. Moles = mass / molar mass = 9.0 g / 18.0 g/mol = 0.50 moles.

qs.q: According to Boyle's law, for a fixed mass of an ideal gas at constant temperature, pressure is inversely proportional to:
qs.e: Boyle's law states P ∝ 1/V (P₁V₁ = P₂V₂) at constant temperature and mass.

qs.q: In the combustion reaction CH₄(g) + 2O₂(g) -> CO₂(g) + 2H₂O(g), what volume of oxygen at s.t.p. reacts with 1.0 dm³ of methane?
qs.e: By Gay-Lussac's law of combining volumes, 1 volume of CH₄ reacts with 2 volumes of O₂, so 1.0 dm³ CH₄ requires 2.0 dm³ O₂.

qs.q: Which term describes a substance that absorbs moisture from the atmosphere without dissolving in it?
qs.e: Hygroscopic substances absorb moisture from air without forming a solution (unlike deliquescent substances which dissolve).

qs.q: How is a homogeneous catalyst distinguished from a heterogeneous catalyst?
o: It exists in the same physical state (phase) as the reactants
It exists in a different physical state from the reactants
It is always a solid metal wire or mesh
qs.e: A homogeneous catalyst is in the same phase (e.g. liquid or gas) as the reacting species.

qs.q: What enthalpy change corresponds to the complete combustion of 1 mole of a compound in excess oxygen at s.t.p.?
qs.e: Standard enthalpy of combustion is the heat released when 1 mole of a substance burns completely in oxygen under standard conditions.

qs.q: What intense characteristic flame test color identifies the presence of sodium ions (Na⁺) in a salt?
qs.e: Sodium ions excite in a Bunsen burner flame to emit a persistent, intense golden-yellow flame.

qs.q: What is the oxidation number of nitrogen in concentrated nitric acid, HNO₃?
qs.e: In HNO₃: H is +1 and O is -2. Sum = +1 + N + 3(-2) = 0 -> N - 5 = 0 -> N = +5.

qs.q: To electroplate a metallic object such as an iron spoon with silver metal, where must the spoon be placed in the electrolytic cell?
o: Suspended freely in the salt bridge
qs.e: In electroplating, the object to be plated is made the cathode (negative electrode) where metal cations undergo reduction: Ag⁺ + e⁻ -> Ag(s).

qs.q: What is the systematic IUPAC name for HC≡C-CH₂-CH₃?
qs.e: A 4-carbon chain with a triple bond starting at carbon 1 is named but-1-yne.

qs.q: Which functional group is present in organic esters (alkanoates)?
qs.e: Esters carry the ester linkage functional group -COO- (alkoxycarbonyl).

qs.q: Which chemical indicator is most appropriate for a volumetric titration between a strong acid (HCl) and a weak base (NH₃)?
qs.e: Titration of a strong acid against a weak base gives an acidic equivalence point (pH ~4-6), so methyl orange (pH range 3.1-4.4) is ideal.

qs.q: Calculate the percentage by mass of oxygen in potassium chlorate, KClO₃. (K = 39.1, Cl = 35.5, O = 16.0)
A sample of helium gas occupies 600 cm³ at 27 °C and 800 mmHg pressure. What volume will it occupy at 127 °C and 600 mmHg pressure?
qs.e: Using combined gas law: T₁ = 300 K, T₂ = 400 K. V₂ = (P₁ x V₁ x T₂) / (P₂ x T₁) = (800 x 600 x 400) / (600 x 300) = 192,000,000 / 180,000 = 1066.67 cm³ ≈ 1067 cm³.

qs.q: Why is a system at chemical equilibrium described as 'dynamic'?
o: Forward and reverse reactions continue to occur simultaneously at equal non-zero rates
All chemical reaction activity has ceased completely
The concentrations of reactants and products are equal
qs.e: Dynamic equilibrium means both forward and reverse processes continue occurring at equal rates, keeping concentrations constant.

qs.q: In an operating Zn-Cu galvanic cell, in which direction do electrons flow through the external metallic wire circuit?
o: From the zinc anode to the copper cathode
From the copper cathode to the zinc anode
From the salt bridge into the cathode solution
qs.e: Zinc is oxidized at the anode releasing electrons, which travel through the external wire circuit to the copper cathode where reduction occurs.

qs.q: Titration of 20.0 cm³ of 0.10 mol/dm³ NaOH solution required 25.0 cm³ of hydrochloric acid (HCl) for complete neutralization. Calculate the concentration of the HCl solution in mol/dm³.
qs.e: HCl + NaOH -> NaCl + H₂O (n_a = 1, n_b = 1). C_a = (C_b x V_b) / V_a = (0.10 mol/dm³ x 20.0 cm³) / 25.0 cm³ = 2.0 / 25.0 = 0.080 mol/dm³.

qs.q: What mass of aluminium metal is deposited at the cathode when 3.0 Faradays of electricity pass through molten alumina? (Al = 27.0)
qs.e: Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ -> Al. Discharge of 1 mole of Al requires 3 Faradays. Therefore, 3.0 Faradays deposit 1.0 mole of Al = 27.0 g.

qs.q: What structural isomerism exists between butane (CH₃-CH₂-CH₂-CH₃) and 2-methylpropane (CH₃-CH(CH₃)-CH₃)?
qs.e: Both have molecular formula C₄H₁₀, but butane has a straight 4-carbon chain while 2-methylpropane has a branched 3-carbon chain, making them chain isomers.

qs.q: What organic products are formed when ethyl ethanoate (CH₃COOCH₂CH₃) undergoes acid-catalyzed hydrolysis upon heating with water?
qs.e: Acid hydrolysis of an ester produces the corresponding carboxylic acid and alcohol: CH₃COOCH₂CH₃ + H₂O ⇌ CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH.

qs.q: During the vulcanization of natural rubber, cross-links are introduced between polyisoprene chains composed of bridges of:
qs.e: Heating with sulfur introduces covalent sulfur bridges (-S-S-) between polyisoprene chains, preventing slipping and enhancing resilience.

qs.q: Which major copper ore is concentrated via froth flotation prior to smelting?
qs.e: Copper pyrites (CuFeS₂) is the principal sulfide ore of copper, concentrated by froth flotation.

qs.q: Which major mineral acid is produced industrially by the Contact process?
qs.e: The Contact process manufactures concentrated sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄) via oxidation of SO₂ to SO₃.

qs.q: Which oxide of nitrogen, commonly known as laughing gas, acts as a potent atmospheric greenhouse gas?
qs.e: Dinitrogen monoxide (N₂O) is a greenhouse gas with a global warming potential ~300 times greater than CO₂.

qs.q: When aqueous silver nitrate (AgNO₃) solution is added to an unknown solution, a white precipitate forms that dissolves in dilute aqueous ammonia. Which anion is present?
qs.e: Ag⁺ + Cl⁻ -> AgCl(s) (white ppt). AgCl dissolves in dilute aqueous NH₃ forming soluble diamminesilver(I) complex [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺.

qs.q: According to VSEPR theory, which molecule possesses a trigonal planar shape with 120° bond angles?
qs.e: Boron in BF₃ has 3 bonding electron pairs and zero lone pairs, forming a trigonal planar molecule with 120° angles.

qs.q: What is the maximum number of electrons that can occupy a single d orbital?
qs.e: According to the Pauli exclusion principle, any single atomic orbital can hold at most 2 electrons with opposite spins. (A d-subshell has 5 orbitals holding 10 electrons total).

qs.q: Complete combustion of 2.10 g of an unknown hydrocarbon gave 6.60 g of carbon dioxide (CO₂). Determine the empirical formula of the hydrocarbon. (C = 12.0, H = 1.0, O = 16.0)
qs.e: Moles CO₂ = 6.60 / 44.0 = 0.150 mol -> Moles C = 0.150 mol. Mass C = 0.150 x 12.0 = 1.80 g. Mass H = 2.10 - 1.80 = 0.30 g. Moles H = 0.30 / 1.0 = 0.30 mol. Ratio C : H = 0.150 : 0.30 = 1 : 2 -> Empirical formula CH₂.

qs.q: A sample of 1.40 g of an ideal gas occupies 1.12 dm³ at s.t.p. Calculate its relative molar mass. (Molar volume at s.t.p. = 22.4 dm³/mol)
qs.e: Moles of gas = 1.12 dm³ / 22.4 dm³/mol = 0.050 mol. Molar mass = mass / moles = 1.40 g / 0.050 mol = 28.0 g/mol.

qs.q: In the Haber process equilibrium N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), an equilibrium mixture contained 0.50 mol/dm³ N₂, 1.00 mol/dm³ H₂, and 2.00 mol/dm³ NH₃ in a 1.0 dm³ vessel. Calculate K_c.
Given average bond enthalpies: C=C = 614 kJ/mol, C-C = 348 kJ/mol, C-H = 413 kJ/mol, and H-H = 436 kJ/mol, calculate ΔH for hydrogenation of ethene: C₂H₄(g) + H₂(g) -> C₂H₆(g).
Calculate the pH of a 0.010 mol/dm³ solution of potassium hydroxide (KOH), assuming complete ionization.
During electrolysis of silver nitrate solution, a current of 1.50 A flows for 3860 seconds. Calculate the mass of silver deposited at the cathode. (Ag = 108.0, Faraday constant F = 96,500 C/mol)
qs.e: Q = I x t = 1.50 A x 3860 s = 5790 C. Moles e⁻ = 5790 / 96500 = 0.060 mol. Reaction: Ag⁺ + e⁻ -> Ag. Moles Ag = 0.060 mol. Mass = 0.060 x 108.0 g/mol = 6.48 g.

qs.q: What is the oxidation number of phosphorus in phosphoric acid, H₃PO₄?
Which alcohol is formed when propanone (CH₃COCH₃) is reduced using sodium borohydride (NaBH₄)?
qs.e: Reduction of ketones (>C=O) with NaBH₄ or LiAlH₄ yields secondary alcohols (propan-2-ol, CH₃CH(OH)CH₃).

qs.q: In the Downs process, what chemical chemical substance is added to sodium chloride to lower its melting point from 801 °C to ~600 °C during industrial extraction of sodium?
qs.e: Adding calcium chloride (CaCl₂) to NaCl forms an electrolyte mixture that melts at ~600 °C, reducing thermal energy requirements.

qs.q: Strong heating of 2.08 g of hydrated barium chloride, BaCl₂·xH₂O, yields 1.77 g of anhydrous BaCl₂. Determine x. (Ba = 137.3, Cl = 35.5, H = 1.0, O = 16.0)
Which kinetic molecular theory assumption fails for real gases under high pressure conditions?
o: Gas particles occupy zero volume relative to total container volume
Collisions between gas particles are perfectly elastic
Particles move in continuous rapid random straight lines
Average kinetic energy is proportional to Kelvin temperature
qs.e: At high pressure, gas molecules are compressed close together, making their actual molecular volumes significant compared to total vessel volume.

qs.q: Titration of 25.0 cm³ of a 0.100 mol/dm³ oxalic acid solution (H₂C₂O₄) required 20.0 cm³ of potassium permanganate (KMnO₄) solution in acidic medium. Calculate the molar concentration of the KMnO₄ solution.
qs.e: Balanced ionic equation: 2MnO₄⁻ + 5H₂C₂O₄ + 6H⁺ -> 2Mn²⁺ + 10CO₂ + 8H₂O (n_a = 5 for oxalic acid, n_b = 2 for KMnO₄). (C_acid x V_acid) / (C_KMnO₄ x V_KMnO₄) = 5 / 2 -> C_KMnO₄ = (2 x 0.100 x 25.0) / (5 x 20.0) = 5.0 / 100.0 = 0.040 mol/dm³.

qs.q: Calculate the lattice enthalpy of potassium chloride, KCl(s), using Born-Haber cycle data: ΔH_f°(KCl) = -436 kJ/mol, ΔH_sub(K) = +89 kJ/mol, IE₁(K) = +419 kJ/mol, ½ D(Cl₂) = +122 kJ/mol, EA₁(Cl) = -349 kJ/mol.
Calculate the standard free energy change ΔG° in kJ for the spontaneous cell reaction Zn(s) + 2Ag⁺(aq) -> Zn²⁺(aq) + 2Ag(s) given E°cell = +1.56 V. (Faraday constant F = 96,500 C/mol)
qs.e: ΔG° = -n F E°cell. Here n = 2 electrons transferred. ΔG° = -2 x 96,500 C/mol x 1.56 V = -301,080 J = -301.08 kJ ≈ -301.1 kJ.

qs.q: Calculate the pH of a buffer solution prepared by mixing 0.10 mol/dm³ ammonia (NH₃) and 0.20 mol/dm³ ammonium chloride (NH₄Cl) at 25 °C. (K_b of NH₃ = 1.80 x 10⁻⁵ mol/dm³)
If a chemical reaction rate doubles for every 10 °C increase in temperature, by what factor does the reaction rate increase when temperature is raised from 20 °C to 60 °C?
qs.e: Temperature rise ΔT = 60 - 20 = 40 °C. Number of 10 °C increments n = 40 / 10 = 4. Rate multiplication factor = 2⁴ = 16 times.

qs.q: What is the total number of protons, neutrons, and electrons in a neutral atom of chlorine-37 (atomic number 17)?
qs.e: For a neutral atom of chlorine-37 (atomic number Z = 17, mass number A = 37): Number of protons = Z = 17; Number of electrons = Z = 17 (since it is neutral); Number of neutrons = A - Z = 37 - 17 = 20.

qs.q: Which periodic trend generally increases from left to right across Period 3 of the Periodic Table?
qs.e: Across a period from left to right, effective nuclear charge increases while shielding remains roughly constant. This pulls valence electrons closer, increasing electronegativity and ionization energy while decreasing atomic radius and metallic character.

qs.q: Which type of chemical bonding involves the electrostatic attraction between sea of delocalized electrons and positively charged metal ions?
qs.e: Metallic bonding is defined as the strong electrostatic attraction between positively charged metal cations arranged in a lattice and a mobile sea of delocalized electrons.

qs.q: What is the molar mass of hydrated copper(II) sulfate, CuSO₄·5H₂O? (Relative atomic masses: Cu = 63.5, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1)
qs.e: Molar mass of CuSO4 = 63.5 + 32 + (4 × 16) = 159.5 g/mol. Molar mass of 5H2O = 5 × (2 × 1 + 16) = 5 × 18 = 90 g/mol. Total molar mass = 159.5 + 90 = 249.5 g/mol.

qs.q: Which gas is liberated at the anode during the electrolysis of concentrated sodium chloride solution (brine) using inert carbon electrodes?
qs.e: In concentrated NaCl solution (brine), chloride ions (Cl⁻) are present in high concentration compared to hydroxide ions (OH⁻). Therefore, Cl⁻ ions are preferentially discharged at the anode (+) to produce chlorine gas: 2Cl⁻(aq) → Cl₂(g) + 2e⁻.

qs.q: Which organic functional group is characterized by the presence of a carbonyl group bonded to a hydroxyl group (-COOH)?
qs.e: The carboxyl functional group (-COOH) consists of a carbonyl group (C=O) directly attached to a hydroxyl group (-OH), which defines carboxylic acids.

qs.q: What is the primary pollutant responsible for acid rain caused by the burning of sulfur-containing fossil fuels?
qs.e: Combustion of coal and heavy fuel oil containing sulfur impurities releases sulfur dioxide (SO₂). SO₂ oxidizes in the atmosphere to SO₃, which reacts with rainwater to form sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄), causing acid rain.

qs.q: Calculate the mass of pure anhydrous sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃) produced when 28.6 g of washing soda crystals (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O) are completely dehydrated by heating. (Na = 23, C = 12, O = 16, H = 1)
A sample of neon gas occupies a volume of 450 cm³ at 27 °C and a pressure of 740 mmHg. Determine its volume at standard temperature and pressure (0 °C and 760 mmHg).
In a titration experiment, 25.0 cm³ of a 0.120 mol/dm³ H₂SO₄ solution required exactly 30.0 cm³ of NaOH solution for complete neutralization. What is the molar concentration of the NaOH solution?
qs.e: Balanced equation: H2SO4 + 2NaOH → Na2SO4 + 2H2O. Stoichiometric ratio: na/nb = 1/2. Using (Ca × Va) / (Cb × Vb) = 1 / 2 => Cb = (2 × Ca × Va) / Vb = (2 × 0.120 × 25.0) / 30.0 = 6.00 / 30.0 = 0.200 mol/dm³.

qs.q: What mass of copper metal is deposited at the cathode when a current of 2.50 A is passed through a solution of CuSO₄ for 32 minutes and 10 seconds? (Cu = 63.5, 1 F = 96,500 C/mol)
qs.e: Time t = (32 × 60) + 10 = 1930 s. Quantity of electricity Q = I × t = 2.50 A × 1930 s = 4825 C. Reaction at cathode: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu(s). 2 moles of electrons (2 × 96500 C = 193,000 C) deposit 1 mole of Cu (63.5 g). Mass of Cu = (4825 C / 193,000 C) × 63.5 g = 0.025 mol × 63.5 g = 1.5875 g ≈ 1.59 g.

qs.q: During the industrial extraction of aluminum by the Hall-Héroult process, molten cryolite (Na₃AlF₆) is added to alumina (Al₂O₃) primarily to:
o: Lower the melting point of alumina and improve electrical conductivity
Act as a reducing agent to convert Al³⁺ to Al metal
Prevent the oxidation of carbon anodes
qs.e: Pure alumina (Al2O3) has a very high melting point (~2072 °C), making direct electrolysis expensive and difficult. Dissolving alumina in molten cryolite lowers the melting mixture temperature to ~950 °C and enhances electrical conductivity.

qs.q: Which set of quantum numbers represents an electron in a 3p orbital?
qs.e: For a 3p subshell: the principal quantum number n = 3. The azimuthal/orbital quantum number for p orbital is l = 1 (where s=0, p=1, d=2, f=3). Magnetic quantum number ml can be -1, 0, or +1. Spin quantum number ms can be +1/2 or -1/2.

qs.q: In the reaction: 2H₂S(g) + SO₂(g) → 3S(s) + 2H₂O(l), which species acts as the reducing agent?
qs.e: In H2S, oxidation state of sulfur is -2. In SO2, oxidation state of sulfur is +4. In elemental S, oxidation state is 0. H2S loses electrons (S increases from -2 to 0), so H2S undergoes oxidation and acts as the reducing agent.

qs.q: A gaseous hydrocarbon contains 85.7% carbon and 14.3% hydrogen by mass. If 0.28 g of the gas occupies 224 cm³ at STP, determine its molecular formula. (C = 12, H = 1, Molar volume at STP = 22.4 dm³/mol)
qs.e: Moles of gas at STP = 0.224 dm³ / 22.4 dm³/mol = 0.010 mol. Molar mass = 0.28 g / 0.010 mol = 28 g/mol. Moles ratio: C = 85.7/12 = 7.14; H = 14.3/1 = 14.3. Ratio C:H = 1:2. Empirical formula = CH2 (mass = 14 g/mol). n = 28 / 14 = 2. Molecular formula = (CH2)2 = C2H4 (ethene).

qs.q: Determine the oxidation state of manganese in potassium manganate(VII), KMnO₄, and in manganese(IV) oxide, MnO₂, respectively.
When sodium ethanoate is heated with soda lime (NaOH/CaO mixture), the organic product formed is:
qs.e: Heating a sodium salt of a carboxylic acid with soda lime causes decarboxylation, removing -COONa as Na2CO3 to yield an alkane with one fewer carbon atom. CH3COONa + NaOH → CH4 + Na2CO3.

qs.q: Which catalyst is used in the Contact Process for the industrial manufacture of sulfuric acid?
qs.e: In the Contact Process, sulfur dioxide (SO2) is oxidized to sulfur trioxide (SO3) at 450 °C using vanadium(V) oxide (V2O5) as the catalyst.

qs.q: Which salt solution will form a white precipitate with dilute HCl that dissolves upon heating and reappears on cooling?
qs.e: Lead(II) ions react with chloride ions to form lead(II) chloride precipitate: Pb²⁺(aq) + 2Cl⁻(aq) → PbCl₂(s). PbCl₂ is insoluble in cold water but soluble in hot water, so the precipitate dissolves when heated and recrystallizes upon cooling.

qs.q:
Consider the following electrochemical cell setup:

If 0.40 Faradays of electricity are passed through the cell containing copper(II) sulfate solution, what volume of oxygen gas (measured at STP) is evolved at the anode? (Molar volume of gas at STP = 22.4 dm³/mol)
qs.e: At the anode, water/OH- is oxidized: 2H2O(l) → O2(g) + 4H+(aq) + 4e-. 4 Faradays of electricity liberate 1 mole of O2 gas (22.4 dm³ at STP). Moles of O2 per Faraday = 1/4 = 0.25 mol/F. For 0.40 F: Moles of O2 = 0.40 × 0.25 = 0.10 mol. Volume of O2 at STP = 0.10 mol × 22.4 dm³/mol = 2.24 dm³.

qs.q: The standard enthalpy of formation of CO₂(g) is -393.5 kJ/mol and for H₂O(l) is -285.8 kJ/mol. If the standard enthalpy of combustion of methane, CH₄(g), is -890.3 kJ/mol, calculate the standard enthalpy of formation of CH₄(g).
For the reversible reaction: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), ΔH = -92 kJ/mol. Which combination of conditions will maximize the equilibrium yield of ammonia (NH₃)?
qs.e: According to Le Chatelier's principle: (1) Pressure: 4 moles of gas on reactant side produce 2 moles on product side. Increasing pressure shifts equilibrium to the right (fewer moles). (2) Temperature: The forward reaction is exothermic (ΔH < 0). Lowering temperature favors the forward exothermic reaction to release heat, shifting equilibrium to the right.

qs.q: What volume of 0.50 mol/dm³ HCl is required to react completely with 2.12 g of anhydrous sodium carbonate, Na₂CO₃? (Na = 23, C = 12, O = 16)
qs.e: Molar mass of Na2CO3 = (23×2)+12+(16×3) = 106 g/mol. Moles of Na2CO3 = 2.12 / 106 = 0.020 mol. Reaction: Na2CO3 + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H2O + CO2. Moles of HCl required = 2 × 0.020 mol = 0.040 mol. Volume of 0.50 mol/dm³ HCl = (0.040 mol / 0.50 mol/dm³) = 0.080 dm³ = 80.0 cm³.

qs.q: During a rate study of the reaction 2N₂O₅(g) → 4NO₂(g) + O₂(g), the concentration of N₂O₅ decreases by 0.24 mol/dm³ in 120 seconds. What is the rate of formation of NO₂ in mol/(dm³·s)?
qs.e: Rate of disappearance of N2O5 = Δ[N2O5]/Δt = 0.24 / 120 = 0.0020 mol/(dm³·s). From reaction stoichiometry, 2 moles of N2O5 form 4 moles of NO2 (a 1:2 ratio). Therefore, rate of formation of NO2 = 2 × (rate of N2O5) = 2 × 0.0020 = 0.0040 mol/(dm³·s).

qs.q: When excess chlorine gas is bubbled through a cold, dilute solution of sodium hydroxide, the main chlorine-containing products formed are:
qs.e: Chlorine undergoes disproportionation in cold, dilute NaOH (aq): Cl2(g) + 2NaOH(aq) → NaCl(aq) + NaClO(aq) + H2O(l). (In hot concentrated NaOH, NaCl and NaClO3 are formed).

qs.q: What is the systematic IUPAC name for the structural isomer of pentane that contains a quaternary carbon atom?
qs.e: Pentane (C5H12) has 3 structural isomers: pentane, 2-methylbutane (isopentane), and 2,2-dimethylpropane (neopentane). 2,2-dimethylpropane has a central carbon bonded to 4 methyl groups, making it a quaternary carbon.

qs.q: Which polymer is formed by condensation polymerization between hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid?
qs.e: Nylon-6,6 is a polyamide synthesized by condensation polymerization of hexamethylenediamine (H2N-(CH2)6-NH2) and adipic acid (HOOC-(CH2)4-COOH), eliminating water molecules.

qs.q: The solubility product, Ksp, of calcium sulfate (CaSO₄) at 25 °C is 2.4 × 10⁻⁵ mol²/dm⁶. Calculate the molar solubility of CaSO₄ in pure water at 25 °C.
qs.e: CaSO4(s) ⇌ Ca²⁺(aq) + SO4²⁻(aq). Let solubility be s mol/dm³. Ksp = [Ca²⁺][SO4²⁻] = s × s = s². s = √(Ksp) = √(2.4 × 10⁻⁵) = 0.0048989 mol/dm³ ≈ 4.90 × 10⁻³ mol/dm³.

qs.q: In a Daniel cell consisting of Zn/Zn²⁺(1 M) and Cu/Cu²⁺(1 M) half-cells, the standard reduction potentials are E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = -0.76 V and E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V. What is the standard cell potential (E°cell)?
qs.e: E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode. Copper has higher reduction potential (+0.34 V) so it acts as cathode. Zinc acts as anode (-0.76 V). E°cell = (+0.34 V) - (-0.76 V) = +0.34 + 0.76 = +1.10 V.

qs.q: An unknown gas X diffuses 1.414 times faster than sulfur dioxide gas (SO₂) under the same conditions of temperature and pressure. Calculate the relative molecular mass of gas X. (S = 32, O = 16)
qs.e: Molar mass of SO2 = 32 + (2×16) = 64 g/mol. By Graham's Law of diffusion: Rate(X) / Rate(SO2) = √(M(SO2) / M(X)). 1.414 = √(64 / M(X)). Squaring both sides: 2.0 = 64 / M(X) => M(X) = 64 / 2.0 = 32 g/mol.

qs.q: Which reagent can be used to distinguish between ethyne (HC≡CH) and ethene (H₂C=CH₂)?
qs.e: Terminal alkynes like ethyne contain acidic hydrogen atoms attached to sp-hybridized carbon. Ethyne reacts with ammoniacal silver nitrate to give a white precipitate of silver dicarbide (Ag2C2). Ethene (an alkene) does not react with Tollens' reagent.

qs.q: Which gas law assumes that gas particles have negligible volume and experience no intermolecular forces of attraction?
qs.e: An ideal gas is a theoretical gas whose molecules occupy negligible space and exert no mutual attraction or repulsion on each other, satisfying PV = nRT.

qs.q: A student accidentally spills concentrated nitric acid on a wooden bench top, causing a yellow stain. What type of reaction causes this color change?
o: Xanthoproteic reaction with proteins in wood
Reduction of nitric acid to yellow NO₂ gas
qs.e: Concentrated nitric acid reacts with aromatic amino acids present in proteins (such as those in skin or wood) to form yellow nitrated protein products. This characteristic reaction is called the xanthoproteic test.

qs.q: A sample of 1.50 g of an organic compound containing C, H, and O was completely burned in excess oxygen, producing 3.30 g of CO₂ and 1.80 g of H₂O. Calculate the empirical formula of the compound. (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)

In an experiment to determine activation energy, a reaction rate constant doubles when the absolute temperature is increased from 300 K to 310 K. Using R = 8.314 J/(mol·K) and ln(2) = 0.693, calculate the activation energy (Ea) for the reaction.

When 50.0 cm³ of 1.0 mol/dm³ HCl is mixed with 50.0 cm³ of 1.0 mol/dm³ NaOH in a calorimeter, the temperature rises by 6.7 °C. Assuming specific heat capacity of solution is 4.18 J/(g·°C) and density is 1.0 g/cm³, calculate the enthalpy change of neutralization per mole of H₂O formed.
qs.e: Total mass of solution = 50.0 + 50.0 = 100.0 g. Heat absorbed q = m × c × ΔT = 100.0 g × 4.18 J/(g·°C) × 6.7 °C = 2800.6 J = 2.8006 kJ. Moles of H+ = Ca × Va = 1.0 × 0.050 = 0.050 mol. Moles of H2O formed = 0.050 mol. ΔH neutralization = -q / n = -2.8006 kJ / 0.050 mol = -56.012 kJ/mol ≈ -56.0 kJ/mol.

qs.q: For the equilibrium system: 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g), Kc = 280 mol⁻¹·dm³ at a given temperature. If at equilibrium [SO₂] = 0.10 mol/dm³ and [SO₃] = 0.70 mol/dm³, calculate the equilibrium concentration of O₂ gas.

What volume of dry chlorine gas at 27 °C and 1.20 atm pressure is produced at the anode during the electrolysis of molten NaCl when a current of 5.0 A is passed for 3 hours and 13 minutes? (R = 0.0821 L·atm/(mol·K), 1 F = 96,500 C/mol)

An acidic salt solution X yields a white precipitate with aqueous ammonia that dissolves in excess ammonia. When treated with dilute HNO₃ followed by AgNO₃, X gives a white precipitate soluble in dilute aqueous ammonia. Solution X contains:
qs.e: Zn²⁺ forms Zn(OH)2 white precipitate with NH3(aq) which dissolves in excess NH3 to give soluble [Zn(NH3)4]²⁺ complex. Cl⁻ gives AgCl white precipitate with AgNO3/HNO3, which is soluble in dilute NH3(aq). Therefore, X is ZnCl2.

qs.q: What is the structural formula and IUPAC name of the major product formed when 2-bromobutane undergoes elimination reaction with hot alcoholic potassium hydroxide (KOH)?
qs.e: Dehydrohalogenation of 2-bromobutane with alcoholic KOH follows Zaitsev's rule, yielding the more substituted, thermodynamically stable alkene as the major product: CH3-CH=CH-CH3 (but-2-ene).

qs.q: During the extraction of iron in a blast furnace, limestone (CaCO₃) is added primarily to decompose into calcium oxide (CaO), which then reacts with silica impurities (SiO₂) to form:
qs.e: Limestone decomposes: CaCO3 → CaO + CO2. The basic oxide CaO reacts with acidic silica impurities (sand): CaO + SiO2 → CaSiO3 (molten calcium silicate slag), which floats above molten iron and is tapped off.

qs.q: Which property of transition metals accounts for their ability to form colored complexes and act as effective catalysts in industrial processes?
o: Presence of partially filled d-orbitals and variable oxidation states
High electronegativity and small atomic radii
Low ionization energy and ionic bonding
High density and high melting points only
qs.e: Transition metals have incompletely filled d-orbitals. Electronic d-d transitions absorb visible light causing color, while accessible variable oxidation states allow them to readily gain/lose electrons during catalysis.

qs.q: Calculate the percentage purity of a sample of limestone if 2.50 g of the impure sample reacts with excess HCl to yield 448 cm³ of carbon dioxide gas at STP. (Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16, Molar volume at STP = 22.4 dm³/mol)
qs.e: Reaction: CaCO3 + 2HCl → CaCl2 + H2O + CO2. Moles of CO2 = 0.448 dm³ / 22.4 dm³/mol = 0.020 mol. Moles of pure CaCO3 = 0.020 mol. Mass of pure CaCO3 = 0.020 mol × 100 g/mol = 2.00 g. Percentage purity = (2.00 g / 2.50 g) × 100% = 80.0%.

qs.q: Which process is used to separate liquid air into nitrogen, argon, and oxygen gas based on differences in their boiling points?
qs.e: Air is liquefied under high pressure and low temperature, then gradually warmed in a fractionating column. Nitrogen (b.p. -196 °C), argon (-186 °C), and oxygen (-183 °C) boil off at distinct temperatures during fractional distillation.

qs.q: A mixture of 20 cm³ of methane (CH₄) and 60 cm³ of oxygen (O₂) is ignited inside a eudiometer at room temperature and pressure. What is the total volume of gaseous product remaining after cooling to room temperature, and what volume of excess reagent remains? (Assume water condenses to liquid)
o: 20 cm³ CO₂ and 20 cm³ excess O₂
20 cm³ CO₂ and 40 cm³ excess O₂
40 cm³ CO₂ and 20 cm³ excess O₂
20 cm³ CO₂ and 10 cm³ excess O₂
qs.e: Combustion equation: CH4(g) + 2O2(g) → CO2(g) + 2H2O(l). By Gay-Lussac's law of combining volumes: 1 vol CH4 requires 2 vol O2 to produce 1 vol CO2. 20 cm³ CH4 requires 2 × 20 = 40 cm³ O2. O2 supplied = 60 cm³, so excess O2 remaining = 60 - 40 = 20 cm³. CO2 produced = 20 cm³. Liquid H2O volume is negligible. Remaining gaseous mixture: 20 cm³ CO2 + 20 cm³ excess O2.

qs.q: A buffer solution is prepared by mixing 500 cm³ of 0.20 mol/dm³ CH₃COOH with 500 cm³ of 0.10 mol/dm³ CH₃COONa. Given Ka for CH₃COOH is 1.8 × 10⁻⁵ mol/dm³, calculate the pH of the resulting buffer solution.
qs.e: After mixing equal volumes (500 cm³ + 500 cm³ = 1000 cm³ = 1 dm³), concentrations are halved: [CH3COOH] = 0.10 mol/dm³, [CH3COO⁻] = 0.050 mol/dm³. Henderson-Hasselbalch equation: pH = pKa + log10([Salt]/[Acid]). pKa = -log10(1.8 × 10⁻⁵) = 4.7447. log10(0.050 / 0.10) = log10(0.5) = -0.3010. pH = 4.7447 - 0.3010 = 4.4437 ≈ 4.44.

qs.q: Calculate the mass of potassium dichromate (K₂Cr₂O₇) required to prepare 250 cm³ of a 0.050 mol/dm³ standard solution used in redox titration. (K = 39, Cr = 52, O = 16)
qs.e: Molar mass of K2Cr2O7 = (39×2) + (52×2) + (16×7) = 78 + 104 + 112 = 294 g/mol. Volume = 250 cm³ = 0.250 dm³. Moles required n = C × V = 0.050 mol/dm³ × 0.250 dm³ = 0.0125 mol. Mass = n × Molar mass = 0.0125 mol × 294 g/mol = 3.675 g ≈ 3.68 g.

qs.q: An organic ester X with formula C₄H₈O₂ undergoes alkaline hydrolysis (saponification) with aqueous NaOH to yield sodium ethanoate and an alcohol Y. Oxidation of alcohol Y with acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ yields ethanoic acid. Identify ester X.
qs.e: Alkaline hydrolysis of ester R-COO-R' yields R-COONa (salt) + R'-OH (alcohol). Since salt is sodium ethanoate (CH3COONa), the carboxylate part is ethanoate (2 carbons). Alcohol Y on oxidation yields ethanoic acid (2 carbons), so Y must be ethanol (CH3CH2OH). Therefore, ester X is ethyl ethanoate (CH3COOCH2CH3, formula C4H8O2).

qs.q: Calculate the standard free energy change (ΔG°) at 298 K for the reaction: 2NO(g) + O₂(g) → 2NO₂(g), given ΔH° = -114.1 kJ and ΔS° = -146.5 J/K.
What is the shape of a water (H₂O) molecule according to VSEPR theory?
qs.e: Central oxygen in H2O has 2 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs (tetrahedral electron geometry). The repulsion from the 2 lone pairs reduces the H-O-H bond angle to ~104.5°, giving the molecule a bent or V-shaped molecular geometry.

qs.q: Which state of matter has a definite volume but no fixed shape, taking the shape of its container?
qs.e: Liquids have intermolecular forces strong enough to hold a fixed volume, but weak enough to allow particles to slide past one another, taking the shape of the container.

qs.q: According to Charles's Law, the volume of a given mass of gas at constant pressure is directly proportional to its:
qs.e: Charles's Law states V ∝ T (in Kelvin) for a fixed mass of gas at constant pressure (V1/T1 = V2/T2).

qs.q: Which acid is present in human stomach juice to aid in digestion?
qs.e: Gastric juice produced in the stomach contains dilute hydrochloric acid (~0.1 M HCl, pH 1.5–2.0) which activates digestive enzymes like pepsin.

qs.q: What general formula represents the homologous series of alkanes?
qs.e: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with single bonds, represented by the general molecular formula CnH2n+2.

qs.q: Which alloy is composed primarily of copper and zinc?
qs.e: Brass is a substitutional alloy composed mainly of copper (Cu) and zinc (Zn). (Bronze is copper and tin).

qs.q: Which noble gas is used to fill electric light bulbs to prevent the tungsten filament from oxidizing?
qs.e: Argon is an inert noble gas used in incandescent light bulbs to provide an unreactive atmosphere, preventing oxidation of the hot tungsten filament.

qs.q: Calculate the mass of magnesium oxide (MgO) formed when 4.80 g of pure magnesium ribbon is burned completely in oxygen. (Mg = 24, O = 16)
qs.e: Balanced equation: 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO. Moles of Mg = 4.80 / 24 = 0.20 mol. Moles of MgO formed = 0.20 mol. Molar mass of MgO = 24 + 16 = 40 g/mol. Mass of MgO = 0.20 mol × 40 g/mol = 8.00 g.

qs.q: A gas sample occupies 600 cm³ at 20 °C. At what temperature (in °C) will its volume double to 1200 cm³ at constant pressure?
What volume of 0.250 mol/dm³ H₂SO₄ is needed to prepare 500 cm³ of 0.050 mol/dm³ dilute H₂SO₄ solution?
How many faradays of electricity are required to deposit 10.8 g of silver at the cathode during the electrolysis of AgNO₃ solution? (Ag = 108)
qs.e: Cathode reaction: Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag(s). 1 mole of e⁻ (1 Faraday) deposits 1 mole of Ag (108 g). Moles of Ag = 10.8 g / 108 g/mol = 0.10 mol. Therefore, Faradays required = 0.10 F.

qs.q: The reaction between ethanol and ethanoic acid in the presence of concentrated H₂SO₄ produces an organic liquid with a sweet fruity odor. This reaction is called:
qs.e: Reox/condensation between an alcohol and a carboxylic acid catalyzed by conc. H2SO4 to yield an ester and water is known as esterification. CH3COOH + C2H5OH ⇌ CH3COOC2H5 + H2O.

qs.q: Which method is most suitable for collecting a sample of dry ammonia gas in the laboratory?
o: Upward delivery (downward displacement of air) over concentrated H₂SO₄ drying agent
Upward delivery through a calcium oxide (quicklime) drying tower
Collection over water through silica gel
qs.e: Ammonia (NH3) is extremely soluble in water and acidic drying agents like conc. H2SO4 (forming ammonium sulfate). It is less dense than air (molar mass 17 vs ~29), so it is dried using quicklime (CaO) and collected by upward delivery (downward displacement of air).

qs.q: Which element has the electron configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁴?
qs.e: Total electrons = 2 + 2 + 6 + 2 + 4 = 16. Element with atomic number 16 is Sulfur (S), located in Period 3, Group 16 (VI A).

qs.q: Which type of oxide is zinc oxide (ZnO), reacting with both acids and strong bases to form salts?
qs.e: Amphoteric oxides exhibit both basic and acidic properties. ZnO reacts with HCl to form ZnCl2 + H2O, and with NaOH to form sodium zincate Na2[Zn(OH)4].

qs.q: An endothermic reaction absorbs 150 kJ of heat from the surroundings. What is the sign and value of its enthalpy change (ΔH)?
qs.e: By convention, endothermic reactions absorb heat from surroundings, so enthalpy of products is greater than enthalpy of reactants: ΔH = H(products) - H(reactants) = +150 kJ.

qs.q: Which hydrocarbon undergoes an addition reaction with bromine water to decolorize it from reddish-brown to colorless?
qs.e: Unsaturated hydrocarbons containing carbon-carbon double bonds (alkenes like propene) or triple bonds undergo rapid addition reactions with bromine water, decolorizing it. Saturated alkanes do not react in the dark.

qs.q: What is the monomer unit used to manufacture poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC)?
qs.e: Poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) is an addition polymer synthesized from the monomer chloroethene (CH2=CHCl), commonly known as vinyl chloride.

qs.q: Which gaseous product is formed when copper metal reacts with concentrated nitric acid?
qs.e: Concentrated nitric acid acts as a strong oxidizing agent: Cu + 4HNO3(conc) → Cu(NO3)2 + 2NO2(g) + 2H2O(l). Brown fumes of nitrogen dioxide (NO2) gas are evolved.

qs.q:
Refer to the reaction rate graph below showing gas evolution over time:
