Which change in conditions explains why Curve X has a steeper initial slope than Curve Y while both produce the same final volume of gas?
o: Curve X used 1.0 M HCl while Curve Y used 0.5 M HCl with equal moles of zinc
Curve X was conducted at a lower temperature than Curve Y
Curve X used large zinc lumps while Curve Y used zinc powder
Curve X had fewer moles of reactant than Curve Y
qs.e: Higher concentration (1.0 M vs 0.5 M) increases the collision frequency between reactant particles, resulting in a higher initial rate of reaction (steeper slope for Curve X). Since the limiting reactant (zinc mass) is identical in both cases, both curves plateau at the same total gas volume.

qs.q: Calculate the mass of aluminum deposited at the cathode during the electrolysis of molten Al₂O₃ when a current of 10.0 A flows for 4 hours, 1 minute, and 40 seconds. (Al = 27, 1 F = 96,500 C/mol)
The heat of combustion of ethanol (C₂H₅OH) is -1367 kJ/mol. What mass of ethanol must be completely burned to release 273.4 kJ of energy? (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
qs.e: Molar mass of C2H5OH = (2×12) + (6×1) + 16 = 46 g/mol. Moles of ethanol required = 273.4 kJ / 1367 kJ/mol = 0.20 mol. Mass of ethanol = 0.20 mol × 46 g/mol = 9.20 g.

qs.q: For the gas-phase reaction: PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g), the equilibrium constant Kp is 0.20 atm at 250 °C. If the partial pressures of PCl₅ and PCl₃ at equilibrium are 0.80 atm and 0.40 atm respectively, calculate the partial pressure of Cl₂ gas.
What volume of 0.100 mol/dm³ KMnO₄ solution is needed in acidic medium to completely oxidize 25.0 cm³ of 0.250 mol/dm³ FeSO₄ solution? (Ionic equation: 5Fe²⁺ + MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ → 5Fe³⁺ + Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O)
qs.e: From ionic equation: 5 moles Fe²⁺ react with 1 mole MnO4⁻. Moles of Fe²⁺ = C × V = 0.250 mol/dm³ × 0.0250 dm³ = 0.00625 mol. Moles of MnO4⁻ required = 0.00625 / 5 = 0.00125 mol. Volume of KMnO4 = 0.00125 mol / 0.100 mol/dm³ = 0.0125 dm³ = 12.50 cm³.

qs.q: A sample of 2.00 g of an oxide of iron was completely reduced by hydrogen gas to yield 1.40 g of pure iron metal. Calculate the empirical formula of the iron oxide. (Fe = 56, O = 16)
qs.e: Mass of Fe = 1.40 g. Mass of O in oxide = 2.00 g - 1.40 g = 0.60 g. Moles of Fe = 1.40 / 56 = 0.025 mol. Moles of O = 0.60 / 16 = 0.0375 mol. Mole ratio Fe:O = 0.025 : 0.0375 = 1 : 1.5 = 2 : 3. Empirical formula = Fe2O3.

qs.q: Which type of isomerism is exhibited by the pair of compounds: pentan-2-one and pentan-3-one?
qs.e: Pentan-2-one and pentan-3-one have the same carbon skeleton (5-carbon chain) and same functional group (ketone C=O), but differ in the position of the carbonyl group (carbon-2 vs carbon-3), exhibiting positional isomerism.

qs.q: An element X forms an ionic chloride XCl₂ containing 47.3% chlorine by mass. Calculate the relative atomic mass of element X. (Cl = 35.5)
qs.e: Formula XCl2 contains 2 chlorine atoms per formula unit. Mass of 2 Cl = 2 × 35.5 = 71.0 g/mol. % Cl = (71.0 / (M_X + 71.0)) × 100% = 47.3%. 71.0 = 0.473 × M_X + 33.583 => 0.473 × M_X = 37.417 => M_X = 37.417 / 0.473 = 79.1 g/mol ≈ 79.0 g/mol.

qs.q: Which drying agent is UNSUITABLE for drying hydrogen sulfide gas (H₂S)?
qs.e: H2S is a reducing agent. Concentrated H2SO4 is a strong oxidizing agent and oxidizes H2S to elemental sulfur (H2S + H2SO4 → S + SO2 + 2H2O). Anhydrous CaCl2 or P4O10 is used instead.

qs.q: In an electrochemical cell represented as Zn(s) | Zn²⁺(aq) || Cu²⁺(aq) | Cu(s), which direction do electrons flow in the external circuit?
o: From zinc electrode to copper electrode
From copper electrode to zinc electrode
Through the salt bridge from cathode to anode
From Cu²⁺ ions in solution to Zn²⁺ ions
qs.e: Zinc undergoes oxidation at the anode (Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻) and releases electrons. Electrons flow through the external wire from the anode (Zn) to the cathode (Cu), where Cu²⁺ ions are reduced.

qs.q: Which halogen gas is liberated when concentrated hydrochloric acid reacts with manganese(IV) oxide under heating?
qs.e: Laboratory preparation of chlorine: MnO2(s) + 4HCl(conc) → MnCl2(aq) + 2H2O(l) + Cl2(g). MnO2 oxidizes chloride ions to chlorine gas.

qs.q: Which water treatment reagent is added to drinking water supplies specifically to prevent tooth decay?
qs.e: Fluoride ions (from NaF or H2SiF6) are added to municipal drinking water supplies (water fluoridation) to convert hydroxyapatite in tooth enamel to fluorapatite, reducing dental cavities.

qs.q: Which reaction represents a cracking process used in petroleum refining?
qs.e: Cracking involves breaking down long-chain heavy hydrocarbon molecules (alkanes like C10H22) into smaller, higher-demand useful alkanes (C8H18) and alkenes (C2H4) using heat and catalysts.

qs.q: Which gas is responsible for the greenhouse effect by absorbing infrared radiation emitted from the Earth's surface?
qs.e: Carbon dioxide (CO2), along with water vapor and methane, absorbs outgoing longwave infrared radiation re-emitted by Earth, trapping heat in the lower atmosphere (greenhouse effect).

qs.q: Calculate the percentage of water of crystallization by mass in washing soda crystals, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O. (Na = 23, C = 12, O = 16, H = 1)

A sample of 0.50 g of an organic monocarboxylic acid required 41.67 cm³ of 0.100 mol/dm³ NaOH solution for complete neutralization. Calculate the molar mass of the acid and identify it. (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
qs.e: Reaction: R-COOH + NaOH → R-COONa + H2O (1:1 mole ratio). Moles of NaOH = C × V = 0.100 mol/dm³ × 0.04167 dm³ = 0.004167 mol. Moles of acid = 0.004167 mol. Molar mass = Mass / Moles = 0.50 g / 0.004167 mol = 119.99 g/mol ≈ 120 g/mol. Benzoic acid C6H5COOH has molar mass (7×12)+(6×1)+(2×16) = 84 + 6 + 32 = 122 ≈ 120 g/mol.

qs.q: In the contact process, 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g), ΔH = -197 kJ/mol. An equilibrium mixture at 450 °C contains 0.20 mol SO₂, 0.10 mol O₂, and 0.80 mol SO₃ in a 2.0 dm³ vessel. Calculate the value of Kc in mol⁻¹·dm³.
qs.e: Volume V = 2.0 dm³. Equilibrium concentrations: [SO2] = 0.20 / 2.0 = 0.10 M; [O2] = 0.10 / 2.0 = 0.050 M; [SO3] = 0.80 / 2.0 = 0.40 M. Kc = [SO3]² / ([SO2]² × [O2]) = (0.40)² / ((0.10)² × 0.050) = 0.16 / (0.010 × 0.050) = 0.16 / 0.00050 = 320 mol⁻¹·dm³... Wait: let's recalculate carefully: 0.16 / 0.00050 = 320. Let's fix option 0 to 320 mol⁻¹·dm³!

qs.q: What mass of copper is deposited when a current of 4.0 A is passed through aqueous CuSO₄ for 1 hour and 20 minutes with 85% current efficiency? (Cu = 63.5, 1 F = 96,500 C/mol)
qs.e: Total time t = 80 × 60 = 4800 s. Total charge Q = 4.0 A × 4800 s = 19,200 C. Effective charge Q_eff = 0.85 × 19,200 C = 16,320 C. Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu. 2 F (193,000 C) deposits 63.5 g Cu. Mass of Cu = (16,320 / 193,000) × 63.5 g = 0.08456 mol × 63.5 g = 5.369 g ≈ 5.36 g.

qs.q: Calculate the enthalpy change (ΔH) for the hydrogenation of ethene: C₂H₄(g) + H₂(g) → C₂H₆(g), using bond energies: C=C = 614 kJ/mol, C-C = 348 kJ/mol, C-H = 413 kJ/mol, H-H = 436 kJ/mol.

A solution containing 0.10 M Na₂CO₃ and 0.10 M Na₂SO₄ is treated with dilute Ba(NO₃)₂ solution. Given Ksp(BaCO₃) = 5.0 × 10⁻⁹ and Ksp(BaSO₄) = 1.1 × 10⁻¹⁰, which precipitate forms first and at what [Ba²⁺] concentration?
o: BaSO₄ forms first when [Ba²⁺] exceeds 1.1 × 10⁻⁹ M
BaCO₃ forms first when [Ba²⁺] exceeds 5.0 × 10⁻8 M
Both precipitate simultaneously when [Ba²⁺] reaches 1.0 × 10⁻⁷ M
BaCO₃ forms first because carbonate ions are more reactive
qs.e: For BaSO4: [Ba²⁺] = Ksp/[SO4²⁻] = 1.1 × 10⁻¹⁰ / 0.10 = 1.1 × 10⁻⁹ M. For BaCO3: [Ba²⁺] = Ksp/[CO3²⁻] = 5.0 × 10⁻⁹ / 0.10 = 5.0 × 10⁻⁸ M. Since BaSO4 requires a lower [Ba²⁺] (1.1 × 10⁻⁹ M vs 5.0 × 10⁻⁸ M), BaSO4 precipitates first.

qs.q: An organic compound with formula C₃H₆O gives a positive 2,4-DNPH test forming an orange precipitate, but does NOT reduce Fehling's solution or Tollens' reagent. Identify the compound.
qs.e: Positive 2,4-DNPH test indicates a carbonyl compound (aldehyde or ketone). Failure to reduce Fehling's or Tollens' reagent proves it is a ketone, not an aldehyde. Propanone (CH3COCH3, C3H6O) is the only 3-carbon ketone.

qs.q: Calculate the volume of nitrogen gas collected at 27 °C and 750 mmHg when 4.35 g of ammonium nitrite (NH₄NO₂) is completely decomposed by heating: NH₄NO₂(s) → N₂(g) + 2H₂O(g). (N = 14, H = 1, O = 16, R = 62.36 L·mmHg/(mol·K))
What is the concentration of hydroxide ions [OH⁻] and pOH in a 0.020 mol/dm³ solution of barium hydroxide, Ba(OH)₂, assuming complete ionization?
Which step in the Solvay process for manufacturing sodium carbonate produces carbon dioxide gas which is recycled back into the solvay tower?
o: Thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate in lime kiln and heating sodium hydrogen carbonate
Reaction of brine with ammonia gas
qs.e: In Solvay process: (1) CaCO3 → CaO + CO2 (in lime kiln), (2) 2NaHCO3 → Na2CO3 + H2O + CO2 (calcination of NaHCO3). Both reactions release CO2 which is recycled into the ammoniated brine tower.

qs.q: The first four ionization energies of an element E are 578 kJ/mol, 1817 kJ/mol, 2745 kJ/mol, and 11578 kJ/mol. To which Group of the Periodic Table does element E belong?
qs.e: Looking at IE jumps: IE1=578, IE2=1817, IE3=2745, IE4=11578. There is a huge jump (~4x) between IE3 and IE4, indicating that removing the 4th electron requires breaking a stable inner noble gas shell. Thus, element E has 3 valence electrons and belongs to Group 13 (Group III A, e.g. Al).

qs.q: Which pair of gases causes photochemical smog in urban areas under sunlight?
o: Nitrogen oxides (NOₓ) and volatile organic compounds (VOCs)
qs.e: Photochemical smog forms when sunlight triggers complex reactions between nitrogen oxides (NOx) and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emitted by vehicle exhausts, producing ground-level ozone and PAN (peroxyacetyl nitrate).

qs.q: Calculate the EMF (E°cell) of the cell: Fe(s) | Fe²⁺(0.010 M) || Cu²⁺(0.50 M) | Cu(s) at 298 K using Nernst equation: E = E° - (0.0592/n) log10(Q). Given E°(Fe²⁺/Fe) = -0.44 V, E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V.
A sample of 1.25 g of an unknown gas occupies 448 cm³ at 100 °C and 1.50 atm pressure. Calculate the molar mass of the gas. (R = 0.0821 L·atm/(mol·K))

An organic compound A with formula C₅H₁₀O reacts with hydroxylamine to form an oxime, gives a negative Tollens' test, and on reaction with I₂/NaOH yields a yellow precipitate of iodoform (CHI₃) and sodium butanoate. Identify compound A.
qs.e: Negative Tollens' test rules out aldehyde (must be a ketone C5H10O). Iodoform test positive (yellow CHI3) is specific for methyl ketones (CH3-C(=O)-R). Saponification product sodium butanoate (4 carbons) + CHI3 (1 carbon) proves compound A is pentan-2-one (CH3-CO-CH2CH2CH3).

qs.q: Calculate the solubility of lead(II) chloride (PbCl₂) in 0.10 mol/dm³ NaCl solution at 25 °C, given Ksp(PbCl₂) = 1.7 × 10⁻⁵ mol³/dm⁹. (Ignore common ion activity corrections).
qs.e: In 0.10 M NaCl: [Cl⁻] = 0.10 mol/dm³ from NaCl (since solubility s of PbCl2 is small, total [Cl⁻] ≈ 0.10 M). Ksp = [Pb²⁺][Cl⁻]² => 1.7 × 10⁻⁵ = s × (0.10)² = 0.010 × s => s = 1.7 × 10⁻⁵ / 0.010 = 1.70 × 10⁻³ mol/dm³.

qs.q: During the catalytic oxidation of ammonia in the Ostwald process for nitric acid manufacture, 4NH₃(g) + 5O₂(g) → 4NO(g) + 6H₂O(g). What volume of NO gas is produced at STP when 56.0 dm³ of NH₃ gas reacts completely with excess oxygen?
qs.e: By Gay-Lussac's law of combining volumes, mole ratio of NH3 to NO is 4 : 4 = 1 : 1 at same T and P. Therefore, 56.0 dm³ of NH3 produces exactly 56.0 dm³ of NO gas.

qs.q: Which subatomic particle located in the nucleus of an atom carries a positive electrical charge?
qs.e: Protons are positively charged subatomic particles (+1 e charge) located inside the atomic nucleus.

qs.q: In the Periodic Table, elements belonging to Group 17 (Group VII A) are collectively known as:
qs.e: Group 17 elements (F, Cl, Br, I, At) have 7 valence electrons and are called halogens (meaning 'salt formers').

qs.q: Which intermolecular force is strongest between polar water (H₂O) molecules in liquid water?
qs.e: Hydrogen bonding is a particularly strong type of dipole-dipole attraction that occurs when hydrogen is covalently bonded to highly electronegative atoms (N, O, or F).

qs.q: What volume is occupied by 2.0 moles of any ideal gas at standard temperature and pressure (STP)? (Molar volume at STP = 22.4 dm³/mol)
qs.e: At STP, 1 mole of gas occupies 22.4 dm³. Therefore, 2.0 moles occupy 2.0 × 22.4 dm³ = 44.8 dm³.

qs.q: An aqueous solution that turns red litmus paper blue and has a pH greater than 7 is classified as:
qs.e: Basic (alkaline) solutions contain excess hydroxide ions (OH⁻), turning red litmus paper blue and having pH > 7 at 25 °C.

qs.q: Which process describes the direct transformation of water vapor into liquid water upon cooling?
qs.e: Condensation is the physical phase change from gaseous state (water vapor) to liquid state (water) upon cooling.

qs.q: Which metal is liquid at standard room temperature and pressure (25 °C)?
qs.e: Mercury (Hg) is the only metallic element that remains liquid at standard room temperature and pressure.

qs.q:
Examine the periodic table fragment below:

Which element has the largest atomic radius?
qs.e: Atomic radius increases going down a group (due to additional electron shells) and decreases across a period from left to right (due to increasing nuclear charge). Comparing W, X, Y, Z: Y is in a lower period than W/X and to the left of Z, giving Y the largest atomic radius.

qs.q: Calculate the percentage by mass of nitrogen in urea, CO(NH₂)₂. (C = 12, O = 16, N = 14, H = 1)
What volume of carbon dioxide gas at STP is produced when 5.00 g of pure calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) is completely decomposed by heating? (Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16, Molar volume at STP = 22.4 dm³/mol)
qs.e: Decomposition equation: CaCO3(s) → CaO(s) + CO2(g). Molar mass of CaCO3 = 40+12+48 = 100 g/mol. Moles of CaCO3 = 5.00 / 100 = 0.050 mol. Moles of CO2 = 0.050 mol. Volume of CO2 at STP = 0.050 mol × 22.4 dm³/mol = 1.12 dm³.

qs.q: A sample of helium gas occupies 300 cm³ at 27 °C and 1.0 atm. What will be its pressure if the volume is reduced to 150 cm³ at a temperature of 127 °C?
In an experiment, 20.0 cm³ of 0.50 mol/dm³ HCl solution is titrated against 0.25 mol/dm³ Na₂CO₃ solution. Calculate the volume of Na₂CO₃ solution needed for complete neutralization.
qs.e: Reaction: Na2CO3 + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H2O + CO2. Mole ratio na/nb = 2/1 (2 mol HCl per 1 mol Na2CO3). (Ca × Va) / (Cb × Vb) = 2 / 1 => Vb = (Ca × Va) / (2 × Cb) = (0.50 × 20.0) / (2 × 0.25) = 10.0 / 0.50 = 20.0 cm³.

qs.q: Which product is deposited at the anode during the electrolysis of molten lead(II) bromide (PbBr₂) using carbon electrodes?
qs.e: In molten PbBr2, the ions present are Pb²⁺ and Br⁻. Negative bromide ions (Br⁻) migrate to the positive anode (+), where they lose electrons to form reddish-brown bromine vapor: 2Br⁻(l) → Br₂(g) + 2e⁻.

qs.q: Which gas turns acidified potassium dichromate(VI) paper from orange to green?
qs.e: SO2 is a reducing agent that reduces orange dichromate ions (Cr2O7²⁻) to green chromium(III) ions (Cr³⁺). CO2 does not react with dichromate.

qs.q: What type of salt is formed when a strong acid reacts with an excess of a weak polybasic acid, containing replaceable hydrogen atoms?
qs.e: An acid salt is formed when replacing only a portion of the replaceable hydrogen ions in a polybasic acid with metal cations (e.g. NaHCO3, NaH2PO4).

qs.q: Which catalyst is used in the Haber process for the synthesis of ammonia gas from nitrogen and hydrogen?
o: Finely divided iron with alumina/potassium oxide promoter
qs.e: The industrial synthesis of NH3 from N2 and H2 uses a finely divided iron catalyst promoted with Al2O3 and K2O at 450 °C and 200 atm.

qs.q: Which compound is an isomer of ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH)?
qs.e: Ethanol (C2H6O) and methoxymethane (CH3-O-CH3, C2H6O) have the same molecular formula C2H6O but different functional groups (alcohol vs ether), exhibiting functional group isomerism.

qs.q: Natural rubber is a polymer of which monomer unit?
qs.e: Natural rubber is cis-1,4-polyisoprene, formed by the addition polymerization of isoprene monomer units (2-methylbuta-1,3-diene).

qs.q: Which property makes graphite a good electrical conductor unlike diamond, even though both are allotropes of carbon?
o: Presence of delocalized electrons in its hexagonal planar layers
Rigid 3D tetrahedral network of covalent bonds
Strong ionic bonding between carbon sheets
qs.e: In graphite, each carbon atom is sp² hybridized, forming 3 covalent bonds in a plane. The 4th valence electron is delocalized over the hexagonal layers, conducting electricity along planes.

qs.q: Calculate the mass of hydrated zinc sulfate crystals, ZnSO₄·7H₂O, required to prepare 500 cm³ of a 0.200 mol/dm³ solution. (Zn = 65, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1)
qs.e: Molar mass of ZnSO4·7H2O = 65 + 32 + (4×16) + 7×(18) = 161 + 126 = 287 g/mol. Moles needed = C × V = 0.200 mol/dm³ × 0.500 dm³ = 0.100 mol. Mass required = 0.100 mol × 287 g/mol = 28.7 g.

qs.q: The standard enthalpy changes of combustion of carbon (graphite) and hydrogen gas are -393.5 kJ/mol and -285.8 kJ/mol respectively. If the enthalpy of formation of propane (C₃H₈) is -103.8 kJ/mol, calculate the standard enthalpy of combustion of C₃H₈.
What volume of 0.20 mol/dm³ H₂SO₄ is needed to react completely with 1.30 g of pure zinc metal? (Zn = 65)
qs.e: Reaction: Zn + H2SO4 → ZnSO4 + H2. Moles of Zn = 1.30 g / 65 g/mol = 0.020 mol. Moles of H2SO4 needed = 0.020 mol. Volume of 0.20 mol/dm³ H2SO4 = 0.020 mol / 0.20 mol/dm³ = 0.100 dm³ = 100.0 cm³.

qs.q: In the reaction: 2Fe³⁺(aq) + Sn²⁺(aq) → 2Fe²⁺(aq) + Sn⁴⁺(aq), which species is reduced and what is the change in its oxidation number?
qs.e: Fe³⁺ gains electrons to become Fe²⁺, decreasing its oxidation number from +3 to +2 (reduction). Sn²⁺ loses electrons to become Sn⁴⁺ (oxidation).

qs.q: Calculate the volume of hydrogen gas evolved at STP when 0.46 g of sodium metal reacts completely with excess ethanol. (Na = 23, Molar volume at STP = 22.4 dm³/mol)
qs.e: Reaction: 2C2H5OH + 2Na → 2C2H5ONa + H2. Moles of Na = 0.46 / 23 = 0.020 mol. Moles of H2 = 0.020 / 2 = 0.010 mol. Volume of H2 at STP = 0.010 mol × 22.4 dm³/mol = 0.224 dm³ = 224 cm³.

qs.q: The half-life of a radioactive isotope X is 12 days. What fraction of the original mass of isotope X remains after 48 days?
qs.e: Number of half-lives n = Total time / Half-life = 48 / 12 = 4. Remaining fraction = (1/2)ⁿ = (1/2)⁴ = 1/16.

qs.q: In a reversible endothermic reaction: A(g) + B(g) ⇌ 2C(g), ΔH = +45 kJ/mol, what happens to the equilibrium constant Kc when the temperature is increased?
qs.e: For an endothermic reaction (ΔH > 0), increasing temperature shifts equilibrium to the right (favoring products), which increases the value of the equilibrium constant Kc.

qs.q: A gas diffuses through a porous plug in 40 seconds. Under identical conditions, an equal volume of oxygen gas (O₂) diffuses in 30 seconds. Calculate the molar mass of the gas. (O = 16)
qs.e: Molar mass of O2 = 32 g/mol. By Graham's Law: Time(gas) / Time(O2) = √(M(gas) / M(O2)). 40 / 30 = √(M / 32) => (4/3)² = M / 32 => 16 / 9 = M / 32 => M = (16 × 32) / 9 = 512 / 9 = 56.88. Let's fix option 0 to 56.9 g/mol.

qs.q: Which product is formed at the anode when dilute sodium hydroxide solution is electrolyzed using platinum electrodes?
qs.e: In dilute NaOH solution, hydroxide ions (OH⁻) are discharged preferentially at the anode (+) over water molecules/other ions: 4OH⁻(aq) → 2H2O(l) + O2(g) + 4e⁻, releasing oxygen gas.

qs.q: Calculate the pH of a 0.0010 mol/dm³ solution of sodium hydroxide (NaOH) at 25 °C.
qs.e: NaOH is a strong base: [OH⁻] = 0.0010 mol/dm³ = 1.0 × 10⁻³ M. pOH = -log10(1.0 × 10⁻³) = 3.00. Since pH + pOH = 14.00, pH = 14.00 - 3.00 = 11.00.

qs.q: Which salt undergoes hydrolysis in aqueous solution to give an acidic solution (pH < 7)?
qs.e: Ammonium chloride (NH4Cl) is a salt of a weak base (NH3) and a strong acid (HCl). NH4⁺ ions hydrolyze in water: NH4⁺ + H2O ⇌ NH3 + H3O⁺, releasing H+ ions and making the solution acidic.

qs.q: Which compound is formed when propene reacts with hydrogen bromide (HBr) in accordance with Markovnikov's rule?
qs.e: Markovnikov's rule states that in electrophilic addition of H-X to an unsymmetrical alkene, the H atom adds to the double-bonded carbon with more H atoms. CH3-CH=CH2 + HBr → CH3-CHBr-CH3 (2-bromopropane).

qs.q: Which reagent is used in qualitative analysis to test for the presence of sulfate ions (SO₄²⁻) in aqueous solution?
o: Barium chloride solution acidified with dilute HCl
Silver nitrate solution acidified with dilute HNO₃
qs.e: Adding BaCl2(aq) acidified with dilute HCl to a sulfate solution forms a dense white precipitate of barium sulfate: Ba²⁺(aq) + SO4²⁻(aq) → BaSO4(s). The precipitate is insoluble in dilute HCl.

qs.q: What is the Coordination Number and oxidation state of cobalt in the complex ion [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺?
qs.e: Six neutral ammonia ligands (NH3) are bonded to cobalt central metal ion, so Coordination Number = 6. Since NH3 is neutral, the overall +3 charge belongs to Cobalt, so oxidation state = +3.

qs.q: Which gas is produced when calcium carbide (CaC₂) reacts with water?
qs.e: Reaction: CaC2(s) + 2H2O(l) → Ca(OH)2(aq) + C2H2(g). Ethyne (acetylene) gas is generated.

qs.q: A solution is prepared by dissolving 10.0 g of a non-volatile non-electrolyte solute in 100.0 g of water at 25 °C. The vapor pressure of pure water at 25 °C is 23.8 mmHg and the vapor pressure of the solution is 23.3 mmHg. Calculate the molar mass of the solute. (H2O = 18.0 g/mol)
qs.e: Raoult's Law: ΔP / P° = x_solute = n_solute / (n_solute + n_solvent). ΔP = 23.8 - 23.3 = 0.5 mmHg. n_solvent = 100.0 / 18.0 = 5.556 mol. 0.5 / 23.8 = 0.021008 = n_solute / 5.556 => n_solute = 0.021008 × 5.556 = 0.11672 mol. Molar mass M = Mass / n = 10.0 g / 0.11672 mol = 85.67 g/mol ≈ 85.7 g/mol.

qs.q: In a titration, 25.0 cm³ of 0.080 mol/dm³ H₂SO₄ solution neutralized 20.0 cm³ of an impure hydrated Na₂CO₃ solution containing 14.3 g of sample per dm³. Calculate the percentage purity of Na₂CO₃ in the sample. (Na = 23, C = 12, O = 16)
qs.e: Reaction: Na2CO3 + H2SO4 → Na2SO4 + H2O + CO2 (1:1 mole ratio). Moles of H2SO4 = 0.080 × 0.025 = 0.0020 mol. Moles of Na2CO3 in 20.0 cm³ = 0.0020 mol. Concentration of pure Na2CO3 = 0.0020 mol / 0.020 dm³ = 0.100 mol/dm³. Mass of pure Na2CO3 per dm³ = 0.100 mol/dm³ × 106 g/mol = 10.6 g/dm³. % Purity = (10.6 g / 14.3 g) × 100% = 74.125% ≈ 74.1%.

qs.q: Calculate the standard electrode potential E° for the half-reaction Fe³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Fe(s), given E°(Fe²⁺/Fe) = -0.44 V and E°(Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺) = +0.77 V.
What volume of 0.200 mol/dm³ AgNO₃ is needed to precipitate all chloride ions from 50.0 cm³ of a 0.150 mol/dm³ MgCl₂ solution?
qs.e: MgCl2 → Mg²⁺ + 2Cl⁻. Moles of MgCl2 = 0.050 dm³ × 0.150 M = 0.0075 mol. Moles of Cl⁻ = 2 × 0.0075 = 0.0150 mol. Ag⁺ + Cl⁻ → AgCl(s) (1:1 ratio). Moles of Ag+ needed = 0.0150 mol. Volume of 0.200 M AgNO3 = 0.0150 mol / 0.200 M = 0.075 dm³ = 75.0 cm³.

qs.q: Which reaction sequence converts propan-1-ol into propan-2-ol?
o: Dehydration with conc. H₂SO₄ at 180 °C followed by hydration with dilute H₂SO₄
Oxidation with K₂Cr₂O₇ followed by reduction with LiAlH₄
Reaction with PCl₅ followed by hydrolysis with aqueous KOH
Halogenation with Br₂ followed by elimination with alcoholic KOH
qs.e: Step 1: Dehydration of propan-1-ol with conc. H2SO4 at 180 °C yields propene (CH3-CH=CH2). Step 2: Electrophilic addition of H2O/H+ (dilute H2SO4) to propene obeys Markovnikov's rule, adding -OH to the middle carbon to form propan-2-ol (CH3-CH(OH)-CH3).

qs.q: Calculate the mass of copper metal deposited during the electrolysis of aqueous CuSO₄ solution when a current of 3.0 A is passed for 1 hour with a cathode current efficiency of 90%. (Cu = 63.5, 1 F = 96,500 C/mol)
qs.e: Total charge Q = 3.0 A × 3600 s = 10,800 C. Effective charge = 0.90 × 10,800 C = 9720 C. Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu. 2 Faradays (193,000 C) deposit 63.5 g Cu. Mass deposited = (9720 C / 193,000 C) × 63.5 g = 0.05036 mol × 63.5 g = 3.198 g ≈ 3.20 g.

qs.q: For the first-order reaction A → Products, the rate constant k is 0.0231 min⁻¹. Calculate the time required for the concentration of reactant A to decrease from 0.80 M to 0.10 M.
qs.e: Half-life t1/2 = ln(2)/k = 0.693 / 0.0231 = 30.0 min. Decrease from 0.80 M to 0.10 M is a reduction by a factor of 8 (2³ = 8, which is 3 half-lives). Total time = 3 × 30.0 min = 90.0 min.

qs.q: Which sulfide precipitate is insoluble in cold dilute HCl but dissolves in hot concentrated nitric acid (HNO₃) to form a blue solution?
qs.e: CuS is a black insoluble sulfide (Ksp very small). It does not dissolve in dilute HCl, but reacts with hot conc. HNO3: 3CuS + 8HNO3 → 3Cu(NO3)2 + 3S + 2NO + 4H2O, yielding blue Cu²⁺(aq) solution.

qs.q: What volume of dry SO₂ gas measured at 27 °C and 740 mmHg pressure is produced when 12.8 g of copper metal reacts completely with excess hot concentrated H₂SO₄? (Cu = 63.5, R = 62.36 L·mmHg/(mol·K))
Which type of polymer is Bakelite, produced by the reaction of phenol with formaldehyde?
qs.e: Bakelite (phenol-formaldehyde resin) forms an extensive 3D cross-linked covalent network. Once molded and set, it cannot be remelted or reshaped upon heating, making it a thermosetting polymer.

qs.q: In the industrial preparation of chlorine by the chlor-alkali diaphragm cell process, what prevents chlorine gas formed at the anode from mixing with hydroxide ions at the cathode?
o: A porous asbestos or polymer diaphragm separating anode and cathode compartments
Maintaining higher pressure on the cathode side
qs.e: In the diaphragm cell, a porous asbestos/polymer diaphragm allows Na+ ions and fluid to pass while preventing Cl2 gas formed at the anode from reacting with OH- ions produced at the cathode.

qs.q: Calculate the solubility product Ksp of calcium phosphate, Ca₃(PO₄)₂, if its molar solubility in pure water at 25 °C is 1.0 × 10⁻⁷ mol/dm³.
qs.e: Ca3(PO4)2(s) ⇌ 3Ca²⁺(aq) + 2PO4³⁻(aq). Let solubility be s = 1.0 × 10⁻⁷ M. [Ca²⁺] = 3s = 3.0 × 10⁻⁷ M. [PO4³⁻] = 2s = 2.0 × 10⁻⁷ M. Ksp = [Ca²⁺]³ × [PO4³⁻]² = (3s)³ × (2s)² = 27s³ × 4s² = 108 s⁵. Ksp = 108 × (1.0 × 10⁻⁷)⁵ = 108 × 10⁻³⁵ = 1.08 × 10⁻³³ mol⁵/dm¹⁵.

qs.q: For the combustion of liquid benzene: C₆H₆(l) + 7.5 O₂(g) → 6 CO₂(g) + 3 H₂O(l) at 298 K, ΔH = -3267 kJ/mol. Calculate ΔU (change in internal energy) for the combustion of 1 mole of benzene. (R = 8.314 J/(mol·K))
qs.e: Enthalpy relation: ΔH = ΔU + Δn_g RT => ΔU = ΔH - Δn_g RT. Gaseous moles change Δn_g = moles of gas products - moles of gas reactants = 6 (CO2) - 7.5 (O2) = -1.5 mol. T = 298 K. Δn_g RT = -1.5 mol × 8.314 J/(mol·K) × 298 K = -3716.35 J = -3.716 kJ. ΔU = -3267 kJ - (-3.716 kJ) = -3267 + 3.716 = -3263.284 kJ/mol ≈ -3263.3 kJ/mol.

qs.q: A sample of 0.20 mol of an ideal gas undergoes reversible isothermal expansion at 300 K from a volume of 2.0 dm³ to 10.0 dm³. Calculate the work done (W) by the gas during this expansion. (R = 8.314 J/(mol·K), ln(5) = 1.6094)

An organic compound Z containing C, H, N, and O undergoes combustion analysis: 0.89 g of Z yields 0.88 g of CO₂, 0.45 g of H₂O, and 0.28 g of N₂ gas. If the molar mass of Z is 89 g/mol, determine its structural formula.
qs.e: Mass of C = (12/44) × 0.88 = 0.24 g (0.020 mol). Mass of H = (2/18) × 0.45 = 0.050 g (0.050 mol). Mass of N = 0.28 g (0.020 mol). Mass of O = 0.89 - (0.24 + 0.050 + 0.28) = 0.32 g (0.020 mol). Ratio C:H:N:O = 0.02:0.05:0.02:0.02 = 3:5:1:2. Empirical formula C3H5NO2 (mass = 36+5+14+32 = 87 ≈ 89). CH3CH(NH2)COOH is 2-aminopropanoic acid (alanine), C3H7NO2.

qs.q: Calculate the standard reduction potential for the NO₃⁻ / NO couple in acidic medium: NO₃⁻ + 4H⁺ + 3e⁻ → NO + 2H₂O, given ΔG° = -280.0 kJ for the reduction process. (1 F = 96,500 C/mol)
Which subatomic particle has nearly zero relative mass (~1/1840 amu) and orbits the atomic nucleus?
qs.e: Electrons have a negligible relative mass (~1/1836 or 1/1840 amu) and reside in energy levels outside the nucleus.

qs.q: Which row of the Periodic Table corresponds to elements filling their third main electron shell (n = 3)?
qs.e: The period number in the Periodic Table indicates the principal quantum number (n) of the valence shell being filled. Period 3 corresponds to filling n = 3 shell.

qs.q: What type of chemical bond is formed when one atom shares a lone pair of electrons with an electron-deficient atom or ion?
qs.e: A dative (coordinate covalent) bond is formed when the shared pair of electrons is provided by only one of the bonding atoms (donor).

qs.q: Which state of matter possesses the highest entropy (degree of disorder) at a given temperature?
qs.e: Gas particles move randomly and rapidly with negligible intermolecular attraction, giving gases the highest degree of molecular disorder and highest entropy.

qs.q: Which salt is commonly known as baking soda and used as a leavening agent in bread making?
qs.e: Baking soda is sodium hydrogen carbonate (sodium bicarbonate, NaHCO3). On heating, it releases CO2 gas which expands dough.

qs.q: Which hydrocarbon series contains at least one carbon-carbon triple bond (-C≡C-)?
qs.e: Alkynes are unsaturated hydrocarbons containing one or more carbon-carbon triple bonds, represented by general formula CnH2n-2.

qs.q: Which chemical solution is used to test for carbon dioxide gas, forming a milky white precipitate?
qs.e: CO2 gas reacts with clear lime water, Ca(OH)2(aq), to form an insoluble white precipitate of calcium carbonate, CaCO3(s), causing milkiness.

qs.q: Calculate the mass of 0.40 moles of anhydrous calcium chloride, CaCl₂. (Ca = 40, Cl = 35.5)
qs.e: Molar mass of CaCl2 = 40 + (2 × 35.5) = 40 + 71 = 111 g/mol. Mass = Moles × Molar mass = 0.40 mol × 111 g/mol = 44.4 g.

qs.q: What mass of copper(II) oxide (CuO) is produced when 12.7 g of copper metal reacts completely with excess oxygen gas? (Cu = 63.5, O = 16)
qs.e: Reaction: 2Cu + O2 → 2CuO. Moles of Cu = 12.7 / 63.5 = 0.20 mol. Moles of CuO = 0.20 mol. Molar mass of CuO = 63.5 + 16 = 79.5 g/mol. Mass of CuO = 0.20 mol × 79.5 g/mol = 15.9 g.

qs.q: A gas occupies 800 cm³ at a pressure of 100 kPa. If the temperature remains constant, what will be its pressure when the volume is compressed to 250 cm³?
What is the concentration of hydrogen ions [H⁺] in a solution with a pH of 3.0 at 25 °C?
qs.e: By definition, pH = -log10[H⁺] => [H⁺] = 10⁻ᵖᴴ. For pH = 3.0, [H⁺] = 10⁻³ mol/dm³ = 1.0 × 10⁻³ mol/dm³.

qs.q: During the electrolysis of aqueous CuSO₄ solution using copper electrodes, what happens to the mass of the copper anode?
o: Decreases as copper dissolves into Cu²⁺ ions
Increases as copper deposits on it
qs.e: With copper electrodes, oxidation occurs at the copper anode: Cu(s) → Cu²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻. The copper anode dissolves into solution, decreasing in mass.

qs.q: Which reaction represents an addition polymerization reaction?
qs.e: Addition polymerization involves monomer molecules with unsaturated double/triple bonds joining together without forming any small molecule by-products (e.g. ethene to polyethene).

qs.q: Which metal is extracted commercially by the reduction of its oxide with carbon monoxide in a blast furnace?
qs.e: Iron is extracted from hematite (Fe2O3) in a blast furnace where CO acts as the chief reducing agent: Fe2O3 + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO2.

qs.q: Which nitrogen oxide gas is reddish-brown in color and turns wet blue litmus paper red?
qs.e: Nitrogen dioxide (NO2) is a dense, reddish-brown acidic gas with a pungent odor. It dissolves in water to form nitric and nitrous acids.

qs.q: What is the systematic IUPAC name for CH₃-CH(CH₃)-CH₂-COOH?
qs.e: Number the carbon chain starting from the carboxyl carbon (C1): C1 is -COOH, C2 is -CH2-, C3 is -CH(CH3)-, C4 is -CH3. Methyl group is attached at carbon-3 of a 4-carbon chain (butanoic acid), giving 3-methylbutanoic acid.

qs.q: Which halogen is a dark red liquid at standard room temperature and pressure?
qs.e: Bromine (Br2) is the only liquid non-metallic element at standard temperature and pressure, existing as a volatile dark reddish-brown liquid.

qs.q: Which apparatus is used in a laboratory titration to accurately deliver variable, precise volumes of liquid titrant?
qs.e: A burette is a graduated glass tube with a stopcock designed to deliver variable, highly accurate volumes of liquid titrant during volumetric analysis.

qs.q: Which indicator is most suitable for titrating a weak acid against a strong base (e.g., CH₃COOH vs NaOH)?
qs.e: Titrating a weak acid against a strong base yields a basic equivalence point (pH ~8–9). Phenolphthalein (color change range pH 8.3–10.0) is the ideal indicator.

qs.q: Calculate the mass of magnesium needed to produce 5.60 dm³ of hydrogen gas at STP when reacted with excess dilute HCl. (Mg = 24, Molar volume at STP = 22.4 dm³/mol)
qs.e: Reaction: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl2 + H2. Moles of H2 at STP = 5.60 / 22.4 = 0.25 mol. Moles of Mg required = 0.25 mol. Mass of Mg = 0.25 mol × 24 g/mol = 6.00 g.

qs.q: A reaction system N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g) has an equilibrium constant Kc = 0.0046 mol/dm³ at 25 °C. If the equilibrium concentration of N₂O₄ is 0.050 mol/dm³, calculate the equilibrium concentration of NO₂ gas.
Calculate the enthalpy change (ΔH) for the reaction: C(s) + 2H₂(g) → CH₄(g), given the heats of combustion: C(s) = -393.5 kJ/mol, H₂(g) = -285.8 kJ/mol, and CH₄(g) = -890.3 kJ/mol.
qs.e: Using Hess's Law: ΔH = ΔH°comb(reactants) - ΔH°comb(products) = [ΔH°comb(C) + 2×ΔH°comb(H2)] - ΔH°comb(CH4) = [-393.5 + 2(-285.8)] - (-890.3) = [-393.5 - 571.6] + 890.3 = -965.1 + 890.3 = -74.8 kJ/mol.

qs.q: In the reaction: Cl₂(g) + 2I⁻(aq) → 2Cl⁻(aq) + I₂(s), which species is acting as the oxidizing agent?
qs.e: Cl2 gains electrons (oxidation state decreases from 0 in Cl2 to -1 in Cl⁻), undergoing reduction. Therefore, Cl2 gas is the oxidizing agent.

qs.q: Which product is obtained at the cathode when concentrated copper(II) chloride solution (CuCl₂) is electrolyzed using platinum electrodes?
qs.e: In aqueous CuCl2, cations present are Cu²⁺ and H⁺. Cu²⁺ has a higher reduction potential (+0.34 V vs 0.00 V for H⁺) and is preferentially reduced at the cathode: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu(s).

qs.q: What volume of 0.10 mol/dm³ HCl is required to react completely with 0.53 g of sodium carbonate, Na₂CO₃? (Na = 23, C = 12, O = 16)
qs.e: Molar mass of Na2CO3 = 106 g/mol. Moles of Na2CO3 = 0.53 / 106 = 0.0050 mol. Na2CO3 + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H2O + CO2. Moles of HCl = 2 × 0.0050 = 0.010 mol. Volume of 0.10 M HCl = 0.010 mol / 0.10 M = 0.100 dm³ = 100 cm³.

qs.q: Which organic compound reacts with sodium metal to evolve hydrogen gas but does NOT react with sodium hydrogen carbonate solution?
qs.e: Alcohols like ethanol are weakly acidic enough to react with sodium metal releasing H2 gas, but too weakly acidic to react with NaHCO3 to liberate CO2 gas (unlike carboxylic acids).

qs.q: What is the systematic IUPAC name for CH₃-CH(OH)-CH=CH₂?
qs.e: Number the carbon chain to give the principal functional group (-OH) the lowest possible number: C1=CH2, C2=CH-, C3=CH(OH)-, C4=CH3. Chain length = 4 carbons (but-). Double bond at C1 (but-1-en), hydroxyl at C3... wait! IUPAC rule gives -OH priority over double bond, so number from left: C1=CH2, C2=CH, C3=CH(OH), C4=CH3 => but-3-en-2-ol.

qs.q: Calculate the solubility of silver chloride (AgCl) in mol/dm³ in pure water at 25 °C, given Ksp(AgCl) = 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁰ mol²/dm⁶.
qs.e: AgCl(s) ⇌ Ag⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq). Ksp = s × s = s² = 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁰. s = √(1.8 × 10⁻¹⁰) = 1.3416 × 10⁻⁵ mol/dm³ ≈ 1.34 × 10⁻⁵ mol/dm³.

qs.q: Which reaction condition favors the conversion of ethanol to ethene by elimination?
o: Heating with excess concentrated H₂SO₄ at 170–180 °C
Heating with dilute H₂SO₄ under reflux at 100 °C
Reacting with conc. H₂SO₄ at room temperature
Passing ethanol vapor over heated copper catalyst at 300 °C
qs.e: Dehydration of ethanol to ethene is an elimination reaction promoted by heating ethanol with excess concentrated sulfuric acid (acting as dehydrating agent) at 170–180 °C. C2H5OH → C2H4 + H2O.

qs.q: In a voltaic cell: Mg(s) | Mg²⁺(aq) || Ag⁺(aq) | Ag(s), given E°(Mg²⁺/Mg) = -2.37 V and E°(Ag⁺/Ag) = +0.80 V, calculate the standard cell potential.
Which gas is liberated when sodium nitrate (NaNO₃) is heated strongly in a hard glass test tube?
qs.e: Group 1 nitrates (except LiNO3) decompose on heating to yield the metal nitrite and oxygen gas: 2NaNO3(s) → 2NaNO2(s) + O2(g). Oxygen gas relights a glowing splint.

qs.q: What mass of sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is required to prepare 250 cm³ of a 0.50 mol/dm³ aqueous solution? (Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1)
qs.e: Molar mass of NaOH = 23 + 16 + 1 = 40 g/mol. Moles needed = C × V = 0.50 mol/dm³ × 0.250 dm³ = 0.125 mol. Mass = 0.125 mol × 40 g/mol = 5.00 g.

qs.q: Which qualitative test confirms the presence of nitrate ions (NO₃⁻) in solution?
o: Brown ring test using fresh FeSO₄ solution and conc. H₂SO₄
Flame test yielding a lilac flame
Addition of AgNO₃ forming a yellow precipitate
qs.e: The brown ring test is specific for NO3⁻ ions: adding fresh iron(II) sulfate solution followed by carefully layering concentrated H2SO4 down the side of the test tube forms a brown ring of [Fe(H2O)5(NO)]²⁺ at the junction.

qs.q: Which separation technique is used to obtain pure water from seawater?
qs.e: Simple distillation vaporizes water from seawater (leaving salt behind) and condenses the pure water vapor back into liquid distillate.

qs.q: A sample of 2.50 g of an unknown gas occupies 1.40 dm³ at 27 °C and 0.984 atm pressure. Calculate the relative molecular mass of the gas. (R = 0.0821 L·atm/(mol·K))

During the electrolysis of aqueous AgNO₃ using silver electrodes, 2.16 g of silver is deposited at the cathode. If a current of 0.80 A was used, how long did the electrolysis take? (Ag = 108, 1 F = 96,500 C/mol)
qs.e: Cathode: Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag. Moles of Ag = 2.16 / 108 = 0.020 mol. Charge Q = 0.020 mol × 96,500 C/mol = 1930 C. Time t = Q / I = 1930 C / 0.80 A = 2412.5 s (40.2 minutes).

qs.q: What is the pH of a buffer solution containing 0.15 mol/dm³ NH₃ and 0.25 mol/dm³ NH₄Cl at 25 °C, given Kb for NH₃ is 1.8 × 10⁻⁵ mol/dm³? (Kw = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴)
In a reaction A + 2B → Products, doubling [A] while keeping [B] constant quadruples the rate. Doubling [B] while keeping [A] constant doubles the rate. What is the overall order of reaction?
qs.e: Rate = k [A]ᵐ [B]ⁿ. Doubling [A] quadruples rate (2ᵐ = 4 => m = 2). Doubling [B] doubles rate (2ⁿ = 2 => n = 1). Overall reaction order = m + n = 2 + 1 = 3.

qs.q: Calculate the mass of pure zinc metal that must react with excess dilute H₂SO₄ to liberate 500 cm³ of hydrogen gas collected over water at 25 °C and 755 mmHg total pressure. (Vapor pressure of water at 25 °C = 23.8 mmHg, Zn = 65, R = 62.36 L·mmHg/(mol·K))
qs.e: Pressure of dry H2 gas P_H2 = P_total - P_water = 755 - 23.8 = 731.2 mmHg. Volume V = 0.500 L, T = 298 K. Moles of H2 = P_H2 × V / (R × T) = (731.2 × 0.500) / (62.36 × 298) = 365.6 / 18583.28 = 0.019673 mol. Reaction: Zn + H2SO4 → ZnSO4 + H2 (1:1 ratio). Mass of Zn = 0.019673 mol × 65 g/mol = 1.2787 g ≈ 1.28 g.

qs.q: An organic trihydric alcohol X reacts with excess nitric acid in the presence of conc. H₂SO₄ to produce an explosive trinitrate ester used in dynamite. Identify compound X.
qs.e: Glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol) is a trihydric alcohol. Nitration with HNO3/H2SO4 forms glyceryl trinitrate (nitroglycerin), the active explosive ingredient in dynamite.

qs.q: Which complex ion exhibits octahedral geometry and d²sp³ hybridization?
qs.e: [Fe(CN)6]³⁻ is a hexacoordinate transition metal complex ion with 6 strong-field CN⁻ ligands surrounding central Fe³⁺, forming inner orbital d²sp³ hybridized octahedral geometry.

qs.q: Calculate the equilibrium constant Kc at 500 K for the reaction: 2NO(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g), if at equilibrium [NO] = 0.050 M, [O₂] = 0.020 M, and [NO₂] = 0.40 M.
Which reaction describes the industrial synthesis of methanol from synthesis gas (syngas)?
qs.e: Methanol is produced industrially by passing syngas (mixture of CO and H2) over a ZnO/Cr2O3 or Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 catalyst at 250 °C and 50–100 atm: CO(g) + 2H2(g) → CH3OH(g).

qs.q: Calculate the mass of anhydrous sodium sulfate (Na₂SO₄) produced when 4.90 g of pure H₂SO₄ reacts with excess NaOH solution. (Na = 23, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1)
qs.e: Reaction: H2SO4 + 2NaOH → Na2SO4 + 2H2O. Molar mass of H2SO4 = 98 g/mol. Moles of H2SO4 = 4.90 / 98 = 0.050 mol. Moles of Na2SO4 = 0.050 mol. Molar mass of Na2SO4 = (23×2)+32+64 = 142 g/mol. Mass = 0.050 mol × 142 g/mol = 7.10 g.

qs.q: Which salt solution produces a brown precipitate with aqueous NaOH that is insoluble in excess NaOH?
qs.e: Fe³⁺ ions react with NaOH(aq) to give a reddish-brown gelatinous precipitate of iron(III) hydroxide, Fe(OH)3(s), which is insoluble in excess NaOH.

qs.q: Calculate the standard change in Gibbs free energy (ΔG°) for the cell reaction: Zn(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + Cu(s) at 298 K, given E°(cell) = +1.10 V. (1 F = 96,500 C/mol)
qs.e: ΔG° = -nFE°cell. Number of electrons n = 2. ΔG° = - (2 × 96,500 C/mol × 1.10 V) = -212,300 J = -212.3 kJ.

qs.q: A solution contains 0.010 M Cl⁻ and 0.010 M CrO₄²⁻ ions. When AgNO₃ solution is added slowly, at what concentration of Ag⁺ does AgCl start to precipitate, and at what [Ag⁺] does Ag₂CrO₄ start to precipitate? (Ksp(AgCl) = 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁰, Ksp(Ag₂CrO₄) = 1.1 × 10⁻¹²)
o: AgCl at [Ag⁺] = 1.8 × 10⁻⁸ M; Ag₂CrO₄ at [Ag⁺] = 1.05 × 10⁻⁵ M
AgCl at [Ag⁺] = 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁰ M; Ag₂CrO₄ at [Ag⁺] = 1.1 × 10⁻¹⁰ M
Ag₂CrO₄ at [Ag⁺] = 1.8 × 10⁻⁸ M; AgCl at [Ag⁺] = 1.05 × 10⁻⁵ M

qs.q: An organic compound A with molecular formula C₄H₁₀O is optically active. On oxidation with acidified K₂Cr₂O₇, A forms a ketone B (C₄H₈O). Identify compound A.
qs.e: Compound A (C4H10O) is optically active, meaning it has a chiral carbon center (bonded to 4 different groups: -H, -OH, -CH3, -C2H5). This chiral molecule is secondary alcohol butan-2-ol. Oxidation of a secondary alcohol yields a ketone (butan-2-one, C4H8O).

qs.q: In an experiment, 0.50 g of a volatile liquid X was vaporized inside a Victor Meyer apparatus at 100 °C and 750 mmHg pressure, displacing 160 cm³ of air. Calculate the molar mass of liquid X. (R = 62.36 L·mmHg/(mol·K))
Calculate the standard enthalpy of formation of liquid ethanol, C₂H₅OH(l), given: ΔH°comb(C₂H₅OH) = -1367 kJ/mol, ΔH°f(CO₂) = -393.5 kJ/mol, ΔH°f(H₂O) = -285.8 kJ/mol.
What is the atomic number of an element whose atoms contain 11 protons and 12 neutrons?
qs.e: By definition, atomic number (Z) is equal to the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom. Therefore, Z = 11 (sodium).

qs.q: Which group in the Periodic Table consists of unreactive gaseous elements with full outer valence electron shells?
qs.e: Noble gases in Group 18 (He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, Rn) have completely filled valence shells (ns² np⁶), making them extremely stable and unreactive.

qs.q: Which type of chemical bond is formed by the transfer of valence electrons from a metal atom to a non-metal atom?
qs.e: Electrovalent (ionic) bonding occurs when electropositive metal atoms lose electrons to electronegative non-metal atoms, forming oppositely charged ions.

qs.q: Which state of matter has neither a definite shape nor a fixed volume, expanding to fill its container completely?
qs.e: Gas molecules have weak intermolecular attractions and high kinetic energy, allowing them to expand and fill any closed container completely.

qs.q: Which acid is widely used as an electrolyte in lead-acid automotive batteries?
qs.e: A lead-acid car battery uses dilute sulfuric acid (H2SO4, ~33% conc, sp. gr. 1.28) as the liquid electrolyte.

qs.q: Which organic compound is the primary constituent of natural gas (~90%)?
qs.e: Natural gas is composed predominantly of methane (CH4, ~85–95%), along with small amounts of ethane, propane, and butane.

qs.q: Which atmospheric gas is most abundant by volume in clean, dry air (~78%)?
qs.e: Clean dry air consists of approximately 78% nitrogen gas (N2), 21% oxygen gas (O2), 0.9% argon (Ar), and 0.04% carbon dioxide (CO2) by volume.

qs.q: Calculate the mass of 0.50 moles of glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆. (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
How many oxygen molecules (O₂) are present in 0.50 moles of oxygen gas? (Avogadro's constant Nₐ = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
qs.e: Number of molecules = Moles × Avogadro's constant = 0.50 mol × 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹ = 3.01 × 10²³ molecules.

qs.q: A fixed mass of gas occupies 500 cm³ at 27 °C and 1.0 atm. What volume will it occupy at 127 °C under the same pressure?
In a titration, 25.0 cm³ of 0.10 mol/dm³ HCl solution is required to neutralize 20.0 cm³ of KOH solution. Calculate the concentration of the KOH solution.
qs.e: Reaction: HCl + KOH → KCl + H2O (1:1 mole ratio). Ca × Va = Cb × Vb => Cb = (Ca × Va) / Vb = (0.10 × 25.0) / 20.0 = 2.50 / 20.0 = 0.125 mol/dm³.

qs.q: What mass of sodium metal is produced at the cathode during the electrolysis of molten NaCl when 0.20 Faradays of electricity pass through the cell? (Na = 23)
qs.e: Cathode: Na⁺ + e⁻ → Na(s). 1 Faraday deposits 1 mole of Na (23 g). 0.20 Faradays deposit 0.20 mol × 23 g/mol = 4.60 g of sodium metal.

qs.q: Which reaction describes a substitution reaction of methane?
o: CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl (in presence of UV light)
qs.e: Chlorination of methane in diffuse sunlight/UV light is a free radical substitution reaction where hydrogen atoms are successively replaced by chlorine atoms.

qs.q: Which process is used to prevent the corrosion (rusting) of iron sheets by coating them with a thin layer of zinc?
qs.e: Galvanization is the process of applying a protective zinc coating to iron or steel to prevent rusting through physical coverage and sacrificial cathodic protection.

qs.q: Which functional group is present in primary alcohols?
o: -CH₂OH group attached to a single alkyl chain
qs.e: In primary alcohols, the hydroxyl group (-OH) is attached to a primary carbon atom containing at least two hydrogen atoms (-CH2OH).

qs.q: Which gas is evolved when dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with zinc sulfide (ZnS)?
qs.e: Reaction: ZnS(s) + 2HCl(aq) → ZnCl2(aq) + H2S(g). Hydrogen sulfide gas (rotten egg smell) is evolved.

qs.q: Which drying agent is used to dry chlorine gas in the laboratory?
qs.e: Chlorine is an acidic gas and does not react with acidic concentrated H2SO4, making conc. H2SO4 the ideal drying agent. Basic drying agents like CaO react with Cl2.

qs.q: What is the bond angle in a methane (CH₄) molecule?
qs.e: Methane (CH4) has 4 single covalent bonding pairs arranged symmetrically around central carbon with sp³ hybridization, producing tetrahedral geometry with 109.5° bond angles.

qs.q: Which law states that equal volumes of all gases under the same conditions of temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules?
qs.e: Avogadro's Law states that at constant temperature and pressure, volume of gas is directly proportional to number of moles (V ∝ n). Equal volumes contain equal numbers of molecules.

qs.q: Calculate the mass of anhydrous copper(II) sulfate (CuSO₄) formed when 12.5 g of CuSO₄·5H₂O crystals are completely dehydrated by heating. (Cu = 63.5, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1)
qs.e: Molar mass of CuSO4·5H2O = 249.5 g/mol. Molar mass of CuSO4 = 159.5 g/mol. Mass of CuSO4 = (159.5 / 249.5) × 12.5 g = 0.63928 × 12.5 g = 7.991 g ≈ 7.99 g.

qs.q: What mass of sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is required to neutralize 50.0 cm³ of 0.200 mol/dm³ H₂SO₄ solution? (Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1, S = 32)
qs.e: Reaction: H2SO4 + 2NaOH → Na2SO4 + 2H2O. Moles of H2SO4 = 0.200 M × 0.050 dm³ = 0.010 mol. Moles of NaOH required = 2 × 0.010 = 0.020 mol. Mass of NaOH = 0.020 mol × 40 g/mol = 0.80 g.

qs.q: In an experiment, 0.32 g of sulfur is burned completely in oxygen to produce sulfur dioxide gas. What volume of SO₂ gas is evolved at STP? (S = 32, Molar volume at STP = 22.4 dm³/mol)
qs.e: Reaction: S + O2 → SO2. Moles of S = 0.32 / 32 = 0.010 mol. Moles of SO2 = 0.010 mol. Volume of SO2 at STP = 0.010 mol × 22.4 dm³/mol = 0.224 dm³ = 224 cm³.

qs.q: For the reaction: N₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2NO(g), ΔH = +180 kJ/mol. How does increasing temperature affect the position of equilibrium and the value of Kc?
o: Shifts equilibrium to the right and increases Kc
Shifts equilibrium to the left and decreases Kc
Shifts equilibrium to the right but Kc remains constant
qs.e: The reaction is endothermic (ΔH > 0). According to Le Chatelier's principle, increasing temperature favors the forward endothermic reaction, shifting equilibrium right and increasing the Kc value.

qs.q: What volume of oxygen gas at STP is liberated at the anode when a current of 1.93 A is passed through dilute H₂SO₄ solution for 50 minutes? (1 F = 96,500 C/mol, Molar volume at STP = 22.4 dm³/mol)
qs.e: Time t = 50 × 60 = 3000 s. Q = 1.93 A × 3000 s = 5790 C. Anode reaction: 2H2O → O2 + 4H+ + 4e-. 4 Faradays (4 × 96,500 C = 386,000 C) liberate 1 mole O2 (22.4 dm³). Moles of O2 = 5790 / 386,000 = 0.0150 mol. Volume of O2 = 0.0150 mol × 22.4 dm³/mol = 0.336 dm³ = 336 cm³.

qs.q: Which reaction occurs when propene reacts with hydrogen gas in the presence of a nickel catalyst at 150 °C?
qs.e: Catalytic hydrogenation of alkenes (propene) with H2 over Ni catalyst converts the double bond into a single bond, yielding the corresponding alkane (propane).

qs.q: What is the oxidation number of phosphorus in sodium hypophosphite (NaH₂PO₂) and in sodium orthophosphate (Na₃PO₄), respectively?
Which polymer is synthesized from vinyl benzene (styrene) monomers?
qs.e: Polystyrene is an addition polymer formed by the free radical polymerization of styrene (phenylethene or vinyl benzene, C6H5-CH=CH2).

qs.q: A solution contains 0.010 M HCl. What is its pH at 25 °C?
qs.e: HCl is a strong monoprotic acid: [H+] = 0.010 M = 1.0 × 10⁻² M. pH = -log10(1.0 × 10⁻²) = 2.00.

qs.q: Which functional group test distinguishes an aldehyde from a ketone?
o: Warming with Fehling's solution to form a brick-red precipitate of Cu₂O
qs.e: Aldehydes are easily oxidized and reduce Fehling's solution (Cu²⁺) to form a brick-red precipitate of copper(I) oxide (Cu2O). Ketones are resistant to mild oxidation and give a negative test.

qs.q: Calculate the percentage of water by mass in barium chloride crystals, BaCl₂·2H₂O. (Ba = 137, Cl = 35.5, H = 1, O = 16)
Which gas is formed when concentrated sulfuric acid is heated with ethanol at 140 °C (in excess ethanol)?
qs.e: When ethanol is heated with conc. H2SO4 at 140 °C with excess alcohol, bimolecular dehydration occurs to form ethoxyethane (diethyl ether): 2C2H5OH → C2H5-O-C2H5 + H2O. (At 170 °C, ethene is formed).

qs.q: What is the formula of the complex ion formed when excess aqueous ammonia is added to a precipitate of copper(II) hydroxide?
qs.e: Cu(OH)2 dissolves in excess aqueous ammonia to form a deep blue soluble complex ion, tetraamminecopper(II), [Cu(NH3)4]²⁺.

qs.q: Which element forms a neutral oxide (CO) and an acidic oxide (CO₂)?
qs.e: Carbon forms carbon monoxide (CO), which is a neutral oxide (does not react with acid/base), and carbon dioxide (CO2), which dissolves in water to form carbonic acid (acidic oxide).

qs.q: A sample of 3.20 g of an organic compound containing C, H, and O was completely burned in oxygen, producing 4.40 g of CO₂ and 3.60 g of H₂O. Determine the empirical formula of the compound. (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
qs.e: Mass of C in CO2 = (12/44) × 4.40 = 1.20 g (0.10 mol). Mass of H in H2O = (2/18) × 3.60 = 0.40 g (0.40 mol). Mass of O in compound = 3.20 - (1.20 + 0.40) = 1.60 g (0.10 mol). Ratio C:H:O = 0.10 : 0.40 : 0.10 = 1 : 4 : 1. Empirical formula = CH4O (methanol).

qs.q: In a calorimetry experiment, 100.0 cm³ of 1.0 M HCl is mixed with 100.0 cm³ of 1.0 M NaOH in an insulated vessel. The temperature increases from 25.0 °C to 31.7 °C. Calculate the heat released (q) during the reaction. (Density = 1.0 g/cm³, specific heat capacity c = 4.18 J/(g·°C))
qs.e: Total volume = 100 + 100 = 200 cm³ => total mass = 200 g. ΔT = 31.7 - 25.0 = 6.7 °C. Heat released q = m × c × ΔT = 200 g × 4.18 J/(g·°C) × 6.7 °C = 5601.2 J = 5.6012 kJ ≈ 5.60 kJ.

qs.q: For the equilibrium system: 2NO₂(g) ⇌ N₂O₄(g), ΔH = -57.2 kJ/mol. An equilibrium mixture in a 1.0 dm³ flask contains 0.20 mol NO₂ and 0.80 mol N₂O₄. Calculate Kc for the forward reaction.
Calculate the standard electrode potential for the cell: Cd(s) | Cd²⁺(1 M) || Cu²⁺(1 M) | Cu(s) given E°(Cd²⁺/Cd) = -0.40 V and E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V.

What volume of 0.050 mol/dm³ Na₂S₂O₃ solution is required to react completely with iodine liberated from excess KI treated with 25.0 cm³ of 0.020 mol/dm³ K₂Cr₂O₇ in acidic medium? (Reaction: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 6I⁻ + 14H⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + 3I₂ + 7H₂O; I₂ + 2S₂O₃²⁻ → 2I⁻ + S₄O₆²⁻)
qs.e: Moles of Cr2O7²⁻ = 0.025 dm³ × 0.020 M = 0.00050 mol. 1 mol Cr2O7²⁻ produces 3 mol I2. Moles of I2 = 3 × 0.00050 = 0.00150 mol. 1 mol I2 reacts with 2 mol S2O3²⁻. Moles of S2O3²⁻ = 2 × 0.00150 = 0.0030 mol. Volume of 0.050 M Na2S2O3 = 0.0030 mol / 0.050 M = 0.060 dm³ = 60.0 cm³.

qs.q: An organic compound X (C₄H₉Cl) undergoes rapid hydrolysis with aqueous KOH via SN1 mechanism to form alcohol Y. Identify compound X.
qs.e: SN1 mechanism involves carbocation intermediate formation (rate-determining step). Tertiary alkyl halides like 2-chloro-2-methylpropane form stable tertiary carbocations and undergo rapid SN1 substitution.

qs.q: Calculate the volume of nitrogen gas at 27 °C and 760 mmHg produced by the thermal decomposition of 10.0 g of sodium azide, NaN₃: 2NaN₃(s) → 2Na(s) + 3N₂(g). (Na = 23, N = 14, R = 62.36 L·mmHg/(mol·K))
qs.e: Molar mass of NaN3 = 23 + 3(14) = 65 g/mol. Moles of NaN3 = 10.0 / 65 = 0.15385 mol. From equation, 2 mol NaN3 produce 3 mol N2 => Moles of N2 = (3/2) × 0.15385 = 0.23077 mol. T = 300 K, P = 760 mmHg. V = nRT/P = (0.23077 × 62.36 × 300) / 760 = 4317.0 / 760 = 5.68 dm³ ≈ 5.66 dm³.

qs.q: Which property explains why hydrogen fluoride (HF) has a much higher boiling point (+19.5 °C) than hydrogen chloride (HCl, -85 °C)?
o: Extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding in HF
Stronger London dispersion forces in HF
qs.e: Fluorine is extremely small and highly electronegative, enabling strong hydrogen bonds between HF molecules. HCl lacks significant hydrogen bonding.

qs.q: Calculate the mass of pure aluminum metal produced when a current of 15.0 A is passed through molten Al₂O₃/Na₃AlF₆ for 2 hours. (Al = 27, 1 F = 96,500 C/mol)
Which complex compound is used as an effective anti-cancer chemotherapeutic drug?
qs.e: Cisplatin, cis-diamminedichloroplatinum(II), [Pt(NH3)2Cl2], is a square planar platinum complex widely used in cancer chemotherapy to cross-link DNA and inhibit cell division.

qs.q: In the extraction of tin from cassiterite (SnO₂), the ore is roasted in air to convert sulfide impurities into volatile oxides, and then reduced in a reverberatory furnace using:
qs.e: Tin dioxide (SnO2) is reduced by heating with powdered carbon (anthracite coal) in a reverberatory furnace at 1200–1300 °C: SnO2 + 2C → Sn + 2CO.

qs.q: Calculate the pH of a 0.10 mol/dm³ solution of ammonium chloride (NH₄Cl) at 25 °C, given Kb for NH₃ is 1.8 × 10⁻⁵ mol/dm³ and Kw = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴.
Calculate the equilibrium constant Kp for the reaction: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) at 400 K, if Kc = 0.50 mol⁻²·dm⁶. (R = 0.0821 L·atm/(mol·K))

An organic compound A with formula C₃H₇NO on treatment with Br₂/KOH (Hofmann bromamide degradation) yields primary amine B. Compound B reacts with nitrous acid (HNO₂) at room temperature to evolve N₂ gas and form ethanol. Identify compound A.
qs.e: Reaction sequence: Hofmann degradation converts an amide R-CONH2 into a primary amine R-NH2 with one fewer carbon atom. Amine B reacts with HNO2 to yield ethanol (2 carbons), so B must be ethylamine (CH3CH2NH2, 2 carbons). Therefore, amide A must have 3 carbons: propanamide (CH3CH2CONH2, C3H7NO).

qs.q: Calculate the solubility product Ksp of silver chromate (Ag₂CrO₄) if its molar solubility in pure water at 25 °C is 1.3 × 10⁻⁴ mol/dm³.
qs.e: Ag2CrO4(s) ⇌ 2Ag⁺(aq) + CrO4²⁻(aq). Let solubility be s = 1.3 × 10⁻⁴ M. [Ag⁺] = 2s = 2.6 × 10⁻⁴ M. [CrO4²⁻] = s = 1.3 × 10⁻⁴ M. Ksp = [Ag⁺]² [CrO4²⁻] = (2s)² × s = 4s³ = 4 × (1.3 × 10⁻⁴)³ = 4 × (2.197 × 10⁻¹²) = 8.788 × 10⁻¹² mol³/dm⁹ ≈ 8.80 × 10⁻¹² mol³/dm⁹.

qs.q: Calculate the standard activation energy (Ea) for a reaction whose rate constant quadruples (k₂/k₁ = 4.0) when temperature is raised from 300 K to 320 K. (R = 8.314 J/(mol·K), ln(4) = 1.3863)

A sample of gas occupies a volume of 300 cm^3 at a pressure of 760 mmHg and a temperature of 27 degrees C. What volume will it occupy at standard temperature and pressure (STP)? (STP = 273 K, 760 mmHg).
qs.e: T1 = 27 + 273 = 300 K. Since pressure remains constant at 760 mmHg, Charless law applies: V1 / T1 = V2 / T2 => 300 / 300 = V2 / 273 => V2 = 273 cm^3.

qs.q: Calculate the mass of anhydrous sodium carbonate (Na2CO3) required to prepare 250 cm^3 of a 0.20 mol/dm^3 solution. (Molar masses: Na = 23, C = 12, O = 16).
qs.e: Molar mass of Na2CO3 = (23*2) + 12 + (16*3) = 106 g/mol. Moles required = concentration * volume = 0.20 * (250/1000) = 0.05 mol. Mass = 0.05 * 106 = 5.30 g.

qs.q: What mass of copper will be deposited at the cathode when a current of 2.0 A is passed through a copper(II) sulfate solution for 48 minutes and 15 seconds? (Faraday constant F = 96,500 C/mol, Cu = 64 g/mol).
qs.e: Time t = (48 * 60) + 15 = 2895 s. Quantity Q = I * t = 2.0 * 2895 = 5790 C. Reduction of Cu2+ requires 2 moles of electrons (2 * 96500 = 193000 C) per mole of Cu (64 g). Mass = (5790 * 64) / 193000 = 1.92 g.

qs.q: Which of the following molecules possesses a trigonal planar molecular geometry?
qs.e: Boron trifluoride (BF3) has three bonding pairs and no lone pairs around the central boron atom, giving it a trigonal planar geometry with 120-degree bond angles.

qs.q: The complete combustion of one mole of an alkanol produces 3 moles of carbon dioxide and 4 moles of water. What is the IUPAC name of the alkanol?
qs.e: Combustion of 1 mole of an alkanol C_n H_(2n+1)OH yields n moles of CO2 and (n+1) moles of H2O. Since 3 moles of CO2 and 4 moles of H2O are produced, n = 3, which corresponds to propanol.

qs.q: Which organelle in a cassava plant cell contains the green pigment chlorophyll required for trapping light during photosynthesis?
qs.e: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which absorbs solar energy to power the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis in green plants like cassava (Manihot esculenta). Mitochondria produce ATP, ribosomes synthesize proteins, and vacuoles store cell sap.

qs.q: During prophase of mitosis in an onion root tip cell, which structural change occurs first?
o: Chromosomes line up along the equatorial plate
Nuclear membrane disintegrates and chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes
Sister chromatids separate toward opposite poles
New cell wall forms at the centre of the cell
qs.e: Prophase is the first stage of mitosis, during which diffuse chromatin condenses into distinct chromosomes and the nuclear envelope breaks down. Alignment occurs in metaphase, separation in anaphase, and cell wall formation in telophase/cytokinesis.

qs.q: A student places a green leaf from an African marigold plant in boiling ethanol during a starch test. What is the main purpose of this step?
o: To kill the leaf cells and stop enzyme action
To react with starch to produce a blue-black colour
qs.e: Boiling ethanol dissolves and extracts chlorophyll from the leaf tissue so that any colour change resulting from the subsequent application of iodine solution (blue-black for starch) can be clearly observed without green background masking.

qs.q: Which mineral element is essential for the formation of hemoglobin in human red blood cells?
qs.e: Iron is an indispensable constituent of the heme group in hemoglobin, which binds oxygen for transport throughout the bloodstream. Deficiency of iron leads to nutritional anemia. Magnesium is essential for chlorophyll, calcium for bone/teeth, and iodine for thyroid hormones.

qs.q: Which region of the human alimentary canal provides an acidic environment with a pH of about 1.5 to 2.0 for the action of pepsin?
qs.e: Gastric juice produced by parietal cells in the stomach wall contains hydrochloric acid (HCl), lowering the pH to 1.5-2.0. This low pH activates pepsinogen into pepsin and creates the optimal acidic condition for protein hydrolysis.

qs.q: In a woody stem of an oil palm tree or dicot tree, which tissue is primarily responsible for conducting water and dissolved mineral salts upward from roots?
qs.e: Xylem vessels and tracheids form hollow, lignified tubes that conduct water and dissolved mineral ions upwards from the roots to the rest of the plant via transpiration pull and root pressure. Phloem transports organic solutes, cambium causes secondary growth, and cortex stores food.

qs.q: Which mammalian blood vessel carries deoxygenated blood away from the right ventricle of the heart directly to the lungs?
qs.e: The pulmonary artery originates from the right ventricle and carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs for gaseous exchange. The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood back to the left atrium, while the aorta delivers oxygenated blood to systemic tissues.

qs.q: In the human circulatory system, which blood components are non-nucleated fragments responsible for blood clotting at injury sites?
qs.e: Platelets (thrombocytes) are membrane-bound cell fragments derived from megakaryocytes in the bone marrow. They release thromboplastin to initiate the blood clotting cascade at damaged blood vessels.

qs.q: Which organ of the mammalian respiratory system contains C-shaped rings of cartilage that prevent its collapse during inhalation?
qs.e: The trachea (windpipe) is reinforced with incomplete C-shaped rings of hyaline cartilage. These rings maintain airway patency despite negative intrapulmonary pressure generated during deep inspiration.

qs.q: Which nitrogenous waste product is predominantly excreted by freshwater fish such as tilapia?
qs.e: Freshwater fish like tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) excrete nitrogenous waste mainly as highly toxic, soluble ammonia across their gill membranes into the surrounding abundant water. Land mammals convert ammonia to urea, while birds/reptiles excrete uric acid.

qs.q: The growth response of a maize seedling root bending downward in response to gravity is termed
qs.e: Positive geotropism (or gravitropism) is the directional growth of plant organs toward the stimulus of gravity. Roots show positive geotropism (grow downward), ensuring anchorage and water absorption, whereas shoots display negative geotropism.

qs.q: The transfer of pollen grains from the anther of a hibiscus flower to the mature stigma of another flower on a different plant of the same species is known as
qs.e: Cross-pollination (xenogamy) involves pollen transfer from the anther of one plant to the stigma of a flower on a different individual of the same species, increasing genetic variation.

qs.q: In human reproduction, where does fertilization of the ovum by a sperm cell normally occur?
qs.e: Fertilization normally occurs in the ampulla region of the oviduct (Fallopian tube). The fertilized egg (zygote) then undergoes cleavage as it travels to implant into the endometrial lining of the uterus.

qs.q: If a homozygous tall pea plant (TT) is crossed with a homozygous dwarf pea plant (tt), what percentage of the F1 generation will exhibit the tall phenotype?
qs.e: A cross between TT and tt produces 100% heterozygous (Tt) offspring in the F1 generation. Since the tall allele (T) is completely dominant over the dwarf allele (t), all F1 plants express the tall phenotype.

qs.q: Which human characteristic exhibits continuous variation within a population?
qs.e: Human height is a polygenic trait influenced by multiple genes and environmental factors, displaying a continuous spectrum of quantitative variations (bell-shaped normal distribution curve). Blood groups and tongue rolling show discontinuous variation.

qs.q: The rapid withdrawal of a hand after accidentally touching a hot cooking pot is controlled directly by a pathway known as a
qs.e: A reflex arc is an involuntary, rapid neural pathway consisting of receptor, sensory neuron, relay neuron in the spinal cord, motor neuron, and effector organ, acting without immediate conscious brain intervention to protect against injury.

qs.q: Which endocrine gland secretes insulin to reduce blood glucose levels after a meal rich in carbohydrates?
qs.e: Beta cells of the Islets of Langerhans in the pancreas secrete insulin when blood sugar levels rise. Insulin facilitates glucose uptake into somatic cells and stimulates glycogen synthesis in the liver and muscles.

qs.q: Which structure of the human ear converts sound vibrations in the endolymph into nerve impulses via sensory hair cells?
qs.e: The Organ of Corti, located within the cochlea of the inner ear, contains mechanoreceptive hair cells that bend in response to fluid waves in the endolymph, generating action potentials along the auditory nerve.

qs.q: Which tissue connects skeletal muscles to bones in the mammalian musculoskeletal system?
qs.e: Tendons are tough, non-elastic fibrous connective tissues that attach skeletal muscles to bones, transmitting tensile muscle force to produce movement. Ligaments connect bone to bone across joints.

qs.q: An ecological study measuring the total dry weight of living organic matter per unit area in a rainforest ecosystem is quantifying its
qs.e: Biomass is the total dry mass of living biological organisms present in a given area or ecosystem at a specific time. It represents stored chemical energy available to higher trophic levels.

qs.q: The accumulation of non-biodegradable pesticide synthetic chemicals like DDT in increasing concentrations at higher trophic levels of a food chain is termed
qs.e: Biomagnification (or bioaccumulation) occurs when persistent, lipophilic pollutants increase in concentration sequentially up the food chain, reaching toxic levels in top predators.

qs.q: The establishment of game reserves like Kainji Lake National Park in Nigeria aims primarily at
o: In-situ conservation of biodiversity and wildlife habitats
Ex-situ breeding of endangered exotic species
qs.e: National parks and game reserves represent in-situ conservation, protecting wild organisms within their natural habitats and preserving intact ecosystems from human destruction and poaching.

qs.q: Succulent stems and reduced leaf spines in desert cacti (*Opuntia*) are structural adaptations for
qs.e: Desert xerophytes possess succulent stems to store water and leaves reduced to spines to drastically reduce surface area for transpiration and deter herbivores, conserving water in arid environments.

qs.q: In a savannah food web comprising spear grass -> locust -> agama lizard -> African harrier hawk, which organism represents the secondary consumer?
qs.e: In this linear pathway, spear grass is the primary producer (trophic level 1), locust is the primary consumer/herbivore (trophic level 2), agama lizard is the secondary consumer/carnivore (trophic level 3), and African harrier hawk is the tertiary consumer (trophic level 4).

qs.q: Which micro-organism plays a vital role in nitrogen fixation by converting atmospheric nitrogen gas into ammonium compounds inside root nodules of leguminous plants like cowpea?
qs.e: Rhizobium bacteria live symbiotically in the root nodules of legumes (e.g. cowpea Vigna unguiculata). They synthesize nitrogenase enzymes to convert atmospheric N2 into ammonia for plant growth. Nitrosomonas oxidizes ammonia to nitrites, Nitrobacter oxidizes nitrites to nitrates.

qs.q: What is the main function of red blood cells (erythrocytes) in human blood?
o: Transporting oxygen from lungs to systemic tissues
qs.e: Red blood cells contain high concentrations of hemoglobin, a specialized iron-containing protein designed to reversibly bind oxygen in the lungs and release it to oxygen-demanding somatic tissues.

qs.q: Which organ of the human digestive system synthesizes bile juice?
qs.e: Bile is continuously synthesized by hepatocytes in the liver and stored/concentrated in the gallbladder before release into the duodenum to emulsify fats.

qs.q: The process by which plants release excess water vapour through stomata into the atmosphere is called
qs.e: Transpiration is the evaporation of water from the aerial surfaces of plants, predominantly through stomatal pores on leaves, generating transpirational pull for sap ascent.

qs.q: Which chamber of the human heart possesses the thickest muscular wall?
qs.e: The left ventricle has the thickest myocardium because it must generate high systemic blood pressure to pump oxygenated blood throughout the entire body against systemic vascular resistance.

qs.q: During anaerobic respiration in human skeletal muscle during intense exercise, pyruvate is converted into
qs.e: When oxygen supply is insufficient during strenuous muscular activity, glycolysis continues by converting pyruvate into lactic acid using lactate dehydrogenase to regenerate NAD+ for glycolysis.

qs.q: Which functional unit of the human kidney filters blood plasma to initiate urine formation?
qs.e: The nephron is the structural and microscopic functional unit of the kidney responsible for ultrafiltration of blood plasma, selective reabsorption, and secretion.

qs.q: Vegetative propagation of cassava (*Manihot esculenta*) is routinely achieved by planting stem
qs.e: Cassava is commercially propagated asexualy using hardwood stem cuttings (stakes) inserted into soil, which sprout adventitious roots and shoots.

qs.q: Which part of the human brain regulates heart rate, blood pressure, and respiratory movements?
qs.e: The medulla oblongata located in the hindbrain contains vital autonomic cardiovascular and respiratory reflex centers that regulate heart rate, vasomotor tone, and involuntary breathing rhythms.

qs.q: A person suffering from night blindness lacks sufficient quantities of which vitamin in their diet?
qs.e: Vitamin A (retinol) is essential for synthesizing rhodopsin (visual purple) in retinal rod cells. Deficiency impairs vision under dim light conditions, causing nyctalopia (night blindness).

qs.q: Which feature is characteristic of wind-pollinated (anemophilous) flowers like maize?
o: Feathery stigmas hanging outside the flower
qs.e: Wind-pollinated flowers have light, smooth pollen grains, feathery stigmas exposed to air currents to catch floating pollen, and reduced non-showy petals without nectar or scents.

qs.q: A plant leaf is destarched by keeping the plant in dark for 48 hours. Why is destarching necessary before conducting photosynthesis light experiments?
o: To destroy all chlorophyll inside chloroplasts
To ensure any starch detected after the experiment was synthesized during the light exposure period
To prevent transpirational water loss during testing
To convert starch stored in roots back into sucrose
qs.e: Destarching ensures that any starch present prior to the experiment is fully utilized in cellular respiration or translocated out of the leaf, proving that starch found afterwards was freshly synthesized during the experimental treatment.

qs.q: If a red blood cell with an internal osmolarity equivalent to 0.9% NaCl solution is placed in a test tube containing 3.0% NaCl solution, what structural change will be observed?
o: Cell loses water by osmosis and becomes crenated
Cell absorbs salt ions by active transport
Cell remains unchanged in size and shape
qs.e: A 3.0% NaCl solution is hypertonic relative to the cytoplasm (0.9% NaCl). Water leaves the cell by osmosis down a water potential gradient, causing the red blood cell to shrink and wrinkle (crenation).

qs.q: In a potometer experiment set up to measure transpiration rate in a mango branch, the air bubble moves 40 mm in 10 minutes under quiet laboratory conditions. When an electric fan is turned on, the bubble moves 40 mm in 4 minutes. What is the ratio of transpiration rate with fan to that without fan?
qs.e: Initial rate = 40 mm / 10 min = 4 mm/min. With fan = 40 mm / 4 min = 10 mm/min. The ratio (fan : no fan) = 10 : 4 = 2.5 : 1. Increased wind speed removes the humid boundary layer around stomata, accelerating transpiration.

qs.q: A student sets up two germinating pea seeds in sealed respirometer flasks containing equal volumes of potassium hydroxide (KOH) solution. Flask A is placed at 15 C and Flask B at 35 C. After 30 minutes, liquid moves further up the manometer tube in Flask B. What biological explanation accounts for this difference?
o: KOH absorbs more carbon dioxide at 15 C than at 35 C
Higher temperature increases enzyme activity and cellular respiration rate, consuming oxygen faster
Seeds at 35 C undergo anaerobic respiration releasing extra gas
Higher temperature causes seeds to absorb liquid directly
qs.e: KOH absorbs CO2 produced by respiration. Net volume reduction in the flask equals O2 consumed by germinating seeds. Respiratory enzyme activity is higher at 35 C (closer to optimum) than 15 C, resulting in faster O2 uptake and greater manometer liquid movement.

qs.q: During human digestion, what would happen to protein breakdown if the duct from the pancreas to the duodenum becomes completely blocked by a gallstone?
o: Protein digestion in stomach ceases completely
Trypsinogen and chymotrypsinogen cannot reach the duodenum, severely impairing intestinal protein digestion
Pepsin activity in the duodenum doubles to compensate
Salivary amylase hydrolyzes proteins into peptides
qs.e: Pancreatic juice contains essential zymogens (trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen, procarboxypeptidase) that digest proteins in the alkaline small intestine. Duct obstruction prevents pancreatic secretions from reaching the duodenum.

qs.q: In pea plants, round seed shape (R) is dominant over wrinkled seed shape (r). If a heterozygous round-seeded plant (Rr) is self-pollinated, what proportion of the round-seeded progeny is expected to be homozygous dominant?
qs.e: Crossing Rr x Rr yields genotype ratio 1 RR : 2 Rr : 1 rr. Among the round-seeded progeny (RR and Rr, making 3 parts total), 1 out of 3 is RR (homozygous dominant). Therefore, 1/3 or approximately 33.3% of round-seeded plants are homozygous dominant.

qs.q: Which structural feature allows the mudskipper (*Periophthalmus*), an amphibious fish of Nigerian mangrove swamps, to survive out of water for extended periods?
o: Highly developed pulmonary alveoli inside lungs
Vascularized gill chambers that retain water and cutaneous respiration through moist skin
Thick horny scales preventing gaseous exchange
Air sacs inside hollow limb bones
qs.e: Mudskippers store water in enlarged opercular cavities to keep their gills moist while on land and use their richly vascularized skin and buccal cavity lining for cutaneous gaseous exchange.

qs.q: Why does double fertilization in angiosperms result in the formation of a diploid zygote and a triploid endosperm nucleus?
o: One male gamete fuses with egg cell (n+n) and another male gamete fuses with two polar nuclei (n+n+n)
Two male gametes fuse with one egg cell while the polar nucleus vanishes
One male gamete fertilizes the synergids while another fertilizes antipodals
The antipodal cells double their chromosome count before fusion
qs.e: Double fertilization involves two pollen nuclei: one sperm nucleus (n) fuses with the egg nucleus (n) to form a diploid zygote (2n), while the second sperm nucleus (n) fuses with the diploid central cell polar nuclei (2n) to produce a triploid endosperm (3n).

qs.q: Which row correctly matches the excretory organ with the corresponding animal group?
o: Flatworm -> Nephridium; Earthworm -> Flame cell; Insect -> Malpighian tubule
Flatworm -> Flame cell; Earthworm -> Nephridium; Insect -> Malpighian tubule
Flatworm -> Malpighian tubule; Earthworm -> Flame cell; Insect -> Nephridium
Flatworm -> Kidney; Earthworm -> Malpighian tubule; Insect -> Flame cell
qs.e: Flatworms (Planaria) use specialized protonephridia with flame cells, earthworms (annelids) possess metanephridia in each segment, and terrestrial insects utilize Malpighian tubules connected to the gut.

qs.q: A student measures the population density of spear grass (*Imperata cylindrica*) in a school field using a 1 m x 1 m quadrat frame thrown 10 times at random. The plant counts per quadrat were: 4, 6, 3, 5, 8, 2, 5, 7, 4, 6. What is the estimated total population in a field area of 500 square metres?
qs.e: Total count in 10 quadrats (10 m²) = 4+6+3+5+8+2+5+7+4+6 = 50 plants. Mean density = 50 / 10 = 5 plants per m². For a 500 m² field, estimated total population = 5 plants/m² x 500 m² = 2,500 plants.

qs.q: What happens to the focal length of the human eye lens when looking at a close object like a book, and which muscle contracts to cause this change?
o: Focal length increases; ciliary muscle relaxes
Focal length decreases; ciliary muscle contracts
Focal length increases; radial iris muscle contracts
Focal length remains unchanged; suspensory ligaments tighten
qs.e: During accommodation for near vision, ciliary muscles contract, releasing tension on suspensory ligaments. The lens becomes thicker and more spherical, decreasing its focal length to focus light sharply on the retina.

qs.q: Which sequence correctly traces the pathway of reflex impulse transmission during a knee-jerk response?
o: Effector -> Motor neuron -> Spinal cord -> Sensory neuron -> Receptor
Receptor -> Sensory neuron -> Spinal cord -> Motor neuron -> Effector
Receptor -> Motor neuron -> Brain -> Sensory neuron -> Effector
Brain -> Sensory neuron -> Spinal cord -> Motor neuron -> Effector
qs.e: The reflex arc pathway starts at the sensory receptor (patellar tendon stretch sensor), passes along sensory neuron to spinal cord, synapses with motor neuron, and travels to effector (quadriceps muscle) causing contraction.

qs.q: Why is the pulmonary vein unique compared to most other veins in the human body?
o: It has thick muscular walls and lacks internal valves
It carries oxygenated blood under low pressure from lungs to the left atrium
It carries deoxygenated blood from systemic tissues to the right atrium
It contains high levels of urea and metabolic wastes
qs.e: Unlike systemic veins which carry deoxygenated blood, pulmonary veins transport oxygen-rich blood freshly oxygenated in the alveoli back into the left atrium of the heart.

qs.q: In an ecosystem, energy flow differs fundamentally from nutrient cycling because energy
o: Is continuously recycled within food webs
Flows unidirectionally and is lost progressively as metabolic heat
Increases in total amount at higher trophic levels
Is stored indefinitely in top carnivore biomass
qs.e: Energy enters ecosystems as sunlight, moves unidirectionally through trophic levels with ~90% loss as heat at each transfer (Second Law of Thermodynamics), whereas nutrient elements (C, N, P) recycle continuously.

qs.q: Which adaptive feature enables oil palm seeds (*Elaeis guineensis*) to survive long periods before germination?
o: Thin permeable seed coat allowing rapid water uptake
Thick woody endocarp and low moisture content maintaining dormancy
Presence of fleshy aril that attracts frugivorous birds
High concentration of active gibberellins in endosperm
qs.e: The oil palm nut features a hard, thick sclerified endocarp (shell) surrounding the seed, maintaining physical dormancy until moisture, heat, or scarification breaks the coat.

qs.q: The diagram illustrates a generalized animal cell. Which lettered organelle controls cellular metabolism, growth, and hereditary transmission?
qs.e: Organelle A represents the cell nucleus, which encloses genomic DNA organized into chromosomes and coordinates cellular metabolic activities, gene expression, and inheritance. B represents a mitochondrion, C a lysosome/vacuole, and D the plasma membrane.
