qs.q: When a government reorganizes state enterprises to run strictly as profit-oriented, self-sustaining businesses while retaining full government ownership, the policy executed is
qs.e: Commercialization transforms state enterprises to operate on commercial business principles without transferring equity to private buyers, unlike privatization.

qs.q: The African Union (AU) replaced the Organization of African Unity (OAU) in 2002 primarily to shift focus from anti-colonial liberation to
o: economic integration, good governance, and conflict management across Africa
establishing a single socialist continental political party
forming a permanent joint African standing army against Europe
dissolving national borders across all member states
qs.e: The AU was established at Durban in 2002 (following the 1999 Sirte Declaration) to move beyond OAU's anti-colonial mandate toward deeper economic integration, democracy, and peacekeeping.

qs.q: Which major political party led by Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe formed a national coalition government with the Northern People's Congress (NPC) following the 1959 federal elections?
o: National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons (NCNC)
qs.e: After the 1959 pre-independence elections, the NPC (led by Ahmadu Bello/Tafawa Balewa) and the NCNC (led by Azikiwe) formed a coalition government, making Balewa Prime Minister and Azikiwe Senate President/Governor-General.

qs.q: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, the revenue allocation principle that mandates a percentage of natural resource revenues be returned directly to the states of origin is the
qs.e: Section 162(2) of the 1999 Constitution mandates that at least 13% of revenue derived from natural resources must be allocated to producing states based on the derivation principle.

qs.q: In political theory, A.V. Dicey's third posture of the Rule of Law emphasizes that constitutional law is not the source but the consequence of the rights of individuals as defined and enforced by the courts. This principle is best embodied in the common law tradition through
o: judicial decisions protecting fundamental rights in concrete legal disputes
executive emergency proclamations signed by the monarch
codified statutes passed by a revolutionary constituent assembly
statutory instruments promulgated by administrative boards
qs.e: Dicey argued that in Britain, individual liberties grew out of judicial precedent and court decisions in actual disputes, making rights the foundation rather than a gift of written constitutional codes.

qs.q: The 1951 Macpherson Constitution was structurally unstable because while it created central ministers, it failed to give them full departmental ministerial responsibility, leading to severe conflict between central ministers and regional political leaders known as the
o: Western regional state of emergency of 1962
qs.e: Under the 1951 Macpherson Constitution, ministers lacked executive authority over portfolios. In 1953, NCNC central ministers refused to resign when requested by the party, triggering the Eastern regional constitutional crisis.

qs.q: In a presidential federal state, when the Supreme Court invokes the 'doctrine of covering the field', it invalidates state legislation on a concurrent matter because
o: federal legislation on that subject matter is comprehensive and demonstrates federal intent to regulate the entire area
the state governor failed to sign the bill before publication
the state assembly lacked a simple quorum during debate
the subject matter is explicitly listed on the Residual List
qs.e: The doctrine of covering the field holds that where the federal parliament has enacted a complete and exhaustive law on a concurrent subject, any state law on the same subject—even if consistent—is superseded.

qs.q: The 1988 Civil Service Reform in Nigeria abolished the post of Head of Service and made Permanent Secretaries political appointees who retired with the administration that appointed them. The 1997 Ayida Panel subsequently recommended
o: reinstating the Head of Service and restoring career tenure to Permanent Secretaries
privatizing all administrative ministries into state corporations
transferring civil service recruitment directly to state governors
abolishing the Civil Service Commission entirely
qs.e: The Allison Ayida Panel (1994-1997) reviewed the civil service and recommended reversing the politicization introduced in 1988, reinstating the Head of Service and career tenure for Permanent Secretaries.

qs.q: The UN Security Council's decision-making structure incorporates the 'veto power' held by its five permanent members (P5). Under Article 27(3) of the UN Charter, a negative vote by any P5 member on a substantive matter results in
o: the immediate defeat of the resolution regardless of majority support
transferring the vote to the International Court of Justice
requiring a simple two-thirds vote in the General Assembly to override
suspending the offending permanent member from the council
qs.e: Under Article 27(3) of the UN Charter, decisions on substantive matters require nine affirmative votes including the concurring votes of all permanent members. A single P5 negative vote vetoes the resolution.

qs.q: Which type of government is headed by a monarch whose powers are limited by a written or unwritten constitution?
qs.e: A constitutional monarchy is a system where a king or queen acts as Head of State within the parameters of a constitution, unlike an absolute monarchy where the ruler exercises unrestrained authority.

qs.q: The economic and political system in which private individuals and corporations own capital goods and control property is called
qs.e: Capitalism is characterized by private ownership, competitive markets, profit motive, and minimal direct state ownership of production.

qs.q: A constitution that is contained within a single formal legal document is described as
qs.e: A written constitution consolidates the fundamental laws and governing principles of a state into a single formal codified text.

qs.q: In a presidential system of government, the Head of State and Head of Government are combined in the person of the
qs.e: Unlike a parliamentary system where the ceremonial Head of State and executive Head of Government are separate, the presidential system combines both roles in the President.

qs.q: The organ of government responsible for interpreting laws and administering justice is the
qs.e: The judiciary interprets statutes, applies legal principles, resolves legal disputes between parties, and protects constitutional rights.

qs.q: The basic political right granted to citizens to vote in democratic elections is referred to as the
qs.e: Franchise (or suffrage) is the constitutional or statutory right of qualified citizens to participate in voting during public elections.

qs.q: In Nigeria, the public institution established to investigate complaints of administrative injustice and corruption against public officers is the
qs.e: The Public Complaints Commission acts as Nigeria's administrative ombudsman, investigating citizen grievances regarding unfair treatment by government agencies.

qs.q: Political ideology that advocates gradual democratic reforms to achieve equitable wealth distribution while retaining democratic political institutions is
qs.e: Democratic socialism seeks social welfare and wealth redistribution through constitutional, parliamentary means rather than violent revolution.

qs.q: When legislative powers are concentrated in a single national parliament while sub-national units derive their limited powers entirely from the center, the state is
qs.e: In a unitary system, sovereignty resides exclusively in the central authority; local or regional governments exist at the central government's discretion.

qs.q: Under the principle of checks and balances, the President can check the power of the legislature by exercising the power to
qs.e: A presidential veto allows the chief executive to refuse signature on a bill passed by parliament, forcing the legislature to reconsider or secure an extraordinary majority.

qs.q: The bicameral legislature at the federal level in Nigeria consists of the
o: House of Chiefs and House of Commons
qs.e: Under Section 4 of the 1999 Constitution, the federal legislative arm is the National Assembly, comprising the Senate and the House of Representatives.

qs.q: The administrative doctrine that civil servants must not participate publicly in political party electioneering is known as civil service
qs.e: Civil service neutrality demands that career bureaucrats remain non-partisan so they can serve whichever political party wins executive power.

qs.q: Pressure groups that promote broad societal causes or ethical ideals rather than defending the economic self-interest of their members are classified as
qs.e: Cause (or promotional) groups campaign for issues benefiting society as a whole (e.g. human rights, environmental protection), unlike sectional interest groups.

qs.q: The Lyttelton Constitution of 1954 was historic in Nigerian political development because it formally introduced
qs.e: The 1954 Lyttelton Constitution officially established Nigeria as a federation, creating division of powers between central and regional governments.

qs.q: Which major political party formed the official opposition in the Western Regional House of Assembly following the 1951 elections?
o: National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons (NCNC)
qs.e: In the West, Obafemi Awolowo's Action Group formed the regional government after the 1951 election, while Nnamdi Azikiwe's NCNC became the main opposition.

qs.q: In a federal state, subjects listed on the Exclusive Legislative List are reserved solely for legislation by the
qs.e: The Exclusive Legislative List contains matters of national importance (defence, foreign affairs, currency) over which only the federal parliament can make laws.

qs.q: A legal resident alien can acquire citizenship of Nigeria after satisfying long residency, good character, and language requirements through
qs.e: Section 27 of the 1999 Constitution lays out the requirements for foreign nationals to acquire Nigerian citizenship through naturalization.

qs.q: Which international peacekeeping operation marked Nigeria's first major United Nations peacekeeping deployment shortly after independence in 1960?
o: United Nations Operation in the Congo (ONUC)
qs.e: Nigeria deployed troops to the Congo under ONUC in 1960, establishing its reputation as a major peacekeeper in international affairs.

qs.q: The Organization of African Unity (OAU) was founded in May 1963 in which African capital city?
qs.e: 32 independent African states signed the OAU Charter on May 25, 1963, in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

qs.q: In political theory, Fascism is characterized by extreme nationalism, totalitarian state control, and the subordination of individual rights to the state under a
qs.e: Fascism relies on authoritarian autocracy led by a dictator who suppresses political opposition and subordinating society to state power.

qs.q: A core limitation of A.V. Dicey's concept of equality before the law in modern democratic governance is the existence of
o: diplomatic immunity and executive immunity for sitting heads of state
universal adult suffrage in national elections
independent judicial review by apex courts
public trial requirements in criminal matters
qs.e: Diplomatic immunity and executive immunity (such as Section 308 of Nigeria's Constitution) shield specific officials from prosecution, modifying strict equality before the law.

qs.q: In a parliamentary cabinet system, the concept of 'fusion of powers' means that members of the executive branch are simultaneously
o: appointed life judges in the Supreme Court
career civil servants in government ministries
qs.e: In parliamentary systems, the Prime Minister and cabinet ministers are drawn directly from and remain accountable members of the legislature.

qs.q: The stage during a bill's progress in parliament where lawmakers debate the broad underlying principles and purpose of the proposed statute is the
qs.e: At the first reading the bill title is introduced; at the second reading, the general principles, policy aims, and merits of the bill are debated by the full house.

qs.q: The prerogative power of the executive president to commute or pardon a convicted person's criminal sentence is termed the
qs.e: Under Section 175 of the 1999 Constitution, the President exercises the prerogative of mercy to grant pardons or commute sentences upon advisory counsel.

qs.q: The 1960 Independence Constitution of Nigeria retained the British monarch as ceremonial Head of State, represented locally by the
qs.e: Between 1960 and 1963, Nigeria was a constitutional monarchy under Queen Elizabeth II, represented in Lagos by Governor-General Nnamdi Azikiwe.

qs.q: Which major political party in Northern Nigeria was formed in 1950 by Mallam Aminu Kano to champion the rights of the common people (Talakawa)?
qs.e: NEPU was founded in August 1950 by radical reformers led by Aminu Kano to challenge feudal oppression and advocate for the Talakawa in the North.

qs.q: An electoral reform introduced in Nigeria by the Electoral Act 2022 to eliminate ballot stuffing and voter impersonation is the mandatory deployment of the
o: Option A4 open ballot voting system
qs.e: The Electoral Act 2022 legalized the BVAS technology for electronic voter accreditation (facial/fingerprint verification) and live election result upload.

qs.q: The administrative body responsible for the recruitment, promotion, and discipline of federal civil servants in Nigeria is the
qs.e: The Federal Civil Service Commission is the statutory executive body tasked with recruiting, promoting, and disciplining civil servants in federal ministries.

qs.q: Which revenue allocation formula conflict frequently arises between oil-producing states and the federal government in Nigerian federalism?
o: percentage share assigned to the derivation principle versus national interest pool
funding allocations to the armed forces versus police
customs duties collected at maritime ports versus border posts
distribution of value added tax between local councils
qs.e: The tension centers on how much revenue derived from mineral resources should go directly to producing states via derivation versus the central distributive pool.

qs.q: Local government councils generate internal revenue primarily through
o: tenement rates, market stall fees, and licensing charges
petroleum profit taxes and mining royalties
corporate income taxes on multinational firms
qs.e: Local councils rely internally on property/tenement rates, market fees, motor park fees, and local licensing fees, as major taxes belong to federal/state tiers.

qs.q: The fundamental rights enshrined in Chapter IV of the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria can be suspended during a state of emergency proclaimed under Section
qs.e: Section 305 of the 1999 Constitution empowers the President to issue a proclamation of a state of emergency, which permits temporary restriction of certain rights.

qs.q: The primary military peacekeeping force established by ECOWAS in 1990 to intervene in the Liberian civil war was named
qs.e: The Economic Community of West African States Monitoring Group (ECOMOG) was created in August 1990 as a regional peacekeeping armed force led by Nigeria.

qs.q: When a military government comes to power via a coup d'etat, it typically suspends parliament and rules by issuing executive
o: decrees at federal level and edicts at state level
acts of parliament and statutory instruments
judicial orders and writs of certiorari
qs.e: Military governments suspend constitutional lawmaking structures and enact laws directly as Decrees (central military government) and Edicts (state military governors).

qs.q: In local government administration, the State Joint Local Government Account (SJLGA) established under Section 162(6) of the 1999 Constitution was criticized because it allowed states to
o: deduct or divert funds meant for local government councils
transfer local funds directly to foreign development banks
abolish local government council elections nationwide
increase local council tax rates without approval
qs.e: State governments frequently manipulated the SJLGA to withhold or divert federal allocations intended for local councils, undermining local financial autonomy until recent judicial rulings.

qs.q: In comparative political analysis, 'de facto' authority differs from 'de jure' authority because de facto authority rests on
o: actual physical possession and exercise of power regardless of legal right
strict compliance with established constitutional provisions
hereditary succession sanctioned by traditional custom
electoral mandate ratified by an independent electoral commission
qs.e: De facto authority exists in fact and exercise of power (e.g. military junta after a successful coup), whereas de jure authority exists by legal right under the constitution.

qs.q: Which landmark judicial doctrine obliges lower courts to follow legal principles established by higher courts in earlier similar cases?
qs.e: Stare decisis (judicial precedent) ensures legal consistency by binding lower courts to follow prior decisions made by superior courts on similar legal questions.

qs.q: The 1979 Constitution of Nigeria marked a major constitutional departure because it abandoned the British parliamentary model and adopted the
qs.e: The 1979 Constitution replaced the Westminster parliamentary system with an executive presidential system modeled on the United States.

qs.q: Proportional representation electoral systems encourage multi-party parliamentary systems because legislative seats are allocated based on
o: the percentage of total national or district votes each party receives
who wins the majority in single-member geographic constituencies
the age and seniority of individual candidates on the ballot
direct appointment by the executive head of state
qs.e: Proportional representation awards seats in proportion to total party vote share, allowing minor parties to secure representation without winning single-member majorities.

qs.q: In administrative law, delegated legislation can be declared 'ultra vires' by the judiciary if the executive rulemaking authority
o: exceeds the scope of power conferred by the parent statute
consults relevant interest groups prior to publication
publishes the regulation in the official government gazette
applies the rule uniformly across all administrative districts
qs.e: The doctrine of ultra vires renders administrative regulations null and void if the issuing authority acts beyond the explicit boundary set by the parent Act of Parliament.

qs.q: During the Second Republic (1979-1983), the political party led by Chief Obafemi Awolowo that implemented free primary education and free healthcare in Western states was the
qs.e: The UPN, led by Awolowo, made four cardinal programs—including free education and free health care—its defining policy platform in the Second Republic.

qs.q: Which diplomatic crisis prompted Nigeria to nationalize the assets of British Petroleum (BP) and Barclays Bank in 1979?
o: Britain's willingness to allow oil sales to white-minority ruled Rhodesia and South Africa
Britain's refusal to grant loans for the Ajaokuta steel complex
A territorial dispute over the Bakassi Peninsula
The expulsion of Nigerian diplomats from London
qs.e: In 1979, the Obasanjo military regime nationalized BP assets to pressure the UK government against supplying oil to apartheid South Africa and Rhodesia ahead of Zimbabwean independence.

qs.q: The principle of 'Federal Character' enshrined in Section 14(3) of the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria was designed to
o: ensure equitable representation of all states and ethnic groups in public appointments
guarantee federal military control over state police commands
eliminate all state government ministries in favor of federal agencies
enforce a single official language across all government offices
qs.e: Federal character aims to promote national unity and prevent domination by one ethnic group or state by ensuring balanced representation across federal institutions and agencies.

qs.q: In a parliamentary system, when the executive requests the monarch or Governor-General to dissolve parliament before its full term expires, the primary objective is usually to
o: seek a fresh mandate from the electorate at an advantageous political moment
avoid submitting the national budget to legislative scrutiny
prevent the opposition from forming a pressure group
suspend fundamental human rights during civil unrest
qs.e: Dissolution of parliament triggers a general election, allowing the governing party to capitalize on high popularity or resolve a parliamentary deadlock.

qs.q: The first military coup d'etat in Nigeria on January 15, 1966, resulted in the overthrow of the First Republic and the assassination of Prime Minister
qs.e: The Jan 15, 1966 coup led by Major Chukwuma Nzeogwu led to the deaths of Prime Minister Tafawa Balewa, Northern Premier Ahmadu Bello, and Western Premier Ladoke Akintola.

qs.q: Which major organ of the United Nations is responsible for maintaining international peace and security and possesses the power to authorize military action or sanctions?
qs.e: Under Chapter VII of the UN Charter, the UN Security Council is the primary organ empowered to impose binding sanctions or authorize military force to maintain global peace.

qs.q: In constitutional theory, Max Weber's classification of authority identifies three pure types of legitimate rule. The authority exercised by an elected president operating strictly within defined constitutional provisions is
qs.e: Legal-rational authority rests on belief in the legality of enacted rules and the right of those elevated to authority under such rules to issue commands.

qs.q: The 1953 Motion for Self-Government in 1956, moved in the House of Representatives by Chief Anthony Enahoro, caused a severe political breakdown because Northern delegates led by Sir Ahmadu Bello proposed replacing '1956' with
qs.e: Northern delegates, fearing Southern domination, substituted Enahoro's '1956' date with 'as soon as practicable', triggering walkouts, insults in Lagos, and the Kano riots of 1953.

qs.q: When a citizen files a writ of 'quo warranto' in a superior court, the applicant is asking the court to
o: inquire by what statutory authority a person is holding or exercising a public office
command a custodian to produce an illegally detained prisoner in court
transfer a civil lawsuit from a state court to a federal tribunal
restrain an inferior administrative panel from exceeding its jurisdiction
qs.e: Quo warranto ('by what warrant?') challenges an individual's legal right to hold or exercise a public office, franchise, or position of state authority.

qs.q: In July 2024, the Supreme Court of Nigeria delivered a landmark constitutional judgment regarding local government autonomy, declaring that
o: federal allocations must be paid directly to democratically elected local government councils, bypassing state accounts
state governors possess absolute constitutional authority to dissolve elected local councils at will
local government areas are administrative departments of state ministries without financial standing
the National Assembly lacks legislative power to create or regulate local council revenue
qs.e: In July 2024, the Supreme Court ruled that state governments cannot withhold or manage funds meant for local councils and ordered direct payment from the federation account to elected councils.

qs.q: Which basic concept of government describes a community of people bound by common historical, cultural, or linguistic heritage living in a defined territory?
qs.e: A nation is primarily a socio-cultural entity defined by shared culture, language, or heritage, whereas a state is a legal political entity with political sovereignty.

qs.q: An economic system where the state owns and operates all major industries and centrally plans economic production is called
qs.e: Socialism relies on public/state ownership of basic means of production and central planning, contrasting with capitalist market systems.

qs.q: The fundamental legal document that establishes the structure, functions, and limitations of government organs is the
qs.e: A constitution is the supreme law of a nation that defines the framework of government and sets out individual rights and duties.

qs.q: A legislative body that consists of two distinct lawmaking chambers is described as
qs.e: A bicameral legislature features two chambers (e.g., Senate and House of Representatives), while a unicameral legislature has only one.

qs.q: In a democracy, the judicial principle that protects individuals from unlawful or arbitrary arrest and detention is the writ of
qs.e: Habeas corpus ('bring the body') requires law enforcement to present a detained person before a court to determine the legality of their detention.

qs.q: Which tier of government in Nigeria is presided over by an executive Chairman and an elected Legislative Council?
qs.e: Local government councils are headed by executive Chairmen working alongside elected ward councillors.

qs.q: The specialized agency of the United Nations responsible for global public health promotion and disease control is the
qs.e: WHO is the UN agency dedicated to international public health, epidemic response, and medical standards.

qs.q: The informal process through which individuals absorb political beliefs, values, and civic behaviors from family, peers, and schools is called political
qs.e: Political socialization is the lifelong learning process whereby citizens internalize political orientation and civic values.

qs.q: A constitutional system where the head of state is a non-hereditary president elected directly or indirectly by citizens is a
qs.e: A republic is a state without a hereditary monarch, where supreme power resides in the people and elected representatives.

qs.q: The doctrine of Rule of Law requires that government action must be guided by clear statutory laws rather than arbitrary executive discretion, promoting the
o: supremacy of law over official discretion
immunity of civil servants from civil trial
dominance of military decrees over statutes
qs.e: Supremacy of law means no executive officer can act arbitrarily; all state actions must be grounded in valid, pre-existing legal statutes.

qs.q: In a cabinet system of government, the titular Head of State performs primarily ceremonial duties, while real executive power is exercised by the
qs.e: In a parliamentary system (e.g. Britain or Nigeria 1960-1966), the Prime Minister leads the executive cabinet and holds real political authority.

qs.q: Which pre-independence Nigerian constitution introduced regional houses of assembly in the North, West, and East for the first time?
qs.e: The 1946 Richards Constitution created regional councils/assemblies for Northern, Western, and Eastern regions, laying the groundwork for regionalism.

qs.q: An association of workers formed to defend and promote their economic interests through collective bargaining with employers is a
qs.e: Trade unions (e.g., NLC, TUC) are economic pressure groups representing employees to secure fair wages and safe working conditions.

qs.q: An electoral district that elects only one representative to parliament is referred to as a
qs.e: A single-member district returns a single candidate chosen under First-Past-The-Post or majority voting.

qs.q: The permanent administrative structure organized in a strict hierarchy with written rules, specialized functions, and merit recruitment is called
qs.e: Bureaucracy, as defined by Max Weber, is the formal administrative system characterizing civil service and public administration.

qs.q: Which body in Nigeria is constitutionally mandated to organize, conduct, and supervise presidential, gubernatorial, and legislative elections?
qs.e: INEC is the federal constitutional body responsible for national and state-level elections in Nigeria under Item 56 of the Exclusive List.

qs.q: Under Nigerian law, a foreigner who marries a Nigerian citizen can apply to acquire Nigerian citizenship through
qs.e: Section 26 of the 1999 Constitution permits foreign women married to Nigerian citizens to acquire Nigerian citizenship by registration.

qs.q: The diplomatic stance where a nation avoids binding military treaties with major power blocs during global conflicts is termed
qs.e: Non-alignment allows developing nations to maintain sovereign decision-making without joining opposing military coalitions.

qs.q: The Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) was founded in September 1960 in Baghdad by five founding oil-producing nations. Nigeria joined OPEC in
qs.e: Nigeria became the 11th member of OPEC in July 1971 under the military administration of General Yakubu Gowon.

qs.q: When a charismatic leader rallies citizens behind an emotional cause outside established constitutional procedures, political authority relies on
qs.e: Charismatic authority stems from extraordinary personal devotion and heroism attributed to an individual leader rather than formal laws or traditional customs.

qs.q: In political theory, Anarchism is an extreme ideology that calls for the immediate abolition of
o: all formal state institutions and compulsory government laws
religious institutions and places of worship
qs.e: Anarchism opposes all forms of hierarchical state authority, arguing that humans can organize society cooperatively without government coercion.

qs.q: The 1963 Republican Constitution of Nigeria altered the executive structure by converting the office of Governor-General into a ceremonial
qs.e: The 1963 Constitution declared Nigeria a republic, replacing Queen Elizabeth II with a ceremonial President (Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe) as Head of State.

qs.q: The legislative privilege that protects lawmakers from civil prosecution or defamation charges for statements made on the floor of parliament is
qs.e: Parliamentary immunity (or privilege) allows lawmakers to debate controversial national issues freely without fear of legal prosecution or arrest for speeches made inside the chamber.

qs.q: When a superior court issues a writ of 'certiorari', it directs a lower court or administrative tribunal to
o: send the record of a trial or proceeding up to the superior court for judicial review
release a suspect immediately from police custody
perform a neglected statutory public duty
prohibit a party from leaving the judicial jurisdiction
qs.e: Certiorari is an extraordinary prerogative writ ordering a lower tribunal to transfer case records to a higher court so that errors of law or jurisdictional excesses can be corrected.

qs.q: Which prominent political party in the Second Republic was led by Mallam Aminu Kano and championed progressive populist policies in Kano and Kaduna states?
qs.e: The PRP, formed by Mallam Aminu Kano in 1978, carried forward NEPU's democratic socialist ideology, winning the governorships of Kano (Rimi) and Kaduna (Balarabe Musa).

qs.q: The technique used by pressure groups to directly persuade, brief, and supply research data to lawmakers during committee hearings is known as
qs.e: Lobbying involves interest group representatives interacting directly with legislators and bureaucrats to influence pending bills and administrative policies.

qs.q: An absolute majority electoral system requires a winning candidate to secure
o: more than 50 percent of the total valid votes cast
the highest number of votes even if below 40 percent
two-thirds of all registered voters in the country
a unanimous vote from legislative electors
qs.e: Absolute majority requires 50% + 1 of votes cast, often necessitating run-off elections if no candidate reaches that threshold in the first round.

qs.q: Public corporations in Nigeria differ from civil service government departments because public corporations are
o: created by specific statutes as autonomous corporate bodies with financial independence
directly staffed by military personnel without board directors
exempt from all federal taxes and judicial oversight
qs.e: Public corporations (e.g. NPA, FAAN) are established by specific enabling legislation as legal entities capable of suing and being sued and operating commercial services.

qs.q: Which administrative commission established in 1954 recommended separate civil service structures for the regional governments in Nigeria?
qs.e: The Gorsuch Commission of 1954 reviewed public service structures following the Lyttelton Constitution and established separate regional civil services.

qs.q: Under Nigerian federalism, items on the Concurrent Legislative List can be legislated upon by
o: both the National Assembly and State Houses of Assembly
only the Federal House of Representatives
only State Local Government Area Councils
the Supreme Court and Judicial Service Commission
qs.e: The Concurrent List contains subjects (such as higher education, electricity, and health) where both federal and state legislatures have authority to pass laws.

qs.q: The system of local government where traditional rulers retain executive council authority alongside nominated local elders is termed the
o: sole authority or traditional council system
qs.e: Before the 1976 reforms, several Northern and Western local administrations operated as traditional sole authorities dominated by emirs or chiefs.

qs.q: In foreign policy formulation, 'economic diplomacy' launched under General Ibrahim Babangida's regime by Foreign Minister Ike Nwachukwu aimed to
o: attract foreign direct investment and promote Nigerian export markets
isolate Nigeria from global financial institutions like the IMF
ban all foreign companies operating inside Nigeria
subsidize imports from neighboring West African states
qs.e: Economic diplomacy (late 1980s) restructured Nigerian foreign policy to prioritize trade expansion, investment attraction, and debt restructuring.

qs.q: The second military coup in Nigeria, executed on July 29, 1966, was triggered primarily by Northern officer discontent with Major-General Aguiyi-Ironsi's promulgation of
qs.e: Decree 34 abolished federalism and introduced a unitary system, raising fears of Southern domination and sparking the July 1966 counter-coup.

qs.q: Which organ of the United Nations is composed of all member states, operating on the principle of one nation, one vote?
qs.e: The UN General Assembly is the main deliberative body where every member nation has equal representation and single voting power.

qs.q: A core structural defect of the 1951 Macpherson Constitution was that regional party leaders chose to stay in regional assemblies while sending subordinate lieutenants to the central legislature, causing
o: central ministers to lack genuine party authority over regional premiers
the total abolition of regional executive councils
the immediate transition to a unitary state
the suspension of all judicial appointments
qs.e: Dominant party leaders (Awolowo in West, Bello in North) remained in regional assemblies, making regional governments politically stronger than the central government.

qs.q: In parliamentary practice, a 'filibuster' is a tactical maneuver employed by legislative minorities to
o: delay or block a vote on a bill by delivering exceptionally lengthy speeches
force the immediate dissolution of the cabinet by executive order
override a presidential veto without a quorum
expel opposition members from standing committees
qs.e: Filibustering uses prolonged debate and procedural delays to prevent a legislative body from reaching a final vote on a proposed measure.

qs.q: When a court applies the legal principle of 'locus standi' in a constitutional challenge, it evaluates whether the plaintiff possesses
o: a sufficient legal interest or direct injury to initiate the court action
the financial resources to pay judicial court fees
qs.e: Locus standi requires that a person demonstrating a constitutional grievance must show direct personal legal standing or harm resulting from the contested law or action.

qs.q: The concept of 'administrative discretion' grants civil servants leeway in interpreting and applying statutes, but it carries the risk of
o: bureaucratic arbitrariness and inconsistency in policy execution
qs.e: Administrative discretion allows flexibility, but without clear standards, officials may make subjective, inconsistent, or abusive enforcement decisions.

qs.q: Which major political alliance was formed in 1964 between the NCNC and Action Group to contest the 1964 federal elections against the Northern People's Congress alliance?
qs.e: UPGA was formed in 1964 by NCNC, AG, UMBC, and NEPU to challenge the NNA (NPC and Akintola's NNDP) in the controversial 1964 federal election.

qs.q: The 1978 Land Use Act in Nigeria nationalized land ownership by vesting all urban land within a state in the governor in trust for the people. This reform aimed to
o: facilitate government land acquisition for public infrastructure and curb land speculation
transfer rural farmlands exclusively to foreign agribusinesses
abolish all state ministry of lands departments
qs.e: Promulgated under General Obasanjo, the Land Use Act sought to simplify public land access for developmental projects and standardize land tenure.

qs.q: A major criticism leveled against the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria regarding its federal structure is that it
o: over-concentrates legislative items and revenue resources in the federal center
gives state governors full command over the armed forces
abolishes the Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction
prohibits state legislatures from passing taxation statutes
qs.e: Critics argue that having 68 items on the Exclusive List leaves states financially dependent on federal revenue allocations, weakening true federalism.

qs.q: The Technical Aid Corps (TAC) scheme was established by Nigeria in 1987 as a foreign policy tool designed to
o: provide skilled Nigerian professionals to developing African, Caribbean, and Pacific countries
recruit foreign mercenaries for ECOMOG peacekeeping duties
export petroleum products at zero cost to Western allies
subsidize university education for European exchange students
qs.e: Created under Minister Ike Nwachukwu, TAC shares Nigerian expertise (teachers, doctors, engineers) with ACP nations as an instrument of South-South cooperation.

qs.q: Which organ of the African Union (AU) consists of fifteen elected member states responsible for monitoring security threats and authorizing regional peace operations?
qs.e: The PSC is the AU's standing decision-making body for conflict prevention, management, and resolution across the African continent.

qs.q: The Third Military Regime in Nigeria (1975-1979) led by General Murtala Muhammed and General Olusegun Obasanjo distinguished itself by
o: implementing a structured transition program that voluntarily handed power to a civilian president
indefinitely postponing elections and banning all trade unions
withdrawing Nigeria from the United Nations and Commonwealth
qs.e: The Murtala/Obasanjo regime created 19 states, drafted the 1979 Constitution, and successfully handed power to civilian President Shehu Shagari on October 1, 1979.

qs.q: In Nigeria's presidential system, the constitutional rule that prohibits the President from unilaterally dissolving the National Assembly serves primarily as a
o: check and balance safeguarding legislative independence
qs.e: In a presidential framework with separation of powers, the President cannot dissolve parliament at will (unlike in parliamentary models), ensuring legislative independence and checks and balances.

qs.q: In constitutional theory, 'constitutionalism' is distinguished from mere possession of a constitution because constitutionalism fundamentally demands
o: effective legal limitations on governmental powers to safeguard individual liberties
having a lengthy written document drafted by military decree
concentrating absolute authority in a unicameral assembly
prohibiting judicial review over legislative acts
qs.e: Constitutionalism is the doctrine that government power must be limited by law, preventing arbitrary rule and safeguarding fundamental human rights.

qs.q: The 1958 Willink Commission was appointed by the British colonial administration in Nigeria primarily to investigate
o: the fears of ethnic minorities and propose means of allaying them
the financial viability of creating a central bank
the feasibility of adopting a unicameral federal parliament
boundary disputes between the Northern and Western regions
qs.e: The Henry Willink Commission was set up in 1957 to address minority fears of majority domination in the North, West, and East prior to independence.

qs.q: In administrative law, the writ of 'prohibition' differs from the writ of 'certiorari' because prohibition is issued to
o: prevent an inferior tribunal from proceeding with a matter currently exceeding its jurisdiction
quash an illegal judgment that has already been delivered by a lower court
compel a reluctant administrative board to perform a statutory duty
order law enforcement to produce a detainee in open court
qs.e: Prohibition acts preventively to stop ongoing or future lower court proceedings lacking jurisdiction, whereas certiorari acts curatively to quash completed decisions.

qs.q: The 1995 draft constitution produced during the Abacha regime introduced the concept of rotational presidency and six geopolitical zones, but it was never formally promulgated because
o: General Abacha died in June 1998, and General Abdulsalami Abubakar initiated a fresh transition resulting in the 1999 Constitution
the Supreme Court declared the constitutional conference illegal
all state assemblies voted unanimously against rotational presidency
the United Nations placed economic sanctions on the constitution
qs.e: Abacha's sudden death in June 1998 led to General Abdulsalami Abubakar taking power and setting up the Niki Tobi Committee, which revised the 1979 Constitution into the 1999 Constitution.

qs.q: The Commonwealth of Nations Harare Declaration of 1991 set out fundamental political values binding on all member states, emphasizing
o: democracy, rule of law, fundamental human rights, and good governance
obligatory military assistance during international conflicts
adoption of a uniform currency across member nations
strict adherence to British statutory court precedents
qs.e: The 1991 Harare Declaration updated the 1971 Singapore Declaration, establishing democratic standards, human rights, and constitutional government as conditions of Commonwealth membership.

qs.q: The organizational arm of state authority responsible for implementing policies and enforcing laws passed by parliament is the
qs.e: The executive branch executes statutes, directs foreign policy, maintains public order, and administers government services.

qs.q: Which form of government is characterized by governance by a small group of privileged individuals or wealthy elites?
qs.e: An oligarchy is a system of rule concentrated in the hands of a small elite group based on wealth, nobility, or military status.

qs.q: A system of government guided entirely by religious laws and ruled by religious leaders is known as a
qs.e: A theocracy recognizes divine guidance or religious clerics as the supreme civil authority.

qs.q: The document presented by a political party outlining its goals, policies, and program prior to an election is called a party
qs.e: A party manifesto lays out the official political promises and public policies a party intends to implement if elected to power.

qs.q: The fundamental law of the land that cannot be altered by regular statutory legislation is the
qs.e: A constitution is the supreme law; ordinary statutes enacted by parliament must conform to its provisions.

qs.q: Which sub-regional West African treaty established ECOMOG as a interventionist military peacekeeping organ in 1990?
qs.e: ECOMOG was established under the auspices of ECOWAS to respond to West African armed conflicts, starting with Liberia.

qs.q: In a democracy, the official count of eligible citizens residing within geographic boundaries for electoral districting is a national
qs.e: A national population census provides demographic data essential for delimiting electoral constituencies and revenue allocation.

qs.q: Which form of authority described by Max Weber relies on age-old customs, hereditary rule, and established patriarchal deference?
qs.e: Traditional authority rests on established cultural customs and hereditary legitimacy, such as traditional monarchs or emirs.

qs.q: The doctrine asserting that parliament has supreme lawmaking authority and cannot be overridden by any court or external body is parliamentary
qs.e: Parliamentary sovereignty (e.g., in the British unwritten constitutional tradition) means parliament can pass or unmake any law without judicial invalidation.

qs.q: A key difference between a presidential system and a parliamentary system is that in a presidential system, ministers are usually
o: appointed from outside parliament and accountable directly to the President
elected members of parliament holding cabinet seats
career civil servants appointed for life
qs.e: In a presidential system, separation of powers prevents ministers from being sitting legislators; they are executive appointees.

qs.q: The presiding officer of the upper house of parliament in Nigeria is the
o: Speaker of the House of Representatives
qs.e: The Senate President presides over the Senate, the upper chamber of Nigeria's National Assembly.

qs.q: The administrative principle requiring that civil servants must not publicly claim personal credit for successful policies is civil service
qs.e: Anonymity shields bureaucrats from direct political scrutiny or praise, placing public responsibility on the elected minister.

qs.q: Pressure groups that employ unconstitutional methods such as violent protests, riots, or strikes without formal leadership are termed
qs.e: Anomic pressure groups are spontaneous, short-lived, and often violent interest groups arising in response to immediate crises.

qs.q: Which Nigerian constitutional development introduced a central Council of Ministers and regional executive autonomy in 1951?
qs.e: The 1951 Macpherson Constitution created a central Council of Ministers and expanded regional legislative autonomy across North, West, and East.

qs.q: The political party led by Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe in the Second Republic (1979-1983) that drew primary support from Southeastern Nigeria was the
qs.e: The NPP was formed in 1978 and led by Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe, winning state governorships in Imo, Anambra, and Plateau in 1979.

qs.q: In federal revenue sharing in Nigeria, the allocation formula is designed to distribute funds from the
qs.e: Under Section 162 of the 1999 Constitution, all federal revenues (tax, oil) flow into the Federation Account for sharing among federal, state, and local tiers.

qs.q: The legal mechanism of losing citizenship when a person voluntarily acquires citizenship of another non-African country is termed
qs.e: Under Section 28 of the 1999 Constitution, a naturalized Nigerian loses Nigerian citizenship if they voluntarily acquire foreign citizenship.

qs.q: Which international financial institution headquartered in Washington, D.C., provides long-term development loans and structural adjustment assistance to member countries?
qs.e: The World Bank focuses on long-term economic development and poverty reduction, while the IMF addresses balance of payments crises.

qs.q: Which military government in Nigeria introduced the Land Use Decree of 1978 and nationalized land tenure across the country?
qs.e: The Olusegun Obasanjo Supreme Military Council promulgated the Land Use Decree No. 6 of 1978 in March 1978.

qs.q: In political analysis, a state that possesses formal legal recognition by the international community but lacks internal control over armed warlords is experiencing a crisis of
qs.e: Empirical sovereignty refers to actual internal effective control and police power over territory, distinct from formal juridical recognition.

qs.q: Feudalism as a socio-political ideology was based primarily on hierarchical obligations between lords and vassals linked by land holdings known as
qs.e: Feudalism structured society around land grants (fiefs) given by lords to vassals in exchange for military service and feudal dues.

qs.q: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, the process for creating a new state requires a mandatory approval by two-thirds majority in the National Assembly followed by a referendum supported by
o: at least two-thirds majority of the people in the area concerned
a simple majority of state governors
unanimous consent of the Supreme Court
a federal executive order signed by the President
qs.e: Section 8(1) of the 1999 Constitution details the onerous multi-step process for state creation, including two-thirds assembly support and a two-thirds referendum result.

qs.q: Which constitutional principle ensures that lawmakers cannot pass retroactive criminal legislation punishing actions that were lawful when committed?
o: prohibition of ex post facto laws
qs.e: Ex post facto law prohibitions (Section 36(8) of Nigeria's Constitution) protect individuals by forbidding retroactive criminal laws.

qs.q: The power of the executive president to issue binding directives having the force of statutory law during a legislative recess is called issuing an
qs.e: Executive orders allow the President to direct administrative operations or enforce laws within constitutional authority.

qs.q: <svg width="280" height="110" style="background-color:white" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect x="5" y="5" width="270" height="100" fill="none" stroke="#000" stroke-width="2"/><text x="15" y="25" font-size="12" fill="#000">Nigerian Judicial Hierarchy</text><text x="15" y="45" font-size="11" fill="#000">1. Apex Court -> Supreme Court</text><text x="15" y="65" font-size="11" fill="#000">2. Intermediate -> Court of Appeal</text><text x="15" y="85" font-size="11" fill="#000">3. High Courts & Sharia/Customary Courts</text></svg> Referring to the judicial hierarchy diagram above, which court serves as the intermediate appellate court between the High Courts and the Supreme Court of Nigeria?
qs.e: The Court of Appeal (Section 237 of the 1999 Constitution) hears appeals originating from High Courts and specialized tribunals before any further appeal to the Supreme Court.

qs.q: In the 1959 pre-independence elections in Nigeria, which political party won the largest number of seats in the Federal House of Representatives?
o: National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons (NCNC)
qs.e: The NPC won 134 out of 312 seats in the House of Representatives, forming a coalition government with the NCNC.

qs.q: Which technique is commonly used by promotional pressure groups to generate public sympathy and pressure government officials through media publicity?
o: public relations campaigns and press conferences
qs.e: Promotional groups rely on public relations, news conferences, petitions, and media outreach to mobilize public opinion.

qs.q: An electoral system that combines single-member constituency voting with proportional party list allocation to produce proportional representation is a
qs.e: MMP allows voters two votes—one for a local district representative and one for a party list—ensuring overall proportional representation.

qs.q: The process of transferring public state enterprise ownership to private investors through public share offerings or asset sales is known as
qs.e: Privatization sells state assets or equity to private shareholders to promote market efficiency and reduce state financial burden.

qs.q: Which landmark commission report in 1988 reorganized the Nigerian civil service to make federal ministries operate strictly under professionalized departments?
o: Dotun Philips Civil Service Reform Commission
qs.e: The 1988 Dotun Philips report restructured ministries into specialized departments to enhance administrative professionalism.

qs.q: Under Nigerian federalism, the distribution of residual legislative powers means that subjects not listed in either the Exclusive or Concurrent Lists belong to the
qs.e: Residual powers automatically vest in state legislatures under the 10th Amendment structure of federal constitutions, including Nigeria's.

qs.q: The major reform that abolished the four regional structures in Nigeria and created 12 states in May 1967 was instituted by decree under
qs.e: On May 27, 1967, General Gowon issued Decree No. 14 dividing Nigeria into 12 states to replace the four regions.

qs.q: In local government, the administrative head of civil servants in a local government council is designated as the
qs.e: HOLGA leads the career civil servants within a local government administration.

qs.q: Which organ of the United Nations serves as the principal judicial organ for resolving legal disputes submitted by sovereign states?
qs.e: The ICJ (seated at The Hague, Netherlands) is the primary judicial organ of the UN for state-to-state litigation.

qs.q: Totalitarianism differs from standard authoritarianism because a totalitarian regime seeks to
o: exercise total ideological control over all public and private aspects of citizens' lives
maintain a competitive multi-party parliamentary system
protect judicial independence and fundamental human rights
decentralize administrative powers to local municipalities
qs.e: Totalitarianism attempts complete control over society, economy, culture, and private life through pervasive state propaganda and terror.

qs.q: In a bicameral legislature, when the Senate and House of Representatives pass conflicting versions of the same bill, the disagreement is reconciled by setting up a joint
qs.e: A Conference Committee composed of members from both legislative houses meets to resolve differences between Senate and House versions of a bill.

qs.q: The 1979 Constitution introduced the Code of Conduct Bureau (CCB) and Code of Conduct Tribunal (CCT) primarily to enforce public officer accountability by preventing
o: conflict of interest, illicit enrichment, and corruption among public officials
state creation petitions by ethnic minorities
qs.e: The CCB and CCT mandate asset declarations by public officers to prevent corruption and abuse of office.

qs.q: During the Third Republic transition, the June 12, 1993 presidential election was annulled by the military administration of General Ibrahim Babangida despite being widely acclaimed as
o: the free, fair, and peaceful election won by Chief M.K.O. Abiola
an illegal election boycotted by all political parties
a landslide victory for the National Republican Convention
a violent election declared invalid by the Supreme Court
qs.e: The June 12 election was universally regarded as Nigeria's freest and fairest election, won by SDP candidate Chief M.K.O. Abiola before Babangida annulled it.

qs.q: The principle of 'collective responsibility' in a parliamentary cabinet system requires a minister who publicly disagrees with a major cabinet decision to
o: override the Prime Minister in parliament
appeal to the Supreme Court for protection
petition the opposition party for support
qs.e: Collective responsibility dictates that all cabinet members must publicly support government decisions or resign if they cannot support cabinet policy.

qs.q: The 1922 Clifford Constitution was criticized by early Nigerian nationalists because the Legislative Council's jurisdiction was limited to the Southern Provinces, leaving the Northern Provinces to be governed by executive decrees issued by the
qs.e: The 1922 Legislative Council made laws only for the Colony and Southern Provinces; the North was governed directly by proclamation of the Governor.

qs.q: Which prominent pressure group in Nigeria organized nationwide industrial strikes in 2003 and 2012 to protest federal government removal of petroleum subsidies?
qs.e: The NLC, as the central trade union federation, led general strikes against fuel price hikes and subsidy removal in 2003, 2012, and subsequent years.

qs.q: In electoral systems, 'gerrymandering' refers to the unconstitutional or unethical practice of redrawing electoral constituency boundaries to
o: give an unfair political advantage to a specific ruling party or group
ensure equal land mass across all voting districts
guarantee universal voter turnout in rural areas
increase the number of judicial court divisions
qs.e: Gerrymandering manipulates district borders to concentrate or dilute specific voter demographics, favoring one political party.

qs.q: Which sub-regional defense protocol authorized ECOMOG intervention in Sierra Leone in 1997 to restore the democratically elected government of President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah?
o: ECOWAS Protocol on Mutual Assistance in Defence
qs.e: The ECOWAS 1981 Protocol on Mutual Assistance in Defence provided the legal basis for ECOMOG forces (led by Nigeria) to restore Kabbah's government.

qs.q: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, the National Judicial Council (NJC) was created to safeguard judicial independence by taking responsibility for
o: recommending the appointment and discipline of judicial officers to the executive
passing statutory bills governing court procedures
conducting police investigations into federal crimes
qs.e: The NJC (Third Schedule) isolates judicial appointments, promotions, and discipline from direct political manipulation by governors or the president.

qs.q: The primary objective of Nigeria's participation in the creation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) in 2019 was to
o: boost intra-African trade, industrialization, and economic integration
impose import tariffs on all West African commodities
replace national currencies with a single continental coin
restrict labor migration across North African states
qs.e: AfCFTA aims to create a single liberalized market across Africa to expand intra-continental trade and industrial diversification.

qs.q: In political theory, the doctrine of 'popular sovereignty' asserted by Jean-Jacques Rousseau posits that ultimate legitimate political authority resides in
o: the general will of the entire citizenry
the hereditary rights of landed aristocrats
the divine right of ruling monarchs
the administrative expertise of civil service bureaucrats
qs.e: Rousseau argued that true sovereignty belongs collectively to the people ('general will') and cannot be transferred to a monarch or elite.

qs.q: The 1975 Udoji Public Service Review Commission in Nigeria was groundbreaking because it attempted to modernize civil service management by introducing
o: Management by Objectives (MBO) and Project Performance Budgeting System (PPBS)
complete privatization of state civil service posts
military rank classification across administrative cadres
abolition of civil service pension schemes
qs.e: Udoji recommended modern management techniques like MBO and PPBS to transform the civil service from routine administration to result-oriented management.

qs.q: In constitutional law, the doctrine of 'implied powers' establishes that the national legislature possesses authority to enact laws on subjects not explicitly named in the constitution if those laws are
o: necessary and proper for carrying into execution express constitutional powers
approved unanimously by state house assemblies
signed by the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court
qs.e: Implied powers allow parliament to enact legislation reasonably related to executing its explicit enumerated constitutional responsibilities.

qs.q: During the 1962 Western Nigeria constitutional crisis, the Regional Governor (Sir Adesoji Aderemi) dismissed Premier Samuel Ladoke Akintola based on a petition signed by a majority of lawmakers outside the House floor. The Privy Council upheld the dismissal, leading to the enactment of the
o: 1963 Republican Constitution amendment requiring removal votes to occur inside the legislative floor
immediate creation of Mid-Western region in 1962
abolition of all state governorships nationwide
dissolution of the Supreme Court of Nigeria
qs.e: After the Privy Council ruled in Aderemi v. Akintola, Nigeria nullified the ruling retrospectively in the 1963 Constitution, mandating that premier removals must occur via formal floor votes.

qs.q: The African Peer Review Mechanism (APRM) established under NEPAD in 2003 is a voluntary self-monitoring instrument designed to foster
o: good governance, political stability, and socio-economic development through peer assessment
joint military interventions against unconstitutional regime changes
standardized customs tariffs across central African states
the mandatory adoption of a unicameral presidential model
qs.e: APRM allows AU member states to evaluate each other's governance standards, human rights performance, and economic management constructively.

qs.q: The structured administrative organization created to assist the executive in formulating and executing public policies is the
qs.e: The civil service consists of professional career officials working in ministries and departments to carry out executive policies.

qs.q: Which political concept denotes the allegiance, loyalty, and civic duties owed by an individual to a sovereign state?
qs.e: Citizenship defines the legal relationship between an individual and a state, granting rights and imposing civic obligations.

qs.q: The system of governance where political authority is held entirely by a single central government without semi-autonomous states is
qs.e: A unitary government concentrates supreme lawmaking and executive authority in a single central capital.

qs.q: Which arm of government is empowered to pass national budget appropriation bills into law?
qs.e: The legislature holds the power of the purse, scrutinizing and passing national annual budget appropriation bills.

qs.q: The non-military international association uniting former territories of the British Empire and the United Kingdom is the
qs.e: The Commonwealth of Nations is a voluntary association of independent states, mostly former British colonies, promoting democracy and cooperation.

qs.q: In Nigeria, the highest court of final appeal in all civil and criminal matters is the
qs.e: The Supreme Court of Nigeria is the apex judicial body whose decisions are final and binding on all lower courts.

qs.q: An unconstitutional takeover of state government power by officers of the armed forces is termed a
qs.e: A coup d'etat is the sudden, force-backed overthrow of an existing government, usually by a faction within the military.

qs.q: In political science, 'political culture' refers to the shared set of attitudes, values, feelings, and beliefs that shape political behavior within a
qs.e: Political culture represents the collective orientations, traditions, and norms governing civic participation and governmental legitimacy in a state.

qs.q: Communalism as a traditional African political concept emphasizes social harmony, collective land stewardship, and community decision-making through
qs.e: Traditional communalism stresses collective welfare, mutual obligation, and egalitarian consensus rather than individualistic capitalism.

qs.q: A core feature of a rigid constitution is that it can only be amended through a special onerous procedure involving a
o: supermajority vote in parliament and concurrence by sub-national units
simple majority vote in the lower house
direct executive order from the President
judicial decree issued by the Chief Justice
qs.e: Rigid constitutions require extraordinary steps, such as two-thirds legislative majorities and approval by state assemblies.

qs.q: The principle that administrative agencies must grant individuals a fair hearing before taking punitive decisions affecting their rights is part of
o: natural justice and the Rule of Law
qs.e: Natural justice (audi alteram partem—hear the other side) requires fair, unbiased administrative procedures before penalizing anyone.

qs.q: In a presidential system, the President exercises the executive power of 'veto' primarily to prevent parliament from enacting laws that are
o: unconstitutional or contrary to executive policy priorities
supported by a two-thirds legislative majority
qs.e: The presidential veto acts as a check on legislative power, stopping bills deemed detrimental or unconstitutional unless overridden.

qs.q: Which organ of government is charged with confirming executive appointments of federal ministers, ambassadors, and supreme court justices in Nigeria?
qs.e: Section 147 and Section 231 of the 1999 Constitution mandate Senate confirmation for ministerial and top judicial nominations.

qs.q: The political party that won the 1979 presidential election and formed the federal government during Nigeria's Second Republic was the
qs.e: The NPN, led by Alhaji Shehu Shagari, won the 1979 presidential election and governed Nigeria during the Second Republic (1979-1983).

qs.q: The professional association representing Nigerian lawyers that acts as a major promotional pressure group on rule of law and human rights is the
qs.e: The NBA frequently intervenes in public interest litigation, defending fundamental rights and judicial independence.

qs.q: The electoral system where voters cast a single vote for a political party list and seats are distributed in direct proportion to total party votes is
qs.e: Under Party List PR, political parties present ranked candidate lists and fill legislative seats based on their national or regional percentage share.

qs.q: The 1976 Local Government Reforms in Nigeria created uniform local government councils across the country serving populations of roughly
qs.e: The 1976 Reform guidelines standardized local council sizes to populations between 150,000 and 800,000 to ensure viable administrative units.

qs.q: Which founding principle of ECOWAS allows citizens of member states to travel, reside, and establish businesses across West Africa without entry visas?
o: Protocol on Free Movement of Persons, Rights of Residence and Establishment
qs.e: The 1979 ECOWAS Protocol guarantees 90-day visa-free entry and residence rights across member states for West African citizens.

qs.q: Nigeria's foreign policy initiative under General Murtala Muhammed in 1975 achieved a historic diplomatic victory in Africa by recognizing the MPLA as the legitimate government of
qs.e: In January 1976, Murtala Muhammed delivered his famous 'Africa Has Come of Age' speech at the OAU, backing the MPLA in Angola against Western intervention.

qs.q: A major distinction between 'power' and 'authority' in political science is that power relies on coercion or force, whereas authority rests on
qs.e: Power is the ability to compel obedience through force or sanctions; authority is legitimate power accepted willingly by citizens.

qs.q: The political ideology of Socialism emphasizes that key national economic assets and public utilities should be owned by
o: the state on behalf of the public
qs.e: Socialism advocates public ownership of commanding heights of the economy (railways, steel, electricity) to prevent exploitation.

qs.q: The 1963 Republican Constitution of Nigeria was created through an Act passed by the Nigerian Parliament rather than a British Order-in-Council, making it an
qs.e: An autochthonous constitution originates locally within the sovereign nation itself rather than being enacted by a colonial authority.

qs.q: The legislative process where a proposed bill is sent to a specialized committee of lawmakers to examine clause-by-clause details and take public submissions is the
qs.e: At the committee stage, standing or select committees conduct detailed line-by-line scrutiny and public hearings on the bill.

qs.q: Which legal doctrine prevents courts from adjudicating hypothetical or political disputes that lack concrete legal controversy between adverse parties?
qs.e: Justiciability requires that a court dispute present a real legal issue appropriate for judicial resolution rather than an abstract political question.

qs.q: Which major political party in the Fourth Republic was formed in 1998 by a coalition of political figures opposing military rule and governed Nigeria from 1999 to 2015?
qs.e: The PDP was formed in 1998, won the 1999 general elections under Olusegun Obasanjo, and maintained presidency until 2015.

qs.q: A primary objective of civil service neutral recruitment managed by independent civil service commissions is to eradicate
o: political patronage and nepotism in public appointments
qs.e: Civil Service Commissions conduct merit-based, non-partisan hiring to eliminate political favoritism (the spoils system).

qs.q: In electoral administration, the process of 'voter registration' is designed to create an accurate and verifiable
o: voters' register to prevent double voting and fraud
tax assessment list for local councils
qs.e: An accurate voters' register ensures that only eligible, registered citizens can vote and prevents electoral impersonation or multiple voting.

qs.q: Which statutory administrative mechanism allows citizens in Nigeria to challenge illegal tax assessments levied by revenue authorities?
qs.e: Tax Appeal Tribunals provide specialized quasi-judicial administrative review for taxpayers disputing assessments by FIRS or state tax boards.

qs.q: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, the creation of new Local Government Areas by state governments becomes constitutionally effective only after approval by the
o: National Assembly through a constitutional amendment inserting the LGAs into the First Schedule
Federal Executive Council led by the President
Supreme Court in a plenary judgment
Revenue Mobilization Allocation and Fiscal Commission
qs.e: Section 8(8) requires that state creation of new local councils must be transmitted to and ratified by the National Assembly via constitutional amendment.

qs.q: The 'indigenization' policy implemented in Nigeria under the Nigerian Enterprises Promotion Decrees of 1972 and 1977 aimed to
o: transfer controlling equity and management of major domestic economic enterprises to Nigerian citizens
ban all international trade with European economies
nationalize foreign diplomatic embassies in Lagos
qs.e: The Indigenization Decrees reserved specific sectors (retail, transportation, light manufacturing) for 100% Nigerian ownership and mandated majority local equity in others.

qs.q: Under Nigerian citizenship laws, dual citizenship is legally permissible for any person who is a citizen of Nigeria by
qs.e: Under Section 28 of the 1999 Constitution, natural-born Nigerian citizens retain Nigerian citizenship even if they hold foreign citizenship by birth or naturalization.

qs.q: Nigeria played a central role in establishing the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) during the Cold War to safeguard developing nations from
o: being drawn into super-power geopolitical rivalries and proxy wars
participating in international trade with United Nations members
receiving foreign aid from international banks
qs.e: NAM enabled developing countries in Africa, Asia, and Latin America to maintain independence without submitting to US or Soviet alignment.

qs.q: Which major military regime in Nigeria created nine new states in 1991, bringing the total number of states in the federation to 30?
qs.e: General Babangida created 9 additional states on August 27, 1991 (expanding from 21 to 30 states), along with creating new LGAs.

qs.q: The African Union's New Partnership for Africa's Development (NEPAD) adopted in 2001 was designed as a strategic framework to promote
o: sustainable socio-economic growth, poverty eradication, and economic empowerment across Africa
military defense pacts against European allies
the creation of a single African central bank in Cairo
the abolition of national parliaments across West Africa
qs.e: NEPAD was spearheaded by leaders including Nigeria's Obasanjo and South Africa's Mbeki to drive African-led economic revitalization and good governance.

qs.q: In comparative government, 'liberal democracy' is distinguished from 'illiberal democracy' primarily by the presence of
o: robust protection for individual civil liberties and independent judicial institutions
holding periodic voting elections regardless of press freedom
a single ruling dominant party controlling national media
qs.e: Illiberal democracies hold elections, but lack key constitutional protections such as judicial independence, free press, and individual rights found in liberal democracies.

qs.q: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, if the President vetoes a bill passed by the National Assembly, parliament can override the presidential veto by passing the bill again with a
o: two-thirds majority vote in both the Senate and House of Representatives
simple majority vote in the Senate only
unanimous vote in the House of Representatives
three-fourths majority vote of the Council of State
qs.e: Section 58(5) empowers the National Assembly to override a presidential veto if two-thirds of members in both chambers re-pass the bill.

qs.q: Which constitutional mechanism prevents the executive branch from spending public funds without prior legislative authorization?
qs.e: Section 80 of the 1999 Constitution dictates that no money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Revenue Fund except as authorized by an Appropriation Act.

qs.q: The 1953 Kano Riots were a direct political repercussion of inter-regional friction caused by Northern delegates being insulted in Lagos following the debate over Chief Anthony Enahoro's
qs.e: Tensions following Northern opposition to Enahoro's 1956 self-government motion spilled over into anti-Southern riots when Samuel Akintola toured Kano in May 1953.

qs.q: In political party merger dynamics, the creation of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in February 2013 was historic because it united major opposition parties including the
o: Action Congress of Nigeria (ACN), Congress for Progressive Change (CPC), and All Nigeria Peoples Party (ANPP)
People's Democratic Party (PDP), Labour Party (LP), and APGA
National Party of Nigeria (NPN), UPN, and NPP
NCNC, Action Group, and Northern People's Congress
qs.e: The APC was formed in 2013 by a merger of the ACN, CPC, ANPP, and a faction of APGA, forming a united opposition that won the 2015 presidential election.

qs.q: The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) acts as an institutional pressure group in Nigeria primarily using industrial strikes to demand
o: university autonomy, improved academic funding, and implementation of signed agreements
the privatization of all public federal universities
the abolition of state secondary education boards
the direct appointment of university vice-chancellors by state governors
qs.e: ASUU uses collective industrial action to push the federal government for increased university funding, research infrastructure, and institutional autonomy.

qs.q: In federal political systems, 'fiscal federalism' addresses the financial relationships and revenue sharing mechanisms between
o: different tiers of government in a federal state
public state enterprises and foreign commercial banks
the military high command and state civil services
qs.e: Fiscal federalism governs how taxing powers and expenditure responsibilities are divided among federal, state, and local governments.

qs.q: Under Section 30 of the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, a naturalized citizen can be deprived of Nigerian citizenship by the President if the individual is sentenced to imprisonment for a term of not less than
o: three years within seven years after becoming naturalized
six months within one year of naturalization
twenty years in a foreign country
one month for a civil traffic offense
qs.e: Section 30(2)(a) stipulates that naturalization can be revoked if the person is convicted and sentenced to 3+ years imprisonment within 7 years of naturalization.

qs.q: The Gulf of Guinea Commission (GGC) established in 2001 by Nigeria and neighboring coastal states aims to enhance regional cooperation in
o: maritime security, crude oil exploitation, and conflict prevention in the Gulf of Guinea
standardizing agricultural import tariffs across landlocked states
creating a single monetary union for West African central banks
qs.e: The GGC fosters maritime security, anti-piracy, and joint oil resource management among nations bordering the Gulf of Guinea.

qs.q: Which major constitutional reform introduced under General Sani Abacha created six additional states in October 1996, bringing Nigeria to its current 36-state structure?
qs.e: On October 1, 1996, General Abacha created 6 new states (Bayelsa, Ebonyi, Ekiti, Gombe, Nasarawa, and Zamfara), bringing the total to 36 states.

qs.q: Under Article 51 of the United Nations Charter, sovereign member states possess the inherent right of
o: individual or collective self-defense if an armed attack occurs
vetoing resolutions in the UN General Assembly
expelling neighboring member states without trial
qs.e: Article 51 explicitly preserves a nation's inherent right to individual or collective self-defense against armed aggression until the Security Council takes action.

qs.q: In administrative theory, Max Weber highlighted 'impersonality' as a defining characteristic of ideal bureaucracy. Impersonality requires civil servants to execute public duties
o: without personal bias, favoritism, or emotional attachment toward individual citizens
by changing administrative rules arbitrarily based on public pressure
strictly according to verbal directives issued by ruling party officials
by delegating lawmaking authority to private commercial boards
qs.e: Impersonality ensures equal treatment under standardized administrative rules, preventing personal bias or favoritism in service delivery.

qs.q: The 1954 Lyttelton Constitution established a residual list of legislative powers. Under this constitutional arrangement, residual powers were assigned exclusively to the
o: regional legislatures of the North, West, and East
central House of Representatives in Lagos
Council of State and Privy Council
qs.e: The 1954 Lyttelton Constitution gave federal parliament exclusive powers, placed shared subjects on a concurrent list, and granted residual powers to the regions.

qs.q: When the Supreme Court of Nigeria exercises its 'original jurisdiction' under Section 232 of the 1999 Constitution, it hears legal disputes directly between
o: the Federation and a State, or between States in their legal capacities
individual private citizens disputing land ownership
commercial banks contesting central bank currency regulations
qs.e: Section 232 confers original jurisdiction on the Supreme Court to try disputes between the Federal Government and States, or among States.

qs.q: In electoral systems, the 'duverger's law' in political science states that single-member district simple-majority electoral systems (First-Past-The-Post) naturally tend to produce a
qs.e: Maurice Duverger demonstrated that First-Past-The-Post voting favors a two-party system because minor parties are penalized by 'wasted vote' dynamics.

qs.q: The 1974 Jerome Udoji Public Service Review Commission introduced the concept of open reporting and performance evaluation in the civil service to replace the traditional
