Refusing to fight against the Philistines at Michmash
Appointing his son Jonathan as military commander
qs.e: 1 Samuel 15 shows Saul sparing Agag and choice livestock under pressure, prompting Samuel to say 'to obey is better than sacrifice'.

qs.q: Why did Rehoboam reject the advice of the elders after Solomon's death?
o: He preferred the harsh approach of his youthful peers to show strength
The elders proposed abolishing Israel's standing army
The elders advocated worshipping Egyptian deities
qs.e: 1 Kings 12:8-14 describes Rehoboam abandoning the wise counsel of the elders for the harsh advice of the young men who grew up with him.

qs.q: What lesson did Elijah learn from God at Mount Horeb in the still small voice?
o: God operates not only in spectacular display but in quiet inward conviction
Divine judgment requires immediate military force
Prophets must isolate themselves permanently from society
Israel would never recover from Baal worship
qs.e: 1 Kings 19:11-13 shows God revealing Himself not in wind, earthquake, or fire, but in a still small voice, reassuring Elijah of silent divine work.

qs.q: In the Sermon on the Mount, what core attitude does Jesus require regarding interpersonal anger?
o: Reconciliation with one's brother before presenting gifts at the altar
Publicly exposing the wrongdoer in the synagogue
Ignoring personal offense while seeking political justice
qs.e: In Matthew 5:23-24, Jesus emphasizes prioritizing interpersonal reconciliation over religious ritual offerings.

qs.q: What central truth is taught in Jesus' parable of the lost sheep?
o: God actively seeks out individual lost sinners with persistent joy
Losing one sinner is acceptable if ninety-nine remain safe
Sinners must earn their return before being accepted
qs.e: Luke 15:4-7 illustrates God's compassionate initiative in searching for one lost soul and rejoicing when found.

qs.q: What primary lesson did the apostles learn when Jesus calmed the storm on the Sea of Galilee?
o: Jesus possesses divine authority over natural elements
Disciples should avoid boat travel during stormy seasons
Physical danger proves a lack of personal faith
qs.e: Mark 4:39-41 records the disciples marvelling at Jesus calming the sea, recognizing His sovereign authority over nature.

qs.q: Why did the early Jerusalem believers sell their property and share resources in Acts 2 and 4?
o: To ensure no member suffered poverty and to reflect unity of heart
Because Roman taxes prohibited private land ownership
They expected the immediate physical end of the universe that week
The apostles commanded financial equality as a legal prerequisite
qs.e: Acts 2:44-45 and 4:32-35 highlight voluntary fellowship, brotherly love, and care so that none among them lacked.

qs.q: In Genesis 15, how did God confirm His covenant promise of land and offspring to Abraham?
o: By passing as a smoking firepot and flaming torch between divided animal pieces
By presenting Abraham with a golden crown at Hebron
By raining fire upon enemy kings in Mesopotamia
By sending an archangel to write the covenant on stone tablets
qs.e: Genesis 15:17-18 describes God alone passing through the sacrifice in the form of a smoking furnace and burning lamp, solemnizing the unconditional covenant.

qs.q: What significant theological lesson emerges from Jacob's dream at Bethel in Genesis 28?
o: God's presence and covenant promise extend beyond ancestral home boundaries
Angels require ladder structures to access earthly sanctuaries
Bethel was destined to replace Jerusalem as Israel's sole temple site
Vows are binding only if God grants immediate material prosperity
qs.e: Genesis 28:15-16 shows Jacob realizing God was present with him during exile, affirming divine omnipresence and covenant faithfulness.

qs.q: How did Joseph demonstrate spiritual wisdom when revealing his identity to his brothers in Egypt?
o: He attributed his past suffering to God's sovereign plan for preserving life
He demanded that his brothers pay compensation for their past cruelty
He forced his brothers to become servants to Benjamin
He concealed his identity until Jacob died in Canaan
qs.e: In Genesis 45:5-8, Joseph comforted his brothers by acknowledging that God sent him ahead to preserve life during the severe famine.

qs.q: Why did God instruct Israel to collect only a double portion of manna on the sixth day in the wilderness?
o: To observe the seventh-day Sabbath rest without gathering labor
Because manna production ceased permanently after six days
To test whether Israel could store food in Egyptian baskets
To reserve food supplies for pagan travelers in Sinai
qs.e: Exodus 16:22-26 explains that the double portion on the sixth day was provided so the people could rest on the holy Sabbath.

qs.q: What spiritual flaw is demonstrated by Israel's decision to make a golden calf at Sinai in Exodus 32?
o: Impatience and replacing spiritual faith with tangible idols
Desire to return immediately to Egyptian military rule
Refusal to offer physical sacrifices to God
qs.e: Exodus 32 reveals Israel's anxiety during Moses' delay, causing them to seek visible representation through idolatry.

qs.q: What spiritual reality caused Gideon to reduce his military army from 32,000 to 300 men in Judges 7?
o: To prevent Israel from boasting that their own strength saved them
Because 31,700 soldiers lacked basic military equipment
To satisfy Midianite terms for conditional peace
Because the camp lacked sufficient water supplies
qs.e: Judges 7:2 states explicitly that God reduced the army so Israel could not claim 'My own hand has saved me'.

qs.q: Why was Eli judged by God according to 1 Samuel 2 and 3?
o: He failed to restrain his sons Hophni and Phinehas from corrupting sacred duties
He refused to anoint Saul as king over Israel
He offered unauthorized sacrifices at Shiloh without levitical consent
He joined the Philistine military against David
qs.e: 1 Samuel 3:13 states judgment came upon Eli's house because his sons blasphemed God and Eli did not restrain them.

qs.q: What was the direct theological cause of the split of the United Kingdom under Rehoboam?
o: Solomon's idolatry and apostasy in his later years
David's census of the fighting men in Israel
qs.e: 1 Kings 11:11-13 indicates God tore the kingdom away from Solomon's son due to Solomon turning his heart after foreign gods.

qs.q: Why did Elisha refuse to accept gifts from Naaman after healing his leprosy?
o: To demonstrate that divine healing and grace are freely given without commercial gain
Because Naaman belonged to the enemy nation of Syria
To compel Naaman to worship exclusively in Samaria
Because Elisha's covenant law forbade receiving metal tokens
qs.e: In 2 Kings 5:15-16, Elisha refused compensation to highlight that Yahweh's salvation and healing cannot be bought.

qs.q: What prophetic message did Nehemiah emphasize when rebuilding Jerusalem's walls despite opposition?
o: Faithfulness to God combined with vigilant practical defense
Total reliance on Persian military garrisons for safety
Abandoning agricultural work until the temple was completed
Compromising with Sanballat to achieve political peace
qs.e: Nehemiah 4:14 & 20 shows Nehemiah organizing guards with swords and spears while encouraging faith: 'Our God will fight for us'.

qs.q: In Proverbs, what is stated as the foundational beginning of true wisdom?
qs.e: Proverbs 9:10 explicitly declares that 'The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, and knowledge of the Holy One is understanding'.

qs.q: What key theological theme dominates Isaiah's prophecy regarding the Suffering Servant in Isaiah 53?
o: Substitutionary atonement for the sins of humanity
Political liberation of Jerusalem from Babylon
Establishment of an earthly levitical priesthood
Rebuilding the physical walls of Zion
qs.e: Isaiah 53:5 teaches substitutionary bearing of transgressions: 'He was wounded for our transgressions, He was bruised for our iniquities'.

qs.q: What moral accusation did the prophet Amos bring against the ruling class of Samaria in Amos 5?
o: Oppressing the poor and trampling on the needy while maintaining hypocritical religious rituals
Failing to build fortification walls around Mount Gerizim
Refusing to pay annual tribute to the king of Judah
qs.e: Amos 5:11-12 & 21-24 rebukes those who afflict the just, take bribes, and turn aside the poor, demanding justice to flow like waters.

qs.q: In the parable of the Prodigal Son, what does the elder brother's reaction represent?
o: Self-righteous legalism and resentment toward God's grace extended to repentant sinners
Proper respect for parental authority and financial thrift
The restoration of familial property rights in Israel
The necessary discipline required before restoring a sinner
qs.e: Luke 15:28-32 highlights the elder brother's bitterness, depicting the Pharisaic attitude that resents undeserved mercy.

qs.q: Why did Peter and John tell the Sanhedrin in Acts 4 that they could not stop speaking about Jesus?
o: Divine obedience supersedes human prohibition when human orders contradict God
They sought political revolution against Jewish authorities
They were protected by Roman citizenship rights
The temple police lacked legal jurisdiction in Jerusalem
qs.e: Acts 4:19-20 records Peter and John answering whether it is right in the sight of God to listen to human authority rather than God.

qs.q: How does the narrative of Melchizedek in Genesis 14 prefigure Christ's priesthood according to biblical theology?
o: He combined royal kingship and divine priesthood without levitical lineage
He sacrificed bulls on Mount Moriah before Abraham
He built the first sanctuary building in Salem
He led Abraham's army to defeat Chedorlaomer
qs.e: Genesis 14:18-20 and Hebrews 7 show Melchizedek as King of Salem and Priest of Most High God, prefiguring Christ's eternal non-levitical priesthood.

qs.q: What was the significance of God commanding Hosea to marry Gomer, an unfaithful woman?
o: To illustrate prophetically Israel's spiritual adultery and Yahweh's enduring redeeming love
To punish Hosea for questioning divine judgment on Israel
To demonstrate that civil law applied equally to prophets
To show that Canaanite marriages were legally permissible
qs.e: Hosea 1-3 uses Hosea's painful marriage to Gomer as a living object lesson of God's heartbroken yet merciful covenant love for unfaithful Israel.

qs.q: In Jeremiah 31, how does the New Covenant differ fundamentally from the Sinai Covenant?
o: God writes His law directly upon human hearts rather than external stone tablets
It strictly requires physical animal sacrifices in Jerusalem
It applies exclusively to the physical descendants of Levi
It abolishes moral accountability for individual believers
qs.e: Jeremiah 31:31-34 contrasts the Old Covenant with the New Covenant where God promises to put His law in their inward parts and write it on their hearts.

qs.q: What was the primary theological significance of the veil in the temple tearing from top to bottom at Jesus' death?
o: Direct access to God's presence was opened through Christ's finished sacrifice
The physical building of the temple was rendered completely indestructible
The levitical high priest was granted political authority over Judea
The Roman soldiers were appointed custodians of the Holy of Holies
qs.e: Matthew 27:51 and Hebrews 10:19-20 interpret the torn veil as opening direct, unhindered access to God through the body of Jesus.

qs.q: Why was Stephen's speech before the Sanhedrin in Acts 7 considered provocative by the religious leaders?
o: He demonstrated that God is not confined to a physical building and accused them of resisting the Holy Spirit
He advocated violent rebellion against Roman rule in Judea
He denied the historical existence of Abraham and Moses
He claimed that Jewish believers should abandon the Scriptures
qs.e: Acts 7:48-53 shows Stephen testifying that the Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands and convicting the council of persecuting the prophets.

qs.q: What crucial principle did the Jerusalem Council in Acts 15 establish regarding Gentile converts?
o: Gentiles are saved by grace through faith without requiring circumcision or Mosaic law compliance
Gentiles must adopt full ceremonial Mosaic customs after baptism
Gentile converts must establish separate non-Jewish assemblies
Gentiles must pay annual tithes directly to the temple priesthood
qs.e: Acts 15:10-11 records Peter and James affirming that salvation comes through the grace of the Lord Jesus equally to Jews and Gentiles.

qs.q: In Romans 5, how does Paul contrast the consequence of Adam's disobedience with Christ's obedience?
o: Adam brought condemnation and death to all, whereas Christ brought justification and life
Adam brought physical weakness while Christ brought economic prosperity
Adam affected only Old Testament saints while Christ affects New Testament believers
Adam established Mosaic ritual law while Christ abolished civil law
qs.e: Romans 5:18-19 explains that through one man's offense judgment came upon all, but through the righteousness of One came justification of life.

qs.q: According to Paul in 1 Corinthians 13, why is love greater than spiritual gifts such as prophecies or tongues?
o: Spiritual gifts are temporary whereas divine love is eternal and character-defining
Love enables believers to perform larger miraculous signs
Spiritual gifts are restricted to apostles while love is restricted to elders
Love replaces the need for faith and hope in eternity
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 13:8-13 highlights that gifts of prophecy and tongues will cease, but love never fails and abides forever.

qs.q: What ethical duty does Paul urge Christian workers to observe in Colossians 3:23?
o: Perform all work heartily as unto the Lord and not unto human masters
Seek immediate promotion through public competition
Demand maximum financial compensation from employers
Refuse secular employment under non-Christian authorities
qs.e: Colossians 3:23 instructs believers: 'And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men'.

qs.q: Why did Paul urge the church in Galatians to stand firm against legalistic circumcision demands?
o: Relying on physical law rituals for justification nullifies the sufficiency of Christ's grace
Circumcision was prohibited by Roman imperial law
The Galatians were ethnically exempt from moral principles
Paul wanted to establish a new human religion separate from Abraham
qs.e: Galatians 5:2-4 warns that if believers depend on circumcision for justification, Christ profiteth them nothing, falling from grace.

qs.q: In Galatians 6:1-2, how should a Christian community handle a believer caught in a transgression?
o: Restore the person in a spirit of gentleness while bearing one another's burdens
Immediately expel the offender publicly without opportunity for repentance
Ignore the sin to avoid judging fellow believers
Impose financial penalties to compensate the community
qs.e: Galatians 6:1 commands those who are spiritual to restore such a one in gentleness, considering oneself, and fulfilling the law of Christ.

qs.q: In Ezekiel's vision of the valley of dry bones (Ezekiel 37), what deep theological truth was communicated to the exiles?
o: God's Spirit possesses sovereign power to revitalize and restore a spiritually dead, hopeless nation
Physical resurrection occurs only for levitical priests buried in Judea
The Babylonian army would be converted to Yahweh worship
Israel's national restoration depended solely on human military alliance
qs.e: Ezekiel 37:11-14 uses the restoration of dry bones by God's Spirit to promise national and spiritual regeneration to despairing Israel in exile.

qs.q: How does Habakkuk's spiritual trajectory evolve from Habakkuk 1 to Habakkuk 3?
o: From questioning divine justice in using Babylon to triumphant trust in God's ultimate sovereignty
From national pride to advocating complete surrender to Chaldean idolatry
From active priesthood to total abandonment of prophetic ministry
From military defense to establishing a monastic community at Mount Seir
qs.e: Habakkuk begins perplexed by God using wicked Babylon (Hab 1) but concludes with unwavering faith in God despite total material loss (Hab 3:17-19).

qs.q: In Romans 3:25, what does Paul mean when he describes Christ as a propitiation (hilasterion)?
o: Christ satisfied God's holy justice and turned away divine wrath through His sacrificial blood
Christ provided an example of moral martyr courage for political reformers
Christ restored levitical ritual purity to the earthly temple in Jerusalem
Christ granted universal salvation without requiring repentance or faith
qs.e: Romans 3:25 refers to Christ as the propitiatory sacrifice (mercy seat) through whom divine justice is satisfied and wrath appeased by faith in His blood.

qs.q: What is the primary theological argument in Galatians 3 regarding the relationship between the Law and the Abrahamic promise?
o: The Law, given 430 years later, cannot annul or alter God's prior grace covenant with Abraham
The Law completely abolished the covenant of promise made to Abraham
The Abrahamic promise was temporary until Moses instituted ritual laws
The Law granted salvation whereas Abraham's promise conferred only land
qs.e: Galatians 3:17 proves that the Mosaic Law introduced 430 years later does not set aside or invalidate the covenant previously confirmed by God to Abraham.

qs.q: In Philippians 2:5-11, what profound christological truth is conveyed by Christ's kenosis (self-emptying)?
o: Though existing in the form of God, He voluntarily humbled Himself to servant status and death on the cross
He temporarily shed His divine identity and ceased to be God while on earth
He emptied Himself of moral perfection to experience human sinfulness
He refused earthly kingship solely to pursue academic scholarship in Rome
qs.e: Philippians 2:6-8 details how Christ, being in the form of God, made Himself of no reputation, taking the form of a bondservant and humbling Himself unto death.

qs.q: What creatures did God bring forth on the fifth day of creation according to Genesis 1?
qs.e: Genesis 1:20-23 records that on the fifth day God created sea creatures and winged birds to fill the waters and skies.

qs.q: Where did God command Abraham to take Isaac to offer him as a burnt offering in Genesis 22?
qs.e: In Genesis 22:2, God commanded Abraham to take Isaac to the land of Moriah and offer him upon one of the mountains.

qs.q: Whose dreams did Joseph interpret while imprisoned in Egypt according to Genesis 40?
o: Pharaoh's chief cupbearer and chief baker
qs.e: Genesis 40 describes Joseph interpreting the dreams of Pharaoh's chief butler (cupbearer) and chief baker while in prison.

qs.q: What final catastrophic plague convinced Pharaoh to let the Israelites depart from Egypt?
qs.e: Exodus 12:29-31 details the tenth plague, the death of all firstborn in Egypt, which prompted Pharaoh to immediately release Israel.

qs.q: What was the secret source of Samson's supernatural physical strength as a Nazirite in Judges?
o: His uncut hair as a sign of his consecration to God
His heavy iron armor and sword
Special herbal food provided by Delilah
A sacred amulet worn around his neck
qs.e: Judges 16:17 states Samson revealed that no razor had ever touched his head because he was a Nazirite dedicated to God from birth.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Sower, what happened to the seeds that fell on good ground?
o: They yielded a rich harvest of thirty, sixty, or a hundredfold
They were eaten by birds of the air
They withered quickly under the hot sun
They were choked by surrounding thorns
qs.e: Matthew 13:8 explains that seed sown on good soil produced a abundant crop, some a hundred, sixty, or thirty times what was sown.

qs.q: What was the first miracle performed by Jesus recorded in the Gospel of John at Cana of Galilee?
o: Turning water into wine at a wedding feast
qs.e: John 2:1-11 records Jesus changing water into wine at Cana, describing it as the beginning of His miraculous signs.

qs.q: Why did God bless the seventh day and make it holy in Genesis 2?
o: Because on that day He rested from all His work of creation
To establish a day for agricultural trade in Eden
Because Adam and Eve were created on that day
To commemorate the victory over darkness
qs.e: Genesis 2:3 states God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it because in it He rested from all His work which God created and made.

qs.q: Why was Moses told to remove his sandals at the burning bush in Exodus 3?
o: Because the ground where he stood was holy due to God's presence
To follow ancient Midianite shepherd customs
Because his sandals were made of Egyptian leather
To prepare for an immediate ritual cleansing bath
qs.e: Exodus 3:5 records God instructing Moses to take off his sandals because the place where he was standing was holy ground.

qs.q: Why did Gideon put out a fleece of wool on the threshing floor in Judges 6?
o: To confirm God's promise that He would save Israel through him
To prepare a warm blanket for the Israelite altar
To measure the night humidity in the Valley of Jezreel
To barter for weapons with the Midianites
qs.e: Judges 6:36-40 records Gideon requesting signs with the fleece to be assured that God would deliver Israel by his hand.

qs.q: When God appeared to Solomon in a dream at Gibeon, what did Solomon ask for?
o: An understanding heart to judge God's people and discern good from evil
Long life, vast wealth, and military victory over enemies
A grand palace exceeding the glory of Egypt
The immediate destruction of all rival nations
qs.e: 1 Kings 3:9 shows Solomon requesting wisdom and an understanding heart to govern Israel wisely, which pleased the Lord.

qs.q: Why did Jeroboam I erect golden calves at Bethel and Dan after the kingdom split?
o: To prevent the northern tribes from traveling to Jerusalem to worship
Because the northern tribes had converted to Egyptian religion
To fulfill a prophetic instruction given by Ahijah
qs.e: 1 Kings 12:26-28 explains Jeroboam feared allegiance would return to Rehoboam if the northern kingdom continued worshiping in Jerusalem.

qs.q: How did Elisha assist the poor widow of a prophet who was threatened by creditors in 2 Kings 4?
o: He miraculously multiplied her single jar of oil to pay her debts
He gave her silver coins from the royal treasury
He commanded the creditors to forgive all debts under Mosaic law
He found employment for her sons in Samaria
qs.e: 2 Kings 4:1-7 records Elisha multiplying the widow's small oil supply so she could sell it, pay off her debts, and support her family.

qs.q: What message did the angel Gabriel deliver to Mary at the Annunciation in Luke 1?
o: She would conceive by the Holy Spirit and give birth to the Son of the Highest
She would travel to Jerusalem to marry a priest
Her son would lead a rebellion against Roman authority
She was to remain in Nazareth until Bethlehem was rebuilt
qs.e: Luke 1:31-35 describes Gabriel announcing to Mary that she would conceive Jesus through the Holy Spirit and He would reign forever.

qs.q: In the Sermon on the Mount, why does Jesus describe His disciples as 'the salt of the earth'?
o: They are called to exert a preserving and purifying moral influence in society
They are expected to accumulate material riches for the church
They should isolate themselves from non-believers
They must practice ceremonial washings daily
qs.e: Matthew 5:13 uses salt as a metaphor for believers preserving moral purity and adding divine flavor to a corrupt world.

qs.q: How did the friends of the paralytic man demonstrate faith in Luke 5 when bringing him to Jesus?
o: They uncovered the roof and lowered his bed into the crowded room
They confronted the Pharisees in public debate
They offered money to the disciples for a private healing session
They carried him on a three-day journey to Jerusalem
qs.e: Luke 5:18-20 highlights their determination and faith in overcoming the crowd by letting the paralytic down through the tiles.

qs.q: For what price did Judas Iscariot agree to betray Jesus to the chief priests?
qs.e: Matthew 26:15 records Judas agreeing to hand over Jesus to the chief priests for thirty pieces of silver.

qs.q: What visible sign accompanied the outpouring of the Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost in Acts 2?
o: Divided tongues as of fire appearing on the believers
A pillar of cloud overshadowing the upper room
A sudden earthquake opening the prison doors
A flash of blinding lightning from heaven
qs.e: Acts 2:3 describes divided tongues as of fire resting on each of them as the Holy Spirit came upon the gathered believers.

qs.q: What dramatic event led to Saul's conversion on the road to Damascus in Acts 9?
o: A sudden light from heaven shone and the risen Jesus spoke to him
An angel struck him with physical blindness in a synagogue
He heard Stephen preaching in Damascus
A prophet named Agabus confronted him at the city gates
qs.e: Acts 9:3-5 details Saul being surrounded by heavenly light and hearing Jesus say, 'Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?'.

qs.q: Why did Rebekah arrange for Jacob to receive Isaac's patriarchal blessing instead of Esau?
o: She recalled God's prophecy that the elder brother would serve the younger
She wanted Jacob to inherit Esau's hunting bows and arrows
Isaac had commanded her to select his spiritual successor
Esau had moved permanently to Egypt
qs.e: Genesis 25:23 foresaw that the older would serve the younger; Rebekah acted on this divine revelation when Isaac prepared to bless Esau.

qs.q: What strategic policy did Joseph implement in Egypt to prepare for the seven years of famine?
o: Storing one-fifth of the grain crop during seven years of abundance
Importing wheat from Canaan and Syria on credit
Mandating that all citizens convert to agricultural labor
Exporting Egyptian cattle to neighboring lands
qs.e: Genesis 41:34-36 details Joseph advising Pharaoh to collect twenty percent of the harvest during the good years to survive the coming famine.

qs.q: Why did God command Moses to make a bronze serpent and set it on a pole in Numbers 21?
o: So that anyone bitten by fiery serpents who looked at it would live
To serve as a military standard against Edomite forces
To replace the ark of the covenant during desert marches
To symbolize God's judgment upon Pharaoh's magicians
qs.e: Numbers 21:8-9 explains that looking upon the bronze serpent provided God's remedy for those bitten by venomous snakes.

qs.q: What tragic event resulted from Jephthah's rash vow before fighting the Ammonites in Judges 11?
o: He felt bound to offer his only daughter after she met him first upon his return
His army refused to fight against Ammon
He lost his leadership post over Gilead
The priests at Shiloh excommunicated him
qs.e: Judges 11:30-39 records Jephthah vowing to offer whatever came out of his house first, which turned out to be his only child.

qs.q: Why did David refuse to strike King Saul when he had the opportunity in the cave at En-gedi?
o: He respected Saul as the LORD's anointed and trusted God for vindication
He feared a mutiny among his six hundred followers
Saul was accompanied by a powerful Philistine guard
David had sworn a sacred non-aggression pact with Abner
qs.e: 1 Samuel 24:6 records David saying he would not stretch out his hand against his master because he was the anointed of the LORD.

qs.q: How did the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite symbolize the coming division of Solomon's kingdom in 1 Kings 11?
o: He tore his new garment into twelve pieces and gave ten to Jeroboam
He broke two clay jars before the elders of Jerusalem
He poured water on twelve stones at Shiloh
He extinguished ten lamps in the temple sanctuary
qs.e: 1 Kings 11:30-31 describes Ahijah tearing his garment into twelve pieces, offering ten to Jeroboam to represent ten tribes.

qs.q: Why did Elijah confront King Ahab in Naboth's vineyard in 1 Kings 21?
o: Because Ahab murdered Naboth and seized his inherited land unjustly
Because Ahab established Baal altars inside the vineyard
Because Naboth was a levitical priest serving under Elijah
Because Ahab sold the vineyard to Syrian traders
qs.e: 1 Kings 21:17-19 records Elijah delivering divine judgment against Ahab for orchestrating Naboth's murder to take his ancestral vineyard.

qs.q: When Job lost his children, wealth, and health, what was his faithful spiritual response in Job 1?
o: He worshipped God, stating 'The LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away'
He cursed his birthday and denounced his ancestral tribe
He blamed his friends for bringing spiritual curses
He demanded immediate financial compensation from God
qs.e: Job 1:20-21 shows Job falling to the ground in worship and declaring, 'Blessed be the name of the LORD', refusing to sin.

qs.q: What spiritual response did Isaiah give when he saw the vision of God's holiness in Isaiah 6?
o: He confessed his unclean lips and responded 'Here am I; send me'
He fled from the temple in terror toward Tarshish
He requested twelve legions of angels to guard Judah
He argued that he was too young to speak to kings
qs.e: Isaiah 6:5-8 records Isaiah confessing his sinfulness, receiving cleansing by a live coal, and willingly answering God's call.

qs.q: What fundamental moral summary of God's requirements is stated in Micah 6:8?
o: To do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God
To offer thousand rams and ten thousand rivers of oil
To enforce civil laws with absolute military severity
To build grand sanctuaries across all cities of Judah
qs.e: Micah 6:8 clearly summarizes true religion: doing justice, loving lovingkindness/mercy, and walking humbly with God.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Good Samaritan, who proved to be a true neighbor to the wounded traveler?
o: The Samaritan who showed active mercy and care regardless of ethnic boundaries
The priest who passed by quickly to maintain ceremonial purity
The Levite who inspected the victim before continuing his journey
The Roman soldier who reported the crime to local magistrates
qs.e: Luke 10:33-37 demonstrates that neighborly love is defined by practical mercy toward anyone in need, exemplified by the Samaritan.

qs.q: Why was the resurrection of Lazarus in John 11 a pivotal miracle in Jesus' public ministry?
o: It demonstrated Jesus' divine power over death while prompting the chief priests to plot His execution
It led directly to Jesus being crowned earthly king in Samaria
It convinced Pontius Pilate to release all Galilean prisoners
It caused the Sanhedrin to abolish temple sacrifices
qs.e: John 11:43-53 shows Lazarus raised after four days, demonstrating Jesus as the Resurrection and Life, which triggered the ruling council's plot.

qs.q: What happened when Peter denied knowing Jesus three times during the Lord's trial?
o: The rooster crowed, and Peter remembered Jesus' word and wept bitterly
Peter was immediately arrested and placed in Roman chains
The high priest banished Peter from Jerusalem
Peter fled to Galilee to resume his fishing business permanently
qs.e: Luke 22:60-62 describes the rooster crowing, Jesus looking at Peter, and Peter going out to weep bitterly in deep remorse.

qs.q: How did Philip minister to the Ethiopian eunuch traveling on the Gaza road in Acts 8?
o: He explained the messianic prophecy in Isaiah 53 and baptized him upon his confession of faith
He persuaded him to bring financial tithes to the Jerusalem church
He warned him against reading Old Testament scriptures in public
He invited him to meet the apostles in Samaria
qs.e: Acts 8:30-38 describes Philip preaching Jesus starting from Isaiah 53, leading to the eunuch's faith and immediate baptism.

qs.q: In Romans 3:28, what is Paul's central conclusion concerning human justification?
o: A person is justified by faith apart from the deeds of the law
Justification is achieved by combining ceremonial obedience with good works
Only levitical descendants receive justification through divine covenant
Works of the law are sufficient for justification without personal faith
qs.e: Romans 3:28 explicitly concludes that man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law, emphasizing grace.

qs.q: What historic proclamation did Cyrus king of Persia make in Ezra 1 regarding the Jewish exiles?
o: He authorized the exiles to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the house of the LORD
He ordered all exiles to integrate permanently into Persian cities
He declared Persian deities superior to all national gods
He demanded that temple treasures be kept in Babylon indefinitely
qs.e: Ezra 1:1-4 details King Cyrus' decree fulfilling Jeremiah's prophecy by permitting the Jews to return and rebuild the Jerusalem temple.

qs.q: What ultimate conclusion regarding human existence is reached in Ecclesiastes 12:13?
o: Fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole duty of man
Pursue intellectual philosophy and physical pleasure above all else
Accumulate vast earthly possessions to secure future generations
Avoid all social responsibilities and live in isolated reflection
qs.e: Ecclesiastes 12:13 concludes the preacher's search by declaring that fearing God and keeping His commandments is man's all-encompassing duty.

qs.q: Why did Jeremiah purchase a field in Anathoth while Jerusalem was besieged by Babylonians in Jeremiah 32?
o: To demonstrate prophetic confidence that houses and fields would again be bought in the land
To profit from falling real estate prices during wartime
Because the king of Judah forced him to buy levitical land
To build a secret refuge for the remaining prophets
qs.e: Jeremiah 32:15 records God commanding Jeremiah to buy the field as a tangible sign of promise that restoration would surely follow exile.

qs.q: What prophetic vision in Joel 2:28 was quoted by Peter on the Day of Pentecost in Acts 2?
o: God pouring out His Spirit on all flesh, leading to prophecy and spiritual renewal
A severe locust swarm destroying the fields of the ungodly
The rebuilding of Solomon's temple by foreign kings
The permanent cessation of all miraculous signs in Israel
qs.e: Acts 2:16-18 quotes Joel 2:28-29, pointing to the Pentecost outpouring as the fulfillment of God pouring out His Spirit on all people.

qs.q: In the Sermon on the Mount, how does Jesus reinterpret the traditional command 'An eye for an eye'?
o: He commands His followers not to resist an evil person but to turn the other cheek
He requires double financial damages for personal injuries
He instructs believers to appeal immediately to Roman courts
He limits retaliation to exact physical compensation
qs.e: Matthew 5:38-39 contrasts legalistic retaliation with Christ's call to non-vengeance, patience, and overcoming evil with good.

qs.q: What spiritual lesson is conveyed by Jesus' agony and prayer in the Garden of Gethsemane?
o: Complete submission of human will to the Father's sovereign redemptive plan
Avoidance of physical suffering whenever possible
Reliance on human disciples for spiritual protection
qs.e: Luke 22:42 illustrates Christ's total obedience: 'Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done'.

qs.q: Why were Ananias and Sapphira severely judged in Acts 5?
o: They lied to the Holy Spirit by deceptively withholding part of their land sale proceeds
They refused to allow apostles into their household
They traded with pagan merchants in Samaria
They publicly denied Christ's resurrection before elders
qs.e: Acts 5:3-4 shows Peter confronting Ananias for hypocritically pretending to give the full amount while lying to God the Holy Spirit.

qs.q: What main truth did Peter learn from his vision of the sheet with unclean animals at Joppa in Acts 10?
o: God has declared Gentiles clean and welcomed into the gospel covenant without Jewish ritual laws
Believers should adopt strict vegetarian dietary habits
Levitical food laws were reinstated for all apostles
Angels bring spiritual food directly to faithful ministers
qs.e: Acts 10:28 records Peter acknowledging: 'God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean', opening salvation to Gentiles.

qs.q: What resulted when Paul and Silas prayed and sang hymns at midnight in the Philippian jail in Acts 16?
o: A great earthquake opened prison doors, leading to the conversion of the jailer and his household
The Roman magistrate arrived personally to set them free with honor
A violent mob stormed the prison and released all prisoners
The guards fled in terror leaving the city undefended
qs.e: Acts 16:25-34 records the miraculous earthquake, Paul saving the jailer from suicide, and preaching the gospel to his family.

qs.q: In Galatians 5:22-23, how does Paul describe the essential character evidence of a Spirit-led life?
o: The fruit of the Spirit: love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance
Strict adherence to dietary laws and new moon festivals
Accumulation of ecclesiastical titles and administrative power
The capability to perform public political debate in synagogues
qs.e: Galatians 5:22-23 contrasts fleshly desires with the ninefold spiritual character produced in believers by the Holy Spirit.

qs.q: In 1 Peter 2:9, how does Peter describe the identity and purpose of the Christian community?
o: A chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, called to show forth God's praises
An elite political council established to rule earthly governments
A secluded monastic group avoiding all contact with society
A temporary organization operating until the Jerusalem temple is restored
qs.e: 1 Peter 2:9 affirms the exalted spiritual position of believers as God's special people called to declare His wonderful works.

qs.q: In Daniel 7:13-14, what messianic figure is depicted receiving an everlasting kingdom from the Ancient of Days?
o: One like the Son of Man coming with the clouds of heaven
A temporal king of the Hasmonean dynasty
The archangel Michael dressed in royal robes
A restored levitical high priest residing in Zion
qs.e: Daniel 7:13-14 presents 'one like the Son of Man' receiving dominion, glory, and an everlasting kingdom, a title Jesus frequently applied to Himself.

qs.q: What double aspect of messianic ministry is foretold in Malachi 3:1-3?
o: Sending a messenger to prepare the way, followed by the Lord purifying the sons of Levi like gold and silver
Rebuilding the city walls of Jerusalem while defeating the Edomites in battle
Abolishing all civil law while granting temporal wealth to Israel
Establishing a physical throne in Babylon while closing the temple
qs.e: Malachi 3:1-3 prophesies the forerunner (John the Baptist) and the Lord coming to His temple to refine and purify His worshipers.

qs.q: In Romans 8:29-30, what sequence outlines God's sovereign redemptive chain for believers?
qs.e: Romans 8:29-30 presents the unbroken chain of divine salvation: whom He foreknew, He predestined, called, justified, and glorified.

qs.q: In Ephesians 6:10-18, why does Paul instruct believers to put on the whole armor of God?
o: To stand firm against spiritual wickedness in high places rather than wrestling against flesh and blood
To prepare for military conquest against political oppressors
To earn spiritual salvation through personal ascetic discipline
To establish civil authority over Roman officials in Ephesus
qs.e: Ephesians 6:12 clarifies that the believer's struggle is spiritual, requiring divine armor to resist demonic schemes.

qs.q: In James 2:14-26, how does James harmonize true saving faith with active good works?
o: Genuine faith is demonstrated and completed by works, whereas faith without works is dead
Works provide justification prior to faith in God
Faith is unnecessary if a person performs humanitarian acts
Works are required only for Old Testament believers
qs.e: James 2:17 & 22 teaches that faith, if it has not works, is dead in itself, pointing out that Abraham's faith was perfected by his actions.

qs.q: Which Old Testament prophet declared that a virgin would conceive and bear a son named Immanuel?
qs.e: Isaiah 7:14 prophesies that the Lord Himself shall give a sign: 'Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel'.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Mustard Seed, what characteristic feature of the kingdom of God is emphasized?
o: It begins from tiny origins and expands into a great kingdom
It remains hidden and inaccessible to all humans
It causes immediate destruction to surrounding nations
It produces fruit only in the desert regions
qs.e: Matthew 13:31-32 describes the mustard seed as smaller than all seeds, yet growing into a large tree where birds can nest, illustrating kingdom growth.

qs.q: How many loaves of bread and fish did Jesus use to miraculously feed the five thousand men in the wilderness?
qs.e: Matthew 14:17-21 records Jesus taking five loaves and two fish, blessing them, and feeding five thousand men besides women and children.

qs.q: What symbolic act did Pontius Pilate perform before the crowd to disclaim responsibility for Jesus' condemnation?
o: He washed his hands in water
qs.e: Matthew 27:24 records Pilate taking water and washing his hands before the multitude, saying, 'I am innocent of the blood of this just person'.

qs.q: In which Syrian city were the disciples of Jesus first called 'Christians' according to Acts 11?
qs.e: Acts 11:26 states explicitly that 'the disciples were called Christians first in Antioch'.

qs.q: Where were Peter and John going when they healed the lame man in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth?
o: Into the Temple at the hour of prayer, being the ninth hour
To the Roman governor's palace in Caesarea
qs.e: Acts 3:1 records Peter and John going up together into the temple at the ninth hour of prayer when they encountered the lame man.

qs.q: Who was chosen as Paul's chief missionary companion during his first missionary journey in Acts 13?
qs.e: Acts 13:2-4 records the Holy Spirit setting apart Barnabas and Saul (Paul) for the work of their first missionary journey.

qs.q: Why did God create woman from Adam's rib in Genesis 2?
o: To provide a suitable helper and companion so man would not be alone
Because man lacked physical strength to tend the garden alone
To establish a legal priesthood over Eden
Because animals refused to inhabit the garden
qs.e: Genesis 2:18 & 21-22 explains that God saw it was not good for man to be alone and created woman as a suitable helper.

qs.q: What supreme lesson of faith did Abraham demonstrate when prepared to sacrifice Isaac in Genesis 22?
o: Absolute trust in God's faithfulness and provision even when promises seemed endangered
Desire to win public acclaim among Canaanite neighbors
Reluctance to pass on his inheritance to his son
Blind obedience to local pagan customs
qs.e: Genesis 22:12 & Hebrews 11:17-19 highlight Abraham's unwavering faith that God was able to raise Isaac even from the dead.

qs.q: On what medium were the Ten Commandments originally recorded by God for Moses at Mount Sinai?
o: Two stone tablets written with the finger of God
Parchment scrolls sealed with royal wax
Golden sheets carried in the ark
qs.e: Exodus 31:18 describes God giving Moses two tablets of testimony, stone tablets written with the finger of God.

qs.q: Why did David select five smooth stones from the brook before facing Goliath in 1 Samuel 17?
o: As effective ammunition for his sling, trusting in the name of the LORD
To build an emergency altar on the battlefield
Because military armor was strictly forbidden by Samuel
To demonstrate his skill in ancient archery
qs.e: 1 Samuel 17:40 & 45 shows David taking smooth stones for his sling while declaring that he came against Goliath in the name of the LORD of hosts.

qs.q: How was Elijah taken up into heaven at the end of his earthly ministry in 2 Kings 2?
o: In a whirlwind accompanied by a chariot and horses of fire
In a gentle cloud during an altar sacrifice
By an angelic host during a battle with Syria
Through a sudden earthquake at Mount Horeb
qs.e: 2 Kings 2:11 records a chariot of fire and horses of fire separating Elijah and Elisha, and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.

qs.q: Why were Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego thrown into Nebuchadnezzar's fiery furnace in Daniel 3?
o: They refused to bow down and worship King Nebuchadnezzar's golden image
They stole royal treasures from the temple of Babylon
They refused to pay annual civil taxes to the king
They organized a political rebellion among Jewish captives
qs.e: Daniel 3:12-18 details their steadfast refusal to worship the golden statue, declaring allegiance to the true God alone.

qs.q: How were the Magi guided to find the young child Jesus in Bethlehem according to Matthew 2?
o: By a miraculous star that appeared in the East and went before them
By an official decree issued by King Herod
By a vision given to the chief priests in Jerusalem
By a map provided by Roman governors
qs.e: Matthew 2:1-9 describes the wise men following the star which led them to the place where the young child was.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son, how did the father respond when his repentant son returned home?
o: He ran, embraced him, kissed him, and ordered a joyful celebration feast
He made him a hired servant for seven years as restitution
He forced him to reside outside the family estate
He demanded that he repay all squandered inheritance first
qs.e: Luke 15:20-24 records the father's compassionate welcome, bestowing a robe, ring, shoes, and killing the fatted calf in celebration.

qs.q: What reaction did the disciples have when they saw Jesus walking on the Sea of Galilee during a storm?
o: They were terrified, thinking He was a ghost, until He reassured them
They immediately jumped into the sea to swim to Him
They criticized Him for putting Himself in danger
They mistook Him for a Roman rescue boat
qs.e: Matthew 14:26-27 records that the disciples were troubled, saying 'It is a spirit!', but Jesus said, 'Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid'.

qs.q: Who were the first witnesses to find the empty tomb on the first day of the week in Luke 24?
o: Mary Magdalene and other women carrying burial spices
Peter and John arriving with Roman soldiers
The chief priests inspecting the tomb seal
qs.e: Luke 24:1-3 describes the women arriving early at the tomb with spices, finding the stone rolled away and the tomb empty.

qs.q: Why was Stephen executed by the Jewish council in Acts 7?
o: Because he boldly testified against their spiritual blindness and proclaimed Jesus at God's right hand
Because he stole levitical offerings from the temple treasury
Because he led an armed uprising in Judea
Because he refused to pay Roman imperial taxes
qs.e: Acts 7:54-60 describes the council's fury at Stephen's witness, resulting in him being cast out of the city and stoned.

qs.q: In Ephesians 6:2-3, what unique blessing is attached to the commandment 'Honor thy father and mother'?
o: That it may be well with thee and thou mayest live long on the earth
That thou shalt inherit double material wealth in Israel
That thou shalt be appointed a leader in the church
That thy sins will automatically be forgiven without sacrifice
qs.e: Ephesians 6:2-3 notes this is the first commandment with a promise: 'That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth'.

qs.q: How did Jacob obtain Esau's rights as firstborn son in Genesis 25?
o: By trading a dish of red lentil stew to famished Esau in exchange for his birthright
By defeating Esau in a wrestling match at Peniel
By purchasing Esau's hunting bows with silver coins
By receiving an official ruling from Isaac in public court
qs.e: Genesis 25:29-34 details Esau despising his birthright and selling it to Jacob for a meal of bread and pottage of lentils.

qs.q: Why did Joseph order his silver cup to be hidden in Benjamin's sack in Genesis 44?
o: To test whether his brothers had truly repented and would protect Benjamin
To frame Benjamin so he could retain him as a slave permanently
To enrich his brothers before sending them home to Canaan
To fulfill an Egyptian legal requirement for foreign travelers
qs.e: Genesis 44 shows Joseph testing his brothers' character to see if they would sacrifice Benjamin as they had done to him years earlier.

qs.q: What administrative counsel did Jethro offer Moses in Exodus 18 to prevent exhaustion?
o: Appoint trustworthy leaders over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens to judge minor matters
Transfer all judicial decisions to the levitical priests
Disband the assembly of elders and rule by absolute decree
Require citizens to resolve disputes without judicial intervention
qs.e: Exodus 18:21-22 records Jethro advising Moses to delegate lesser cases to capable, God-fearing leaders, preserving Moses' strength.

qs.q: How was Sisera, commander of Jabin's army, killed after fleeing the battlefield in Judges 4?
o: Jael drove a tent peg through his temple while he slept in her tent
Deborah defeated him in single combat on Mount Tabor
Barak captured him in the Kishon valley
His own soldiers turned against him in retreat
qs.e: Judges 4:21 describes Jael taking a tent peg and wooden hammer and driving it into Sisera's temple while he was fast asleep.

qs.q: Why did Samuel rebuke King Saul severely at Gilgal in 1 Samuel 13?
o: Saul presumed to offer the burnt offering himself instead of waiting for Samuel
Saul fled from the Philistines without offering sacrifices
Saul appointed non-levitical priests at Shiloh
Saul dismantled the sacred altar at Gilgal
qs.e: 1 Samuel 13:8-14 shows Saul panicking and illegally offering sacrifices, leading Samuel to declare that Saul's kingdom would not endure.

qs.q: What sign occurred when Jeroboam stretch out his hand against the man of God from Judah at Bethel?
o: His hand withered instantly so he could not pull it back, and the altar split apart
Fire fell from heaven and consumed Jeroboam's sacrifice
A sudden earthquake destroyed the golden calf
Jeroboam was struck with physical blindness
qs.e: 1 Kings 13:4-5 describes Jeroboam's hand drying up when he ordered the prophet's arrest, confirming God's judgment.

qs.q: What instructions did Elisha give to Naaman the Syrian commander for the healing of his leprosy?
o: Go and wash seven times in the Jordan River
Offer seven bulls on Mount Carmel
Travel to Jerusalem to be cleansed by high priests
Drink holy water from the well of Samaria
qs.e: 2 Kings 5:10 records Elisha sending a messenger telling Naaman to wash seven times in the Jordan so his flesh would be restored.

qs.q: In Proverbs 6:6, to what creature does the sage direct the lazy person for a lesson in industry?
qs.e: Proverbs 6:6 admonishes: 'Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise', praising her self-motivated diligence.

qs.q: What truth did God reveal to Jeremiah regarding his prophetic calling in Jeremiah 1:5?
o: Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee, and ordained thee a prophet unto the nations
Thou shalt receive royal power over the house of David
Thy prophetic ministry will bring immediate peace to Jerusalem
Thou art chosen because of thy great military skill
qs.e: Jeremiah 1:5 emphasizes divine foreknowledge and sovereign appointment prior to Jeremiah's birth.

qs.q: Why did Jonah attempt to flee to Tarshish rather than go to Nineveh as God commanded?
o: He knew God was gracious and feared Nineveh would repent and escape judgment
He feared Nineveh's military forces would execute him on arrival
He lacked financial resources to make the journey overland
He believed prophetic ministry was restricted to the land of Israel
qs.e: Jonah 4:2 reveals Jonah's motive: he knew God was a gracious God, merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in lovingkindness.

qs.q: In the Sermon on the Mount, what spiritual focus does Jesus advocate concerning treasure?
o: Lay up treasures in heaven where neither moth nor rust destroys, for where your treasure is, your heart is
Accumulate earthly wealth to finance synagogue activities
Store gold in Jerusalem temple vaults for safekeeping
Trade goods continuously to maximize profit for charity
qs.e: Matthew 6:19-21 instructs disciples to prioritize heavenly, eternal treasures over earthly, perishable riches.

qs.q: What core principle of stewardship is illustrated in the Parable of the Talents in Matthew 25?
o: Faithful multiplication of God-given abilities brings commendation, while slothful neglect brings condemnation
Equal distribution of material wealth must be enforced by church leaders
Financial risk-taking is forbidden under divine law
Unused resources are automatically forgiven by the master
qs.e: Matthew 25:14-30 shows the master rewarding servants who productively used their talents and punishing the unprofitable, lazy servant.

qs.q: What miracle did Peter perform in Joppa recorded in Acts 9?
o: He raised Dorcas (Tabitha), a woman full of good works, from the dead
He healed the Roman centurion Cornelius of paralysis
He blinded Simon the sorcerer for offering money
He opened prison doors through prayer
qs.e: Acts 9:36-41 records Peter praying by Dorcas' body and saying 'Tabitha, arise', whereupon she opened her eyes and sat up.

qs.q: How did Paul use an Athenian altar inscription in Acts 17 to introduce the true God to the Areopagus?
o: He referenced the altar 'TO THE UNKNOWN GOD' to proclaim the Creator who does not dwell in man-made temples
He commended their pagan worship as equal to Christian faith
He ordered the immediate destruction of all Athenian monuments
He quoted only levitical legal texts to non-Jewish philosophers
qs.e: Acts 17:22-24 shows Paul taking the altar inscription 'TO THE UNKNOWN GOD' as a point of contact to preach the Creator of heaven and earth.

qs.q: In Ephesians 2:8-9, how does Paul define the relationship between faith, grace, and human effort in salvation?
o: By grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast
Salvation is earned through meticulous adherence to Mosaic ritual laws
Faith is a human work that obligates God to grant eternal life
Grace is granted only after a person completes righteous deeds
qs.e: Ephesians 2:8-9 explicitly teaches that salvation is an unearned gift of divine grace accessed through faith, ruling out self-boasting.

qs.q: What religious reforms did King Asa carry out in Judah according to 1 Kings 15 and 2 Chronicles 14?
o: He removed pagan altars, destroyed idols, and commanded Judah to seek the LORD
He rebuilt the golden calves in Dan and Bethel
He banned levitical sacrifices in the Jerusalem temple
He established military treaties with Syria to replace faith
qs.e: 2 Chronicles 14:2-5 records Asa doing what was good and right, taking away foreign altars and high places, and breaking down sacred pillars.

qs.q: How did Ezra lead a spiritual renewal among the returned Jewish exiles in Nehemiah 8?
o: By publicly reading and clearly explaining the Book of the Law of Moses to all the people
By organizing an army to conquer neighboring Samaritan towns
By ordering the immediate construction of a new royal palace
By enforcing mandatory military service for all Levites
qs.e: Nehemiah 8:1-8 describes Ezra the scribe reading the Law from morning till midday while Levites helped the people understand the meaning.

qs.q: What lesson regarding divine sovereignty over nations did Jeremiah observe at the potter's house in Jeremiah 18?
o: Just as the potter reshapes marred clay, God has absolute authority to mold, spare, or judge nations according to their response
The material quality of clay determines the potter's ultimate success
God cannot alter His pronounced judgments regardless of national repentance
Pottery making is a sacred levitical duty restricted to priests
qs.e: Jeremiah 18:1-10 uses the potter shaping clay to illustrate God's sovereign freedom to relent of judgment if a nation repents.

qs.q: Why did the prophet Amos condemn Israel's religious festivals in Amos 5:21-24?
o: Because their solemn assemblies were accompanied by social injustice and oppression of the poor
Because they failed to burn sufficient animal fat on the altars
Because they conducted worship outside the city walls of Samaria
Because they allowed foreign merchants to participate in feasts
qs.e: Amos 5:21-24 declares God hates their feast days when unaccompanied by righteousness, demanding justice to roll down like waters.

qs.q: What demonstrated the faith of the woman with the issue of blood in Mark 5?
o: She believed that merely touching the fringe of Jesus' garment would heal her
She publicly requested a spoken word of healing from the synagogue ruler
She brought expensive spices to offer the disciples
She fasted for seven days before approaching Jesus
qs.e: Mark 5:27-28 records her faith: 'If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole', resulting in immediate healing.

qs.q: What primary mandate is given in the Great Commission in Matthew 28:19-20?
o: Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them and teaching them to observe all Christ's commands
Establish political authority in Jerusalem before spreading outward
Rebuild physical temple sanctuaries across Asia Minor
Limit preaching exclusively to the lost sheep of the house of Israel
qs.e: Matthew 28:19-20 outlines Christ's universal command to make disciples worldwide, baptizing and teaching them.

qs.q: Why were seven men of honest report appointed in Acts 6?
o: To oversee the daily distribution of food to widows so the apostles could devote themselves to prayer and preaching
To serve as military guards for the Jerusalem church leaders
To collect Roman taxes from Christian households
To write official gospel accounts for foreign churches
qs.e: Acts 6:1-6 describes selecting seven Spirit-filled men to care for widow ministry, freeing apostles for prayer and the ministry of the word.

qs.q: What resulted when Philip preached Christ in the city of Samaria in Acts 8?
o: Unclean spirits were cast out, many paralytics were healed, and there was great joy in that city
The Samaritans drove Philip out of their territory
The Roman governor arrested Philip for disturbing public order
Simon the sorcerer became the head apostle of Samaria
qs.e: Acts 8:5-8 records Philip's effective ministry in Samaria marked by miracles, deliverance, and great communal joy.

qs.q: In Romans 6:3-4, what spiritual reality is signified by Christian baptism?
o: Burial with Christ into death so that just as Christ was raised, believers walk in newness of life
A ceremonial washing required to enter Jewish synagogues
An outward pledge of allegiance to Roman civil authorities
A physical ritual that guarantees immunity from earthly suffering
qs.e: Romans 6:3-4 explains baptism as identification with Christ's death and resurrection, empowering a holy life.

qs.q: How does Paul describe the unity and diversity of spiritual gifts in 1 Corinthians 12?
o: There are diversities of gifts but the same Spirit, operating like different members of one human body
Every believer must manifest identical spiritual gifts to prove salvation
Gifts are reserved exclusively for ordained apostles and prophets
Spiritual gifts create hierarchical rank within the local congregation
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 12:4-12 compares the church to a human body with diverse members working harmoniously under one Spirit.

qs.q: In Romans 12:1-2, what does Paul urge believers to present to God as spiritual service?
o: Their bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable, being transformed by the renewing of their mind
Animal sacrifices at the Jerusalem altar on major feast days
Financial riches accumulated through secular commerce
Formal legal petitions requesting exemption from Roman law
qs.e: Romans 12:1-2 calls for total personal dedication as a living sacrifice, rejecting worldly conformity for mental and moral renewal.

qs.q: What sharp rebuke did the prophet Haggai deliver to the returned exiles in Haggai 1:4?
o: Is it time for you to dwell in your paneled houses while this house of the LORD lies in ruins?
Why have you failed to build defensive military walls around Jerusalem?
Why do you continue to use Persian currency instead of levitical shekels?
Is it proper to engage in commerce on pagan feast days?
qs.e: Haggai 1:4 rebukes the returnees for self-centered luxury while neglecting the reconstruction of God's temple.

qs.q: What key spiritual principle is declared in Zechariah 4:6 regarding the completion of Zerubbabel's temple work?
o: Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit, saith the LORD of hosts
Through human wisdom and political diplomacy shall Jerusalem stand
By military conquest shall the foundation of Zion be established
Through the abundance of gold and silver shall the sanctuary be raised
qs.e: Zechariah 4:6 reassures Zerubbabel that divine task completion relies not on human strength or resources but on God's Holy Spirit.

qs.q: In 2 Corinthians 5:17-21, how does Paul describe the believer's new status and mission?
o: If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation, and God has given believers the ministry of reconciliation
Believers become sinless angelic beings exempt from physical death
The law of Moses is reinstated to govern human political structures
Believers are appointed temporal rulers over worldly kingdoms
qs.e: 2 Corinthians 5:17-18 declares that in Christ old things pass away, all things become new, and believers are entrusted with ambassadorial reconciliation.

qs.q: In Colossians 1:15-18, what supreme claims does Paul make regarding the person of Jesus Christ?
o: He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn over all creation, by whom all things were created, and head of the church
He is a exalted created angel who served as Moses' mediator at Sinai
He is a moral prophet whose teachings complement pagan philosophy
He was an earthly king whose reign ended at the Roman trial
qs.e: Colossians 1:15-18 presents a high Christology: Christ as Creator, Sustainer, divine Image, and preeminent Head of the church.

qs.q: In 1 John 4:7-12, what is identified as the supreme evidence that a person knows God?
o: Unselfish love for one another, because God is love and demonstrated His love by sending His Son
The ability to speak multiple foreign languages without study
Strict observance of levitical food restrictions
Accumulating deep academic knowledge of scripture without practical action
qs.e: 1 John 4:7-8 explicitly states: 'Beloved, let us love one another: for love is of God... He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love'.

qs.q: On which day of creation did God create land animals and make mankind in His own image according to Genesis 1?
qs.e: Genesis 1:24-31 records that on the sixth day God created land creatures and formed humanity in His own image and likeness.

qs.q: What name did Abraham give to his promised son born to Sarah in their old age?
qs.e: Genesis 21:1-3 details Sarah giving birth to Isaac as God had promised to Abraham in his old age.

qs.q: How did God provide drinking water for the thirsty Israelites at Rephidim in Exodus 17?
o: Moses struck the rock at Horeb with his staff, causing water to pour out
A sudden heavy rainstorm filled the dry wadis
The elders dug twelve fresh wells in the wilderness
An angel turned salty water into fresh water
qs.e: Exodus 17:6 records God telling Moses to strike the rock at Horeb with his rod, and water gushed out for the people to drink.

qs.q: Under what tree did the prophetess Deborah sit while judging the children of Israel in Judges 4?
o: The palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel
qs.e: Judges 4:5 describes Deborah dwelling under the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in Mount Ephraim where Israel came to her for judgment.

qs.q: What clothing and food characterized John the Baptist during his wilderness ministry in Matthew 3?
o: Camel's hair clothing with a leather belt, eating locusts and wild honey
Fine linen garments, eating unleavened bread and olives
Woolen robes, eating sheep meat and grain
Levitical priestly vestments, eating temple bread
qs.e: Matthew 3:4 describes John's raiment of camel's hair, a leathern girdle about his loins, and his meat was locusts and wild honey.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Wheat and Tares, who sowed the weeds among the good wheat?
qs.e: Matthew 13:25-28 explains that while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat and went his way.

qs.q: What inscription was written over Jesus' cross by Pontius Pilate in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin?
o: Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews
qs.e: John 19:19-20 states Pilate wrote the title: 'JESUS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE JEWS' in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin.

qs.q: Why did Joseph's brothers travel from Canaan down to Egypt in Genesis 42?
o: To buy grain during a widespread severe famine
To search for Joseph who was lost in Egypt
To trade livestock for Egyptian weapons
To pay annual tribute to Pharaoh
qs.e: Genesis 42:1-3 records Jacob sending ten of his sons down to Egypt to buy corn because the famine was severe in Canaan.

qs.q: How did God visibly lead the Israelites on their journey through the wilderness day and night in Exodus 13?
o: By a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night
By a burning torch carried by levitical priests
By an angelic army visible on the horizon
By sending a golden eagle ahead of the camp
qs.e: Exodus 13:21-22 explains that the LORD went before them by day in a pillar of cloud to lead the way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light.

qs.q: How was Saul publicly confirmed as king over Israel by Samuel at Mizpah in 1 Samuel 10?
o: By casting lots before the tribes of Israel until Saul of the tribe of Benjamin was chosen
Through a military victory over Egypt
By a vote of the elders of Judah
By building a royal palace at Shiloh
qs.e: 1 Samuel 10:20-24 describes Samuel gathering the tribes, casting lots, and identifying Saul, whereupon the people shouted 'God save the king!'.

qs.q: What harsh response did Rehoboam give to the elders of Israel when they asked for tax relief in 1 Kings 12?
o: My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to your yoke; my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions
I will reduce all taxation by half to build national unity
I will abolish the forced labor system established by Solomon
I will consult the prophets before making any economic decisions
qs.e: 1 Kings 12:14 records Rehoboam delivering this arrogant response, which alienated the ten northern tribes and caused the kingdom split.

qs.q: What miracle did Elisha perform when a prophet dropped a borrowed iron axe head into the Jordan River in 2 Kings 6?
o: He cut a stick, threw it into the water, and caused the iron axe head to float
He dove into the river and retrieved it by hand
He commanded the river water to dry up completely
He bought a new iron axe head from Syrian merchants
qs.e: 2 Kings 6:5-7 describes Elisha throwing a stick into the spot, making the iron float so the prophet could pick it up.

qs.q: What moral counsel is given in Proverbs 15:1 regarding conflict resolution?
o: A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger
Defend your honor vigorously regardless of the listener's reaction
Avoid speaking to offenders until they offer financial compensation
Answer hostility with greater harshness to demonstrate strength
qs.e: Proverbs 15:1 contrasts the calming effect of gentle speech with the destructive provocation caused by harsh words.

qs.q: What divine declaration was heard from heaven when Jesus was baptized by John in Matthew 3?
o: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased
Behold the king who will conquer Roman armies
Listen to Him for He is the chief high priest
This is the prophet predicted by Moses at Sinai
qs.e: Matthew 3:17 records the Father's voice from heaven affirming Jesus' divine sonship and pleasure.

qs.q: In the Sermon on the Mount, what encouragement does Jesus offer concerning persistence in prayer in Matthew 7?
o: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you
Pray only in public synagogues to ensure God hears
Repeat long ceremonial prayers continuously throughout the day
Fast for forty days before making any prayer request
qs.e: Matthew 7:7-8 assures believers that earnest, persistent prayer is answered by a loving heavenly Father.

qs.q: When Jesus cleansed ten lepers in Luke 17, how many returned to express gratitude to Him?
o: Only one, who was a Samaritan
Five returned while five went home
None returned because they fled to the priests
qs.e: Luke 17:15-18 notes that out of ten healed, only one—a foreigner/Samaritan—returned to fall at Jesus' feet and give thanks.

qs.q: Which apostle became the first of the Twelve to be martyred when killed by King Herod Agrippa I in Acts 12?
qs.e: Acts 12:1-2 records Herod Agrippa I executing James the brother of John with the sword.

qs.q: How was Peter miraculously rescued from prison on the night before his scheduled execution in Acts 12?
o: An angel of the Lord struck his chains off and led him past guards through locked iron gates
A sudden earthquake shook the prison foundation
Christian believers bribed the Roman prison guards
Herod Agrippa issued an unexpected royal pardon
qs.e: Acts 12:6-11 details the angel awakening Peter, making his chains fall off, and leading him safely into the city.

qs.q: Why did the citizens of Lystra attempt to offer sacrifices to Paul and Barnabas in Acts 14?
o: Because they healed a man crippled from birth and mistook them for gods (Mercury and Jupiter)
Because Paul spoke fluent Greek philosophy in the public square
Because they predicted an unexpected heavy rainstorm
Because they brought financial gifts from Antioch
qs.e: Acts 14:8-13 describes the crowd at Lystra seeing the crippled man healed and calling Barnabas Jupiter and Paul Mercury.

qs.q: What primary responsibility did God assign to Adam in Genesis 2:15 regarding the Garden of Eden?
o: To dress it and to keep it
To build city walls around it
To offer animal burnt sacrifices in it
To clear all trees to plant wheat
qs.e: Genesis 2:15 states the LORD God took the man and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it (cultivate) and to keep (guard) it.

qs.q: How did Abraham plead with God on behalf of Sodom in Genesis 18?
o: He interceded repeatedly, asking if God would spare the city if fifty down to ten righteous were found
He led a military force to evacuate righteous citizens
He offered personal sacrifices on Mount Hebron
He asked God to destroy the city immediately without warning
qs.e: Genesis 18:23-33 displays Abraham's persistent intercession for Sodom based on God's justice and mercy.

qs.q: Why was Joseph imprisoned in Egypt despite his moral innocence in Genesis 39?
o: Potiphar's wife falsely accused him of attempted assault after he refused her advances
He refused to pay taxes on Potiphar's agricultural yield
He was caught trying to escape back to Canaan
He interpreted Pharaoh's dreams without royal permission
qs.e: Genesis 39:14-20 records Potiphar's wife framing Joseph with his left-behind garment, leading to Joseph's imprisonment.

qs.q: How did Jephthah's Gileadite troops identify fleeing Ephraimites at the passages of Jordan in Judges 12?
o: They made them pronounce the word 'Shibboleth', which Ephraimites pronounced as 'Sibboleth'
By inspecting their weapons and armor design
By asking for their levitical genealogy
By demanding payment in silver coins
qs.e: Judges 12:5-6 records the famous linguistic test where Ephraimites could not frame to pronounce 'Shibboleth' correctly.

qs.q: How did the prophet Nathan convict King David of his sin regarding Bathsheba and Uriah in 2 Samuel 12?
o: He told a parable of a rich man stealing a poor man's single beloved ewe lamb, declaring 'Thou art the man!'
He brought legal charges against David in the assembly of elders
He pronounced immediate loss of the throne before foreign kings
He wrote a prophetic curse on the doorposts of the palace
qs.e: 2 Samuel 12:1-7 records Nathan using the ewe lamb parable to stir David's sense of justice before applying it directly to David.

qs.q: Why was Gehazi, Elisha's servant, struck with Naaman's leprosy in 2 Kings 5?
o: He secretly pursued Naaman and dishonestly asked for silver and garments in Elisha's name
He refused to pour water on Elisha's hands
He worshiped Syrian gods at Damascus
He revealed Israel's military secrets to Syria
qs.e: 2 Kings 5:20-27 describes Gehazi's greed and deceit, resulting in Naaman's leprosy clinging to him and his descendants.

qs.q: What report from Jerusalem caused Nehemiah to weep, fast, and pray before God in Nehemiah 1?
o: The wall of Jerusalem was broken down and its gates burned with fire, placing the survivors in distress
The temple was converted into a pagan shrine by Samaritans
The Persian king had ordered the execution of all Jewish governors
A severe drought had destroyed all crops in Judea
qs.e: Nehemiah 1:3-4 describes Hanani's report about Jerusalem's ruin, which moved Nehemiah to deep sorrow and earnest prayer.

qs.q: What spiritual breakthrough did Job experience after God spoke to him out of the whirlwind in Job 42?
o: He repented in dust and ashes, declaring 'I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee'
He demanded that God explain why his children died
He built seven new altars at Uz to offer sacrifices
He argued that his three friends were entirely correct
qs.e: Job 42:1-6 shows Job humbling himself in awe of God's unsearchable majesty and sovereign wisdom.

qs.q: What comforting message of hope did Jeremiah send to the Jewish exiles in Babylon in Jeremiah 29:11?
o: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end
God will immediately destroy Babylon within three days
Return secretly to Jerusalem without waiting for royal permission
Abandon all hope of ever returning to your ancestral land
qs.e: Jeremiah 29:11 reassures the exiles that God's overarching purpose for them is peace, restoration, and a hopeful future.

qs.q: How did Hosea's redemption of Gomer in Hosea 3 reflect God's relationship with Israel?
o: It portrayed Yahweh buying back unfaithful Israel to restore covenant love despite her idolatry
It showed that marriage covenants could be annulled by civil decree
It demonstrated that prophets were exempt from family laws
It illustrated God's permanent rejection of northern Israel
qs.e: Hosea 3:1-2 shows Hosea purchasing Gomer back, illustrating God loving Israel even while they looked to other gods.

qs.q: What warning is delivered in the Parable of the Unforgiving Servant in Matthew 18?
o: God will not extend forgiveness to those who refuse to forgive their fellow human beings from the heart
Financial debts should never be forgiven under any circumstances
Servants must pay interest on all loans granted by masters
Forgiveness is restricted to members of one's immediate family
qs.e: Matthew 18:32-35 warns that severe judgment awaits those who receive immense divine mercy yet remain harsh and unforgiving.

qs.q: What miracle occurred when Jesus commanded the unclean spirits to leave the demoniac in Gadara in Mark 5?
o: The demons entered a herd of about two thousand swine, which rushed down a steep bank into the sea and drowned
The man was immediately struck with dumbness
The city council crowned Jesus king of Decapolis
The demons transformed into birds and flew away
qs.e: Mark 5:11-13 records the demoniac healed and restored to his right mind, while the swine ran into the sea.

qs.q: What profound confession did Thomas make when he saw the resurrected Jesus in John 20?
o: Master, let us build three tabernacles!
I now believe that Thou art an angel!
qs.e: John 20:28 records Thomas seeing Jesus' hands and side, prompting his full christological confession: 'My Lord and my God!'.

qs.q: In Romans 1:16, why is Paul unashamed of the gospel of Christ?
o: Because it is the power of God unto salvation to everyone that believeth, to the Jew first and also to the Greek
Because it guarantees immediate political freedom from Rome
Because it elevates Jewish ritual law over all civil governments
Because it grants worldly prestige and material prosperity
qs.e: Romans 1:16 declares the gospel as divine power bringing universal salvation to all who believe.

qs.q: What advice did Paul give in 1 Thessalonians 5:16-18 regarding the ongoing attitude of believers?
o: Rejoice evermore. Pray without ceasing. In every thing give thanks
Fast three times a week and isolate from unbelievers
Seek public office to enforce Christian doctrine legally
Mourn continuously until Christ returns in glory
qs.e: 1 Thessalonians 5:16-18 presents three concise standing instructions for daily Christian posture in God's will.

qs.q: What obstacle faced Zerubbabel and Joshua when rebuilding the temple in Ezra 4?
o: Opposition and false accusations from neighboring adversaries seeking to stop the work
A lack of timber from the forests of Lebanon
Rejection of the project by King Cyrus of Persia
qs.e: Ezra 4:1-5 describes how the people of the land weakened the hands of Judah and hired counselors to frustrate their purpose.

qs.q: What key truth was revealed in Ezekiel's vision of the divine throne-chariot by the Chebar river in Ezekiel 1?
o: God's glory and sovereign presence are not tied to Jerusalem's temple but accompany His people in exile
The Babylonian empire was completely immune to divine judgment
Temple sacrifices were permanently required in Babylon
Ezekiel was appointed earthly king of Judah
qs.e: Ezekiel 1 shows God's mobile, majestic glory appearing in Babylon, proving Yahweh's omnipresence and care for exiles.

qs.q: Which major biblical principle quoted in Romans, Galatians, and Hebrews originates from Habakkuk 2:4?
o: The just shall live by his faith
Eye for an eye and tooth for a tooth
The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom
qs.e: Habakkuk 2:4 states 'the just shall live by his faith', a foundational verse for the New Testament doctrine of justification by faith.

qs.q: In the Sermon on the Mount, why does Jesus teach that 'Ye cannot serve God and mammon' in Matthew 6:24?
o: Devotion to wealth creates divided loyalty, making wholehearted spiritual service impossible
Wealth is inherently evil and cannot be owned by Christians
Money belongs exclusively to Caesar and cannot be blessed
Servants are forbidden from receiving financial wages
qs.e: Matthew 6:24 warns that a person will either hate one and love the other, showing that material riches and God cannot share supreme allegiance.

qs.q: What warning is emphasized in the Parable of the Wise and Foolish Virgins in Matthew 25?
o: Believers must maintain personal spiritual readiness and vigilance for Christ's return
Oil supplies should be traded only during daytime hours
Wedding feasts should be restricted to invited guests
Sharing spiritual grace with others is mandatory at all times
qs.e: Matthew 25:1-13 highlights the necessity of spiritual preparation (extra oil), concluding 'Watch therefore, for ye know neither the day nor the hour'.

qs.q: How did the early church select Matthias to replace Judas Iscariot among the Twelve in Acts 1?
o: They nominated two qualified men, prayed for divine guidance, and cast lots
Peter appointed him by apostolic decree without consulting others
The Roman governor selected him from qualified Galileans
They held a vote among all citizens of Jerusalem
qs.e: Acts 1:21-26 records setting qualifications (witness of Jesus' ministry and resurrection), praying to God who knows hearts, and casting lots.

qs.q: Why did Peter sternly rebuke Simon the Sorcerer in Samaria in Acts 8?
