o: Simon offered money to purchase the power of imparting the Holy Spirit through laying on of hands
Simon attempted to lead a Samaritan rebellion against Jerusalem
Simon refused to be baptized after hearing Philip preach
Simon claimed to be the high priest of Judea
qs.e: Acts 8:18-22 shows Peter rebuking Simon: 'Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money'.

qs.q: What famous reaction did King Agrippa II express during Paul's legal defense in Acts 26?
o: Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian
Thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad
This man deserves immediate crucifixion in Rome
Thou hast violated the sacred law of Moses
qs.e: Acts 26:28 records Agrippa saying to Paul, 'Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian' after hearing Paul's powerful gospel testimony.

qs.q: What spiritual truth did Paul learn from God regarding his 'thorn in the flesh' in 2 Corinthians 12?
o: My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness
Physical suffering proves a lack of personal faith
Angelic intervention will remove all physical afflictions immediately
Suffering is reserved only for false prophets
qs.e: 2 Corinthians 12:9 records God's response to Paul's three prayers, revealing that divine power operates most clearly through human weakness.

qs.q: In Philippians 4:11-13, what secret of contentment does Paul share with the church?
o: He has learned to be content in whatever state he is, doing all things through Christ who strengthens him
He relies on financial contributions from Macedonia to maintain peace
He avoids all challenging circumstances by fleeing persecution
He achieves inner peace through Stoic philosophical meditation
qs.e: Philippians 4:11-13 affirms Paul's Christ-centered resilience whether facing abundance or need.

qs.q: In 1 Thessalonians 4:13-18, what hope does Paul offer regarding believers who have died?
o: They will be raised first at Christ's coming and together with living believers be caught up to meet the Lord
They undergo temporary purgation before entering paradise
Their souls sleep permanently without conscious future resurrection
They are reincarnated into future generations of believers
qs.e: 1 Thessalonians 4:14-17 comforts believers with the promise of resurrection and the glorious bodily return of Christ.

qs.q: In 1 Kings 13, what remarkable prophecy was spoken against the altar at Bethel by the anonymous man of God from Judah?
o: A child named Josiah would be born to the house of David and sacrifice Jeroboam's idolatrous priests upon it
The altar would be destroyed immediately by Assyrian armies
The golden calf would melt during a supernatural lightning storm
The altar would remain untouched until the Roman conquest
qs.e: 1 Kings 13:2 specifically names Josiah 300 years before his birth, predicting he would burn the bones of pagan priests upon Jeroboam's altar.

qs.q: In Jeremiah 29:4-7, what unexpected instructions did Jeremiah send to the Jewish exiles living in Babylon?
o: Build houses, plant gardens, marry, have children, and seek the peace and welfare of Babylon
Organize a guerrilla army to overthrow Nebuchadnezzar
Refuse all economic engagement with Babylonian citizens
Flee immediately into the Arabian desert
qs.e: Jeremiah 29:4-7 instructed exiles to settle down, prosper, and pray for Babylon's peace during their seventy-year captivity.

qs.q: In Romans 11:17-24, what does Paul's illustration of the cultivated and wild olive trees teach Gentle believers?
o: Gentiles are wild olive branches grafted into Abraham's covenant tree and must not boast against the natural Jewish branches
Gentiles have permanently replaced Jewish believers in God's plan
Natural branches were broken off so Gentiles could establish a new tree
The root of the olive tree represents Roman legal traditions
qs.e: Romans 11:17-20 warns Gentile believers against spiritual arrogance, reminding them that they are supported by the patriarchal root through faith.

qs.q: In 2 Thessalonians 2:3-4, what events does Paul state must occur before the Day of the Lord arrives?
o: The apostasy (falling away) occurs first, and the man of lawlessness (son of perdition) is revealed
The Jerusalem temple is rebuilt out of gold by Roman governors
All nations convert to Christian faith through angelic preaching
The Mosaic law is reinstated worldwide by apostolic decree
qs.e: 2 Thessalonians 2:3-4 explains that Christ's return will not happen until the rebellion comes and the man of sin exalts himself above God.

qs.q: In Hebrews 12:1-2, how are believers instructed to run the Christian spiritual race?
o: Laying aside every weight and sin, running with endurance while fixing eyes upon Jesus, the author and finisher of faith
Relying on competitive human motivation to surpass fellow runners
Earning salvation through superior physical speed and athletic discipline
Avoiding all trials and conflicts along the race path
qs.e: Hebrews 12:1-2 calls believers surrounded by a cloud of witnesses to strip off impediments and focus steadfastly on Jesus.

qs.q: Where did God place Adam and Eve to live in perfect harmony and fellowship at the beginning of creation?
qs.e: Genesis 2:8 records that the LORD God planted a garden eastward in Eden and placed the man whom He had formed there.

qs.q: How many sons did Jacob father who became the patriarchs of the twelve tribes of Israel?
qs.e: Genesis 35:22-26 lists the twelve sons of Jacob, whose descendants constituted the twelve tribes of Israel.

qs.q: Who was appointed by God to serve as Moses' spokesman before Pharaoh because of his eloquence?
qs.e: Exodus 4:14-16 records God appointing Aaron the Levite to serve as Moses' mouth and spokesman.

qs.q: Which king of Israel built the glorious temple for Yahweh in Jerusalem as promised to David?
qs.e: 1 Kings 6 describes King Solomon constructing the temple of the LORD in Jerusalem over a seven-year period.

qs.q: What request did blind Bartimaeus make when Jesus called him near Jericho in Mark 10?
o: Lord, that I might receive my sight
Lord, grant me silver and gold
Lord, make me a ruler in Israel
qs.e: Mark 10:51 records Bartimaeus saying, 'Lord, that I might receive my sight', resulting in his immediate healing.

qs.q: What miraculous event occurred in the Jerusalem temple sanctuary when Jesus died on the cross?
o: The veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom
The golden altar of incense collapsed into dust
The ark of the covenant disappeared in fire
qs.e: Matthew 27:51 states that at Jesus' death, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom.

qs.q: What generous act did Barnabas perform in Acts 4 to support needy believers in Jerusalem?
o: He sold a field he owned and brought the money to lay at the apostles' feet
He donated his house in Cyprus for church meetings
He built a public soup kitchen in Samaria
He paid off all debts owed by Christian widows
qs.e: Acts 4:36-37 records Barnabas selling his land and bringing the proceeds to the apostles to distribute to those in need.

qs.q: What was the core meaning of Pharaoh's dual dreams interpreted by Joseph in Genesis 41?
o: Seven years of great agricultural abundance would be followed by seven years of severe famine
Egypt would face seven military invasions followed by seven years of peace
Pharaoh would reign for fourteen years before handing power to his son
Seven diseases would strike Egypt unless levitical sacrifices were offered
qs.e: Genesis 41:29-30 details Joseph explaining that seven years of plenty would be swallowed up by seven years of devastating famine.

qs.q: Why did Aaron build a golden calf for Israel while Moses was on Mount Sinai in Exodus 32?
o: The people pressured him when Moses delayed returning from the mountain
Pharaoh's army ordered Aaron to restore Egyptian worship
Aaron sought to usurp Moses' leadership over the wilderness camp
God commanded Aaron to test Israel's loyalty with an idol
qs.e: Exodus 32:1-4 describes the people gathering against Aaron because Moses delayed, urging him to make gods to go before them.

qs.q: How did Ehud deliver Israel from King Eglon of Moab in Judges 3?
o: He fashioned a two-edged dagger, gained a private audience, and assassinated Eglon
He led a night ambush against the Moabite camp at Jericho
He challenged Eglon's champion to single combat
He poisoned the royal wine at Eglon's banquet
qs.e: Judges 3:15-22 details Ehud's secret mission, thrusting his double-edged dagger into Eglon while delivering a message from God.

qs.q: What challenge did Elijah issue to the 450 prophets of Baal at Mount Carmel in 1 Kings 18?
o: The God who answers by fire on the altar sacrifice is the true God
Whichever group builds the largest altar will win royal favor
The prophets of Baal must call down rain before noon
Whichever deity parts the Kishon river is God
qs.e: 1 Kings 18:24 records Elijah's contest setup: 'call ye on the name of your gods, and I will call on the name of the LORD: and the God that answereth by fire, let him be God'.

qs.q: What timeless wisdom directive is given in Proverbs 3:5-6?
o: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths
Rely on human wisdom in commercial trade while trusting God for spiritual health
Seek first material prosperity so that thou mayest build holy altars
Do not trust friends or neighbors in times of national crisis
qs.e: Proverbs 3:5-6 instructs believers to maintain total trust in Yahweh rather than self-reliant intellect, promising divine direction.

qs.q: Why was Daniel unharmed after spending the night in the lions' den in Daniel 6?
o: God sent His angel to shut the lions' mouths because Daniel was found innocent
The lions had been fed prior to Daniel being thrown in
Daniel used physical weapons to defend himself
King Darius secretly released the lions before midnight
qs.e: Daniel 6:22 records Daniel testifying to Darius: 'My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths, that they have not hurt me'.

qs.q: Why did King Herod order the murder of male children in Bethlehem in Matthew 2?
o: He sought to eliminate the newborn King of the Jews reported by the Magi
To suppress a political rebellion initiated by Zealots
Because Bethlehem refused to pay Roman imperial taxes
To fulfill a decree issued by Emperor Augustus
qs.e: Matthew 2:16 describes Herod's fury upon realizing the Magi tricked him, prompting the massacre of toddlers to protect his throne.

qs.q: In the Sermon on the Mount, what title does Jesus bestow upon peacemakers in Matthew 5:9?
o: They shall be called the children of God
They shall inherit all earthly kingdoms
They shall be appointed judges in Israel
They shall receive double financial rewards
qs.e: Matthew 5:9 declares: 'Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God'.

qs.q: What spiritual folly is exposed in Jesus' Parable of the Rich Fool in Luke 12?
o: Storing up material wealth for oneself while failing to be rich toward God
Failing to build larger barns to protect grain from moisture
Lending money to poor neighbors without charging interest
Refusing to hire day laborers during harvest season
qs.e: Luke 12:16-21 warns against material greed, ending with God calling the man a fool for prioritizing temporary wealth over eternal spiritual status.

qs.q: What command did Jesus speak to calm the raging storm on the Sea of Galilee in Mark 4?
qs.e: Mark 4:39 records Jesus rebuking the wind and saying to the sea, 'Peace, be still', whereupon the wind ceased and there was a great calm.

qs.q: What mercy-filled prayer did Stephen offer as he was being stoned in Acts 7?
o: Lord, lay not this sin to their charge
Lord, strike my executioners with blindness
Lord, destroy the temple council immediately
Lord, avenge my innocent blood upon Rome
qs.e: Acts 7:60 records Stephen kneeling down and crying with a loud voice, 'Lord, lay not this sin to their charge', reflecting Christlike forgiveness.

qs.q: In Romans 13:1, what principle regarding governing authorities is taught to Christians?
o: Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers, for there is no power but of God
Believers must disobey all non-Christian governments by default
Civil laws do not apply to baptized citizens of heaven
Christians should actively seek the military overthrow of secular rulers
qs.e: Romans 13:1 teaches that civil government is ordained by God and deserves respectful obedience unless it directly violates divine law.

qs.q: How did the serpent deceive Eve in the Garden of Eden in Genesis 3?
o: By twisting God's command and falsely promising that eating the fruit would make them as gods, knowing good and evil
By physically forcing her to pick the fruit
By claiming that God had abandoned the garden
By offering her material silver and gold
qs.e: Genesis 3:1-5 records the serpent casting doubt on God's word and lying 'Ye shall not surely die', tempting Eve with godlike knowledge.

qs.q: What covenant sign did God place in the sky following the Flood in Genesis 9?
o: A rainbow as a perpetual token that water would never again destroy all flesh
A flaming pillar visible over Mount Ararat
A glowing cloud hovering over the ark
A golden star appearing at sunset
qs.e: Genesis 9:12-15 details God placing His bow in the cloud as an everlasting covenant pledge with all earthly creatures.

qs.q: Why did Moses flee from Egypt to the land of Midian in Exodus 2?
o: Pharaoh sought to kill him after learning Moses had slain an Egyptian taskmaster
God commanded him to embark on a forty-year fast
The Israelites banished him for interfering in their dispute
He wished to join Jethro's commercial trading caravans
qs.e: Exodus 2:11-15 records Moses killing the Egyptian to defend a fellow Hebrew, but fleeing when Pharaoh discovered the matter.

qs.q: How is Jael described in Deborah and Barak's victory song in Judges 5?
o: Blessed above women shall Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite be
A warrior queen ruling over Mount Ephraim
A prophetess serving at the tabernacle in Shiloh
A Canaanite spy who deceived Israel
qs.e: Judges 5:24 praises Jael in song for her decisive action in killing Sisera and bringing victory to Israel.

qs.q: What covenant of friendship did Jonathan seal with David in 1 Samuel 18?
o: He loved David as his own soul and gave him his royal robe, tunic, sword, bow, and belt
He agreed to share the throne of Israel equally with David
He promised to betray King Saul at the battle of Gilboa
He gave David ownership of all Benjaminite ancestral lands
qs.e: 1 18:1-4 describes Jonathan's deep covenant love for David, stripping himself of his royal armor and garments to give to David.

qs.q: What judgment did the prophet Ahijah announce against Jeroboam's family in 1 Kings 14?
o: Because Jeroboam made golden idols, his dynasty would be completely cut off and destroyed
Jeroboam's lineage would rule the northern kingdom forever
Jeroboam would be captured and taken exile to Babylon
Jeroboam's palace would be converted into a levitical sanctuary
qs.e: 1 Kings 14:7-11 details Ahijah's severe judgment upon Jeroboam's house for leading Israel into idolatrous sin.

qs.q: How did Elisha restore the dead son of the Shunammite woman to life in 2 Kings 4?
o: He prayed to the LORD, lay upon the child, stretched himself out on him twice, and the child sneezed seven times and opened his eyes
He commanded the child's mother to wash him in the Jordan River
He anointed the child with holy oil brought from Mount Carmel
He touched the child with Elijah's mantle
qs.e: 2 Kings 4:32-35 details Elisha's intense prayer and physical contact, resulting in God bringing the boy back to life.

qs.q: Why did Mordecai refuse to bow down before Haman in Esther 3?
o: As a devout Jew, he reserved religious bowing and prostration for God alone
He claimed higher royal rank than Haman in Persia
Haman refused to pay Mordecai's military wages
Mordecai belonged to the royal family of Media
qs.e: Esther 3:2-5 records Mordecai refusing to bow down or pay homage to Haman, citing his Jewish faith and principles.

qs.q: What transformation does God promise to Israel in Ezekiel 36:26?
o: A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh
A guaranteed conquest of all surrounding Gentile empires
A permanent restoration of Solomon's physical temple wealth
An exemption from all future physical suffering and trials
qs.e: Ezekiel 36:26 prophesies internal spiritual renewal where God replaces hard, rebellious hearts with responsive hearts of flesh.

qs.q: In Malachi 3:8-10, of what sin does God accuse the people of Israel?
o: Robbing God by withholding tithes and offerings from the temple storehouse
Failing to build defensive walls around Jerusalem
Trading with Philistine merchants on Sabbath days
qs.e: Malachi 3:8-10 rebukes the nation for withholding tithes, promising that bringing the full tithe will open the windows of heaven with blessing.

qs.q: In the Sermon on the Mount, who does Jesus declare blessed in the opening Beatitude (Matthew 5:3)?
o: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven
Blessed are the wealthy: for they can build synagogues
Blessed are the mighty warriors: for they shall rule earth
Blessed are the learned scribes: for they know the law
qs.e: Matthew 5:3 begins the Sermon on the Mount by pronouncing blessing on those who recognize their spiritual poverty and need for God.

qs.q: What shared lesson is conveyed by the twin parables of the Hidden Treasure and the Pearl of Great Price in Matthew 13?
o: The kingdom of heaven is of such supreme worth that it is worth sacrificing everything else to possess it
Material riches are hidden by God to test human patience
Merchants should search exclusively for physical gemstones
Kingdom blessings are earned through monetary investments
qs.e: Matthew 13:44-46 illustrates individuals selling all they have with joy to obtain the priceless treasure of God's kingdom.

qs.q: What sacrament did Jesus institute during the Last Supper with His disciples in Matthew 26?
o: The Lord's Supper, taking bread and wine as His body and the blood of the new covenant shed for remission of sins
The annual water purification ritual of Jordan
The formal ordination of high priests
qs.e: Matthew 26:26-28 details Jesus blessing bread ('This is my body') and the cup ('This is my blood of the new testament'), instituting Holy Communion.

qs.q: What was the immediate outcome of Peter's sermon on the Day of Pentecost in Acts 2?
o: About three thousand souls were pricked in their heart, repented, and were baptized
The Sanhedrin arrested Peter and James immediately
The Roman soldiers disbanded the early church assembly
The crowd drove the apostles out of Jerusalem to Samaria
qs.e: Acts 2:37-41 records the conviction of the hearers, resulting in three thousand converts added to the church that day.

qs.q: In Romans 10:9-10, what double confession and belief are required for salvation?
o: Confessing with the mouth the Lord Jesus and believing in the heart that God raised Him from the dead
Confessing sin to levitical priests and offering animal sacrifices
Believing in the Old Testament law and obeying traditional customs
Confessing church membership and giving tithes publicly
qs.e: Romans 10:9-10 states clearly: 'that if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved'.

qs.q: What was Isaac doing when he first saw Rebekah arriving with Abraham's servant in Genesis 24?
o: He went out to meditate in the field at the eventide
He was offering a burnt sacrifice on Mount Moriah
He was negotiating water rights with Abimelech
He was hunting wild game in the Negev desert
qs.e: Genesis 24:63 records that Isaac went out to meditate in the field at eventide, lifted up his eyes, and saw the camels coming.

qs.q: What specific command did Joseph give concerning his physical remains in Genesis 50:25?
o: God will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones from hence to the Promised Land
Bury me in the royal pyramid next to Pharaoh
Leave my tomb untouched in Memphis permanently
Scatter my ashes in the Nile river during harvest
qs.e: Genesis 50:25 records Joseph making the children of Israel swear to carry his bones up to Canaan, fulfilled during the Exodus (Exodus 13:19).

qs.q: How did King David express holy joy when bringing the Ark of the Covenant into Jerusalem in 2 Samuel 6?
o: He danced before the LORD with all his might, clothed in a linen ephod
He rode in a golden chariot surrounded by royal bodyguards
He marched silently at the head of a solemn military column
He wore Saul's royal crown and held a scepter
qs.e: 2 Samuel 6:14 describes David dancing before Yahweh with all his strength, expressing exuberant praise for the ark's arrival.

qs.q: What historical role did Zerubbabel, Ezra, and Nehemiah respectively play in restoring post-exilic Judah?
o: Zerubbabel rebuilt the temple, Ezra restored spiritual law teaching, and Nehemiah rebuilt Jerusalem's walls
Zerubbabel conquered Samaria, Ezra built palaces, and Nehemiah served as high priest
Zerubbabel wrote prophecies, Ezra commanded the army, and Nehemiah led temple choirs
Zerubbabel translated scriptures, Ezra built fortifications, and Nehemiah fought Persia
qs.e: Scripture outlines Zerubbabel leading temple rebuilding (Ezra 3-6), Ezra renewing Torah teaching (Ezra 7-10), and Nehemiah repairing city walls (Nehemiah 1-6).

qs.q: When news of Job's afflictions reached his three friends, how did they initially minister to him in Job 2?
o: They sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights in silence, seeing his grief was great
They immediately accused him of secret wicked sins
They offered sacrifices at Bethel on his behalf
They urged him to curse God and die
qs.e: Job 2:11-13 records Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar arriving, weeping, tearing their robes, and sitting silently with Job for seven days in deep empathy.

qs.q: Why was Jeremiah thrown into the muddy cistern dungeon of Malchiah in Jeremiah 38?
o: The princes accused him of weakening the soldiers' hands by preaching surrender to the Babylonians
He refused to pay royal taxes to King Zedekiah
He attempted to escape Jerusalem to flee to Egypt
He broke the physical vessels in the temple sanctuary
qs.e: Jeremiah 38:1-6 shows the officials demanding Jeremiah's death for his faithful prophetic warning that staying in Jerusalem meant death while surrendering meant life.

qs.q: In Amos 8:1-2, what did the vision of a basket of summer fruit (qayits) symbolize for Israel (qets)?
o: The end had come upon God's people Israel; He would not pass by them any more
A season of unprecedented financial prosperity for Samaritan merchants
The immediate harvest of righteousness following repentance
A guarantee of protection against foreign invaders
qs.e: Amos 8:1-2 uses a Hebrew wordplay between 'summer fruit' (qayits) and 'the end' (qets) to signify that Israel was ripe for judgment.

qs.q: What caused Peter to begin sinking when he walked on the water toward Jesus in Matthew 14?
o: When he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid and began to sink, crying 'Lord, save me!'
A sudden wave overturned his boat
Jesus commanded him to return to the ship
The other disciples called him back in fear
qs.e: Matthew 14:29-30 shows Peter walking on water by faith, but sinking when he shifted his focus from Jesus to the stormy wind.

qs.q: How did Jesus reveal Himself to the two disciples on the road to Emmaus in Luke 24?
o: He expounded in all the Scriptures the things concerning Himself, and their eyes were opened in the breaking of bread
He performed a spectacular miracle in the public square of Emmaus
He showed them the written decree of Pilate
He transformed into an angelic appearance on the road
qs.e: Luke 24:27 & 30-31 records Jesus explaining messianic prophecy along the walk, and being recognized during the blessing and breaking of bread.

qs.q: In Acts 2:42, what four foundational practices characterized the early Jerusalem church?
o: Apostles' doctrine, fellowship, breaking of bread, and prayers
Animal sacrifice, temple fasting, circumcisions, and tithes
Synagogue debates, military training, political lobbying, and feasts
Ascetic fasting, monastic vows, silence, and isolation
qs.e: Acts 2:42 lists the four core pillars of early Christian church life: teaching, fellowship, communion, and prayer.

qs.q: In 1 Corinthians 15:14-19, why does Paul argue that the physical resurrection of Jesus Christ is essential to Christian faith?
o: If Christ be not risen, then is our preaching vain, your faith is also vain, and ye are yet in your sins
Without the resurrection, moral living is still sufficient for salvation
The resurrection matters only for Jewish believers in Jerusalem
Christ's resurrection was merely a spiritual metaphor without bodily reality
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 15:14-19 establishes bodily resurrection as the irreplaceable lynchpin of gospel truth and believer's hope.

qs.q: In 2 Chronicles 20, how did King Jehoshaphat and Judah gain victory over the combined armies of Moab, Ammon, and Mount Seir?
o: By appointing singers to praise the beauty of holiness in front of the army, whereupon the LORD set ambushes against the enemies
Through a surprise cavalry charge led by Jehoshaphat at dawn
By purchasing advanced iron chariots from Syria
By retreating behind Jerusalem's walls until famine struck the enemy
qs.e: 2 Chronicles 20:21-23 records Jehoshaphat stationing worshipers ahead of soldiers, leading God to cause the enemy coalition to destroy themselves.

qs.q: What fundamental messianic timeline and redemption purpose is foretold in Daniel 9:24-26 (Seventy Weeks)?
o: Seventy weeks are determined to finish transgression, make an end of sins, make reconciliation for iniquity, and anoint the Most Holy before Messiah is cut off
The Babylonian empire will endure for seventy generations before falling to Rome
The physical Jerusalem temple will never suffer destruction or desolation
Israel will conquer Persia within seventy years of exile
qs.e: Daniel 9:24-26 presents the prophetic Seventy Weeks decree focusing on messianic atonement, righteousness, and the cutting off of Messiah.

qs.q: Which prophetic image in Zechariah 9:9 was fulfilled during Jesus' Triumphal Entry into Jerusalem?
o: Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion... behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass
The Messiah coming upon a fiery warhorse with ten thousand saints
The King descending on a cloud of fire to destroy Roman palaces
The Redeemer arriving in a golden chariot with levitical trumpeter banner
qs.e: Zechariah 9:9 is quoted in Matthew 21:5, highlighting Messiah's humility, peace, and righteous reign.

qs.q: In Romans 9:11-13, how does Paul illustrate God's sovereign freedom in divine election?
o: Before the children were born or had done good or evil, God said 'The elder shall serve the younger', as it is written 'Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated'
God chose Jacob because Jacob possessed superior moral character to Esau
Divine election depends entirely on human ancestry and physical circumcision
Esau forfeited election solely by selling his birthright
qs.e: Romans 9:11-13 uses Jacob and Esau to prove that God's purpose according to election stands not of works but of Him who calls.

qs.q: In 1 Corinthians 3:11-15, how does Paul describe the future evaluation of a Christian worker's service at the judgment seat of Christ?
o: Each worker's build upon the foundation of Christ (gold, silver, precious stones vs wood, hay, stubble) will be tested by fire
All works are automatically accepted without distinction or testing
Workers who built with wood will forfeit their personal salvation entirely
Evaluation is based on the quantity of material riches donated to the church
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 3:11-15 describes the testing by fire where eternal rewards depend on quality and motive, while the believer himself is saved.

qs.q: According to Genesis 1:28, what primary mandate was given to humanity over the rest of creation?
o: To build altars of worship across the land
To exercise stewardship, be fruitful, and fill the earth
To guard the tree of life from wild beasts
To name all animals and classify them
qs.e: In Genesis 1:28, God blessed humanity and commanded them to be fruitful, multiply, fill the earth, and exercise responsible dominion/stewardship over creation.

qs.q: What landmark covenant promise did God make to Abraham when calling him to leave Haran in Genesis 12:1-3?
o: That he would build a magnificent temple in Canaan
That he would become a great nation and all families of the earth would be blessed through him
That his line would produce earthly kings immediately
That he would never experience famine or trial
qs.e: God promised Abraham in Genesis 12:1-3 that He would make him a great nation, bless him, and through his seed all families of the earth would be blessed.

qs.q: Which miraculous sign was first given to Moses at Mount Horeb to validate his divine commission before Israel in Exodus 4:2-5?
o: Water turning into blood in a basin
The earth opening beneath his feet
A sudden pillar of fire descending
His staff turning into a serpent
qs.e: When Moses questioned whether Israel would believe him, God commanded him to cast his rod on the ground, and it turned into a serpent as a miraculous sign.

qs.q: Which judge delivered Israel from the oppression of Eglon king of Moab by using a concealed left-handed dagger in Judges 3?
qs.e: Ehud, a Benjaminite, prepared a two-edged dagger, hid it under his clothing, and assassinated Eglon king of Moab, delivering Israel from eighteen years of servitude.

qs.q: Who was secretly anointed as the first king over Israel by the prophet Samuel at Ramah in 1 Samuel 10?
qs.e: 1 Samuel 10 records that Samuel took a flask of oil, poured it on Saul's head, and anointed him king over God's inheritance, Israel.

qs.q: Which prophet confronted King Ahab over the illegal murder and seizure of Naboth's vineyard in 1 Kings 21?
qs.e: Elijah the Tishbite was sent by God to confront King Ahab in Naboth's vineyard, pronouncing judgment on Ahab and Jezebel for their murderous wickedness.

qs.q: In which Judean village was Jesus born in fulfillment of the messianic prophecy in Micah 5:2 and Matthew 2:1-6?
qs.e: Micah 5:2 prophesied that the Ruler of Israel would come forth from Bethlehem Ephrathah, which Matthew 2 confirms was fulfilled at the birth of Jesus.

qs.q: Why did Abraham purchase the cave of Machpelah from Ephron the Hittite in Genesis 23 rather than accept it as a gift?
o: To fulfill a ritual requirement specified in the Mosaic Law
To erect an altar for burnt offerings to God
To establish legal, unassailable ownership of land in Canaan for a burial place
To prevent the Hittites from claiming tribute from his sons
qs.e: Abraham insisted on paying full price for Machpelah so that he would hold an undeniable legal title to land in Canaan as a permanent family burial site.

qs.q: What was the immediate political reason Pharaoh elevated Joseph to governor over Egypt in Genesis 41?
o: Joseph accurately interpreted Pharaoh's dreams and proposed a wise agricultural storage plan for the coming famine
Joseph revealed a secret plot by court officials against Pharaoh
Joseph led Egypt's army to victory against foreign invaders
Joseph introduced a new taxation system that doubled royal revenue
qs.e: Pharaoh recognized God's spirit and wisdom in Joseph after he interpreted the dreams of seven fat and seven lean cows and outlined a national strategy for grain reserves.

qs.q: The annual celebration of the Passover feast in Exodus 12 was designed primarily to serve as a perpetual reminder of
o: The giving of the Ten Commandments at Mount Sinai
The division of Canaan among the twelve tribes
Israel's agricultural harvest in the Sinai desert
God's mighty deliverance of Israel from Egyptian bondage through the blood of the lamb
qs.e: Passover commemorated the night God spared the firstborn of Israel whose doorposts were marked with blood and redeemed His people from Egyptian slavery.

qs.q: What fatal compromise led to Samson's eventual loss of strength and capture by the Philistines in Judges 16?
o: He allied himself with the Moabites against Israel
He refused to offer sacrifices before battle
He appointed foreign priests to minister at Shiloh
He broke his Nazirite vow by revealing the secret of his strength to Delilah
qs.e: Samson compromised his Nazirite consecration to God by confiding in Delilah, leading to his hair being shaved, his departure of divine power, and his capture.

qs.q: Why did the prophet Samuel announce God's rejection of Saul as king in 1 Samuel 15?
o: Saul married foreign wives who turned his heart to idol worship
Saul attempted to build a temple without priestly authorization
Saul disobeyed God's explicit command by sparing Agag and the best livestock of Amalek
Saul failed to consult the Urim and Thummim before going to war
qs.e: Samuel told Saul that 'to obey is better than sacrifice' because Saul compromised God's direct command regarding Amalek by sparing King Agag and choice animals.

qs.q: What critical political mistake caused Rehoboam to lose ten tribes of Israel in 1 Kings 12?
o: He moved the royal capital from Jerusalem to Samaria
He abolished the priesthood of Aaron and instituted golden calf worship
He refused to lower the heavy tax and labor burdens imposed by his father Solomon
He made a military alliance with Egypt against northern Israel
qs.e: Rehoboam rejected the mature counsel of the elders and arrogantly promised harsher labor burdens, prompting Jeroboam and the ten northern tribes to secede.

qs.q: What miracle did Elisha perform for the destitute widow of a prophet in 2 Kings 4:1-7 to save her sons from slavery?
o: He commanded manna to fall around her tent every morning
He turned river water into wine for her family to sell
He multiplied five loaves of barley bread to feed her household
He multiplied her remaining jar of oil to fill every borrowed vessel until her debt was cleared
qs.e: Elisha instructed the widow to gather empty vessels from neighbors; her single jar of oil miraculously kept pouring until every container was full, enabling her to pay her creditor.

qs.q: Which Persian king issued the historic decree in Ezra 1 permitting Jewish exiles to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the Temple?
qs.e: In fulfillment of Jeremiah's prophecy, King Cyrus of Persia issued an edict in his first year allowing the Jews to return to Jerusalem and rebuild Yahweh's house.

qs.q: According to Proverbs 1:7, what is declared to be the absolute beginning or foundation of true knowledge?
o: Accumulation of material wealth and influence
The acquisition of extensive worldly education
The fear and reverence of the Lord
qs.e: Proverbs 1:7 states: 'The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and instruction.'

qs.q: In Hosea 1-3, God commanded the prophet Hosea to marry Gomer, an unfaithful wife, primarily to illustrate
o: Israel's spiritual adultery against God and God's persistent redeeming love
The military defeat awaiting the northern kingdom
The social plight of abandoned women in Samaria
The legal steps required for divorce in ancient Israel
qs.e: Hosea's marriage to unfaithful Gomer served as a living prophetic sign of Israel's covenant unfaithfulness to Yahweh and God's relentless, merciful love seeking her return.

qs.q: At the baptism of Jesus by John in the Jordan River (Matthew 3:16-17), what divine confirmation occurred?
o: An angel appeared and placed a golden crown on Jesus' head
The sun turned dark for three hours during the immersion
The Holy Spirit descended like a dove, and a heavenly voice declared Jesus as God's beloved Son
The waters of the Jordan split into two halves before the crowd
qs.e: Matthew 3:16-17 records the heavens opening, the Spirit descending as a dove upon Jesus, and the Father's voice testifying, 'This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.'

qs.q: What supernatural events accompanied the outpouring of the Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost in Acts 2?
o: A voice from heaven calling all apostles by name
A bright light that blinded all the priests in the Temple
An earthquake that opened the prison doors across Jerusalem
A sound like a rushing mighty wind, cloven tongues as of fire, and speaking in other tongues
qs.e: Acts 2:1-4 describes a sudden sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, divided tongues like fire resting on them, and believers speaking in other tongues as the Spirit gave utterance.

qs.q: According to Genesis 3:14-19, what primary sentence was pronounced upon the serpent following humanity's temptation and fall?
o: It would be banished to the desert lands forever
It was cursed above all livestock, condemned to crawl on its belly, and destined for perpetual enmity with the woman's offspring
It was barred from ever entering the garden again
It lost the ability to speak to human beings
qs.e: Genesis 3:14-15 details the curse upon the serpent, including crawling on its belly, eating dust, and the prophetic announcement of enmity between its seed and the woman's seed.

qs.q: Jacob's night of wrestling with a divine stranger at Peniel in Genesis 32:24-30 transformed his spiritual life because he
o: Obtained earthly wealth from the local inhabitants
Learned secret military tactics to defeat Esau's army
Was appointed high priest over his family clan
Acknowledged his utter dependence on God, received a new name (Israel), and secured God's blessing
qs.e: At Peniel, Jacob held on for God's blessing, admitted his old self ('Jacob' the grasper), and received the new name 'Israel', signifying victory through divine grace and surrender.

qs.q: How did Joseph demonstrate genuine reconciliation and spiritual maturity toward his brothers when revealing his identity in Genesis 45?
o: He demanded a public apology and restitution of money before forgiving them
He forced them to sign a treaty of peace before Pharaoh
He required them to remain in prison for three days to test their honesty
He reassured them that God sent him ahead to Egypt to preserve life, removing their fear of revenge
qs.e: In Genesis 45:5-8, Joseph comforted his terrified brothers by explaining that God overruled their evil intent to send him to Egypt for the preservation of many lives.

qs.q: Why was Israel's worship of the golden calf at Mount Sinai in Exodus 32 considered a fundamental breach of their covenant with God?
o: Because it violated the first two commandments against idolatry and representing God through images
Because they failed to offer a sin offering before dancing
Because Aaron performed the sacrifice without Moses' personal permission
Because they used Egyptian gold instead of Canaanite gold
qs.e: The golden calf violated the foundational covenant terms (Exodus 20) prohibiting worship of other gods and fashioning graven images to represent Yahweh.

qs.q: What divine principle was illustrated when God instructed Gideon to reduce his military force from 32,000 to 300 men in Judges 7?
o: That only men with professional swords were qualified for holy war
That God preferred stealth attacks over pitched battles
That victory in divine warfare depends not on human numbers but on God's power, so Israel could not boast
That small armies move faster across mountainous terrain
qs.e: God explicitly told Gideon in Judges 7:2 that Israel had too many soldiers, lest they claim glory for themselves rather than attributing deliverance to God alone.

qs.q: David's refusal to kill King Saul in the cave of En-gedi (1 Samuel 24) demonstrated his profound respect for the principle that
o: Caves were sacred ground where blood could not be shed
Saul was protected by foreign mercenaries
One must never harm the Lord's anointed king, trusting God alone for vindication
Saul's army was too close for a safe escape
qs.e: David restrained his men from harming Saul, declaring in 1 Samuel 24:6 that he would not stretch out his hand against his master because Saul was the Lord's anointed.

qs.q: Jeroboam I established royal shrines with golden calves at Bethel and Dan primarily to achieve what political objective in 1 Kings 12?
o: To prevent northern Israelites from traveling to Jerusalem to worship and returning allegiance to Rehoboam
To fulfill an ancient prophecy spoken to King David
To promote artistic craftsmanship across northern cities
To satisfy the demands of his foreign Egyptian wives
qs.e: Jeroboam feared that if his people went up to offer sacrifices at Yahweh's temple in Jerusalem, their hearts would return to the House of David and kill him (1 Kings 12:26-28).

qs.q: Why was Naaman the Syrian military commander initially enraged by Elisha's instructions to wash seven times in the Jordan River in 2 Kings 5?
o: Because Elisha required him to renounce his Syrian citizenship
Because Naaman believed seven was an unlucky number in Syrian culture
Because Elisha did not meet him in person and he considered Israel's rivers inferior to Abana and Pharpar in Damascus
Because Elisha charged a high fee for the prophetic consultation
qs.e: Naaman expected Elisha to come out, stand, call on God's name, and wave his hand. He disdained the humble Jordan River compared to Syria's famous rivers until his servants advised humility.

qs.q: Nehemiah's immediate spiritual response upon hearing that Jerusalem's walls were broken down and its gates burned (Nehemiah 1) was to
o: Mourn, fast, and pray to the God of heaven, confessing the sins of Israel
Resign his official post as royal cupbearer
Recruit an immediate mercenary army from Susa
Send an angry letter of protest to Sanballat the Horonite
qs.e: Nehemiah 1:4 records that when Nehemiah heard the report, he sat down, wept, fasted, and prayed for days, confessing corporate sins and pleading for divine favor before King Artaxerxes.

qs.q: In the book of Job, Job's steadfast integrity despite the tragic loss of his possessions, children, and health directly disproved Satan's accusation that
o: Job had secretly committed grave crimes against his neighbors
Job served God only because God had placed a protective hedge of prosperity around him
Human beings are incapable of enduring physical pain
Angels were superior to humans in righteous living
qs.e: Satan asserted in Job 1:9-11 that Job's piety was purely self-serving ('Doth Job fear God for nought?'). Job's perseverance proved genuine love and worship of God independent of material reward.

qs.q: Jeremiah's description of the New Covenant in Jeremiah 31:31-34 highlights its superiority over the Sinai covenant because God's law would be
o: Engraved on golden tablets kept in the Ark
Written directly upon human hearts and minds, accompanied by full forgiveness of sins
Enforced strictly by civil magistrates across the nations
qs.e: Jeremiah 31:33-34 emphasizes an internal transformation where God puts His law in their inward parts and writes it on their hearts, ensuring intimate knowledge of God and personal pardon.

qs.q: Amos sternly rejected Israel's elaborate religious assemblies and sacrifices in Amos 5:21-24 because their worship was empty without
o: Heavy monetary contributions to the Temple fund
The attendance of the king and royal court
Justice rolling down like waters and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream
qs.e: Amos 5:24 declares: 'But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.' God hates ritual hypocrisy when social justice and ethical integrity are lacking.

qs.q: In the parable of the Prodigal Son (Luke 15:25-32), the elder brother's angry refusal to join the celebration exposed his own
o: Secret desire to travel to a far country
Fear that the family estate would be completely bankrupt
Self-righteous, transactional attitude and lack of compassionate love for his restored brother
qs.e: The elder brother viewed his relationship with his father in terms of dutiful slave labor ('these many years do I serve thee') and resented grace shown to the repentant younger brother.

qs.q: Why was the healing of the ten lepers in Luke 17:11-19 notable regarding the one who returned to give thanks to Jesus?
o: He was a priest who certified his own healing
He was a Samaritan outsider who alone demonstrated deep gratitude and faith
He was the wealthiest among the ten
He had been sick longer than all the others
qs.e: Although ten were cleansed, only one returned to fall at Jesus' feet and glorify God—and Jesus noted with sorrow that this thankful believer was a foreigner (a Samaritan).

qs.q: At the Jerusalem Council in Acts 15:1-21, the apostles and elders established that Gentile believers were saved by grace and should not be required to
o: Be circumcised or observe the ceremonial Law of Moses
Pay taxes to the Roman authorities
Fast on the Jewish Day of Atonement
qs.e: Acts 15 affirmed Peter and Paul's testimony that God cleansed Gentile hearts by faith, concluding that placing the yoke of ceremonial Mosaic circumcision on Gentiles was unnecessary.

qs.q: Comparing the creation perspective of Genesis 1 with Genesis 2 reveals that Genesis 2 focuses specifically on
o: The intimate creation of man from dust, his moral responsibility in Eden, and the origin of marriage
The chronological division of seven literal solar days
The cosmological formation of galaxies and stars
The angelic rebellion prior to human existence
qs.e: While Genesis 1 provides a broad transcendent overview of cosmic order, Genesis 2 focuses on humanity's relational context: forming man from dust, placing him in Eden, and fashioning woman.

qs.q: In Genesis 22, Abraham's willingness to offer Isaac as a burnt offering demonstrates that genuine biblical faith is tested by one's readiness to
o: Surrender even the most cherished promise to the absolute lordship and trustworthiness of God
Seek public praise from surrounding Canaanite tribes
Construct altars on every prominent mountain
Perform complex religious rituals without assistance
qs.e: Abraham's trial proved that he feared God above all else, trusting that God was able to raise Isaac even from the dead (Hebrews 11:17-19) to fulfill His covenant promises.

qs.q: When Moses interceded for Israel following the golden calf idolatry in Exodus 32:11-14, his prayer prevailed because he appealed to
o: God's covenant promises to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and God's own glory among the nations
Israel's military usefulness in conquering Canaan
Aaron's personal ignorance of idol worship
The financial cost of the Tabernacle materials
qs.e: Moses argued that destroying Israel would cause Egyptians to mock Yahweh's intentions and reminded God of His sworn covenant oaths to the patriarchs.

qs.q: The prophetic rebuke delivered by Nathan to King David in 2 Samuel 12:1-12 succeeded in convicting David because Nathan used a parable that
o: Directly named Bathsheba and Uriah from the beginning
Frightened David with threats of foreign invasion
Appealed to David's former sense of justice as a shepherd before applying 'Thou art the man!'
Exposed David's financial mismanagement of royal treasury
qs.e: Nathan told a story about a rich man stealing a poor man's single beloved ewe lamb. David's righteous indignation was aroused, allowing Nathan to declare: 'Thou art the man!'

qs.q: The persistent spiritual flaw known in Old Testament history as 'the sin of Jeroboam son of Nebat' consisted in
o: Establishing unauthorized worship places and syncretistic golden calves, leading Israel into idolatry
Imposing illegal military conscription on northern tribes
Abolishing the observance of the Sabbath day
Selling Temple vessels to Syrian merchants
qs.e: Jeroboam I set a catastrophic precedent by making golden calves at Dan and Bethel and appointing non-Levitical priests, a sin repeated by successive northern kings.

qs.q: Ezra's drastic reform regarding intermarriage with pagan nations in Ezra 9-10 was driven by the urgent spiritual conviction that
o: Jerusalem suffered from severe food shortages
Unlawful intermarriage threatened holy seed purity and compromised Israel's covenant identity, risking renewed exile
Persian royal decree forbade mixed marriages
Foreign wives were stealing gold from the rebuilt Temple
qs.e: Ezra recognized that idolatrous intermarriage was the exact sin that caused the original Exile, so spiritual renewal required repenting of covenant infidelity.

qs.q: The ultimate conclusion reached in Ecclesiastes 12:13-14 regarding the purpose of human existence is that man must
o: Seek continuous earthly pleasure to offset human suffering
Fear God and keep His commandments, for God will bring every work into judgment
Pursue maximum intellectual knowledge before death
Accumulate vast wealth to leave as an inheritance
qs.e: Ecclesiastes concludes: 'Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man. For God shall bring every work into judgment...'

qs.q: Ezekiel's vision of the valley of dry bones coming to life in Ezekiel 37:1-14 conveyed the theological message that
o: Egyptian mummification was a pagan error
God possessed sovereign power to restore spiritually dead and hopeless Israel back to their land
Physical resurrection would occur immediately in Babylon
Israelite soldiers killed in battle would form a heavenly army
qs.e: The dry bones represented exiled Israel complaining 'our hope is lost'. God showed Ezekiel that His Spirit would breathe life into the nation and restore them to the land of Israel.

qs.q: In Jesus' teaching on salt and light in Matthew 5:13-16 (Sermon on the Mount), believers are warned that losing spiritual distinctiveness causes them to become
o: Good for nothing except to be cast out and trampled underfoot by men
Ineligible for leadership in civil government
qs.e: Jesus taught that if salt loses its savor/flavor, it loses its preservative value and is cast out. Believers must maintain distinct holy living to glorify God before others.

qs.q: During the Last Supper in Matthew 26:26-28, Jesus gave profound theological meaning to the Passover cup by identifying it as
o: A symbol of political freedom from Roman rule
The wine of royal celebration in David's kingdom
A memorial of the manna eaten in the wilderness
His blood of the new covenant, shed for many for the remission of sins
qs.e: Jesus took the cup saying, 'Drink ye all of it; for this is my blood of the new testament [covenant], which is shed for many for the remission of sins.'

qs.q: Stephen's defense before the Sanhedrin in Acts 7 delivered a powerful critique of Jewish temple-exclusivism by demonstrating that
o: God's presence and activity were never localized to one building, for 'the Most High dwelleth not in temples made with hands'
Solomon built the Temple using foreign pagan labor
Sacrifices performed in Jerusalem were inferior to Abraham's altars
The Temple was constructed on improper geological ground
qs.e: Stephen surveyed biblical history (Abraham in Mesopotamia, Joseph in Egypt, Moses in Midian/Sinai) to prove God reveals Himself anywhere, warning against making the Temple an idol.

qs.q: Analyzing Joseph's declaration to his brothers in Genesis 50:19-20 ('Ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good') highlights the profound doctrine of
o: Universal salvation of all people regardless of repentance
Fatalistic determinism where human choices carry no moral weight
Angelic intervention replacing human free will
Divine providence overruling human sin and evil actions to accomplish His redemptive purpose
qs.e: Genesis 50:20 articulates divine providence: human actors are morally responsible for evil intent, yet God sovereignly orchestrates events to fulfill His good redemptive plans.

qs.q: The translation of Elijah in a whirlwind (2 Kings 2:9-12) and Elisha's request for a 'double portion' of Elijah's spirit signifies that spiritual leadership succession requires
o: Approval from the reigning king of Israel
Unwavering spiritual discernment, persistence, and alignment with God's prophetic mantle
Formal academic training in foreign prophetic schools
Inheriting physical property and royal titles
qs.e: Elijah told Elisha that receiving the double portion (firstborn heir's spiritual inheritance) depended on remaining vigilant to see Elijah when taken, symbolizing spiritual devotion and readiness.

qs.q: In Micah 6:6-8, the prophet contrasts grand ritual offerings (thousands of rams, rivers of oil, firstborn sacrifices) with God's true requirement, which is to
o: Do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with your God
Institute strict daily fasting for all citizens
Rebuild the physical walls of Jerusalem twice
Conquer surrounding pagan nations by sword
qs.e: Micah 6:8 synthesizes prophetic religion: God rejects extravagant ceremonialism devoid of heart righteousness, requiring ethical justice, steadfast mercy, and humble fellowship with God.

qs.q: In Romans 5:1-2, Paul articulates the primary theological benefits of justification by faith, stating that believers possess
o: Automatic political dominance over hostile nations
Immunity from all temporal suffering and earthly poverty
Peace with God through Jesus Christ, access by faith into divine grace, and joyful hope of God's glory
Exemption from civil obedience to secular authorities
qs.e: Romans 5:1-2 teaches: 'Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ: By whom also we have access by faith into this grace wherein we stand...'

qs.q: In 1 Corinthians 12:12-27, Paul uses the metaphor of the human body to teach that unity and diversity in the Christian church require
o: Mutual interdependence, respect for every member's gift, and absence of division in the body
Hierarchical dominance of prominent gifts over lesser gifts
Separation of spiritual members from weaker members
Uniformity where every member performs identical duties
qs.e: Paul explains that just as a physical body has many distinct members working together, the church consists of diverse spiritual gifts designed for mutual care, interdependence, and harmony.

qs.q: What reason did Cain give to God when questioned about Abel's whereabouts in Genesis 4:9?
o: 'I do not know where he went'
'He has gone into the fields to tend the sheep'
qs.e: When God asked Cain, 'Where is Abel thy brother?', Cain evasively replied, 'I know not: Am I my brother's keeper?' (Genesis 4:9).

qs.q: Which son of Isaac sold his birthright for a single meal of bread and lentil stew in Genesis 25:29-34?
qs.e: Esau came from the field faint with hunger and impetuously traded his spiritual birthright to Jacob for a pot of red stew.

qs.q: Which prophetess and judge commanded Barak to lead Israel's army against Sisera at Mount Tabor in Judges 4?
qs.e: Deborah, a prophetess who judged Israel under the palm tree between Ramah and Bethel, summoned Barak to lead Israel against Jabin's commander Sisera.

qs.q: What giant Philistine champion from Gath did young David slay with a sling and a stone in 1 Samuel 17?
qs.e: David confronted Goliath of Gath, who had defied the armies of the living God, striking him in the forehead with a sling stone.

qs.q: Which prophet tore his new garment into twelve pieces and gave ten to Jeroboam to symbolize the division of Israel in 1 Kings 11?
qs.e: Ahijah the Shilonite met Jeroboam outside Jerusalem, tore his new cloak into twelve pieces, and told Jeroboam to take ten pieces as a sign of his rule over ten tribes.

qs.q: In which city did Jesus perform His first recorded miracle by turning water into wine at a wedding feast (John 2:1-11)?
qs.e: John 2 records that Jesus performed His beginning of signs at Cana in Galilee, manifesting His glory so that His disciples believed in Him.

qs.q: Who was the Roman governor who sentenced Jesus to be crucified despite declaring Him innocent in Luke 23?
qs.e: Pontius Pilate, the Roman governor of Judea, yielded to the pressure of the crowd and religious leaders, handing Jesus over to be crucified.

qs.q: What was the covenant sign given by God to Noah after the Flood in Genesis 9:12-17 promising never again to destroy all flesh by water?
qs.e: God set His bow in the cloud as an everlasting covenant token between God and the earth that waters would no more become a flood to destroy all life.

qs.q: In Genesis 39, why was Joseph cast into prison while serving in Potiphar's house?
o: He organized a revolt among Egyptian servants
He interpreted dreams without royal permission
Potiphar's wife falsely accused him after he refused her adulterous advances
He stole gold vessels from Potiphar's treasury
qs.e: Joseph stood firm in moral integrity against Potiphar's wife ('How then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?'), leading her to falsely accuse him.

qs.q: What divine instruction was given to Israel regarding the gathering of manna in the wilderness in Exodus 16?
o: Only the priests were allowed to collect manna
Each person should gather a double portion every single day
Store manna in jars for thirty days to prevent spoilage
Gather daily only what was needed for that day, except on the sixth day when a double portion was gathered for the Sabbath
qs.e: Exodus 16 prescribed gathering daily bread for each day to teach daily dependence on God, with a double portion on Friday so no gathering occurred on the Sabbath.

qs.q: When Solomon succeeded David as king (1 Kings 3:5-14), what did he ask God for when offered any request in a dream at Gibeon?
o: An understanding heart to judge God's people and discern between good and evil
Inexhaustible silver and gold for the royal treasury
Territorial expansion into Syria and Egypt
Long life and victory over all his political enemies
qs.e: Solomon humbly requested wisdom and an understanding heart to govern Israel wisely, which pleased God so much that He added riches and honor as well.

qs.q: How did God manifest His presence to Elijah when he fled in discouragement to Mount Horeb in 1 Kings 19?
o: In a blinding flash of lightning from heaven
In a roaring windstorm that rent the mountains
In a still small voice (a gentle whisper) after the wind, earthquake, and fire
qs.e: 1 Kings 19:11-12 states that the Lord was not in the strong wind, the earthquake, or the fire, but spoke to Elijah in a still small voice.

qs.q: Why were Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego thrown into the burning fiery furnace by King Nebuchadnezzar in Daniel 3?
o: They refused to bow down and worship Nebuchadnezzar's golden image
They ate unclean food from the king's royal table
They refused to pay taxes to the Babylonian empire
They plotted to overthrow the king's governors
qs.e: The three Hebrew youths stood firm in their allegiance to Yahweh, refusing to bow to Nebuchadnezzar's sixty-cubit gold statue, declaring God was able to deliver them.

qs.q: According to Proverbs 6:6-8, what character trait is commended when people are urged to 'Go to the ant, thou sluggard'?
o: Proactive diligence, foresight, and hard work without needing a supervisor
qs.e: Proverbs 6 commends the ant for preparing her food in the summer and gathering provisions in the harvest without a ruler, rebuking laziness.

qs.q: During his call vision in Isaiah 6:5-7, how was Isaiah's sense of guilt and unclean lips removed?
o: An angel poured holy anointing oil on his head
By washing his hands in a golden basin
He recited a formal prayer of purification
One of the seraphim touched his lips with a live coal taken from the altar with tongs
qs.e: After Isaiah cried 'Woe is me!', a seraph touched his mouth with a burning coal from the altar, declaring his iniquity was taken away and his sin purged.

qs.q: What main message did John the Baptist preach in the wilderness of Judea in Matthew 3:1-2?
o: 'Build synagogues in every city of Israel'
'Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand'
'Bring your tithes to the Temple in Jerusalem'
qs.e: John the Baptist served as the forerunner preaching a baptism of repentance for the remission of sins, announcing the near arrival of the kingdom of heaven.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Sower (Matthew 13:18-23), what does the seed sown among thorns represent?
o: A person who rejects the gospel immediately upon hearing
A person who receives the word with joy but falls away during persecution
A person who hears the word, but worldly cares and deceitfulness of riches choke the word
A fruitful believer who produces a hundredfold yield
qs.e: Jesus explained that thorny ground represents one who hears the word, but anxiety about life and the lure of wealth choke it so that it becomes unfruitful.

qs.q: Why were Ananias and Sapphira struck dead in Acts 5:1-11?
o: They betrayed Peter to the Roman authorities
They lied to the Holy Spirit and the church by pretending to donate the full price of their sold land while keeping back part
They preached false doctrine to Gentile converts
They refused to give any money to the poor
qs.e: Peter pointed out that their sin was not keeping property, but deceitfully pretending total sacrifice while retaining part of the price, thereby lying to the Holy Spirit.

qs.q: In Galatians 5:22-23, Paul lists nine virtues that constitute the 'fruit of the Spirit' to demonstrate that spiritual maturity produces
o: Strict adherence to legalistic outward regulations
The ability to speak in angelic tongues exclusively
A transformed character reflecting love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, and temperance
qs.e: Paul contrasts the works of the flesh with the unified fruit of the Spirit, showing that living by the Spirit produces Christlike character against which there is no law.

qs.q: In Genesis 4:3-7, why did God accept Abel's offering while having no respect for Cain's offering?
o: Abel offered his best firstlings in faith and obedience, whereas Cain's heart and attitude lacked genuine faith
Cain offered wild berries instead of cultivated crops
Abel was older than Cain and had priestly priority
Cain brought his offering to the wrong location
qs.e: Hebrews 11:4 explains that by faith Abel offered a more excellent sacrifice than Cain. God evaluated not merely the material but the reverent faith and righteous heart of the giver.

qs.q: When God commanded Abraham to offer Isaac as a burnt offering on Mount Moriah in Genesis 22, Abraham's prompt obedience revealed his
o: Absolute trust that God was faithful and able to fulfill His covenant even if He raised Isaac from the dead
Ignorance of the true nature of God
Desire to gain favor with neighboring pagan tribes
qs.e: Abraham demonstrated supreme faith by obeying immediately, believing that God who promised a great nation through Isaac could perform resurrection (Hebrews 11:17-19).

qs.q: In Exodus 3, when Moses hesitated at the burning bush saying 'Who am I?', God answered his insecurity primarily by promising
o: 'Certainly I will be with thee', guaranteeing His divine presence and power
To destroy Pharaoh immediately before Moses arrived
To equip Moses with a royal Egyptian army
To make Aaron the leader instead of Moses
qs.e: God answered Moses' self-doubt by focusing not on Moses' adequacy but on God's abiding presence: 'Certainly I will be with thee' (Exodus 3:12).

qs.q: Jephthah's rash vow before fighting the Ammonites in Judges 11 highlights the tragic danger of
o: Refusing to train soldiers in archery
Accepting leadership from elders of Gilead
Making foolish, bargain-driven vows to God without considering the moral consequences
qs.e: Jephthah vowed that whatever came out of his house first upon return would be offered as a burnt offering, resulting in his only daughter coming out to meet him.

qs.q: When King David brought the Ark of the Covenant to Jerusalem in 2 Samuel 6, what solemn lesson was demonstrated by the death of Uzzah?
o: That only the king could touch the Ark during transport
That foreign oxen should never carry holy sacred vessels
That Jerusalem was not yet ready for the Ark
That holy things must be treated with reverence according to God's ordained instructions, not human convenience
qs.e: Uzzah touched the Ark when oxen stumbled. Numbers 4 forbade non-Levites from touching holy items; God required obedience to His sacred ordinances, not improvised methods.

qs.q: How did Elisha restore life to the dead son of the Shunammite woman in 2 Kings 4:32-35?
o: He touched the child with Elijah's mantle
He anointed the child's head with oil from a golden horn
He stretched himself upon the child, prayed earnestly to the Lord, and the child sneezed seven times and opened his eyes
He commanded the mother to bathe the child in the Jordan River
qs.e: Elisha went into the room, shut the door, prayed, and lay upon the child putting his mouth on his mouth and hands on his hands until the boy's flesh grew warm and he revived.

qs.q: In Jeremiah 1:11-14, what two symbolic visions were shown to Jeremiah to confirm his prophetic appointment?
o: A basket of summer fruit and a plumb line
A chariot of fire and a flying scroll
A rod of an almond tree (God watching over His word) and a boiling pot facing from the north (disaster coming)
A golden lampstand and two olive trees
qs.e: Jeremiah saw an almond rod ('shaqed') signifying God watching ('shoqed') over His word to perform it, and a boiling pot tilted from the north symbolizing judgment via Babylon.

qs.q: The prophecy in Joel 2:28-29 ('I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh') was cited by Peter on the day of Pentecost (Acts 2:16-18) to explain that
o: The outpouring of the Holy Spirit fulfilled Old Testament promise for believers across age, gender, and social status
All believers were required to move to Judea
The Temple in Jerusalem would immediately be destroyed
Gentiles were required to observe Jewish feast days
qs.e: Peter declared that the Pentecost miracle fulfilled Joel's prophecy that God's Spirit would be poured out universally upon sons, daughters, young men, old men, and servants.

qs.q: In the Lord's Prayer (Matthew 6:9-13 / Sermon on the Mount), what priority is established by placing 'Hallowed be thy name' and 'Thy kingdom come' before personal petitions?
o: That God's glory, holiness, and sovereign will must hold first place in a believer's prayers
That personal forgiveness is unnecessary if one prays for the kingdom
That prayer should only consist of liturgical praise without personal requests
That human material survival takes precedence over spiritual matters
qs.e: Jesus taught believers to align their desires first with God's honor and kingdom before asking for daily bread, forgiveness, and protection from temptation.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10:25-37), why did Jesus use a Samaritan as the hero who showed true neighborly love?
o: Because Samaritans were the official priests of the Jerusalem Temple
To encourage Jews to adopt Samaritan religious customs
To challenge religious prejudice and show that true neighborliness is defined by practical mercy, not ethnic or ceremonial status
Because the priest and Levite had already died on the road
qs.e: Jews despised Samaritans, yet Jesus showed that the hated Samaritan embodied true neighborly love by showing compassion where religious Jewish leaders passed by.

qs.q: In Luke 5:17-26, when four friends lowered a paralyzed man through the roof, why were the scribes and Pharisees offended by Jesus' response?
o: Because the healing took place on a high holy day
Because Jesus damaged the physical roof of the house
Because the paralytic was a Roman soldier
Because Jesus declared 'Thy sins be forgiven thee', claiming divine authority to forgive sins
qs.e: The Pharisees reasoned, 'Who is this which speaketh blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone?' Jesus then healed the man to prove His authority to forgive sins.

qs.q: What vision did Peter see on the rooftop in Joppa (Acts 10:9-16) prior to visiting Cornelius in Caesarea?
o: An angel holding a sword standing over the city
A golden altar with seven burning lamps
A fiery chariot ascending into the clouds
A sheet let down from heaven containing all kinds of four-footed beasts, reptiles, and birds
qs.e: God showed Peter a vessel like a great sheet filled with unclean animals and commanded 'Kill and eat', teaching Peter not to call any person clean or unclean whom God has cleansed.

qs.q: How did Philip respond when the Holy Spirit directed him to the chariot of the Ethiopian Eunuch on the road to Gaza (Acts 8:26-39)?
o: He asked for a monetary gift before explaining scripture
He commanded the Eunuch to travel to Jerusalem for circumcision
He ran to the chariot, heard him reading Isaiah 53, explained the gospel of Jesus, and baptized him
He advised the Eunuch to study the Law under Gamaliel
qs.e: Philip obeyed immediately, opened his mouth at Isaiah 53 ('He was led as a sheep to the slaughter'), preached Jesus to him, and baptized him in nearby water.

qs.q: In Acts 16:25-34, what was the immediate spiritual outcome of Paul and Silas praying and singing hymns at midnight in the Philippian jail?
o: They escaped undetected into the wilderness
The prison guards fled in terror
A great earthquake shook the prison foundations, leading to the conversion and baptism of the jailer and his household
The Roman magistrate immediately released them with an official apology
qs.e: The earthquake opened doors and unfastened chains. When the jailer was about to kill himself, Paul reassured him, leading the jailer to ask, 'Sirs, what must I do to be saved?'

qs.q: According to James 1:22-25, hearing the word of God without practicing it is compared to a person who
o: Plants seeds in rich fertile soil during spring
Sails a ship without an iron anchor
Builds a house upon solid bedrock
Looks at his natural face in a mirror and immediately walks away forgetting what he looked like
qs.e: James warns against self-deception: one who hears but does not obey is like a man beholding his natural face in a glass who goes his way and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.

qs.q: What primary theological truth is taught by God's judgment upon the builders of the Tower of Babel in Genesis 11:1-9?
o: That God opposes urban development entirely
That multilingualism was a reward for architectural achievement
That brick construction is inferior to stone building
That human self-exaltation and autonomous pride apart from God result in confusion and division
qs.e: The Babel project sought to 'make us a name' in proud defiance of God's mandate to fill the earth. God confused their language to humble human pride and scatter them.

qs.q: The prophet Shemaiah's message to King Rehoboam in 1 Kings 12:21-24 ('This thing is from me') prevented civil war between Judah and northern Israel by demonstrating that
o: The division of the kingdom was an accomplishment of divine judgment against Solomon's idolatry
Rehoboam's army was too poorly equipped for battle
Northern Israel had made a military treaty with Egypt
qs.e: When Rehoboam assembled 180,000 soldiers to fight Israel, Shemaiah delivered God's word stating the division fulfilled Yahweh's judgment, prompting Rehoboam to disband his troops.

qs.q: Job's rebuke of his three friends (Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar) centered on their erroneous theological assumption that
o: All human suffering is a direct, proportional punishment for specific personal sins committed by the sufferer
God does not intervene in human affairs
Riches are a sign of divine disfavor
Sacrifices are completely useless in worship
qs.e: Job's friends held a rigid retribution dogma that because Job suffered terribly, he must have committed grave secret sins. Job maintained his innocence against their false accusations.

qs.q: The book of Habakkuk addresses the perplexing dilemma of divine justice, concluding in Habakkuk 2:4 with the foundational truth that
o: The proud man's soul is not upright, but the just shall live by his faith
God's laws change according to geopolitical circumstances
Military force is the only solution to national oppression
The wicked will always prosper without end
qs.e: Habakkuk questioned why God used wicked Babylon to discipline Judah. God revealed that worldly powers collapse in pride, whereas the righteous person perseveres by steadfast faith.

qs.q: In the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5:17-20), Jesus clarified His relationship to the Old Testament Scriptures by declaring that He came NOT to destroy the Law or Prophets, BUT to
o: Restrict scripture interpretation to the Pharisaic school
Replace the Law with Roman civil statutes
Abolish every moral requirement for believers
Fulfill them completely through His life, teaching, and sacrificial work
qs.e: Jesus stated: 'Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.' He revealed the full spiritual depth and completion of God's Law.

qs.q: During Jesus' prayer agony in the Garden of Gethsemane (Matthew 26:36-46), His words 'Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt' express
o: A desire to flee from Jerusalem before arrest
A reluctance to fulfill His earthly ministry
A dispute among the Trinity regarding salvation
The agonizing human reality of His impending suffering combined with total, sinless submission to the Father's redemptive will
qs.e: Gethsemane showcases Jesus' genuine humanity facing the horrific weight of bearing sin and divine judgment, embraced through absolute, obedient submission to the Father's will.

qs.q: The communal life of the early believers in Jerusalem described in Acts 2:44-47 and 4:32-35 was characterized spiritually by
o: Isolation from the surrounding Jewish community
Forced state communism under apostolic decree
Compulsory taxation on all Jerusalem residents
Voluntary unity, generous sharing of possessions to meet needs, gladness of heart, and continuous praise
qs.e: The early church practiced voluntary, Spirit-led generosity: believers held all things common, selling property to distribute to anyone in need, resulting in favor with all people.

qs.q: In Acts 8:9-24, Simon Magus the sorcerer was severely rebuked by Peter because Simon attempted to
o: Perform magic arts inside a Christian church
Claim that he was the high priest of Jerusalem
Purchase the power of imparting the Holy Spirit with money, treating divine grace as a commercial commodity
Forbid Philip from preaching in Samaria
qs.e: Simon offered money saying, 'Give me also this power'. Peter answered: 'Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money.'

qs.q: Paul's dramatic conversion on the Damascus road in Acts 9:1-19 fundamentally altered his theology because he realized that persecuting Christians was actually
o: A waste of Pharisaic financial resources
Persecuting Jesus Christ Himself, the risen and glorified Lord
A violation of Roman military law
qs.e: The voice from heaven declared: 'Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? ... I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.' Paul learned the organic union between Christ and His persecuted Church.

qs.q: In Philippians 2:5-11, Paul presents the 'mind of Christ' as the ultimate model for Christian living, highlighting Jesus' voluntary movement from
o: Earthly poverty to political kingship in Rome
Minor prophet status to angelic priesthood
A quiet life in Nazareth to military leadership
Equality with God to self-emptying humbleness, servant obedience unto death on the cross, and subsequent divine exaltation
qs.e: The Kenosis passage describes Christ emptying Himself, taking the form of a servant, humbling Himself unto the death of the cross, wherefore God highly exalted Him.

qs.q: In 2 Samuel 7, God's covenant response to David's desire to build a house (temple) for Yahweh inverted David's intention by promising that
o: David must abdicate his throne in favor of Jonathan's son
David's military conquests would cease immediately
Yahweh would build a 'house' (an enduring royal dynasty) for David, establishing his throne forever in Christ
The Temple must be built in Samaria rather than Jerusalem
qs.e: When David proposed building a house of cedar for God, God answered that He would build David a house—an everlasting kingdom and dynasty fulfilled ultimately in the Messiah.

qs.q: Zerubbabel and Jeshua's refusal of Samaritan assistance in rebuilding the Temple in Ezra 4:1-3 was based on the principled conviction that
o: The Persian king prohibited foreign workers in Jerusalem
Samaritans demanded ownership of the Temple treasury
Religious syncretism would compromise the covenant purity and true worship of Yahweh
qs.e: The returned exiles knew that spiritual compromise and syncretistic worship had brought down Israel previously; true restoration required uncompromising commitment to Yahweh alone.

qs.q: In Peter's ministry at Lydda and Joppa (Acts 9:32-43), the healing of bedridden Aeneas and the raising of benevolent Dorcas (Tabitha) resulted in
o: Widespread spiritual awakening and many turning to the Lord across those coastal regions
The establishment of a monastic order in Joppa
Immediate Roman persecution against all apostles
Peter's appointment as civil governor of Judea
qs.e: Acts 9 notes that when Aeneas was healed and Dorcas raised to life, the miraculous power of God caused all who dwelt at Lydda, Saron, and Joppa to turn to the Lord in faith.

qs.q: In Romans 3:21-26, Paul describes God's righteousness revealed in Christ's atonement as 'propitiation', demonstrating that God can be BOTH
o: Lawgiver at Sinai and philosopher in Athens
Just (upholding His holy law against sin) and the Justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus
A harsh judge to Gentiles and a lenient father to Jews
A distant ruler and an earthly monarch
qs.e: Romans 3:26 explains that Christ's sacrificial death satisfied divine justice for sin so that God remains righteous while mercifully declaring righteous those who trust in Jesus.

qs.q: In 1 Peter 1:6-7, the apostle explains that believers experience various trials and suffering in order that
o: God may punish them for secret ancestral sins
The genuineness of their faith, being much more precious than gold refined by fire, may result in praise and glory at Christ's revelation
They may earn salvation through personal endurance
They may prove superior to non-believers in physical endurance
qs.e: Peter compares trials to a furnace refining gold: suffering tests and purifies true faith, removing dross so that it redounds to praise, honor, and glory when Jesus Christ appears.

qs.q: What name did Jacob give to the place where he saw a ladder reaching from earth to heaven in a dream in Genesis 28?
qs.e: Jacob named the place Bethel ('House of God'), declaring, 'Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not.'

qs.q: Which officer of Pharaoh's guard purchased Joseph as a slave from the Ishmeelites in Genesis 37:36?
qs.e: Genesis 37:36 records that the Midianites sold Joseph into Egypt unto Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard.

qs.q: How did Jael kill Sisera, the commander of Jabin's Canaanite army, while he slept in her tent in Judges 4?
o: By driving a tent peg through his temple into the ground
By striking him with a sword
By trapping him in a pit
qs.e: Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite, gave Sisera milk to drink, covered him with a blanket, and drove a wooden tent spike through his temple with a mallet.

qs.q: Which Judean king was struck with leprosy when he arrogantly attempted to burn incense on the altar in the Temple (2 Chronicles 26)?
