qs.e: King Uzziah became proud and intruded into the holy priest's role to burn incense; God immediately smote him with leprosy on his forehead.

qs.q: Which prophet was swallowed by a great fish when he attempted to flee to Tarshish instead of preaching to Nineveh (Jonah 1)?
qs.e: Jonah ran away from Yahweh's commission to Nineveh, boarded a ship to Tarshish, was thrown overboard during a storm, and was swallowed by a large fish.

qs.q: Who was the righteous elderly man in Jerusalem who took the infant Jesus in his arms at the Temple and praised God (Luke 2:25-32)?
qs.e: Simeon had been promised by the Holy Spirit that he would not see death before seeing the Lord's Christ; he held Jesus and proclaimed the Nunc Dimittis.

qs.q: Which miracle of Jesus involved restoring a man's sight at the pool of Siloam after applying clay to his eyes in John 9?
o: Healing of the blind man at Bethsaida
Healing of the man born blind
Healing of the two blind men of Jericho
qs.e: In John 9, Jesus spat on the ground, made clay, anointed the eyes of a man blind from birth, and told him to wash in Siloam, restoring his sight.

qs.q: According to Genesis 2:18-24, why did God create woman from one of Adam's ribs?
o: To establish a legal system of property inheritance
To provide a servant to tend the gardens
Because it was not good for man to be alone, providing a suitable helper and partner for covenant union
Because Adam asked God for a companion
qs.e: God observed that 'It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him', instituting companionate marriage.

qs.q: In Genesis 17, what physical covenant sign did God institute with Abraham and his male descendants?
qs.e: Genesis 17:10-11 establishes circumcision of every male child on the eighth day as the physical sign of God's everlasting covenant with Abraham's offspring.

qs.q: While in Egyptian prison (Genesis 40), Joseph demonstrated his gift of dream interpretation by interpreting the dreams of Pharaoh's
o: Chief army general and chief treasurer
qs.e: Joseph correctly interpreted the butler's dream of three vine branches (restoration in three days) and the baker's dream of three baskets (execution in three days).

qs.q: What was the final, devastating tenth plague brought upon Egypt that forced Pharaoh to let Israel depart in Exodus 11-12?
o: Three days of total darkness over Egypt
The death of all firstborn humans and beasts across Egypt
The plague of hail and fire
The plague of locusts devouring crops
qs.e: At midnight, the Lord smote all the firstborn in Egypt, from Pharaoh's heir to the captive in dungeon, leading Pharaoh to urgently expel Israel.

qs.q: When two women presented a living baby and a dead baby to King Solomon in 1 Kings 3:16-28, how did Solomon reveal the real mother?
o: He interviewed neighbors from their village
He asked the high priest to draw lots
He commanded the baby to be cut in two with a sword, knowing the true mother would yield her rights to save her child
qs.e: Solomon's decree to divide the child triggered the true mother's deep maternal compassion, willing to give up the child so he might live.

qs.q: How did God sustain Elijah by the brook Cherith during the drought in 1 Kings 17:1-6?
o: Ravens brought him bread and meat morning and evening, and he drank from the brook
Angels brought him manna every morning
A widow provided meal and oil daily
He found wild honey and locusts in the desert
qs.e: 1 Kings 17:6 records that ravens brought Elijah bread and flesh in the morning and evening, and he drank water from the brook Cherith.

qs.q: Why was Daniel thrown into the lions' den in Daniel 6?
o: He continued praying to Yahweh three times daily despite a royal decree forbidding prayer to any god except the king
He led a rebellion among Median officials
He damaged the idols in the Babylonian temple
He refused to pay royal taxes to King Darius
qs.e: Daniel's rivals tricked Darius into signing an unalterable decree; Daniel faithfully prayed facing Jerusalem three times a day as before, refusing compromise.

qs.q: In Jeremiah 18:1-10, what primary lesson did God teach Jeremiah at the potter's house?
o: That clay vessels should never be used in Temple sacrifices
That Israel's destruction was irreversible under any circumstances
That God holds sovereign authority to reshape and reform nations based on their repentance or disobedience
That pottery was Israel's main commercial export
qs.e: God showed Jeremiah that as clay is in the potter's hand to reshape spoiled vessels, so is Israel in Yahweh's hand to relent of judgment if they repent.

qs.q: In Matthew 6:25-34 (Sermon on the Mount), Jesus admonished His disciples against material anxiety by pointing to
o: God's providential care for the birds of the air and the lilies of the field
The financial wisdom of King Solomon
The military strength of Roman garrisons
The storage grain bins of Egyptian rulers
qs.e: Jesus taught that if God feeds birds and clothes wild lilies, He will much more care for His children, commanding them to 'seek ye first the kingdom of God'.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Pharisee and the Tax Collector (Luke 18:9-14), why did the tax collector go home justified rather than the Pharisee?
o: The tax collector was a descendant of Aaron
The tax collector paid a larger donation to the Temple
The tax collector humbly confessed his sin ('God be merciful to me a sinner'), while the Pharisee prayed self-righteously boasting of his good works
The Pharisee stood in the wrong section of the court
qs.e: Jesus taught that everyone who exalts himself shall be humbled, but he who humbles himself before God in sincere repentance will be justified.

qs.q: In Acts 3, what miracle performed by Peter and John at the Beautiful Gate of the Temple drew a massive crowd?
o: Healing a man lame from his mother's womb who walked, leaped, and praised God
Turning water into oil for Temple lamps
Raising a dead girl to life
Calming a sudden dust storm over Jerusalem
qs.e: Peter said, 'Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk', healing the lame beggar instantly.

qs.q: Why were seven men full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom appointed in Acts 6:1-6?
o: To draft letters to Gentile churches in Syria
To collect Temple taxes from foreign converts
To oversee the daily distribution of food to Hellenistic Jewish widows, resolving internal complaint and allowing apostles to focus on prayer and word
To serve as military officers for the Jerusalem church
qs.e: The church appointed the Seven (including Stephen and Philip) to manage practical social administration fairly, preserving apostolic focus on prayer and ministry of the Word.

qs.q: When Jacob lived with Laban in Haran (Genesis 29-31), Laban deceived Jacob by substituting Leah for Rachel on the wedding night, demonstrating the principle that
o: Jacob preferred Leah over Rachel originally
Firstborn daughters had no marriage rights in Haran
Laban was completely above moral criticism
Jacob, who had deceived his father Isaac, experienced the painful consequences of deception himself
qs.e: Jacob's experience with Laban illustrates cause-and-consequence / moral retribution in narrative history: the deceiver Jacob was himself deceived by his uncle regarding the firstborn daughter.

qs.q: When King Saul sought guidance from a medium at Endor prior to the Battle of Mount Gilboa (1 Samuel 28), his action exposed
o: A legal requirement under the Law of Moses
His deep spiritual wisdom in times of national crisis
His desire to make peace with the Philistines
His complete abandonment by God after he repeatedly disobeyed Yahweh and killed the priests of Nob
qs.e: Saul turned to necromancy because Yahweh answered him not by dreams, Urim, or prophets; his illegal resort to a medium confirmed his total spiritual tragic downfall.

qs.q: When a man of God from Judah prophesied against Jeroboam's altar at Bethel in 1 Kings 13, what miraculous sign immediately occurred?
o: Fire descended from heaven and consumed the priest
The golden calf melted into liquid gold
A sudden earthquake destroyed the city walls
The altar split apart and the ashes poured out, while Jeroboam's outstretched hand withered
qs.e: 1 Kings 13:3-5 records that the altar split and ashes poured out according to the prophetic sign, and when Jeroboam put out his hand to command his arrest, his hand withered.

qs.q: What miracle did Elisha perform when a worker lost a borrowed iron axe head in the Jordan River (2 Kings 6:1-7)?
o: He cut a stick, threw it into the water, and the iron axe head floated to the surface
He dived into the river and retrieved it by hand
He commanded the river to dry up temporarily
He paid the owner money to replace the tool
qs.e: When the man cried 'Alas, master! for it was borrowed', Elisha cut a stick, cast it in, and caused the heavy iron head to float, demonstrating God's care for practical human needs.

qs.q: How did Nehemiah overcome the persistent ridicule and military threats of Sanballat and Tobiah while rebuilding Jerusalem's walls (Nehemiah 4)?
o: He prayed to God, set a continuous watch day and night, and armed the workers with swords, spears, and bows
He agreed to meet them for peace talks in the plain of Ono
He paid them tribute money from royal taxes
He abandoned construction until Persian troops arrived
qs.e: Nehemiah combined prayer and practical vigilance: half the men worked while half held weapons, and every builder labored with his sword girded by his side.

qs.q: In Malachi 3:8-10, God accused Israel of robbing Him by withholding tithes and offerings, promising that if they brought full tithes into the storehouse, He would
o: Build a second temple in Jerusalem
Open the windows of heaven and pour out a blessing so great there would not be room enough to receive it
Make them rulers over all surrounding heathen nations
Exempt them from all earthly physical sickness
qs.e: Malachi 3:10 challenges believers to test God through faithful stewardship, promising abundant divine favor and protection against crop devourers.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Talents (Matthew 25:14-30), why was the servant who received one talent condemned by his master upon his return?
o: Because he gave the money to foreign merchants
Because he demanded higher wages before working
Because he lost the money in bad investments
Because he wickedly buried the talent out of fear and sloth, accusing his master of being harsh rather than putting it to productive use
qs.e: The unfaithful servant made excuses, called his master a hard man, and buried his talent. Jesus condemned his lazy, faithless attitude and took away his talent.

qs.q: Before raising Lazarus from the dead in Bethany (John 11), Jesus made what profound messianic declaration to Martha?
o: 'I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman'
'I am the light of the world'
'I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live'
'I am the good shepherd that giveth his life for the sheep'
qs.e: In John 11:25-26, Jesus revealed His divine power over death itself, reassuring Martha that eternal life and physical resurrection rest entirely in Him.

qs.q: When Peter was miraculously released from Herod Agrippa I's prison by an angel in Acts 12:1-17, where did he go to find believers praying for him?
o: To the home of Cornelius in Caesarea
To the Temple court at the Beautiful Gate
To the royal palace of Herod
To the house of Mary, the mother of John Mark, where many were gathered praying
qs.e: Acts 12:12 records that after realizing he was truly freed, Peter came to Mary's house where believers were fervently praying for his release.

qs.q: During Paul's sermon on the Areopagus (Mars' Hill) in Athens in Acts 17:22-31, how did he connect with his Gentile audience?
o: By quoting Old Testament Levitical dietary codes
By condemning Greek philosophy as totally worthless without explanation
By referencing their altar dedicated 'To the Unknown God' and quoting Greek poets to preach the Creator, repentance, and resurrection
By presenting himself as a Roman magistrate
qs.e: Paul used contextual bridges: noting their altar 'To the Unknown God', citing Epimenides/Aratus ('In him we live and move...'), and proclaiming the one True God who raised Jesus.

qs.q: In Romans 4, how does Paul use Abraham to prove the doctrine of justification by faith apart from legal works?
o: Abraham earned righteousness through military victory over four kings
Abraham was justified because he built many stone altars
Abraham believed God and it was counted to him for righteousness BEFORE he was circumcised
Abraham kept the full Levitical Law before Isaac's birth
qs.e: Genesis 15:6 declares Abraham believed God and it was reckoned as righteousness; Paul points out this occurred years before circumcision (Genesis 17), making Abraham the father of all who believe.

qs.q: According to 1 Corinthians 13:13, which three Christian virtues abide permanently, and which is declared to be the greatest?
o: Wisdom, power, and wealth; wealth is greatest
Faith, hope, and love; love is greatest
Fastings, prayers, and alms; fastings is greatest
Prophecy, tongues, and knowledge; tongues is greatest
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 13:13 concludes: 'And now abideth faith, hope, charity [love], these three; but the greatest of these is charity.'

qs.q: In Matthew 7:24-27 (Sermon on the Mount), the wise man who built his house on rock represents a person who
o: Offers expensive animal sacrifices at the Temple
Memorizes the Law of Moses without performing it
Constructs physical houses using solid granite
Listens to Jesus' teachings and actively puts them into practice
qs.e: Jesus explained that everyone who hears His words and DOES them is like a wise man building on rock; when floods come, the house stands firm.

qs.q: When Jesus cleansed the Temple in Jerusalem (Matthew 21:12-13), what reason did He give for driving out buyers and sellers?
o: They were selling animals without priestly licenses
They were operating after sunset on the Sabbath
They were using foreign coins instead of Shekels
'My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves'
qs.e: Jesus overturned moneychangers' tables, rebuking commercial exploitation in holy places by quoting Isaiah 56:7 ('house of prayer') and Jeremiah 7:11 ('den of thieves').

qs.q: What happened to the prophet of Judah in 1 Kings 13 after he was enticed by an old prophet of Bethel to disobey God's command not to eat or drink in Bethel?
o: He was struck with leprosy in Bethel
A lion met him on the road and killed him, leaving his body and donkey standing beside the lion
He was appointed chief priest by Jeroboam
He returned safely to Judah and wrote a book
qs.e: Because the man of God believed a lie and disobeyed Yahweh's explicit instructions not to eat bread in Bethel, a lion killed him on his journey home as divine judgment.

qs.q: In Isaiah 53:4-6, the Servant of the Lord is depicted as bearing human griefs and carrying sorrows, presenting the foundational gospel doctrine of
o: Political emancipation of Israel from Babylon
Substitutionary atonement, where the Servant was wounded for our transgressions and bruised for our iniquities
Symbolic military victory over Gentile empires
qs.e: Isaiah 53 articulates vicarious substitution: 'the LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all', foreshadowing Christ's redemptive sacrifice on the cross.

qs.q: Jesus' Triumphal Entry into Jerusalem riding on a donkey colt (Matthew 21:1-11) fulfilled Zechariah 9:9, demonstrating that the Messiah came as
o: A humble, peaceful King bringing spiritual salvation and peace
A worldly military conqueror riding a war horse to overthrow Rome
A wealthy temporal monarch seeking earthly tribute
A severe priest enforcing legalistic regulations
qs.e: Zechariah 9:9 prophesied: 'Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion... thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass...'

qs.q: In 1 Corinthians 15:12-20, Paul vigorously defends the necessity of the bodily resurrection of Jesus Christ, arguing that if Christ did NOT rise from the dead, then
o: Gentiles must adopt Jewish circumcision immediately
Christian preaching is vain, faith is futile, and believers are still in their sins
The Mosaic ceremonial law remains binding forever
Believers should build larger worship halls
qs.e: Paul asserts that Christ's resurrection is the non-negotiable anchor of Christian salvation; without it, faith is useless, preaching empty, and hope beyond death non-existent.

qs.q: In Romans 13:1-7, Paul outlines the Christian obligation toward civil governing authorities, teaching that rulers are ordained by God to
o: Collect tithes for the Jerusalem Temple
Maintain public order, punish evil conduct, and reward good behavior, acting as ministers of God for good
Enforce Church attendance and Christian baptism
Abolish private property across the nation
qs.e: Romans 13 describes secular government as God's instrument for civic order and justice ('a revenger to execute wrath upon him that doeth evil'), commanding submission and tax payment.

qs.q: In the Annunciation account in Luke 1:26-38, Mary's response to the angel Gabriel ('Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word') exemplifies
o: Total spiritual surrender, humble faith, and obedience to God's redemptive purpose
A demand for personal wealth and royal status
Reluctant acquiescence under threat of divine punishment
qs.e: Mary's Fiat displays supreme faith and humble submission to God's divine calling, accepting the role of bearing the Messiah despite potential social stigma.

qs.q: Why was the widow of Zarephath's willingness to bake a small cake for Elijah first (1 Kings 17:8-16) a profound test of faith?
o: Because baking bread on that day was forbidden by local law
Because she had abundant flour and oil stored in her cellar
Because she was reduced to her last handful of flour and drop of oil, expecting to eat it with her son and die of starvation
Because Elijah was a foreign general from Syria
qs.e: The widow faced extreme scarcity during famine; trusting Elijah's prophetic word to feed God's messenger first resulted in her jar of flour and jug of oil not failing.

qs.q: During the feeding of the 5,000 recorded in John 6:1-14, Jesus tested Philip by asking where bread could be bought, leading to the demonstration that
o: Human financial resources (200 denarii) were completely insufficient, but divine power multiplies humble offerings (five barley loaves and two fish)
Disciples should always carry emergency gold coins
Only wealthy travelers were entitled to eat
The crowd should be sent away immediately to buy food in villages
qs.e: Philip noted 200 denarii would not suffice. Andrew found a boy's five barley loaves and two small fish; Jesus blessed them, feeding the vast crowd with twelve baskets remaining.

qs.q: In Paul's speech to the Ephesian elders at Miletus (Acts 20:17-35), he modeled servant leadership by emphasizing that he
o: Refused to preach to Gentiles in public places
Coveted no man's silver or gold, worked with his own hands for necessities, and remembered Jesus' words: 'It is more blessed to give than to receive'
Appointed himself supreme bishop over all Asian churches
Sought royal wealth and official titles in Ephesus
qs.e: Paul exhorted church leaders to shepherd God's flock selflessly, reminding them of his personal manual labor and quoting Jesus' beatitude on generous giving.

qs.q: When Peter defended his visit to the Gentile house of Cornelius before the Jerusalem church in Acts 11:1-18, what key evidence convinced his critics?
o: Cornelius had given a large monetary donation to the Jerusalem poor
God bestowed the Holy Spirit upon the Gentiles just as He did upon Jewish apostles at Pentecost
The Roman Emperor issued a decree protecting Christians
Cornelius agreed to adopt full Levitical circumcision
qs.e: Peter explained: 'Forasmuch then as God gave them the like gift as he did unto us... what was I, that I could withstand God?' The Jerusalem church glorified God that repentance unto life was granted to Gentiles.

qs.q: In Proverbs 3:5-6, believers are commanded to 'Trust in the LORD with all thine heart', which requires explicitly that they
o: Depend entirely upon human intellectual reasoning
Rely exclusively on material wealth for security
Lean not unto their own understanding, but acknowledge Him in all their ways so He may direct their paths
Avoid seeking counsel from Christian elders
qs.e: Proverbs 3:5-6 warns against self-reliant human rationalization, promising that wholehearted trust and surrender to God ensures clear divine direction in life.

qs.q: In 2 Corinthians 5:17-21, Paul describes the fundamental ministry entrusted to every Christian believer as the ministry of
o: Organizing monastic communities in the wilderness
Reconciliation, proclaiming that God was in Christ reconciling the world unto Himself
qs.e: Paul explains that anyone in Christ is a new creation; God has given believers the ministry of reconciliation, calling them ambassadors for Christ to implore people to be reconciled to God.

qs.q: Comparing the divine calls of Isaiah (Isaiah 6), Jeremiah (Jeremiah 1), and Ezekiel (Ezekiel 1-3) demonstrates that a authentic biblical prophet's authority originates from
o: Direct divine commission, personal cleansing, and empowerment by God's Word and Spirit regardless of human adequacy or opposition
Inherited royal bloodline from King David
qs.e: All major prophetic calls highlight divine initiative: God reveals His holiness/glory, purges guilt or touches the mouth, equips the reluctant prophet, and sends them with His authoritative message.

qs.q: In Galatians 3:23-29, Paul explains the historical purpose of the Mosaic Law prior to Christ's coming by describing the Law as a 'schoolmaster' (paidagogos) designed to
o: Provide eternal life through flawless rule-keeping
Guard and tutor humanity under restraint until Christ came, bringing us to justification by faith
Establish permanent ceremonial distinctions between nations
qs.e: Paul clarifies that the Law acted as a strict guardian/pedagogue exposing sin and pointing to Christ; now that faith has come, believers are mature sons of God in Christ Jesus.

qs.q: The martyrdom of Stephen in Acts 7:54-60 marked a decisive turning point in early church history because it
o: Led to the immediate destruction of the Jerusalem Temple
Ended apostolic preaching in Jerusalem permanently
Triggered severe persecution that scattered believers throughout Judea and Samaria, accelerating worldwide gospel expansion
Prompted the Roman governor to ban Christianity
qs.e: Acts 8:1 records that Stephen's death ignited a great persecution against the Jerusalem church; believers scattered abroad preaching the word everywhere (fulfilling Acts 1:8).

qs.q: In James 2:14-26, the author asserts that 'faith without works is dead', illustrating his point by showing that genuine saving faith MUST be demonstrated by
o: Theoretical agreement with monotheistic theology ('the devils also believe')
Practical actions of love and active obedience, as exemplified by Abraham offering Isaac and Rahab receiving the spies
Erecting physical monuments in sacred places
Strict observance of ceremonial kosher dietary rules
qs.e: James argues that real faith is not passive mental assent but living, active obedience; works are the visible fruit and vindication of genuine saving faith.

qs.q: In Hosea 14, the prophet concludes his message by calling backsliding Israel to repent, describing God's response as healing their backsliding freely because God's anger is
o: Turned away from them, restoring them like the dew making Israel blossom like the lily and olive tree
qs.e: Hosea 14 presents a poetic climax of divine restoration: when Israel repents of idols and trusts God, Yahweh heals their backsliding and loves them freely with vibrant spiritual fruitfulness.

qs.q: Why did Moses flee from Egypt to the land of Midian in Exodus 2:11-15?
o: To escape a severe famine in Goshen
Because God commanded him to leave immediately
To marry the daughter of the king of Midian
Because Pharaoh sought to kill him after Moses killed an Egyptian who was beating a Hebrew
qs.e: When Moses saw an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew brother, he slew the Egyptian. When Pharaoh heard it, he sought to slay Moses, forcing Moses to flee to Midian.

qs.q: Which prophet promised King Hezekiah that God would add fifteen years to his life after Hezekiah wept and prayed in 2 Kings 20?
qs.e: Prophet Isaiah was sent to tell Hezekiah that Yahweh heard his prayer and wept with him, promising to add fifteen years to his life and deliver Jerusalem.

qs.q: Which Roman officer in Capernaum displayed such remarkable faith in Jesus' authority to heal his paralyitc servant that Jesus praised him above all in Israel (Matthew 8:5-13)?
qs.e: The centurion said, 'Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed', drawing Jesus' highest praise.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Rich Fool (Luke 12:13-21), what sudden event rendered all his accumulated wealth useless?
o: God declared: 'Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee'
A severe drought ruined his crops
A sudden fire consumed his barns
qs.e: The rich man planned to build bigger barns and live in self-indulgent ease, but God called him a fool because his physical life ended that very night.

qs.q: What golden article did Judas Iscariot receive as payment from the chief priests for betraying Jesus (Matthew 26:14-16)?
qs.e: Judas covenanted with the chief priests to deliver Jesus to them for thirty pieces of silver, fulfilling the prophetic price of a slave.

qs.q: Who was the Roman governor of Judea before whom Paul defended his faith in Acts 24, who kept Paul in prison hoping for a bribe?
qs.e: Felix listened to Paul reason of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, trembled, yet left Paul bound for two years expecting a bribe.

qs.q: In Galatians 2:11-14, why did Paul publicly confront Peter (Cephas) at Antioch?
o: Peter withdrew and separated himself from eating with Gentile believers out of fear of the circumcised Jewish party
Peter was teaching that Jesus was not the Messiah
Peter refused to preach in Gentile cities
Peter demanded financial tithes from the Antioch church
qs.e: Paul withstood Peter to the face because Peter acted hypocritically by eating with Gentiles until Judaizers arrived, compromising gospel equality.

qs.q: In Genesis 3:16-19, what primary consequences were pronounced upon Adam and Eve following their disobedience?
o: Loss of speech and memory of God
Immediate physical annihilation and banishment from earth
Pain in childbearing for the woman and painful toil upon cursed ground producing thorns for the man
qs.e: The fall brought increased sorrow in conception/childbirth for the woman and cursed the ground so man would eat in sorrow and sweat until returning to dust.

qs.q: How did Jacob obtain his father Isaac's patriarchal blessing intended for Esau in Genesis 27?
o: By defeating Esau in a wrestling match
By purchasing the blessing with silver coins
By disguising himself in Esau's garments and goat skins under his mother Rebekah's guidance
By proving he was the elder twin
qs.e: Rebekah devised a plan to cover Jacob's hands and neck with kids' skins and wear Esau's clothing, deceiving aged blind Isaac into bestowing the firstborn blessing on Jacob.

qs.q: In Genesis 44, how did Joseph test his brothers' genuine repentance and love for Benjamin before revealing his identity?
o: He forced them to work in grain fields for seven years
He required them to bring Jacob to Egypt within 24 hours
He demanded that they build an altar in Egypt
He had his silver cup hidden in Benjamin's sack and threatened to enslave Benjamin, observing Judah's selfless plea to take Benjamin's place
qs.e: Joseph planted his cup in Benjamin's sack. When Judah offered himself as a slave in place of Benjamin to spare their father heartbreak, Joseph saw their true transformation.

qs.q: What sign did Gideon request from God using a fleece of wool on the threshing floor to confirm God would save Israel by his hand (Judges 6:36-40)?
o: The fleece turning from white to purple overnight
Water turning into wine in a bowl beside the fleece
The fleece catching fire without being consumed
First dew on the fleece only with dry ground around, then dry fleece with dew on the surrounding ground
qs.e: Gideon asked for a double fleece test: first dew on wool only with dry soil, then dry wool with wet soil around, proving God's call beyond doubt.

qs.q: In 1 Samuel 26, how did David prove his mercy and loyalty to King Saul when he entered Saul's camp at night at the hill of Hachilah?
o: He took Saul's spear and water jug from beside his head instead of killing him
He left a written letter on Saul's tent door
He captured Abner the army commander
He destroyed Saul's weapons of war
qs.e: David and Abishai entered Saul's camp while all slept. Abishai urged killing Saul, but David refused to strike the Lord's anointed, taking only the spear and water jar.

qs.q: What severe punishment befell Gehazi, Elisha's servant, in 2 Kings 5:20-27 after he secretly ran after Naaman to demand silver and garments?
o: Naaman's leprosy clung to Gehazi and his descendants forever
He was imprisoned by King Joram
He was banished from Israel to Syria
qs.e: Gehazi greedily lied to Naaman for two talents of silver and two changes of clothes. Elisha discerned his deceit and declared Naaman's leprosy would cleave to Gehazi as snow.

qs.q: In Ezekiel 33:1-9, how is the role of a true prophet described using the imagery of a watchman on a city wall?
o: The watchman must lead the soldiers into battle personally
The watchman collects taxes from citizens entering the gate
If the watchman sees the sword coming and blows the trumpet to warn people, he is clear of blood; if he stays silent, the blood is required at his hand
The watchman must build physical fortifications for defense
qs.e: God appointed Ezekiel as a spiritual watchman: faithful warning absolves the prophet of moral responsibility, but failing to warn the wicked makes the watchman accountable for their death.

qs.q: When Jesus was tempted by Satan in the wilderness for forty days (Matthew 4:1-11), how did Jesus overcome every temptation?
o: By calling down angels from heaven to fight Satan
By quoting written Scripture ('It is written...') from Deuteronomy
By arguing using Greek philosophical logic
qs.e: Jesus refuted all three satanic temptations (stones to bread, temple pinnacle jump, world kingdoms) by wielding the sword of the Spirit, declaring 'It is written'.

qs.q: In Matthew 5:43-48 (Sermon on the Mount), what revolutionary ethical standard did Jesus command regarding one's enemies?
o: 'An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth'
'Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you'
'Avoid all contact with people who persecute you'
qs.e: Jesus elevated love above Old Testament retaliation, commanding love and prayer for enemies so believers may be true children of their heavenly Father.

qs.q: In Mark 4:35-41, when a violent storm threatened to swamp their boat on the Sea of Galilee, how did Jesus demonstrate His divine authority?
o: He cast anchor until the storm passed overnight
He stood up, rebuked the wind, and said to the sea 'Peace, be still!', producing a great calm
He instructed the disciples to row faster to shore
He walked away from the boat onto the dry land
qs.e: Jesus commanded the wind and waves: 'Peace, be still!' The wind ceased and there was a great calm, leading the amazed disciples to ask, 'What manner of man is this?'

qs.q: On Paul's first missionary journey (Acts 13:4-12), what occurred when Elymas (Bar-jesus) the sorcerer attempted to turn proconsul Sergius Paulus away from the faith at Paphos?
o: Elymas drove Paul and Barnabas out of the city
Elymas converted immediately and was baptized
Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, pronounced divine judgment of temporary blindness upon Elymas, causing Sergius Paulus to believe
Sergius Paulus had Elymas executed for sorcery
qs.e: Paul rebuked Elymas as a child of the devil and declared a mist and darkness would fall on him. Seeing Elymas struck blind, proconsul Sergius Paulus believed the doctrine of the Lord.

qs.q: In James 3:1-12, the author emphasizes the immense difficulty of controlling human speech by comparing the tongue to
o: A sharp sword used in battle
A small horse's bit, a small ship's rudder, and a small fire setting a forest ablaze
A heavy stone resting at the bottom of a river
A roaring lion seeking prey in the field
qs.e: James uses vivid metaphors (bits turning horses, rudders steering big ships, small sparks kindling great fires) to show how an untamed tongue exerts destructive power.

qs.q: At the dedication of the Jerusalem Temple in 1 Kings 8:22-53, King Solomon's solemn prayer emphasized that when Israel sinned and experienced exile or trial, God would hear them when they
o: Offered thousands of additional bulls in foreign lands
Appointed new kings from foreign nations
Turned back, confessed His name, and prayed toward Yahweh's holy Temple in true repentance
qs.e: Solomon prayed that whenever Israel suffered defeat or exile due to sin, if they repented and prayed toward the Temple, God would forgive and restore them.

qs.q: Nehemiah's secret night inspection of Jerusalem's ruined walls in Nehemiah 2:11-16 before informing the Jewish leaders demonstrated his
o: Lack of trust in Yahweh's protection
Wise strategic planning, quiet evaluation of facts, and prudent leadership before mobilizing the community
Desire to keep the building project entirely private
Fear of being captured by Persian guards
qs.e: Nehemiah quietly inspected the broken walls and burned gates at night with a few men, assessing the true scale of work needed before presenting an inspiring action plan to the leaders.

qs.q: In Ecclesiastes 12:1-7, the Teacher uses poetic imagery describing failing bodily sight, trembling hands, and silver cord loosed to urge people to
o: Avoid all physical work throughout life
Study international laws in foreign lands
Remember their Creator in the days of their youth before old age and physical decline arrive
qs.e: Ecclesiastes 12 metaphorically portrays human aging and death, exhorting young people to dedicate their vigor to God before old age dims their capacity.

qs.q: In Isaiah 7:14, the prophet gave King Ahaz a divine sign during Syria-Ephraim's military threat, announcing that
o: A virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel ('God with us')
Assyria would be destroyed in three days
The Temple would be rebuilt with pure gold
Ahaz would conquer Egypt and Syria combined
qs.e: Isaiah 7:14 delivered the messianic sign of Immanuel, assuring Ahaz of divine presence and deliverance, fulfilled ultimate in Christ (Matthew 1:22-23).

qs.q: In Amos 7:7-9, what did the vision of the Lord standing beside a wall with a plumb line in His hand signify for Israel?
o: That border walls around Samaria needed repair
That the priesthood was performing construction correctly
That Israel was about to build a magnificent new palace
That God was measuring Israel's moral conduct against His righteous standard, finding them crooked and ripe for judgment
qs.e: A plumb line tests vertical accuracy. God showed Amos that Israel had departed from moral truth; He would no longer pass by their idolatrous high places without judgment.

qs.q: In Matthew 7:12 (Sermon on the Mount), Jesus summarized the moral substance of 'the Law and the Prophets' in the Golden Rule, which commands:
o: 'Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them'
'Do unto others as they have done unto you'
'Avoid helping those who do not share your faith'
'Seek first your own legal vindication in court'
qs.e: Jesus distilled biblical ethics into proactive love: treating others with the same care, fairness, and generosity you desire for yourself.

qs.q: In Luke 15:1-10, what common theme connects the Parables of the Lost Sheep and the Lost Coin?
o: The necessity of securing private property against thieves
The danger of shepherd negligence in desert regions
The economic value of agricultural animals and ancient currency
The joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, highlighting God's relentless search for the lost
qs.e: Jesus answered Pharisaic criticism for eating with sinners by showing that God actively seeks lost souls, and all heaven rejoices when one lost sinner repents.

qs.q: When Jesus was tried before High Priest Caiaphas and the Sanhedrin (Matthew 26:62-66), what specific declaration by Jesus caused the High Priest to tear his clothes and accuse Him of blasphemy?
o: Jesus said He would pay taxes to Caesar
Jesus claimed He was born in Bethlehem of Judea
Jesus affirmed He was the Christ, the Son of God, and prophesied they would see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power
Jesus refused to answer any questions
qs.e: When adjured by the living God, Jesus affirmed His messianic deity and Danielic enthronement (Daniel 7:13), prompting Caiaphas to cry 'Blasphemy!' and condemn Him to death.

qs.q: When Stephen was being stoned to death outside Jerusalem in Acts 7:59-60, his final words reflected the Spirit of Jesus by praying:
o: 'Lord Jesus, receive my spirit' and 'Lord, lay not this sin to their charge'
'Lord, rebuild thy Holy Temple in three days'
'Lord, consume these persecutors with fire from heaven'
'Lord, strike the High Priest with silence'
qs.e: Stephen died crying for his spirit's reception into glory and praying forgiveness for his executioners ('Lord, lay not this sin to their charge'), echoing Jesus on the cross.

qs.q: In Ephesians 2:8-10, Paul clarifies the precise relationship between faith, grace, and good works in salvation, stating that believers are saved
o: By strict observance of Sabbath laws and circumcision
By good works first, which earn divine grace
By grace through faith as a free gift of God, created in Christ Jesus unto good works which God prepared beforehand
By personal human wisdom and philosophical discipline
qs.e: Ephesians 2:8-9 states salvation is not of works lest any man boast; verse 10 adds that good works are the intended result/fruit of a newly created life in Christ.

qs.q: In Romans 12:1-2, Paul appeals to believers to present their bodies as a living sacrifice to God, which requires that they
o: Withdraw completely from living in secular society
Offer daily animal burnt sacrifices at an altar
Be not conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of their mind to prove God's good and perfect will
Perform physical asceticism in desert places
qs.e: True spiritual worship ('logical service') involves offering one's entire life to God, resisting worldly conformity, and experiencing mind transformation through the Holy Spirit.

qs.q: In Ephesians 5:21-33, Paul compares the covenant marriage relationship between husband and wife to
o: The political alliance between two sovereign nations
The spiritual mystery of Christ's loving, self-sacrificial relationship with His Church
The master and slave relationship in ancient Rome
qs.e: Paul presents Christ's sacrificial love for the Church as the pattern for husbands loving wives, and the Church's joyful respect for Christ as the model for wives.

qs.q: In Acts 4:18-20, when the Sanhedrin strictly commanded Peter and John not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus, the apostles courageously answered:
o: 'Whether it be right in the sight of God to hearken unto you more than unto God, judge ye. For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard'
'We will obey your command if you pay us compensation'
'We shall move our headquarters to Samaria immediately'
'We appeal directly to Caesar in Rome'
qs.e: Peter and John asserted divine authority over human prohibition, declaring their non-negotiable obligation to witness to the reality of Christ's resurrection.

qs.q: How did Philip's evangelistic preaching in Samaria (Acts 8:4-8) impact the spiritual atmosphere of that city?
o: The citizens refused to listen and drove him away
Unclean spirits were cast out, many paralyzed and lame were healed, and there was great joy in that city
It caused civil riots and military intervention
It led to a debate with Pharisaic scribes
qs.e: Acts 8 records that Samaritans with one accord gave heed to Philip's preaching of Christ, accompanied by miracles of healing and liberation, resulting in widespread joy.

qs.q: In Proverbs 22:6, parents are given a timeless principle regarding child-rearing, which instructs them to
o: Provide abundant material wealth to secure their future
Allow children complete freedom to choose their own moral path without guidance
'Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it'
Send children to foreign countries for secular education
qs.e: Proverbs 22:6 emphasizes foundational moral and spiritual nurture during formative years, establishing character habits that endure throughout adulthood.

qs.q: The story of the death of King Ahab's sons and the extermination of Jezebel's Baal worship by Jehu in 2 Kings 9-10 fulfilled the prophetic curse pronounced earlier by
o: Elijah upon the house of Ahab for the murder of Naboth and widespread idolatry
qs.e: Elijah had prophesied in 1 Kings 21 that judgment would eradicate Ahab's lineage and dogs would eat Jezebel, fulfilled when Jehu executed divine vengeance.

qs.q: In Jeremiah 29:10-14, the prophet wrote a letter to the exiles in Babylon advising them to build houses, plant gardens, and seek the peace of the city because exile would last
o: Five hundred years until the Messiah arrived
Indefinitely without any hope of return
Seventy years, after which God would visit them and fulfill His good word to return them to Jerusalem
qs.e: Jeremiah countered false prophets who promised quick return, revealing God's plan for a 70-year exile ('I know the thoughts that I think toward you... thoughts of peace').

qs.q: When Paul defended himself before King Herod Agrippa II and Festus in Acts 26:19-23, he summarized his entire apostolic commission by declaring that he was
o: Teaching that the Law of Moses should be enforced across Rome
Collecting money for his personal retirement
'Not disobedient unto the heavenly vision', preaching repentance and turning to God across Judea and Gentile lands
Seeking political appointment in Roman government
qs.e: Paul explained to Agrippa that his resurrection vision of Jesus compelled him to preach repentance and good works across Damascus, Jerusalem, Judea, and Gentile nations.

qs.q: In 2 Corinthians 9:6-7, Paul outlines biblical principles of Christian financial stewardship, teaching that God loves a giver who gives
o: To gain earthly political leverage over others
Cheerfully, bountifully, and purposefully as he has decided in his heart
Only when public recognition is guaranteed
Grudgingly or out of legal necessity to satisfy church rules
qs.e: Paul contrasts sowing sparingly/bountifully: 'Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.'

qs.q: The miracle of the resurrection of Jesus Christ on the first day of the week (Matthew 28 / Luke 24) validated Jesus' identity by proving that
o: Jesus was merely an earthly king seeking temporal rule
Roman soldiers had failed to guard the tomb properly
The Jewish Sanhedrin had made a legal mistake
God overturned human condemnation, defeating sin and death, and confirming Jesus as the Son of God with power
qs.e: Romans 1:4 states Jesus was declared to be the Son of God with power by the resurrection from the dead. Death could not hold Him, proving His sinless sacrifice was accepted.

qs.q: In Galatians 5:16-18, Paul describes the inner conflict within a believer between the 'flesh' and the 'Spirit', teaching that victory is achieved when believers
o: Isolate themselves from all contact with unbelievers
Walk in the Spirit, thereby not fulfilling the lust of the flesh
Rely on human willpower and legalistic rituals
qs.e: Paul explains that the flesh lusts against the Spirit and the Spirit against the flesh. Yielding to the Holy Spirit's guidance liberates believers from bondage to fleshly desires.

qs.q: In 1 Kings 18:21, Elijah confronted Israel on Mount Carmel with a searching question regarding their spiritual indecision, asking:
o: 'Why do ye refuse to pay tithes in Jerusalem?'
'How long halt ye between two opinions? if the LORD be God, follow him: but if Baal, then follow him'
'Why have ye built altars to foreign kings?'
'Where are the priests of Aaron's line?'
qs.e: Elijah challenged the syncretistic compromise of Israel, demanding an exclusive choice between the true God Yahweh and false Baal worship before calling down fire.

qs.q: In Luke 1:46-55, Mary's song of praise (the Magnificat) glorifies God primarily because He has
o: Exalted the rich and proud rulers of Jerusalem
Built a new earthly palace for David's family
Regarded the low estate of His handmaiden, scattered the proud, put down the mighty, and filled the hungry with good things
Granted military conquest to the Jewish nation
qs.e: The Magnificat celebrates divine grace reversing human pride: God exalts the humble, satisfies the needy, and fulfills His mercy promised to Abraham.

qs.q: In Acts 18:1-3 & 24-28, Priscilla and Aquila demonstrated exemplary Christian service by partnering with Paul in tentmaking and by
o: Building the first physical cathedral in Corinth
Taking eloquent Apollos aside at Ephesus and explaining to him the way of God more accurately
Leading a revolt against the Roman governor Gallio
qs.e: When Apollos preached fervently knowing only John's baptism, Priscilla and Aquila mentorship corrected his understanding with gentleness, equipping him as a powerful defender of Christ.

qs.q: According to 2 Timothy 3:16-17, all Scripture is given by inspiration of God (theopneustos) and is profitable for
o: Replacing personal prayer and Holy Spirit guidance
Gaining temporal fame among worldly philosophers
Doctrine, reproof, correction, and instruction in righteousness, that the man of God may be complete and equipped for every good work
Secular political governance and financial speculation
qs.e: Paul affirms divine inspiration and absolute sufficiency of Scripture to instruct, correct, train in holy living, and thoroughly equip believers for divine service.

qs.q: When King Asa of Judah faced a vast Ethiopian army of one million men in 2 Chronicles 14:9-15, his victorious prayer rested on the conviction that
o: Mercenaries from Egypt would arrive in time
Ethiopian soldiers would surrender without fighting
It is nothing with God to help, whether with many or with them that have no power, trusting in Yahweh's name
Judah's chariots were superior in speed
qs.e: Asa cried to Yahweh: 'LORD, it is nothing with thee to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power: help us, O LORD our God; for we rest on thee...' God struck the Ethiopians.

qs.q: In Romans 8:28-30, Paul outlines the 'golden chain' of redemption, revealing that God orchestrates all things for good for those who love Him because they are
o: Foreknown, predestined to be conformed to the image of His Son, called, justified, and glorified
Automatically elevated to civil leadership positions
qs.e: Romans 8:28-30 presents God's unbreakable redemptive purpose: from foreknowledge and predestination to calling, justification, and final glorification in Christ.

qs.q: In 1 Peter 2:9-10, Peter applies Old Testament covenant titles (Exodus 19:5-6) to the New Testament Church, describing believers as a 'chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation' whose primary mission is to
o: Show forth the praises of Him who called them out of darkness into His marvelous light
Govern civil political states across the empire
Enforce Mosaic laws on non-believing nations
Re-establish physical animal sacrifices in Jerusalem
qs.e: Peter highlights the glorious privilege and missional calling of the Church: redeemed by Christ's blood to witness to God's marvelous light and proclaim His virtues.

qs.q: In Ezekiel 47:1-12, the vision of the life-giving river flowing from under the threshold of the Temple toward the Dead Sea symbolizes
o: The expanding, healing, and life-transforming power of divine grace overflowing from God's presence to heal spiritual deadness in the world
The destruction of Jerusalem's water supply
A physical boundary line separating Israel from Moab
A commercial irrigation canal built by Zerubbabel
qs.e: Ezekiel's river deepens as it flows (ankle-deep to swimming depth), turning bitter Dead Sea waters fresh and bringing abundant life, fruitfulness, and healing wherever it goes.

qs.q: The Council of Jerusalem's decision in Acts 15 preserved the core truth of the gospel by declaring that salvation is
o: Reserved strictly for native descendants of Abraham
Dependent upon physical sacrifices at Jerusalem
Achieved through a combination of faith and ceremonial Mosaic observance
Entirely by God's grace through faith in Jesus Christ, removing Jewish ceremonial barriers for Gentile converts
qs.e: Acts 15 affirmed Peter's words ('We believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they'), safeguarding justification by faith alone.

qs.q: In Colossians 1:15-20, Paul presents a sublime Christological hymn, exalting Jesus as the image of the invisible God and Firstborn of all creation because
o: By Him all things were created in heaven and earth, He is before all things, in Him all things hold together, and through His cross He reconciled all things
He was a great moral philosopher superior to Plato
He was appointed earthly king over Israel by Solomon
He was the first angel created in heaven
qs.e: Paul refutes Gnostic heresy by asserting Christ's absolute divine preeminence in both creation and redemption: Creator, Sustainer, Head of the Church, and Reconciler through His blood.

qs.q: Who was the priest-king of Salem who brought out bread and wine to bless Abram in Genesis 14:18-20?
qs.e: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of the Most High God, blessed Abram, and Abram gave him a tenth (tithe) of all spoil.

qs.q: What special garment did Jacob give to Joseph that fueled his brothers' intense envy in Genesis 37:3?
o: A coat of many colors (ornate tunic)
qs.e: Israel loved Joseph more than all his children and made him a coat of many colors, making his brothers hate him.

qs.q: Which first judge of Israel delivered the nation from Cushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia in Judges 3:7-11?
qs.e: The Spirit of the Lord came upon Othniel, Caleb's younger brother, and he judged Israel and prevailed against Cushan-rishathaim.

qs.q: What gifts did the wise men (Magi) present to the infant Jesus in Bethlehem in Matthew 2:11?
o: Purple cloth, fine linen, and pearls
qs.e: Matthew 2:11 records that the Magi fell down and worshipped Him, opening their treasures and presenting gold, frankincense, and myrrh.

qs.q: Which woman had suffered twelve years from a flow of blood and was healed instantly when she touched the fringe of Jesus' garment in Mark 5?
o: The woman with the issue of blood
qs.e: She believed 'If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole'; touching His garment released divine power, and Jesus commended her faith.

qs.q: Who was the Roman ruler of Galilee before whom Pilate sent Jesus during His trial in Luke 23:6-12?
qs.e: Pilate sent Jesus to Herod Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee, who was in Jerusalem; Herod questioned Him and mocked Him in a gorgeous robe.

qs.q: Which island was Paul shipwrecked on while being transported as a prisoner to Rome in Acts 27-28?
qs.e: Acts 28:1 records that after escaping the sea, the passengers and crew discovered that the island was called Melita (Malta).

qs.q: In Genesis 1:26-27, human beings are distinguished from all other divine creations because they alone were created
o: In the image and likeness of God, with moral capacity and spiritual fellowship
Before the plants and animals were formed
qs.e: Genesis 1:27 states: 'So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.'

qs.q: How did Moses provide drinking water for Israel when they murmured at Rephidim (Massah and Meribah) in Exodus 17:1-7?
o: He purified salt water with a piece of wood
He struck the rock at Horeb with his rod as God commanded, and water gushed out
He prayed for rain clouds to cover the camp
He dug deep wells across the desert floor
qs.e: God instructed Moses to take his rod and smite the rock in Horeb in the sight of Israel's elders, providing life-saving water for the people.

qs.q: What riddle did Samson pose to the Philistines during his wedding feast at Timnah in Judges 14:14?
o: 'Which tree yields fruit in winter and leaves in summer?'
'Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness'
'What is sweeter than honey, and what is stronger than a lion?'
'What has eyes but cannot see, and feet but cannot walk?'
qs.e: Samson based his riddle on the lion he slew, in whose carcass bees had built a honeycomb: 'Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness.'

qs.q: How did the prophet Samuel react when King Saul spared Agag king of Amalek and the best livestock in 1 Samuel 15:32-33?
o: He advised Saul to pay a fine to the tabernacle
He offered a burnt offering on Saul's behalf
He declared Saul's kingdom revoked and personally executed Agag before Yahweh in Gilgal
He accepted Saul's apology and blessed the livestock
qs.e: Samuel told Agag 'As thy sword hath made women childless, so shall thy mother be childless among women', and Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the Lord.

qs.q: How did Elijah pray for rain on Mount Carmel after defeating the prophets of Baal in 1 Kings 18:41-45?
o: He offered seven bulls on the mountain peak
He struck the altar with his staff three times
He bowed down on the earth, put his face between his knees, and sent his servant seven times to look toward the sea until a small cloud appeared
He sang a psalm of thanksgiving with the people
qs.e: Elijah prayed intensely with persistent faith; on the seventh look, his servant reported a small cloud like a man's hand rising from the sea, bringing heavy rain.

qs.q: When Ezra read the Book of the Law of Moses publicly before the returned exiles at the Water Gate (Nehemiah 8:1-8), how did the Levites assist the people?
o: By reading clearly, giving the sense, and helping the people understand the meaning
By translating the scroll into Egyptian hieroglyphs
By enforcing mandatory monetary fines for non-attendance
By leading military drills around the walls
qs.e: Ezra standing on a wooden pulpit read the Law, while Levites caused the people to understand: 'So they read in the book in the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense...'

qs.q: According to Proverbs 15:1, how does a believer effectively diffuse interpersonal anger and conflict?
o: By shouting louder than the opponent
A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger
qs.e: Proverbs 15:1 highlights gentle, calm communication as a powerful instrument to defuse hostility, contrasting it with harsh words that escalate strife.

qs.q: What background occupation did the prophet Amos hold before God called him to prophesy to the northern kingdom of Israel (Amos 7:14-15)?
o: A herdsman of Tekoa and a dresser of sycamore fig trees
qs.e: Amos told Amaziah priest of Bethel that he was neither a professional prophet nor a prophet's son, but a humble shepherd and cultivator of sycomore figs when Yahweh took him.

qs.q: In Matthew 6:16-18 (Sermon on the Mount), Jesus instructed His followers that when they fast, they should
o: Refrain from working for seven full days
Disfigure their faces so everyone notices their religious devotion
Anoint their head and wash their face so that fasting is secret before God, who will reward them openly
Announce their fasting schedule in synagogues
qs.e: Jesus denounced hypocrites who seek human admiration during fasting, commanding genuine interior devotion directed solely toward the Father who sees in secret.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Ten Virgins (Matthew 25:1-13), what distinguished the five wise virgins from the five foolish virgins?
o: The wise virgins were related to the bridegroom
The wise virgins remained awake all night without sleeping
The wise virgins took extra oil in vessels with their lamps, while the foolish brought no extra oil
The wise virgins carried expensive golden lamps
qs.e: When the bridegroom was delayed, all slumbered; when the cry came at midnight, the wise had sufficient oil reserve for their lamps, whereas the foolish were unprepared.

qs.q: When Jesus raised Jairus' twelve-year-old daughter from the dead in Mark 5:35-43, what Aramaic phrase did He speak to her?
o: 'Talitha cumi' (meaning 'Little girl, I say unto thee, arise')
qs.e: Jesus took the child by the hand and said 'Talitha cumi'; immediately the girl arose and walked, filling her parents with great astonishment.

qs.q: In 1 Corinthians 6:19-20, Paul urges Christians to flee sexual immorality by reminding them that their physical body is
o: The temple of the Holy Spirit bought with a price, so they must glorify God in body and spirit
An insignificant vessel of no eternal consequence
qs.e: Paul teaches bodily holiness: believers' bodies are indwelt by the Holy Spirit and redeemed by Christ's blood, requiring honoring God in physical conduct.

qs.q: When God warned Adam in Genesis 2:16-17 'of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it', what consequence was announced for disobedience?
o: Reduction of human lifespan to fifty years
'In the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die'
Loss of dominion over wild animals
qs.e: Genesis 2:17 states the solemn divine prohibition: eating of the forbidden tree would result in spiritual separation from God and ultimate physical mortality ('thou shalt surely die').

qs.q: When Jacob slept at Bethel (Genesis 28:10-22) and saw the ladder with angels ascending and descending, what solemn vow did he make to God?
o: To build a stone city at Bethel within seven years
To return to Isaac immediately without going to Haran
To sacrifice all his flocks upon returning
If God would be with him, keep him, and give him bread and clothing, Yahweh would be his God and he would give a tenth (tithe) of all to God
qs.e: Jacob responded to God's covenant promise by setting up a pillar, pouring oil, naming it Bethel, and pledging a tenth of all his future income to God.

qs.q: In Genesis 41, Joseph interpreted Pharaoh's two dreams (seven fat/lean cows and seven full/withered ears of corn) as revealing
o: Seven years of military war followed by seven years of peace
Seven years of rain followed by seven years of floods
Seven years of great abundance across Egypt followed by seven years of severe famine
qs.e: Joseph explained that both dreams carried one message: God revealed seven years of great plenty throughout Egypt followed by seven years of devastating famine.

qs.q: In Exodus 15:1-21, after crossing the Red Sea safely while Pharaoh's chariot army drowned, Moses and Miriam led Israel in
o: A triumphant song of praise glorifying Yahweh as a man of war who triumphed gloriously
Appointing new military commanders for Sinai
Building an iron fortress on the shore
qs.e: Exodus 15 records the Song of the Sea: 'I will sing unto the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.'

qs.q: Following King David's sin of adultery with Bathsheba and murder of Uriah the Hittite (2 Samuel 11-12), David expressed deep heart repentance in Psalm 51 by praying:
o: 'Lord, rebuild my royal palace in Jerusalem'
'Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me'
'Lord, strike my political enemies with blindness'
'Lord, grant me victory over the Ammonites'
qs.e: Psalm 51 records David's heart-broken confession: seeking God's mercy according to His lovingkindness, pleading for inner cleansing and restoration of the joy of salvation.

qs.q: In Ezra 3:1-6, what was the very first action taken by Zerubbabel and Jeshua when the exiles returned to Jerusalem, even before laying the Temple foundations?
o: They rebuilt the altar of the God of Israel to offer daily burnt offerings as prescribed in the Law of Moses
They built royal palaces for civic leaders
They constructed high stone defense walls around the city
They collected gold tribute from surrounding nations
qs.e: Re-establishing true worship took priority: they rebuilt the altar on its original base to offer morning and evening sacrifices and keep the Feast of Tabernacles.

qs.q: In Job 19:25-27, despite immense bodily decay and friend opposition, Job proclaimed his triumphant faith by declaring:
o: 'I shall regain all my physical wealth tomorrow'
'I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth'
'My friends will soon apologize to me in public'
'God has abandoned me forever in the dust'
qs.e: Job expressed sublime resurrection hope: 'I know that my redeemer liveth... and though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God.'

qs.q: In Jeremiah 7:1-15 (The Temple Sermon), Jeremiah warned Judeans against false security in repeating 'The temple of the LORD', declaring that God would treat Jerusalem's Temple as He treated
o: Shiloh, which was destroyed because of Israel's persistent wickedness
qs.e: Jeremiah confronted superstitious reliance on the physical Temple building, reminding them how Yahweh destroyed Shiloh when His people sinned.

qs.q: In Malachi 4:5-6, the prophetic Old Testament canon closes with a promise that before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord, God would send
o: Elijah the prophet to turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers
King Solomon to rebuild the Temple
A military leader to overthrow foreign empires
qs.e: Malachi prophesied the return of Elijah (fulfilled in John the Baptist's ministry in Luke 1:17) to bring spiritual reconciliation and prepare hearts for the Lord.

qs.q: In Matthew 7:1-5 (Sermon on the Mount), Jesus warned against hypocritical judgment of others using the illustration of a person who tries to
o: Build a house on sand without foundation
Sow seed along a rocky path
Light a candle and put it under a bushel
Pull out a tiny speck (mote) from a brother's eye while ignoring a massive wooden beam (plank) in his own eye
qs.e: Jesus instructed disciples to examine and correct their own glaring flaws first before attempting to judge or correct the smaller faults of others.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Wheat and the Tares (Matthew 13:24-30), why did the master instruct servants NOT to pull up the tares immediately?
o: Because tares were valuable crops for livestock
Lest while gathering up the tares, they root up the wheat also; both must grow together until the harvest (end of age)
Because the harvest workers were on strike
Because tares turn into wheat over time
qs.e: Jesus explained that believers and non-believers coexist in the world until final judgment, when angelic reapers will separate tares for burning and gather wheat into the barn.

qs.q: On the road to Emmaus in Luke 24:13-35, how did the resurrected Jesus help the two sad disciples understand His suffering and resurrection?
o: He showed them His physical wounds immediately
Beginning at Moses and all the Prophets, He expounded unto them in all the Scriptures the things concerning Himself
He performed a dramatic nature miracle on the road
He introduced Himself as the High Priest of Jerusalem
qs.e: Jesus opened the Old Testament scriptures to them, showing how Christ had to suffer and enter His glory, causing their hearts to burn within them.

qs.q: In Acts 6:8-15, when Stephen stood trial before the Sanhedrin, what extraordinary appearance was noticed by all who sat in the council?
o: He wore high priestly linen garments
They saw his face as it had been the face of an angel
He was surrounded by Roman guards
A visible halo of fire hovered above his head
qs.e: Acts 6:15 records that all sitting in the Sanhedrin looking steadfastly on Stephen saw his face illuminated with divine glory, like the face of an angel.

qs.q: In James 1:27, 'pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father' is defined practically as
o: Attending daily synagogue services and reciting liturgies
Visiting the fatherless (orphans) and widows in their affliction, and keeping oneself unspotted from the world
Contributing money exclusively to church building funds
qs.e: James summarizes authentic Christian religion as active compassionate care for the vulnerable (orphans and widows) coupled with personal moral purity.

qs.q: In Acts 2:22-36, Peter's Pentecost sermon declared that David's prophecy in Psalm 16 ('Thou wilt not leave my soul in hell') referred NOT to David himself, BUT to
o: The restoration of exiles from Babylon
The bodily resurrection of Jesus Christ, whom God raised up, whereof all the apostles were witnesses
qs.e: Peter explained that David died and his tomb remained in Jerusalem, but as a prophet, David foresaw and spoke of the resurrection of Christ.

qs.q: In Genesis 12 and 20, Abraham twice passed off his wife Sarah as his sister out of fear, demonstrating that even great patriarchs of faith experienced moments of
o: Human weakness and fear-driven compromise, yet God remained faithful to protect His covenant promises
Desire to live permanently in Philistine cities
qs.e: Abraham's repeated lapse in trusting God's protection highlights human vulnerability to fear, set against God's sovereign intervention to safeguard Sarah and the covenant seed.

qs.q: In 1 Kings 11:1-13, the tragic cause of Solomon's spiritual downfall in his old age was that
o: He refused to consult prophets before battle
He exhausted royal funds building the Temple
He loved many foreign women who turned away his heart after other gods, causing Yahweh to rend the kingdom from his line
qs.e: Solomon violated divine commands against marrying idolatrous foreign wives (Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Sidonians), who led him to build high places for Chemosh and Molech.

qs.q: The core argument of Paul's Letter to the Galatians regarding legalism is that adding human works or circumcision to faith in Christ for justification results in
o: Greater spiritual perfection in the church
Perverting the gospel of Christ and placing oneself under a curse, for no man is justified by the law in God's sight
Fulfilling the highest requirements of grace
Promoting faster unity between Jewish and Gentile believers
qs.e: Galatians strongly warns that requiring Mosaic legal observances for salvation invalidates grace ('Christ is become of no effect unto you, whosoever of you are justified by the law').

qs.q: In Luke 22:39-46, during His agony in Gethsemane, Luke notes a unique physical phenomenon indicating Jesus' intense emotional and spiritual anguish:
o: He lost the ability to speak until trial
His sweat was as it were great drops of blood falling down to the ground
A sudden earthquake shook the olive trees
His hair turned snow white overnight
qs.e: Luke the physician records Jesus praying more earnestly in agony: 'and his sweat was as it were great drops of blood falling down to the ground.'

qs.q: In Acts 1:8, before His Ascension, Jesus outlined the geographic blueprint for the global expansion of the Church, promising His disciples power when the Holy Spirit came to be His witnesses in
o: Jerusalem, all Judea, Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth
qs.e: Acts 1:8 provides the structural thesis for the Book of Acts: empowered by the Holy Spirit, gospel witness spreads progressively from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth.

qs.q: In 1 Corinthians 10:1-13, Paul uses Israel's wilderness experiences (eating manna, drinking from the rock, falling into idolatry) as warning examples for Christians, concluding that
o: Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall, for God is faithful to provide a way of escape in temptation
Sacrifices should be restored in Corinth
Old Testament history has no application for modern believers
Believers cannot fall into moral temptation
qs.e: Paul warns against spiritual overconfidence: historical Israel enjoyed supernatural privileges yet fell through idolatry and grumbling; believers must remain watchful.

qs.q: In Jeremiah 32, while Jerusalem was under siege by Nebuchadnezzar's army, Jeremiah bought a field in Anathoth from his cousin Hanamel to symbolize prophetic assurance that
o: Houses, fields, and vineyards would again be possessed in the land after exile
Real estate prices would decline permanently
Jerusalem's army would defeat Babylon the next day
Jeremiah planned to retire from prophetic ministry
qs.e: Even as Babylon was conquering Judea, God commanded Jeremiah to buy property and preserve the deed in an earthen vessel, proving God's promise of future restoration.

qs.q: In Matthew 28:18-20 (The Great Commission), the risen Jesus commanded His disciples to go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in
o: The name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost
The name of John the Baptist
The name of the twelve patriarchs
The name of the High Priest of Jerusalem
qs.e: Jesus claimed all authority in heaven and earth, sending His followers to make disciples worldwide, baptizing in the singular name of the Triune God.

qs.q: In 2 Corinthians 12:7-10, Paul speaks of his 'thorn in the flesh', revealing that God permitted it to keep him from pride, and that God answered his prayer for removal by saying:
o: 'My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness'
'Thou must visit the pool of Siloam'
qs.e: Paul learned that divine power shines brightest through human weakness, leading him to glory in infirmities so Christ's power might rest upon him.

qs.q: In Romans 14:13-23, Paul addresses Christian liberty regarding neutral matters like non-essential foods or special days, establishing the guiding principle that
o: Believers should insist on their legal freedom regardless of others
Differences in opinion should lead to instant excommunication
Strong believers must walk in love, avoiding putting a stumbling block or occasion to fall in a weaker brother's way
All food laws must be strictly enforced by church elders
qs.e: Paul teaches that while all foods are clean in themselves, Christian liberty is constrained by love: never use personal freedom to cause a weaker believer to stumble spiritually.

qs.q: In 1 Kings 17:17-24, how did Elijah restore the life of the widow of Zarephath's son who had stopped breathing?
o: He took him to Mount Horeb for prayer
He anointed the child with holy oil from Shiloh
He carried him up to his upper room, stretched himself upon the child three times, and cried unto Yahweh until the soul of the child came into him again
He instructed the mother to bathe him in the river
qs.e: Elijah prayed passionately ('O LORD my God, let this child's soul come into him again') and stretched himself upon the boy three times, and God revived the child.

qs.q: In Romans 6:1-14, Paul responds to the objection 'Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?' by arguing that water baptism symbolizes that believers have
o: Formally joined a political organization in Rome
Purchased eternal immunity from civil laws
Died to sin with Christ, been buried with Him, and raised to walk in newness of life, so sin no longer has dominion over them
Obtained permission to indulge in moral weakness
qs.e: Paul explains that union with Christ in His death and resurrection breaks the reign of sin in a believer's life; being under grace empowers holy living, not moral laxity.

qs.q: In 1 Corinthians 15:50-57, Paul describes the ultimate triumph over death at the final resurrection, proclaiming that 'corruptible must put on incorruption' and shouting:
o: 'O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory?'
qs.e: Paul celebrates Christ's victory over death and sin: the sting of death is sin, and the strength of sin is the law, but God gives believers victory through Jesus Christ.

qs.q: In Hebrews 11:1-3, faith is defined as 'the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen', through which we understand that
o: The worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear
Human beings evolved from lower biological species
The physical universe was created out of pre-existing visible matter
Faith is merely positive mental wishful thinking
qs.e: Hebrews 11:3 teaches divine creation ex nihilo (out of nothing) by the spoken Word of God, establishing faith as the spiritual foundation for understanding ultimate reality.

qs.q: In 1 Peter 3:13-17, Peter instructs Christians facing unjust suffering for righteousness' sake to maintain a good conscience and be ready always to
o: Deny their faith publicly until persecution passes
Retaliate with legal threats against persecutors
Give an answer (apologia) to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear
qs.e: Peter outlines Christian apologetics under fire: sanctify Christ in your hearts and respectfully, gently articulate the biblical reason for your Christian hope.

qs.q: In Isaiah 11:1-9, the prophet describes the future Messianic King as a 'rod out of the stem of Jesse', characterized by the sevenfold Spirit of the Lord, whose righteous reign will result in
o: Universal peace and harmony in creation, where 'the wolf also shall dwell with the lamb' and the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord
The military destruction of all earthly cities
The building of a physical iron wall around Israel
qs.e: Isaiah 11 depicts the glorious reign of the Messiah: executed with divine wisdom, justice for the poor, and cosmic peace where former natural enemies dwell together in harmony.

qs.q: What request did Solomon make when God appeared to him in a dream at Gibeon?
o: An understanding heart to judge the people
qs.e: In 1 Kings 3:9, Solomon asked God for an understanding heart to judge Israel and discern between good and bad, which pleased the Lord.

qs.q: In Proverbs 3, what is stated as the essential result of trusting the Lord with all one's heart?
o: He shall give thee earthly riches
He shall grant thee victory in war
He shall make thee famous among nations
qs.e: Proverbs 3:5-6 teaches that trusting the Lord with all one's heart and acknowledging Him in all ways leads to Him directing one's paths.

qs.q: Where was Jesus baptized by John the Baptist at the beginning of His public ministry?
qs.e: According to Matthew 3:13 and Mark 1:9, Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan River to be baptized by John.

qs.q: According to the Beatitudes in the Sermon on the Mount, what blessing is promised to the peacemakers?
o: They shall be called the children of God
qs.e: Matthew 5:9 states, 'Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.'

qs.q: Among the ten lepers healed by Jesus, who was the only one who returned to give thanks?
qs.e: Luke 17:15-16 records that out of the ten lepers cleansed, only one returned to glorify God and give thanks, and he was a Samaritan.

qs.q: How many times did Peter deny Jesus before the cock crowed, as foretold by Jesus?
qs.e: In Matthew 26:34, Jesus told Peter that before the cock crowed, he would deny Him three times.

qs.q: What immediate physical event occurred to Saul of Tarsus during his encounter on the road to Damascus?
o: He became mute for three days
He fell blind for three days
He became paralyzed in his legs
qs.e: Acts 9:8-9 states that after seeing the light from heaven, Saul arose from the earth and was blind for three days, neither eating nor drinking.

qs.q: What spiritual consequence immediately followed Adam and Eve eating the forbidden fruit in Genesis 3?
o: Immediate physical death on that very hour
Alienation from God and awareness of their nakedness
Loss of speech and power over animals
Destruction of the Garden of Eden by fire
qs.e: After eating the fruit, Adam and Eve realized their nakedness, hid from God's presence, and suffered broken communion with God.

qs.q: Why was Cain's offering rejected by God while Abel's offering was accepted?
o: Cain offered blood sacrifice while Abel offered vegetables
Cain offered grudgingly without faith and proper heart attitude
Cain offered too little in quantity compared to Abel
God had already cursed the ground so crops could not be offered
qs.e: Genesis 4 and Hebrews 11:4 indicate that Abel offered by faith a more excellent sacrifice, whereas Cain's heart and attitude lacked faith and righteousness.

qs.q: What was the significance of Jacob's vision of the ladder reaching to heaven at Bethel?
o: It signified that Jacob would build the first Temple in Bethel
It assured Jacob of God's abiding presence and covenant protection
It warned Jacob that Esau was pursuing him to kill him
It commanded Jacob to return immediately to his father Isaac
qs.e: Genesis 28 records that God reaffirmed the Abrahamic covenant to Jacob, assuring him 'I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest.'

qs.q: How did Joseph interpret the dream of the chief cupbearer while in Egyptian prison?
o: He would be executed within three days
He would be restored to his office within three days
He would remain in prison for three years
He would become governor over Pharaoh's house
qs.e: Genesis 40:12-13 explains that the three branches meant three days, after which Pharaoh would restore the chief butler/cupbearer to his position.

qs.q: Why did Gideon test the Lord with the fleece of wool before going into battle?
o: To determine which weapons his army should carry
To confirm God's promise that He would save Israel through him
To choose which 300 men should fight against Midian
To ask God to strike the Midianites with blindness
qs.e: Judges 6:36-40 shows Gideon seeking assurance that God would indeed deliver Israel by his hand as promised.

qs.q: What principle did Samuel emphasize when rebuking King Saul for sparing Agag and the livestock?
o: Burnt offerings are superior to tithes
To obey is better than sacrifice
Kings are above the ceremonial law
Mercy to captives is pleasing to God
qs.e: 1 Samuel 15:22 states: 'Hath the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the LORD? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice.'

qs.q: Why did Rehoboam reject the advice of the elder statesmen after Solomon's death?
o: He wanted to lower taxes even further than proposed
He preferred the harsher approach urged by his young peers
The elders advised him to abandon the worship of Yahweh
The northern tribes had already declared war on Jerusalem
qs.e: 1 Kings 12:8-14 notes that Rehoboam rejected the elders' wise counsel to serve the people and accepted the aggressive advice of his young companions.

qs.q: What condition did Elisha give to Naaman the Syrian commander for his leprosy to be healed?
o: Offer a costly sacrifice at the altar in Samaria
Wash seven times in the Jordan River
Bathe in the Abana and Pharpar rivers of Damascus
