Fast for seven days in the temple of Rimmon
qs.e: 2 Kings 5:10 states Elisha sent a messenger saying, 'Go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clean.'

qs.q: What lesson does Jesus teach in the parable of the Good Samaritan regarding neighborliness?
o: Neighborly love is restricted to fellow countrymen and co-religionists
True neighborliness is demonstrated through practical mercy regardless of ethnic barriers
Religious rituals take priority over helping strangers in distress
Levites and priests are exempt from caring for injured travelers
qs.e: Luke 10:30-37 shows that the Samaritan proved to be a neighbor by showing active mercy to a stranger, transcending ethnic animosity.

qs.q: What primary spiritual lesson is taught in the parable of the Prodigal Son?
o: Older brothers are always more righteous than younger brothers
God eagerly welcomes repenting sinners with unconditional mercy
Inheritance should never be divided before a father dies
Sinners must perform years of penance before being accepted
qs.e: Luke 15 illustrates the compassionate response of the father who receives his repentant returning son with joy and forgiveness.

qs.q: What was the main sin of Ananias and Sapphira in the early Jerusalem church?
o: Refusing to sell their property for church welfare
Lying to the Holy Spirit by pretending to give the full price
Stealing money from the common apostolic treasury
Preaching false doctrine regarding the resurrection
qs.e: Acts 5:3-4 shows Peter rebuking Ananias for keeping back part of the price while keeping up the pretense of giving the entire sum, thus lying to the Holy Spirit.

qs.q: How did Paul and Silas respond to being beaten and imprisoned in Philippi?
o: They organized a prison revolt among fellow inmates
They prayed and sang praises to God at midnight
They demanded an immediate audience with Caesar
They cursed the magistrates who ordered their arrest
qs.e: Acts 16:25 states that at midnight Paul and Silas prayed and sang praises unto God, and the prisoners heard them.

qs.q: In the Genesis creation account, what is the significance of light being created on Day 1 before the sun, moon, and stars on Day 4?
o: It shows that physical light originates from human invention
It demonstrates that God Himself is the ultimate source of light independent of celestial bodies
It proves that the heavenly bodies were created before the universe
It indicates that Day 1 and Day 4 refer to the same event
qs.e: God created light by His divine word on Day 1 (Gen 1:3), establishing that light is grounded in God's sovereign command before celestial luminaries were appointed on Day 4.

qs.q: When Abraham interceded for Sodom in Genesis 18, what key attribute of God's character did his prayer highlight?
o: God's severe wrath against all cities
God's justice and willingness to spare judgment for the sake of the righteous
God's requirement of animal sacrifices before hearing prayers
God's preference for Abraham's family over all nations
qs.e: Abraham's question 'Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?' (Gen 18:25) appealed to divine justice and mercy for the righteous.

qs.q: Why did Jacob disguise himself to receive the blessing from his blind father Isaac?
o: Isaac had explicitly asked Jacob to pretend to be Esau
Rebekah instructed him to secure the covenant birthright blessing promised before his birth
Esau had transferred his physical appearance to Jacob through a vow
Laban forced Jacob to claim Esau's identity
qs.e: In Genesis 27, Rebekah devised the plan for Jacob to obtain Isaac's blessing, aligning with the divine word given during her pregnancy that 'the elder shall serve the younger.'

qs.q: When Moses encountered God at the burning bush, what was the primary purpose of revealing the divine name 'I AM THAT I AM'?
o: To show Moses that God had forgotten His covenant with Abraham
To reveal God's eternal, self-existent, and unchanging covenant nature
To explain the secret names of the Egyptian deities
To command Moses to build a tabernacle at Horeb immediately
qs.e: Exodus 3:14 reveals God's self-existence and eternal faithfulness to fulfill His covenant promises to deliver Israel.

qs.q: What administrative advice did Jethro give to Moses at Mount Sinai to prevent him from wearing himself out?
o: Delegate judicial matters to capable, God-fearing men of truth over groups of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens
Refuse to hear any civil cases from the people
Appoint Aaron as the sole supreme judge over Israel
Transfer all decision-making authority to the tribal elders
qs.e: Exodus 18:21-22 records Jethro's counsel to appoint able men to judge minor cases while Moses handled major issues.

qs.q: Why were the Israelites condemned to wander in the wilderness for forty years after sending spies into Canaan?
o: They refused to build an altar at Kadesh-barnea
They believed the pessimistic report of ten spies and rebelled in fear rather than trusting God
Moses lost the tablet containing the Ten Commandments
They attempted to make peace with the Canaanite kings without consulting Joshua
qs.e: Numbers 13-14 records that due to unbelief and rebellion after hearing the report of the ten spies, God sentenced that generation to 40 years of wandering.

qs.q: What moral downfall destroyed Samson's effectiveness as a judge in Israel?
o: He refused to fight against the Philistines
He compromised his Nazirite consecration by revealing his secret to Delilah
He stole consecrated gold from the tabernacle in Shiloh
He made a treaty of alliance with the king of Moab
qs.e: Judges 16 shows how Samson yielded to Delilah's entreaties, disclosing that his strength lay in his Nazirite vow symbolized by his hair.

qs.q: Why did David spare Saul's life when he found him defenseless in the cave at En-gedi?
o: Saul was guarded by a powerful company of soldiers
David respected Saul as the Lord's anointed and trusted God to execute justice in His time
Jonathan begged David on his knees to spare Saul
David was afraid of losing the support of the tribe of Judah
qs.e: 1 Samuel 24:6 records David saying, 'The LORD forbid that I should do this thing unto my master, the LORD'S anointed, to stretch forth mine hand against him.'

qs.q: Why did Jeroboam I erect golden calves at Dan and Bethel immediately after the kingdom divided?
o: To obey a direct prophetic instruction from Ahijah
To prevent his subjects from traveling to Jerusalem to worship and returning their allegiance to Rehoboam
To satisfy the demands of the Canaanite inhabitants in the north
To celebrate the military victory over Judah
qs.e: 1 1 Kings 12:26-28 shows Jeroboam instituted calf worship at Dan and Bethel out of political fear that temple worship in Jerusalem would reunite the kingdom.

qs.q: What theological truth was demonstrated when God raised the widow's son through Elijah at Zarephath?
o: Prophetic authority is limited to the physical boundaries of Israel
God's life-giving power extends beyond Israel to Gentiles who exercise faith
Widows were required to pay tithes before receiving miracles
Elijah possessed inherent divine power independent of Yahweh
qs.e: 1 Kings 17:17-24 shows God displaying His resurrection power through Elijah in Phoenician territory, affirming His sovereign care over Gentiles.

qs.q: What central reform was instituted by King Josiah after Hilkiah found the Book of the Law in the Temple?
o: Building new pagan shrines outside Jerusalem
A thorough purging of idolatry, renewal of the covenant, and national celebration of the Passover
A permanent exile of the Levitical priests to Babylon
A military campaign against the Assyrian empire
qs.e: 2 Kings 22-23 describes Josiah's sweeping spiritual reforms, destruction of pagan high places, and restoration of true worship based on the rediscovered Law.

qs.q: In Job 2, how did Job respond when his wife urged him to 'curse God, and die' during his intense suffering?
o: He rebuked her as speaking foolishly, maintaining that one must accept both good and trouble from God
He admitted that God was unjust in allowing his suffering
He cursed his birth and renounced his faith
qs.e: Job 2:10 records Job's response: 'Shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?' In all this Job did not sin with his lips.

qs.q: What transformation occurred during Isaiah's call vision in Isaiah 6 when he confessed he was a man of unclean lips?
o: He was struck dumb for forty days
A seraph touched his lips with a live coal from the altar, declaring his guilt taken away
He was given a golden crown by the elders
He was instructed to leave the temple and go into Babylon
qs.e: Isaiah 6:6-7 records that a seraph placed a live coal on Isaiah's mouth, purifying his sin so he could answer God's call to be a messenger.

qs.q: What spiritual truth is symbolized by Hosea's marriage to the unfaithful Gomer?
o: God's total abandonment of Israel due to her wickedness
God's relentless, redeeming covenant love for Israel despite her spiritual adultery
The superiority of priestly marriages over prophetic marriages
The necessity of divorcing unfaithful spouses immediately
qs.e: Hosea 1-3 uses Hosea's redemptive love for Gomer to illustrate Yahweh's unmerited, restoring love for idolatrous Israel.

qs.q: What was the significance of Peter's vision of the sheet containing unclean animals at Joppa?
o: It signaled a permanent change in the dietary laws for Jewish priests only
It revealed that God accepts believers from every nation and that no human should be called common or unclean
It instructed Peter to avoid all contact with Roman soldiers
It warned Peter of an impending famine in Judea
qs.e: Acts 10:15, 34-35 shows that Peter understood the vision as God removing the barrier between Jews and Gentiles, preparing him to preach to Cornelius.

qs.q: Why did Joseph test his brothers by planting his silver cup in Benjamin's sack during their second trip to Egypt?
o: To frame Benjamin so he could keep him as a slave while punishing the rest
To test whether his brothers had truly repented of their past envy and would protect Benjamin
To reclaim the silver money they had brought for purchasing grain
To prove to Pharaoh that his brothers were thieves
qs.e: Genesis 44 shows Joseph testing his brothers' character to see if they would abandon Benjamin as they had abandoned him years earlier.

qs.q: What theological warning is illustrated by Jephthah's vow before his victory over the Ammonites in Judges 11?
o: Vows made before battle are invalid under Mosaic law
Making rash, ill-advised vows to God can bring tragic and irreversible personal consequences
Victory in war depends solely on human strategy rather than divine aid
God demands human sacrifice as a condition for granting victory
qs.e: Jephthah's foolish vow resulted in grief regarding his only daughter, warning against uttering hasty, unconsidered vows before the Lord.

qs.q: How did Nehemiah counter the ridicule, plots, and rumors spread by Sanballat and Tobiah during the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls?
o: He paid tribute money to buy off Sanballat and Tobiah
He combined constant prayer to God with practical military vigilance, arming the builders day and night
He postponed the wall project until Ezra returned from Babylon
He asked the Persian king to execute Sanballat
qs.e: Nehemiah 4:8-9, 16-18 shows Nehemiah's strategy of prayer combined with active defense, keeping workers armed while building.

qs.q: What specific message did Jeremiah send in his letter to the Jewish exiles living in Babylon (Jeremiah 29)?
o: Stage an immediate armed rebellion against King Nebuchadnezzar
Settle down, build houses, marry, seek the peace of Babylon, and pray for it, for exile would last seventy years
Refuse to engage in any civil or commercial activity in Babylon
Return secretly to Judah within three months
qs.e: Jeremiah 29:4-10 instructed the exiles to seek the peace and welfare of Babylon where they were carried, trusting God's promise of restoration after 70 years.

qs.q: Why did the prophet Amos direct sharp condemnation against the religious assemblies and solemn feasts in Israel (Amos 5)?
o: The people were not offering enough high-value animal sacrifices
Their worship was outward ritual divorced from personal righteousness, moral purity, and social justice
They were holding worship services on the wrong calendar days
They refused to allow prophets to speak in the sanctuary
qs.e: Amos 5:21-24 highlights God's rejection of religious ceremonies when justice is neglected: 'Let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.'

qs.q: In the encounter with the disciples on the road to Emmaus (Luke 24), how did Jesus reveal Himself to them?
o: By performing a dramatic sign in the sky before disappearing
By explaining the prophecies concerning Himself in the Scriptures and breaking bread with them
By showing them His glorious transfigured appearance
By calling them by name in Hebrew
qs.e: Luke 24:27, 30-31 records that Jesus expounded the Scriptures concerning Himself, and their eyes were opened when He broke bread and blessed it.

qs.q: What was the immediate reaction of the servant girl Rhoda when she heard Peter knocking at the gate after his miraculous prison escape (Acts 12)?
o: She opened the gate immediately and hid Peter in the basement
In her joy she ran back inside without opening the gate to announce that Peter stood outside
She mistook Peter for a thief and called the Roman guards
She refused to answer the door because she thought Peter had been executed
qs.e: Acts 12:13-14 states that when Rhoda recognized Peter's voice, she opened not the gate for gladness, but ran in and told how Peter stood before the gate.

qs.q: In Stephen's defense before the Sanhedrin (Acts 7), what primary charge did he bring against his accusers and their ancestors?
o: They lacked sufficient education in the Greek language
They had always resisted the Holy Spirit and persecuted the prophets sent to them
They had failed to pay tithes for temple maintenance
They had abandoned the practice of animal sacrifices
qs.e: Acts 7:51-52 records Stephen telling the council: 'Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do ye.'

qs.q: How did Philip minister to the Ethiopian eunuch on the road from Jerusalem to Gaza (Acts 8)?
o: He debated him on Greek philosophy
He explained the passage in Isaiah 53 concerning the suffering servant, preached Jesus to him, and baptized him
He commanded him to give away his wealth to the poor in Jerusalem
He gave him a copy of the Torah in Ge'ez
qs.e: Acts 8:34-38 describes Philip starting from the Isaiah prophecy, preaching Christ to the eunuch, and baptizing him upon his confession of faith.

qs.q: In Paul's letter to the Romans (Romans 3), how does he describe the doctrine of justification?
o: Earned through meticulous observance of the ceremonial Mosaic rituals
Granted freely by God's grace through faith in the redemption that is in Christ Jesus
Reserved exclusively for descendants of Abraham according to the flesh
Achieved through human merit and good works combined with law keeping
qs.e: Romans 3:24-28 emphasizes that man is justified freely by grace through faith in Jesus Christ, apart from the deeds of the law.

qs.q: According to Paul in 1 Corinthians 12, what is the primary purpose of spiritual gifts given to believers in the church?
o: To establish spiritual rivalry and rank among believers
For the common good and mutual edification of the unified body of Christ
To enable individual believers to gain financial wealth
To eliminate the need for leadership and order in meetings
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 12:7 states that the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal (for the common good of the church).

qs.q: How did the rebellion of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram (Numbers 16) differ fundamentally from Miriam and Aaron's criticism of Moses in Numbers 12?
o: Miriam and Aaron sought to overthrow the priesthood, while Korah wanted political power over Canaan

Miriam and Aaron challenged Moses' unique prophetic status over his Cushite wife, whereas Korah's rebellion challenged the divine appointment of the levitical priesthood and Moses' leadership entirely
Korah was pardoned after offering incense, whereas Miriam was permanently exiled from camp
Miriam and Aaron were swallowed by the earth, whereas Korah was smitten with leprosy
qs.e: Miriam and Aaron questioned Moses' exclusive prophetic role (Num 12), resulting in Miriam's temporary leprosy. Korah's rebellion challenged the consecrated priestly order and authority (Num 16), leading to the earth swallowing them.

qs.q: Why was David's census of Israel in 2 Samuel 24 judged as a grave sin, and what theological truth was revealed by his choice of punishment?
o: The census violated architectural plans for the temple; David chose war to save money
The census manifested pride and reliance on military strength rather than God; David chose pestilence to throw himself upon God's direct mercy rather than human hands
David omitted levitical priests from the count; he chose three years of famine to test the priests
David counted women and children contrary to custom; he chose exile to appease Syria
qs.e: Counting the military reflected reliance on flesh rather than God. When offered three judgments, David chose pestilence, saying, 'Let us fall now into the hand of the LORD; for his mercies are great' (2 Sam 24:14).

qs.q: How does Ezekiel 18 refute the popular exilic proverb 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge'?
o: By declaring that generational curses automatically condemn children regardless of personal choices
By establishing the principle of individual moral responsibility, asserting that the soul that sins shall die and the righteous child shall live
By teaching that physical sacrifices made by parents can redeem their children's transgressions
By proving that ancestral guilt is transferred perpetually up to ten generations
qs.e: Ezekiel 18:2-4, 20 explicitly refutes fatalistic generational guilt, declaring that each individual is directly accountable to God for his or her own righteousness or wickedness.

qs.q: In Stephen's defense speech before the Sanhedrin (Acts 7), what main historical thesis did he develop to challenge Jewish temple centralism?
o: That the Temple in Jerusalem was built without divine permission or prophetic oversight
That God revealed Himself to patriarchs and leaders outside Jerusalem (in Mesopotamia, Egypt, and Midian), proving His presence is not confined to a building
That synagogue worship in Babylon had completely replaced the Mosaic sacrificial system
That Moses had commanded the destruction of all earthly shrines prior to the exile
qs.e: Stephen cited Abraham in Mesopotamia, Joseph in Egypt, and Moses in Midian/Sinai to show that the Most High dwelleth not in temples made with hands (Acts 7:48).

qs.q: How does Paul's argument in Galatians 3 regarding the 430-year interval between Abraham and the Law establish the priority of grace?
o: It proves that the Law canceled the Abrahamic covenant upon arrival at Mount Sinai
It demonstrates that the Mosaic Law, given 430 years later, cannot annul the prior covenant promise made to Abraham, which is received by faith
It shows that circumcision was instituted under Moses rather than Abraham
It argues that the Law was intended only for Gentile converts rather than Jewish believers
qs.e: Galatians 3:17 teaches that the covenant confirmed before by God in Christ cannot be disannulled by the Law which came 430 years later, proving promise and faith precede the Law.

qs.q: On which day of creation did God rest from all His work, blessing and sanctifying it?
qs.e: Genesis 2:2-3 states that God rested on the seventh day from all His work which He had made, and God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it.

qs.q: What was the final and decisive tenth plague visited upon Egypt before Pharaoh allowed Israel to leave?
o: Death of the firstborn of man and beast
qs.e: Exodus 11-12 describes the tenth plague: the striking down of all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, which compelled Pharaoh to release Israel.

qs.q: What weapon did David use to slay Goliath of Gath during the battle in the Valley of Elah?
o: A shepherd's sling and a smooth stone
qs.e: 1 Samuel 17:49-50 records that David used a sling and stone to strike Goliath in his forehead and bring him down.

qs.q: In which town was Jesus born during the reign of King Herod, according to the Gospel accounts?
qs.e: Matthew 2:1 and Luke 2:4-7 state that Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea, fulfilling prophetic scripture.

qs.q: In the Sermon on the Mount, what response does Jesus promise to those who ask, seek, and knock?
o: They shall receive, find, and have doors opened unto them
They shall be granted earthly kingdom power
They shall never experience earthly trials
They shall be praised by religious leaders
qs.e: Matthew 7:7-8 promises: 'Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.'

qs.q: How many loaves and fishes did Jesus use to miraculously feed the five thousand men?
qs.e: Matthew 14:17-20 records that Jesus took the five loaves and two fishes, blessed them, and fed the crowd of five thousand men besides women and children.

qs.q: What command does Paul give to children regarding their parents in Ephesians 6:1?
o: Obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right
Provide financial income for your parents from youth
Follow your parents only when they agree with culture
Instruct your parents in scriptural doctrine
qs.e: Ephesians 6:1 states: 'Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right.'

qs.q: According to Genesis 1:26-28, what unique privilege and responsibility was given to human beings at creation?
o: To build alter monuments across the earth
To be created in God's image and have dominion over all creation
To live without physical work or bodily responsibility
To govern over angels and heavenly hosts
qs.e: Genesis 1:26-28 states that God created man in His image and gave humans dominion over the fish, birds, livestock, and all the earth.

qs.q: How did Abraham demonstrate extraordinary hospitality to the three unexpected visitors under the oaks of Mamre (Genesis 18)?
o: He asked them for identification before speaking
He eagerly ran to meet them, bowed down, washed their feet, and served a rich meal
He directed them to the nearest inn in Hebron
He offered them silver coins and requested a blessing
qs.e: Genesis 18:1-8 records Abraham running to meet the visitors, bowing, washing their feet, and preparing a meal of fine flour and calf.

qs.q: Why did Pharaoh elevate Joseph to be second-in-command over all the land of Egypt?
o: Joseph defeated the Syrian army in single combat
Joseph interpreted Pharaoh's dreams of seven fat and seven lean cows and proposed a wise food conservation strategy
Joseph offered Pharaoh a large tribute of gold and silver
Pharaoh discovered Joseph was related to the Egyptian nobility
qs.e: Genesis 41 shows Pharaoh recognizing the Spirit of God in Joseph after he interpreted the seven years of plenty and famine and outlined a plan.

qs.q: What was the core theme of the Song of Moses and Miriam recorded in Exodus 15 after crossing the Red Sea?
o: Lamenting the loss of Egyptian food and shelter
Praising Yahweh as a mighty warrior who triumphed gloriously over Pharaoh's horses and riders
Requesting immediate entry into the land of Canaan
Establishing the rules for the levitical priesthood
qs.e: Exodus 15 praises God's glorious victory: 'The LORD is my strength and song... the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.'

qs.q: How was the Canaanite commander Sisera killed after his defeat by Deborah and Barak?
o: He was slain in battle by Barak's sword
Jael invited him into her tent and drove a tent peg through his temple while he slept
He drowned in the swollen waters of the River Kishon
He was captured and executed by the elders of Israel
qs.e: Judges 4:21 records Jael taking a tent peg and hammer, entering quietly while Sisera was fast asleep from exhaustion, and pinning him to the ground.

qs.q: How did King David express deep repentance when confronted by Nathan the prophet over his sin with Bathsheba?
o: He blamed Bathsheba for tempting him
He confessed 'I have sinned against the LORD' and poured out his sorrow in Psalm 51
He offered financial restitution to Uriah's family
He banished Nathan from the royal court
qs.e: 2 Samuel 12:13 records David's immediate confession 'I have sinned against the LORD', which formed the background for his penitential Psalm 51.

qs.q: How did God sustain the prophet Elijah during the severe drought at the brook Cherith?
o: Angels brought him fruit from heaven every morning
Ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning and evening, and he drank from the brook
The widow of Zarephath sent him grain daily
He survived solely on wild honey and locusts
qs.e: 1 Kings 17:4-6 states that God commanded ravens to feed Elijah with bread and meat morning and evening, and he drank of the brook.

qs.q: According to Proverbs 1:7, what is declared to be the foundational beginning of knowledge?
qs.e: Proverbs 1:7 states: 'The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.'

qs.q: In the Parable of the Lost Sheep, what action does the shepherd take upon discovering one sheep missing?
o: He abandons the missing sheep to protect the ninety-nine in the fold
He leaves the ninety-nine in the wilderness and goes after the lost sheep until he finds it
He sends a hired servant to search while he rests
He waits at home for the lost sheep to return on its own
qs.e: Luke 15:4 describes the shepherd leaving the ninety and nine in the wilderness to search diligently for the single lost sheep until found.

qs.q: What specific monetary sum was bargained between Judas Iscariot and the chief priests for delivering Jesus into their hands?
qs.e: Matthew 26:15 records that the chief priests covenanted with Judas Iscariot for thirty pieces of silver.

qs.q: What visible and audible manifestations accompanied the outpouring of the Holy Spirit on the Day of Pentecost (Acts 2)?
o: A sound as of a rushing mighty wind and divided tongues as of fire appearing on the disciples
A voice speaking from a cloud and a descending dove
A pillar of fire leading the believers out of the city
qs.e: Acts 2:2-3 describes a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind and cloven tongues like as of fire sitting upon each of them.

qs.q: What role did Ananias of Damascus play in the conversion story of Saul of Tarsus?
o: He debated Saul in the synagogue
He obeyed God's vision, laid hands on Saul to restore his sight, and baptized him
He reported Saul's presence to the Roman garrison
He accompanied Saul back to Jerusalem immediately
qs.e: Acts 9:10-18 shows Ananias following divine instructions to lay hands on Saul, whereupon scale-like crust fell from Saul's eyes and he was baptized.

qs.q: What divine name was revealed when God provided a ram in the thicket to replace Isaac on Mount Moriah?
qs.e: Genesis 22:14 states that Abraham called the name of that place Jehovah-jireh, meaning 'In the mount of the LORD it shall be provided.'

qs.q: What divine requirement was given to Israel regarding the Passover lamb in Exodus 12?
o: It must be a female sheep three years old with minor defects
It must be a male without blemish of the first year, roasted whole with unleavened bread and bitter herbs
It must be boiled in water for two days before eating
It must be sacrificed at Mount Horeb in secret
qs.e: Exodus 12:5-8 specifies that the lamb must be without blemish, a male of the first year, roasted with fire, and eaten with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.

qs.q: How did God instruct the Israelites to collect manna in the wilderness to teach them daily reliance and Sabbath obedience?
o: Collect a double portion every single day of the week
Gather a single day's portion daily, and a double portion on the sixth day for the Sabbath rest
Gather enough manna on Monday to last the entire week
Allow the Levitical priests to distribute manna equally
qs.e: Exodus 16:16-26 records God's command to gather daily according to need, and double on the sixth day because no manna fell on the Sabbath.

qs.q: How did Jonathan demonstrate unselfish covenant devotion toward David despite King Saul's hatred?
o: Jonathan gave up his claim to the throne, alerted David to Saul's plots, and stripped himself of his royal robe and armor for David
Jonathan led an armed rebellion against his father Saul
Jonathan persuaded Saul to crown David at Hebron immediately
Jonathan fled with David into the land of Philistia
qs.e: 1 Samuel 18:1-4 and 20 record Jonathan's soul being knit to David, giving him his robe and garments, and warning him of Saul's fatal intent.

qs.q: How did Solomon solve the dispute between two harlots claiming ownership of the same living child?
o: He cast lots to determine the rightful mother
He ordered the living child to be cut in two with a sword, exposing the true mother by her compassionate refusal
He awarded the child to the elder woman
He placed the child in the care of the high priest
qs.e: 1 Kings 3:24-27 shows Solomon proposing to divide the child, causing the real mother's heart to yearn for her son and yield him to save his life.

qs.q: What decisive religious reform was carried out by King Asa in the kingdom of Judah (1 Kings 15)?
o: He built altars to Baal in Jerusalem
He removed pagan idols, restored true worship, and deposed his grandmother Maacah for making an obscene image
He allied Judah with Israel to worship at Dan
qs.e: 1 Kings 15:11-13 states Asa did what was right, removing sodomites, destroying idols, and removing his grandmother Maacah from being queen mother for making an idol.

qs.q: What convincing sign proved Yahweh's supremacy over Baal during the contest on Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18)?
o: A sudden earthquake destroyed Baal's altar
Fire fell from heaven and consumed Elijah's sacrifice, wood, stones, dust, and licked up the water in the trench
The prophets of Baal were struck with immediate blindness
A dark rainstorm fell only on the altar of Baal
qs.e: 1 Kings 18:38 records: 'Then the fire of the LORD fell, and consumed the burnt sacrifice, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water.'

qs.q: What spiritual revival occurred when Ezra read the Law of Moses to the returned community in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 8)?
o: The people wept in repentance upon hearing the Law, were comforted, and celebrated the Feast of Tabernacles with great joy
The people revolted against Ezra and demanded Persian laws
The priests refused to translate the Hebrew text into Aramaic
The wall construction was permanently halted
qs.e: Nehemiah 8 records Ezra reading from morning till midday, the Levites giving the sense, and the people weeping, repenting, and keeping the Feast of Booths.

qs.q: When Jeremiah resisted his divine call by claiming 'I cannot speak: for I am a child', how did God reassure him?
o: God gave him physical strength and a military guard
God told him not to say 'I am a child', touched his mouth, put His words in him, and promised to be with him
God appointed Aaron as his official spokesperson
God exempted him from confronting kings and priests
qs.e: Jeremiah 1:7-9 records God reassuring Jeremiah that He would put His words in his mouth and deliver him from fear.

qs.q: Why did Jonah initially attempt to flee to Tarshish rather than go to Nineveh as commanded by God?
o: He was afraid Nineveh's soldiers would execute him instantly
He knew God was gracious and merciful and feared God would spare the hated Assyrian enemy if they repented
He lacked money for the overland journey to Assyria
He believed Nineveh was outside God's jurisdiction
qs.e: Jonah 4:2 reveals Jonah's motive: 'I knew that thou art a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repentest thee of the evil.'

qs.q: How did Jesus counter Satan's three temptations in the wilderness following His baptism?
o: By quoting appropriate passages from the Scriptures introduced with 'It is written'
By calling down legions of angels for defense
By debating Satan on rabbinic traditions
qs.e: Matthew 4:1-11 shows Jesus answering each satanic proposition by quoting Deuteronomy ('It is written...').

qs.q: What divine authority was displayed when Jesus calmed the raging storm on the Sea of Galilee?
o: Authority to foretell future weather patterns
Absolute authority over natural elements by commanding 'Peace, be still!'
Authority to build stronger fishing vessels
qs.e: Mark 4:39-41 records Jesus rebuking the wind and saying to the sea 'Peace, be still!', causing the disciples to marvel 'What manner of man is this, that even the wind and sea obey him?'

qs.q: Why did Jesus drive out the merchants and money changers from the Temple courts in Jerusalem?
o: They were not paying taxes to the Roman governor
They had turned His Father's house, meant to be a house of prayer for all nations, into a den of thieves
They were selling sacrificial animals at lower prices than priests allowed
They belonged to the sect of the Essenes
qs.e: Matthew 21:12-13 and Mark 11:17 state that Jesus rebuked them because 'My house shall be called of all nations the house of prayer? but ye have made it a den of thieves.'

qs.q: Why were seven men full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom chosen in Acts 6?
o: To write the four Gospel accounts
To supervise the daily distribution of food to Hellenistic widows and resolve church murmuring
To lead military defense against the Sanhedrin
To replace the twelve apostles in preaching
qs.e: Acts 6:1-6 shows the seven deacons appointed so the twelve apostles could devote themselves continually to prayer and the ministry of the word.

qs.q: In Galatians 3, how does Paul describe the historical function of the Mosaic Law prior to Christ?
o: As a permanent substitute for divine grace
As a schoolmaster or tutor (paidagogos) to guard humanity and point them to justification by faith in Christ
As an unnecessary burden invented by Jewish elders
As a system intended to grant eternal life directly
qs.e: Galatians 3:24 teaches: 'Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith.'

qs.q: When Joseph revealed his true identity to his brothers in Egypt (Genesis 45), what profound theological insight did he express regarding their past betrayal?
o: That his brothers must pay full financial compensation before forgiveness
That although they intended evil, God sent him ahead to preserve life and remnant on earth
That Pharaoh was responsible for his enslavement rather than his brothers
That God had rejected Israel to build a new nation in Egypt
qs.e: Genesis 45:5, 7-8 shows Joseph forgiving his brothers, explaining that God overruled their actions to bring about preservation of life.

qs.q: What divine judgment fell upon priest Eli and his family due to his failure to restrain his sons Hophni and Phinehas (1 Samuel 2-4)?
o: Eli was exiled to Assyria while his sons were pardoned
Both sons died in battle on the same day, the Ark of God was captured, and the priesthood departed from his line
Eli's sons were struck with leprosy inside the tabernacle
The tabernacle at Shiloh was destroyed by fire immediately
qs.e: 1 Samuel 2:34 and 4:11, 18 record the fulfillment of prophecy: Hophni and Phinehas died in battle, the Ark was taken, and Eli fell and died.

qs.q: How did King Ahab and Queen Jezebel acquire Naboth's vineyard, and what judgment was pronounced by Elijah (1 Kings 21)?
o: By purchasing it at fair price; Elijah praised Ahab's business skill
Jezebel arranged false witnesses to stone Naboth for blasphemy; Elijah prophesied dogs would lick Ahab's blood and destroy Jezebel
By seizing it as royal tax debt; Elijah commanded Ahab to build an altar
By defeating Naboth in civil court; Elijah remained silent
qs.e: 1 Kings 21 describes Jezebel's judicial murder of Naboth, whereupon Elijah confronted Ahab and announced divine retribution against his house and Jezebel.

qs.q: Why was Elisha's servant Gehazi struck with incurable leprosy in 2 Kings 5?
o: He refused to welcome Naaman to Samaria
He secretly pursued Naaman, lied in Elisha's name to take silver and garments, and hid them for personal gain
He broke a ceremonial vow in the temple
He failed to wash in the Jordan River
qs.e: 2 Kings 5:20-27 details Gehazi's deceitful greed in extracting gifts from Naaman, resulting in Naaman's leprosy cleaving unto Gehazi and his seed forever.

qs.q: What is the primary conclusion of the author of Ecclesiastes after examining all human pursuits under the sun?
o: Wealth and political power bring lasting spiritual fulfillment
All earthly labor without God is vanity and vexation of spirit; the duty of man is to fear God and keep His commandments
Human wisdom can fully solve all mysteries of existence
Pleasure and self-indulgence are the highest human goals
qs.e: Ecclesiastes 12:13 concludes: 'Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.'

qs.q: In Jeremiah's Temple Sermon (Jeremiah 7), what false security held by the people of Judah did the prophet fiercely denounce?
o: Their reliance on Egyptian military chariots
Their superstitious belief that the presence of the Temple guaranteed immunity from judgment while they committed theft, murder, and idolatry
Their practice of strict ascetic fasting
Their refusal to observe national civic holidays
qs.e: Jeremiah 7:4-11 rebuked the chant 'The temple of the LORD', warning that God would treat Jerusalem like Shiloh if social injustice and idolatry continued.

qs.q: How does Micah 6:8 summarize the essential requirements that God demands of His people?
o: Offering thousands of rams and rivers of oil in temple worship
To do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God
Building magnificent sanctuaries across all cities
Enforcing strict dietary restrictions on foreign neighbors
qs.e: Micah 6:8 declares: 'He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?'

qs.q: What core warning did Jesus convey in His teaching on judgment in Matthew 7 regarding the mote and the beam?
o: One should judge others immediately before examining oneself
Hypocrisy must be avoided by first correcting one's own major moral flaws before correcting minor faults in others
Religious leaders are exempt from self-examination
qs.e: Matthew 7:3-5 warns against hypocrisy: 'First cast out the beam out of thine own eye; and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brother's eye.'

qs.q: In the Parable of the Talents (Matthew 25), why was the one-talent servant condemned by his master?
o: He invested the money in a failed commercial enterprise
Out of fear, sloth, and a distorted view of his master, he buried his talent and produced no return
He gave the money to foreign enemies
He demanded a higher wage before working
qs.e: Matthew 25:24-30 shows the master condemning the servant as wicked and slothful for hiding his talent in the earth instead of trading or depositing it.

qs.q: What key decree was issued by the Jerusalem Council in Acts 15 regarding Gentile Christians?
o: Gentile converts must be circumcised and observe the full law of Moses
Gentiles were exempted from legalistic ritual requirements, needed only to abstain from idols, sexual immorality, strangled meat, and blood
Gentiles were required to join Jewish synagogues before baptism
Gentile believers were forbidden from holding leadership roles
qs.e: Acts 15:19-29 records James' decision and apostolic letter affirming salvation by grace through faith without forcing circumcision on Gentiles.

qs.q: What theological argument does Paul present in Romans 13:1-7 regarding Christian obligation to civil government?
o: Governments are inherently demonic and should be actively resisted
Civil authorities are ordained by God to maintain order and punish evil, so Christians should submit and pay taxes for conscience' sake
Christians are subject only to church leaders and exempt from civil law
Government submission applies only when rulers are devout Christians
qs.e: Romans 13:1-7 teaches that powers that be are ordained of God as ministers for good, instructing believers to render dues, custom, fear, and honor.

qs.q: How does the structural framework of Genesis 1 creation (Days 1-3 forming domains, Days 4-6 populating domains) communicate theological truth?
o: It indicates that creation was an accidental result of chaotic evolutionary forces
It presents creation as an orderly, divine sanctuary building where God assigns realms (light, sea/sky, land) and places rulers within them before resting
It demonstrates that plant life exists independently without sun or soil
It proves that human beings were created before light and water existed
qs.e: Days 1-3 form environments (light/dark, sky/waters, land/vegetation) and Days 4-6 fill them (luminaries, birds/fish, animals/man), revealing divine order, purpose, and domain design.

qs.q: In Exodus 32-34, on what grounds did Moses successfully intercede for Israel after the Golden Calf idolatry, and what did God reveal about His character in response?
o: Moses offered his own righteous deeds; God revealed that sacrifices supersede repentance
Moses appealed to God's covenant promises to Abraham and His reputation among the Egyptians; God revealed His name as merciful, gracious, long-suffering, yet strictly just
Moses argued that Israel was blameless; God revealed that Aaron was solely guilty
Moses promised Israel would never sin again; God revealed He would destroy all other nations
qs.e: Exodus 32:11-14 and 34:6-7 detail Moses' covenant intercession and God's self-revelation: 'The LORD, The LORD God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth...'

qs.q: What profound spiritual correction did God impart to Elijah at Mount Horeb in 1 Kings 19 following his triumph at Mount Carmel?
o: God taught Elijah that true prophetic victory is achieved only through military conquest
God showed Elijah that divine activity is manifested not merely in dramatic wind, earthquake, or fire, but in a still small voice and in preserving a faithful remnant
God commanded Elijah to retire immediately without appointing any successor
God revealed that Baal worship had completely wiped out all faithful worshipers in Israel
qs.e: 1 Kings 19:11-18 demonstrates God moving beyond sensational manifestations to the quiet, persistent word, assuring Elijah that 7,000 in Israel had not bowed to Baal.

qs.q: How does the Suffering Servant passage in Isaiah 53 synthesize messianic fulfillment and substitutionary atonement?
o: By portraying the Servant as an earthly monarch who conquers Rome through military force
By depicting the Servant as an innocent sin-bearer who was wounded for our transgressions, bruised for our iniquities, and made an offering for sin to justify many
By presenting the Servant as an angelic visitor who avoids physical death
By describing the Servant as a Levitical priest who sacrifices animals in the Jerusalem temple
qs.e: Isaiah 53:4-11 presents substitutionary atonement: 'he was wounded for our transgressions... the LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all... he shall bear their iniquities.'

qs.q: In 1 Corinthians 15, why does Paul assert that the physical resurrection of Christ is the non-negotiable cornerstone of the Gospel?
o: Because without Christ's bodily resurrection, preaching is empty, faith is futile, believers remain dead in sins, and Christian hope is destroyed
Because the resurrection proves that moral laws are no longer relevant for believers
Because only apostles who witnessed the resurrection are eligible for eternal life
Because resurrection guarantees earthly immunity from physical sickness and death
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 15:14-19 argues that if Christ be not risen, then is our preaching vain, and your faith is also vain; ye are yet in your sins.

qs.q: From what raw element did God form man in Genesis 2 before breathing the breath of life into his nostrils?
o: From the water of the deep
From the dust of the ground
From the clay of the riverbank
From the ashes of the altar
qs.e: Genesis 2:7 records: 'And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.'

qs.q: When God called Abram in Genesis 12:1, what command was given to him concerning his homeland?
o: Build an altar in Ur of the Chaldees
Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, unto a land that I will shew thee
Conquer the neighboring kingdoms of Canaan
Remain in Haran until his father Terah died
qs.e: Genesis 12:1 states: 'Now the LORD had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto a land that I will shew thee.'

qs.q: What miraculous transformation occurred when Moses cast his rod on the ground before Pharaoh in Exodus 7?
o: It turned into a flaming sword
qs.e: Exodus 7:10 records that Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh and his servants, and it became a serpent.

qs.q: Who was anointed as the very first human king over the united nation of Israel?
qs.e: 1 Samuel 10:1 records Samuel anointing Saul the son of Kish to be captain over the Lord's inheritance as Israel's first king.

qs.q: What ethical summary statement in Matthew 7:12 is commonly referred to as the Golden Rule?
o: Love thy neighbor and hate thine enemy
Whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them
An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth
Blessed are the meek for they shall inherit the earth
qs.e: Matthew 7:12 teaches: 'Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.'

qs.q: When the disciples saw Jesus walking on the Sea of Galilee during a storm, what was their initial fear?
o: They thought the boat was sinking
They thought they saw a spirit or ghost
They feared Roman soldiers were approaching
They thought a sea monster was attacking
qs.e: Matthew 14:26 records that when the disciples saw Jesus walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, 'It is a spirit; and they cried out for fear.'

qs.q: How many souls responded to Peter's sermon on the Day of Pentecost and were baptized into the early church?
qs.e: Acts 2:41 states: 'Then they that gladly received his word were baptized: and the same day there were added unto them about three thousand souls.'

qs.q: For how many silver pieces did Joseph's brothers sell him to the Ishmaelite caravan bound for Egypt?
qs.e: Genesis 37:28 records that Joseph's brothers sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver.

qs.q: Where did the prophetess Deborah hold court while judging the children of Israel in the book of Judges?
o: Under the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel
At the city gate of Hebron
qs.e: Judges 4:5 records that Deborah dwelt under the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in Mount Ephraim, where Israel came for judgment.

qs.q: Which Canaanite stronghold did King David capture and establish as the capital city of his kingdom?
qs.e: 2 Samuel 5:6-7 records David capturing the stronghold of Zion from the Jebusites and naming it the City of David (Jerusalem).

qs.q: What non-Levitical religious arrangement did Jeroboam institute in Israel to consolidate his political power?
o: He ordained priests from the lowest of the people who were not sons of Levi
He appointed Roman centurions as temple guards
He forced Levitical priests to move to Damascus
He abolished all sacrifices throughout the land
qs.e: 1 Kings 12:31 states Jeroboam made houses of high places and made priests of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi.

qs.q: How did Elisha cross the Jordan River when returning after Elijah was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind?
o: He swam across the river with his disciples
He struck the waters with Elijah's mantle, saying 'Where is the LORD God of Elijah?', and the waters divided
He walked across a stone bridge built by local inhabitants
An angel carried him across the river in a chariot
qs.e: 2 Kings 2:14 records Elisha taking the mantle of Elijah that fell from him, striking the waters, which parted hither and thither.

qs.q: What prophetic sign did Isaiah give to King Ahaz in Isaiah 7:14 regarding the virgin birth?
o: A star would shine over Jerusalem for forty days
Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel
A angel would slay the Assyrian army overnight
The sun would move backward ten degrees
qs.e: Isaiah 7:14 states: 'Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.'

qs.q: What was Amos's background and occupation before God called him to prophesy in Northern Israel?
o: A trained priest in the temple of Jerusalem
A herdman and a gatherer of sycomore fruit from Tekoa
A royal scribe in the court of King Uzziah
qs.e: Amos 7:14-15 states: 'I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet's son; but I was an herdman, and a gatherer of sycomore fruit: And the LORD took me as I followed the flock.'

qs.q: What spiritual truth is emphasized in the Parable of the Mustard Seed (Matthew 13)?
o: The kingdom of God begins small but expands dramatically into a vast worldwide presence
Mustard seeds are sacred plants required for temple offerings
Only small nations can enter the kingdom of God
Faith can grow only during times of agricultural harvest
qs.e: Matthew 13:31-32 illustrates the kingdom of heaven starting as the least of all seeds but growing into a tree where birds roost.

qs.q: What persistent cry did blind Bartimaeus shout as Jesus was leaving Jericho?
o: Master, give me silver and gold!
Jesus, thou Son of David, have mercy on me!
Prophet of Nazareth, tell me my future!
Rabbi, restore the kingdom to Israel!
qs.e: Mark 10:47 records Bartimaeus crying out loudly: 'Jesus, thou Son of David, have mercy on me!'

qs.q: Who provided the new rock-hewn tomb in which the body of Jesus was honorably buried after the crucifixion?
qs.e: Matthew 27:57-60 records that Joseph of Arimathea, a rich disciple, begged the body of Jesus and laid it in his own new tomb.

qs.q: What were the dying words of Stephen as he was being stoned by the Jewish council in Acts 7?
o: Curse these persecutors for their cruelty!
Lord, lay not this sin to their charge
May my death spark a bloody rebellion!
Save me from this violent execution!
qs.e: Acts 7:60 records Stephen kneeling down and crying with a loud voice, 'Lord, lay not this sin to their charge', before falling asleep.

qs.q: Which of the following attributes is explicitly listed by Paul as part of the fruit of the Spirit in Galatians 5?
o: Love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance
Wisdom, wealth, political power, knowledge, physical health
qs.e: Galatians 5:22-23 explicitly details the ninefold fruit of the Spirit: love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance.

qs.q: What physical covenant sign did God command Abraham to institute for all male descendants in Genesis 17?
o: Circumcision on the eighth day after birth
Offering a yearly lamb sacrifice at Bethel
Fasting on the tenth day of the seventh month
qs.e: Genesis 17:10-12 records God commanding circumcision for every male child at eight days old as a sign of the everlasting covenant.

qs.q: Why did Aaron manufacture the Golden Calf for the Israelites at the foot of Mount Sinai (Exodus 32)?
o: Pharaoh commanded him to build an Egyptian god
The people panicked over Moses' long delay on the mountain and demanded gods to go before them
The Levites wanted a physical symbol for tabernacle worship
God tested Aaron by commanding him to melt gold
qs.e: Exodus 32:1 shows the people gathering unto Aaron saying, 'Up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses... we wot not what is become of him.'

qs.q: How did Samson bring about the destruction of the Philistine rulers gathered at the temple of Dagon in Gaza?
o: He set fire to the temple roof with burning torches
He prayed to God for renewed strength and pushed apart the two main supporting pillars
He led an army of Israelites into the temple precinct
He poisoned the wine at their national feast
qs.e: Judges 16:28-30 records Samson praying for strength one last time, taking hold of the two middle pillars, and bowing himself with all his might to pull down the temple.

qs.q: What symbolic act did the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite perform when meeting Jeroboam on the road (1 Kings 11)?
o: He poured oil over Jeroboam's head from a horn
He tore his new garment into twelve pieces and gave ten pieces to Jeroboam
He broke a potter's earthen vessel before the elders
He laid a heavy iron yoke upon Jeroboam's shoulders
qs.e: 1 Kings 11:30-31 details Ahijah catching his new garment, rending it in twelve pieces, and telling Jeroboam to take ten pieces representing ten tribes.

qs.q: What historic royal decree issued by King Cyrus of Persia fulfilled Jeremiah's prophecy regarding the exiles (Ezra 1)?
o: A decree ordering all exiles to convert to Persian religion
A royal proclamation permitting Jewish exiles to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the house of the LORD
A mandate appointing Nehemiah as king over Judah
An order to destroy all remaining Samaritan altars
qs.e: Ezra 1:1-3 records Cyrus issuing a written proclamation throughout his realm allowing God's people to go up to Jerusalem and build the house of the LORD.

qs.q: What practical lesson does Proverbs 6:6-8 draw from observing the habits of the ant?
o: Building strong defense fortifications against predators
Diligent foresight and self-motivated labor in gathering food during harvest without needing a overseer
Living in large hierarchical communities under a king
Exercising silence during times of conflict
qs.e: Proverbs 6:6-8 tells the sluggard to consider the ant, 'Which having no guide, overseer, or ruler, Provideth her meat in the summer, and gathereth her food in the harvest.'

qs.q: Why did Jeremiah purchase a field in Anathoth from his cousin Hanamel while Jerusalem was besieged by Babylonians (Jeremiah 32)?
o: To profit from falling land values during wartime
As a prophetic assurance that houses, fields, and vineyards would again be possessed in the land after exile
To establish a sanctuary for levitical priests
To escape the city wall defenses
qs.e: Jeremiah 32:15 explains the divine sign: 'Houses and fields and vineyards shall be possessed again in this land.'

qs.q: Why did Joseph take Mary and the infant Jesus and flee into Egypt shortly after the visit of the Magi?
o: To fulfill a business contract in Alexandria
An angel warned Joseph in a dream that Herod was searching for the child to destroy Him
To escape a severe drought in Judea
To enroll Jesus in Egyptian rabbinic schools
qs.e: Matthew 2:13 records the angel telling Joseph: 'Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt... for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.'

qs.q: In the Sermon on the Mount, what metaphor does Jesus use in Matthew 5:14-16 to describe the public testimony of His disciples?
o: A hidden treasure in an abandoned field
Ye are the light of the world; a city set on a hill cannot be hidden
A grain of wheat buried deep in soil
A sharp sword held in a scabbard
qs.e: Matthew 5:14-16 compares disciples to a light of the world and a city on a hill, exhorting them to let their light shine before men.

qs.q: What contrast in spiritual attitude is highlighted in the Parable of the Pharisee and the Publican (Luke 18)?
o: The Pharisee prayed with humble contrite faith while the Publican boasted
The Pharisee boasted of his self-righteous works, whereas the contrite Publican prayed 'God be merciful to me a sinner' and was justified
Both men were rejected by God for praying in public
The Publican was condemned for refusing to pay temple tithes
qs.e: Luke 18:9-14 shows the Pharisee trusting in his own righteousness, while the humble tax collector pleaded for mercy and went down justified.

qs.q: When four men lowered a paralytic through the roof to reach Jesus, what was the first statement Jesus made to the paralytic?
o: Arise, take up thy bed and walk immediately!
Son, thy sins be forgiven thee
Why did your friends break open the roof?
Go show thyself to the chief priests
qs.e: Mark 2:5 records that when Jesus saw their faith, He said unto the sick of the palsy, 'Son, thy sins be forgiven thee', demonstrating authority to forgive sins.

qs.q: What was the symbolic meaning of the Temple veil tearing in two from top to bottom at the moment of Christ's death (Matthew 27:51)?
o: It signified that the physical temple structure was unsafe for worshipers
It symbolized that direct access into God's Holy of Holies was now open to all through Christ's sacrifice
It indicated that Roman soldiers had desecrated the inner sanctuary
It marked the beginning of a forty-year period of silent mourning
qs.e: The tearing of the veil (Hebrews 10:19-20) signified the removal of the barrier between God and humanity, opening direct access through Jesus' blood.

qs.q: What happened when Peter and John encountered the lame man at the Beautiful Gate of the Temple (Acts 3)?
o: They gave him ten silver coins from the common chest
Peter declared 'Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk', instantly healing him
They recommended him to the temple welfare office
They instructed him to fast for seven days
qs.e: Acts 3:6-8 records Peter healing the man in Jesus' name, whereupon he leaped up, stood, walked, and entered the temple praising God.

qs.q: How did Paul connect with the Athenian philosophers at the Areopagus (Acts 17) to present the Gospel?
o: He quoted Mosaic dietary laws to prove Jewish moral superiority
He pointed to their altar dedicated 'To the Unknown God' and proclaimed Him as the Creator who raised Jesus from the dead
He condemned Greek architecture and demanded all statues be smashed
He urged them to adopt Roman citizenship
qs.e: Acts 17:22-31 describes Paul starting from their inscription 'To the Unknown God' to preach the sovereign Creator, repentance, and resurrection.

qs.q: Which piece of spiritual armor in Ephesians 6 is identified specifically as the word of God?
qs.e: Ephesians 6:17 explicitly states: 'And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.'

qs.q: What transformative experience occurred to Jacob during his nocturnal struggle at Peniel near the brook Jabbok (Genesis 32)?
o: He was stripped of all his wealth by Esau's scouts
He wrestled with a divine messenger, refused to let go until blessed, and received the name 'Israel'
He saw a vision of twelve thrones in heaven
He was struck dumb until reconciling with Esau
qs.e: Genesis 32:28 records: 'Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed.'

qs.q: What typology is established in Numbers 21 when Moses lifted up the bronze serpent in the wilderness?
o: It prefigured the levitical altar of incense
It prefigured Christ being lifted up on the cross so that whoever believes in Him should have eternal life
It symbolized Israel's victory over the Philistines
It represented the bronze laver used for ceremonial cleansing
qs.e: John 3:14-15 directly applies Numbers 21:8-9: 'And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up.'

qs.q: Why did King Saul resort to consulting a medium at Endor (1 Samuel 28), and what was the outcome?
o: To ask for military reinforcements against Moab; the medium gave him silver
Because God answered him not by dreams, Urim, or prophets; Samuel's spirit appeared and foretold Saul's death and defeat the next day
To seek healing for an incurable disease; he was restored
To learn secret levitical rituals; Samuel blessed his reign
qs.e: 1 Samuel 28 shows Saul turning to necromancy out of spiritual desperation, receiving a message of impending doom and death on Mount Gilboa.

qs.q: How did Elisha assist a poor prophetic widow facing the loss of her two sons to a creditor in 2 Kings 4?
o: He gave her money from the royal treasury
He instructed her to borrow empty vessels, shut the door, and pour her single jar of oil until every vessel was miraculously filled
He commanded the creditor to forgive all debts under Jubilee law
He sent her sons to serve in the temple at Bethel
qs.e: 2 Kings 4:1-7 details Elisha multiplying the widow's oil so she could sell it, pay her debt, and live off the remainder with her sons.

qs.q: Upon receiving news that Jerusalem's walls were broken down and gates burned, what initial actions did Nehemiah take in Susa?
o: He immediately resigned his position as cupbearer and moved to Egypt
He sat down, wept, mourned, fasted, and prayed before the God of heaven confessing Israel's sins
He organized an armed militia from the Persian palace guard
He hired Greek mercenaries to rebuild the walls
qs.e: Nehemiah 1:4 records: 'I sat down and wept, and mourned certain days, and fasted, and prayed before the God of heaven.'

qs.q: How does Proverbs 31 summarize the character and praise of the virtuous woman?
o: Her worth is measured by her external physical beauty and social status
Her price is far above rubies; she works willingly, cares for the poor, speaks wisdom, and fears the LORD
She leaves all domestic labor to servants while attending political assemblies
She avoids commercial enterprise to focus exclusively on quiet contemplation
qs.e: Proverbs 31:10-31 praises the virtuous woman for her industry, charity, wisdom, and godliness: 'Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised.'

qs.q: In Malachi 3:8-10, what solemn charge does God bring against Israel regarding tithes and offerings?
o: They were offering foreign foreign currency in the temple
They were robbing God by withholding tithes and offerings, and were invited to test God by bringing full tithes to open the windows of heaven
They were giving too much money to levitical priests
They were sacrificing animals outside the temple gates
qs.e: Malachi 3:8-10 rebukes the nation for robbing God in tithes and offerings, promising overflowing blessings if they bring all the tithes into the storehouse.

qs.q: What specific instructions did Jesus give regarding prayer in Matthew 6 to guard against hypocrisy?
o: Pray loudly in synagogues so everyone can hear your piety
Enter thy closet, shut thy door, pray to thy Father in secret, and avoid vain repetitions like heathens
Recite long formal prayers written by rabbinic elders
Fast for forty days before making any personal petition
qs.e: Matthew 6:5-7 warns against praying publicly to be seen of men, instructing secret prayer to the Father who sees in secret.

qs.q: In the Parable of the Unforgiving Servant (Matthew 18), why did the king deliver the forgiven servant to the tormentors?
o: The servant failed to double his master's investment
After being forgiven an enormous debt of ten thousand talents, he refused to forgive his fellow servant a small debt of one hundred pence
The servant spoke disrespectfully to the royal council
The servant attempted to flee the country without paying taxes
qs.e: Matthew 18:23-35 shows the master's anger at the servant's heartless refusal to show mercy to a fellow debtor after receiving overwhelming mercy himself.

qs.q: How was communal unity and radical generosity expressed in the early Jerusalem church according to Acts 2 and 4?
o: Believers charged high interest rates on loans to fellow members
They were of one heart and soul, had all things in common, sold possessions, and distributed proceeds to each according to need
Each family kept its private wealth while demanding church subsidies
They tithed exclusively to Roman authorities
qs.e: Acts 2:44-45 and 4:32-35 describe believers sharing all things in common, selling lands and distribution made unto every man according as he had need.

qs.q: In 2 Corinthians 5:17-20, how does Paul define the spiritual status and mission of a believer in Christ?
o: A citizen bound to Mosaic dietary laws to achieve perfection
A new creation in whom old things have passed away, entrusted with the word and ministry of divine reconciliation as Christ's ambassador
A servant subject to worldly philosophies and elementary principles
An isolated ascetic residing far from secular society
qs.e: 2 Corinthians 5:17-20 declares that if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature, and God hath given to us the ministry of reconciliation as ambassadors for Christ.

qs.q: How does the tragedy of Jeroboam's reign (1 Kings 11-13) demonstrate the theological failure of substituting political expediency for divine trust?
o: Jeroboam trusted God fully but was overthrown by Egypt
Despite receiving a divine prophetic promise of an enduring house, Jeroboam established unauthorized calf sanctuaries out of political fear, making Israel to sin and ensuring his dynasty's total ruin
Jeroboam enforced strict levitical purity which angered northern secular tribes
Jeroboam surrendered all northern territory to Solomon's heirs
qs.e: Jeroboam received a promise from Ahijah (1 Kings 11:38) conditional on obedience, but chose political self-preservation through idolatry at Dan and Bethel, bringing judgment upon his house.

qs.q: In post-exilic Judah, how did Ezra's policy on mixed marriages (Ezra 9-10) address the spiritual survival of the returned remnant?
o: By encouraging intermarriage to build trade alliances with neighboring pagan nations
By viewing intermarriage with idolatrous neighbors as a breach of covenant holy seed that threatened total spiritual assimilation, demanding corporate repentance and dissolution of unlawful unions
By establishing tax surcharges on foreign spouses to fund temple sacrifices
By ignoring lineage requirements for levitical priesthood applicants
qs.e: Ezra 9:1-2 and 10:1-12 show Ezra weeping over the holy seed mingling with pagan peoples, recognizing that idolatrous practices threatened the spiritual identity and covenant existence of the restoration community.

qs.q: What radical theological shift does Jeremiah 31:31-34 announce concerning the nature and internal locus of the New Covenant?
o: A covenant requiring stricter external ceremonial rituals and larger animal sacrifices
A covenant written internally upon human minds and hearts rather than external stone tablets, promising universal intimate knowledge of God and permanent forgiveness of sins
A temporary agreement restricted exclusively to the tribe of Levi
A political treaty between Jerusalem and the Babylonian empire
qs.e: Jeremiah 31:31-34 promises: 'I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts... for I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more.'

qs.q: How did Peter's rebuke of Simon Magus in Acts 8 define the fundamental boundary between sorcery and Christian spiritual power?
o: By accepting Simon's money and appointing him an elder in Samaria
By fiercely condemning Simon's attempt to buy the gift of the Holy Spirit with money, proving divine grace cannot be commercialized or manipulated like occult sorcery
By teaching that spiritual gifts can be purchased if prices are approved by apostles
By instructing Simon to offer animal sacrifices in Jerusalem instead
qs.e: Acts 8:20-22 records Peter saying, 'Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money', confronting Simon's corrupt, commercial view of divine power.

qs.q: In Romans 5:12-21, how does Paul construct the theological parallel and contrast between the first Adam and Jesus Christ?
o: Adam and Christ are portrayed as equal moral examples who both failed under temptation

Through Adam's single trespass sin and death entered to reign over humanity, whereas through Christ's single righteous act grace, justification, and eternal life reign abundantly for all who receive Him
Adam brought spiritual life to Gentiles while Christ brought physical life to Jews
Christ came to enforce the condemnation introduced by Adam
qs.e: Romans 5:18-19 states: 'Therefore as by the offence of one judgment came upon all men to condemnation; even so by the righteousness of one the free gift came upon all men unto justification of life.'

qs.q: From which part of Adam's body did God fashion the first woman Eve in Genesis 2?
o: From a lock of his hair
qs.e: Genesis 2:21-22 states that God took one of Adam's ribs while he slept and made a woman to be his companion.

qs.q: On which mountain did Moses receive the two tables of stone containing the Ten Commandments?
qs.e: Exodus 19:20 and 31:18 record that the Lord came down upon Mount Sinai and gave Moses two tables of testimony.

qs.q: How was the prophet Elijah taken up into heaven at the end of his earthly ministry?
o: He died peacefully in his sleep at Gilgal
By a whirlwind in a chariot of fire with horses of fire
He vanished in a cloud on Mount Carmel
He was carried across the Jordan by angels
qs.e: 2 Kings 2:11 records that a chariot of fire and horses of fire appeared, and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.

qs.q: Which angel brought the annunciation message to the Virgin Mary in Nazareth regarding the birth of Jesus?
qs.e: Luke 1:26-27 states that the angel Gabriel was sent from God unto a city of Galilee named Nazareth to Mary.

qs.q: Which model prayer taught by Jesus in Matthew 6 begins with 'Our Father which art in heaven'?
qs.e: Matthew 6:9-13 presents the Lord's Prayer as a model for disciples: 'After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven...'

qs.q: In the Parable of the Lost Coin (Luke 15), what diligent effort does the woman make to find her lost drachma?
o: She hires neighbors to search outside her house
She lights a candle, sweeps the house, and searches diligently until she finds it
She offers a sacrifice at the temple for its return
She waits until daylight to inspect her garden
qs.e: Luke 15:8 describes the woman lighting a candle, sweeping the house, and searching diligently till she finds her lost silver piece.

qs.q: From which Syrian city were Paul and Barnabas set apart and sent out on their first missionary journey?
qs.e: Acts 13:1-3 describes the church at Antioch fasting, praying, and laying hands on Barnabas and Saul to send them forth.

qs.q: Who was Melchizedek, who brought bread and wine to Abram after the rescue of Lot (Genesis 14)?
o: King of Salem and priest of the Most High God
The high priest of the tabernacle at Shiloh
qs.e: Genesis 14:18 states that Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine: and he was the priest of the most high God.

qs.q: How did God supply water to the thirsty Israelites when they murmured at Rephidim (Exodus 17)?
o: He sent a heavy three-day rainstorm
He commanded Moses to strike the rock at Horeb with his rod, and water came out
He turned brackish oasis water into fresh milk
He instructed Joshua to dig deep wells in the desert
qs.e: Exodus 17:6 records God instructing Moses: 'Thou shalt smite the rock, and there shall come water out of it, that the people may drink.'

qs.q: What was Samson's famous riddle presented to the Philistines during his wedding feast at Timnah?
o: Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness
A soft answer turneth away wrath, but grievous words stir up anger
The tree is known by its fruit, and the well by its water
Iron sharpeneth iron, so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend
qs.e: Judges 14:14 records Samson's riddle based on the lion carcass and honey: 'Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness.'

qs.q: What grave crime did King David commit to cover up his adultery with Bathsheba?
o: He banished Bathsheba's father from Jerusalem
He arranged for Uriah the Hittite to be placed in the front line of battle to be killed
He confiscated Uriah's lands and cattle
He bribed the Levites to alter official records
qs.e: 2 Samuel 11:14-15 details David writing a letter to Joab instructing him to set Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle and retire from him.

qs.q: Why did the prophet Elijah declare to King Ahab that there would be neither dew nor rain in Israel for years?
o: Because Israel failed to pay tribute to Phoenicia
Because Ahab had provoked God's wrath by promoting state-sponsored Baal worship under Jezebel
Because the priests had stopped holding national sports festivals
Because Ahab refused to build a new palace in Jezreel
qs.e: 1 Kings 17:1 shows Elijah confronting Ahab's idolatry, declaring no dew nor rain according to his word as divine judgment.

qs.q: In Isaiah 11:6, what poetic imagery describes the harmonious peace of the future messianic kingdom?
o: The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid
Eagles shall nest in the royal palaces of Babylon
Lions shall hunt alongside hunters in peace
The sea shall dry up and become a paved highway
qs.e: Isaiah 11:6 paints a picture of complete messianic peace: 'The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid...'

qs.q: In the Parable of the Sower (Matthew 13), what do the four types of soil represent?
o: Four different geographical regions of ancient Palestine
Four distinct heart conditions and responses to the preaching of God's word
Four agricultural seasons in the Jewish calendar
qs.e: Matthew 13:18-23 explains that the wayside, stony ground, thorny ground, and good ground represent different human responses to the word of the kingdom.

qs.q: What words did Jesus speak when raising Jairus' twelve-year-old daughter from death in Mark 5?
o: Talitha cumi (Damsel, I say unto thee, arise)
Young man, I say unto thee, arise
qs.e: Mark 5:41 records Jesus taking the damsel by the hand and saying 'Talitha cumi; which is, being interpreted, Damsel, I say unto thee, arise.'

qs.q: What dramatic symbolic gesture did Pontius Pilate perform before condemning Jesus to be crucified?
o: He tore his official governor robes
He washed his hands in water before the crowd, declaring himself innocent of Jesus' blood
He broke his wooden staff of office
He placed a wreath on Jesus' head
qs.e: Matthew 27:24 records Pilate taking water and washing his hands before the multitude, saying, 'I am innocent of the blood of this just person: see ye to it.'

qs.q: What miracle did Peter perform at Joppa when Tabitha (Dorcas), a woman noted for charitable acts, died?
o: He gave her family silver for burial
He prayed, turned to her body, commanded 'Tabitha, arise', and she opened her eyes alive
He composed a funeral hymn in her memory
He anointed her clothes for burial
qs.e: Acts 9:40-41 records Peter putting everyone forth, kneeling down to pray, and saying 'Tabitha, arise', whereupon she opened her eyes and sat up.

qs.q: What resulted when Philip went down to the city of Samaria to preach Christ (Acts 8)?
o: The Samaritans drove him out with stones
Unclean spirits were cast out, paralyzed people were healed, and there was great joy in that city
Philip was arrested by Roman soldiers
The Samaritans insisted on building an altar on Mount Gerizim
qs.e: Acts 8:5-8 states that Philip preached Christ in Samaria, miracles were performed, and there was great joy in that city.

qs.q: In Philippians 2:5-8, how does Paul describe the self-emptying humility of Jesus Christ?
o: Christ retained His royal earthly power and conquered Rome
Though being in the form of God, He humbled Himself, took the form of a servant, and became obedient unto death on a cross
Christ refused to take human flesh and remained a spirit
Christ demanded physical worship from earthly kings
qs.e: Philippians 2:6-8 describes Christ taking the form of a servant, made in the likeness of men, humbling Himself unto the death of the cross.

qs.q: What consequence followed the disobedience of Adam and Eve in Genesis 3 regarding their status in Eden?
o: They were promoted to rule over the angels
They were expelled from the Garden of Eden to till the ground and kept from the Tree of Life by cherubim and a flaming sword
They were made immortal rulers over Palestine
They were commanded to build a wooden ark
qs.e: Genesis 3:23-24 records God driving out man from the garden and placing cherubim and a flaming sword to guard the way to the tree of life.

qs.q: Why did Jacob flee from Canaan to Padan-aram to live with his uncle Laban?
o: To search for precious metals in Haran
To escape the murderous wrath of his brother Esau after securing the birthright blessing
To avoid a regional plague in Hebron
To fulfill a military commission from Isaac
qs.e: Genesis 27:41-43 records Rebekah warning Jacob that Esau purposed to kill him, advising him to flee to Laban in Haran until Esau's anger subsided.

qs.q: What two dreams of Joseph caused his brothers' hatred against him to intensify (Genesis 37)?
o: Dreams of seven fat cows and seven lean cows
His brothers' sheaves bowing to his sheaf, and the sun, moon, and eleven stars bowing to him
A dream of a grapevine with three branches and a basket of bread
A dream of a great ladder reaching to heaven
qs.e: Genesis 37:5-10 records Joseph's dreams of the sheaves and heavenly bodies bowing to him, which made his brothers hate him even more.

qs.q: Why was Gideon nicknamed 'Jerubbaal' by his father Joash after destroying the altar of Baal (Judges 6)?
o: Because Gideon sacrificed a bull on the altar
Joash declared 'Let Baal plead against him' because Gideon had thrown down his altar
Because Gideon fled into the desert of Midian
Because Gideon was appointed high priest over Ophrah
qs.e: Judges 6:31-32 records Joash saying that if Baal were a god, let Baal plead for himself, calling Gideon 'Jerubbaal'.

qs.q: How did King David demonstrate exuberant spiritual devotion when bringing the Ark of the Covenant to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 6)?
o: He rode in a golden chariot surrounded by Persian guards
He danced before the LORD with all his might wearing a simple linen ephod
He offered thousands of horses on Mount Zion
He remained seated in silent contemplation
qs.e: 2 Samuel 6:14 records that David danced before the LORD with all his might; and David was girded with a linen ephod.

qs.q: How did God grant victory to King Jehoshaphat when confronted by the vast coalition of Moab and Ammon (2 Chronicles 20)?
o: Jehoshaphat purchased siege engines from Egypt
Jehoshaphat set praise singers before the army to sing 'Praise the LORD', causing God to set ambushes so the enemies destroyed one another
The Israelites launched a surprise night attack on the enemy camp
A wall of fire fell from heaven to burn the invaders
qs.e: 2 Chronicles 20:21-22 states that as singers praised the beauty of holiness, the Lord set ambushments and the enemy forces destroyed each other.

qs.q: How did Elisha neutralize the poisonous wild gourds cooked into the stew for the sons of the prophets at Gilgal (2 Kings 4)?
o: He threw salt into the pot and prayed
He cast meal (flour) into the pot and declared 'Pour out for the people', removing the harm
He commanded the disciples to pour the stew on the ground
He boiled the stew for three additional days
