qs.e: 2 Kings 4:40-41 records Elisha putting flour into the pot, whereupon there was no harm left in the pot.

qs.q: What mixed emotional reactions accompanied the laying of the foundation of the second Temple under Zerubbabel (Ezra 3)?
o: The whole assembly wept bitter tears without any joy
Many shouted aloud for joy while old men who remembered the first temple wept with a loud voice
The priests went on strike over salary disputes
The Persian soldiers celebrated while the Levites mourned
qs.e: Ezra 3:12-13 describes the ancient elders weeping aloud while many shouted for joy, so that people could not discern the noise of joy from weeping.

qs.q: How did Job maintain his spiritual integrity when news arrived that his livestock, servants, and children were destroyed?
o: He cursed his birthday and renounced his heritage
He fell down, worshipped God, and declared 'The LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD'
He blamed his friends for bringing evil upon his house
He demanded immediate financial compensation from his neighbors
qs.e: Job 1:20-21 records Job worshipping God and uttering: 'Naked came I out of my mother's womb... the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.'

qs.q: How did Hosea demonstrate God's redeeming love when his unfaithful wife Gomer sank into slavery (Hosea 3)?
o: He allowed her to remain in bondage to teach her a lesson
He bought her back for fifteen pieces of silver and a measure of barley, instructing her to live faithfully with him
He divorced her legally before the elders of Samaria
He requested the king of Israel to imprison her lovers
qs.e: Hosea 3:1-2 records God commanding Hosea to love a woman beloved of her friend, yet an adulteress, and Hosea bought her for fifteen pieces of silver.

qs.q: What prophetic utterance did devout Simeon proclaim when infant Jesus was presented in the Temple (Luke 2)?
o: This child shall restore the earthly throne of David immediately
Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace... for mine eyes have seen thy salvation
Beware, for Jerusalem shall fall to foreign armies in this child's lifetime
This child shall grow up to be high priest over Israel
qs.e: Luke 2:29-32 records Simeon's Nunc Dimittis praising God for seeing His salvation, a light to lighten the Gentiles and glory of Israel.

qs.q: What faith-filled action brought instant healing to the woman afflicted with a twelve-year issue of blood (Mark 5)?
o: She asked the apostles to lay hands on her head
She came behind Jesus in the crowd and touched the border of His garment, believing she would be made whole
She bathed in the Pool of Bethesda seven times
She brought a costly box of ointment to Jesus
qs.e: Mark 5:27-29 records that she touched His garment, believing 'If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole', and was healed instantly.

qs.q: Why did Demetrius the silversmith incite a massive riot against Paul in Ephesus (Acts 19)?
o: Paul refused to pay city taxes to the Roman governor
Paul's preaching against man-made gods threatened Demetrius' trade in silver shrines of Diana (Artemis)
Paul attempted to close down the local marketplace
Paul urged citizens to overthrow the local city council
qs.e: Acts 19:24-27 shows Demetrius gathering fellow craftsmen, warning that Paul's teaching 'they be no gods, which are made with hands' endangered their wealth and Diana's temple.

qs.q: In 1 Corinthians 13, why does Paul declare love (agape) to be superior to spiritual gifts such as prophecy and tongues?
o: Because love enables believers to acquire earthly wealth
Because gifts like prophecy and tongues will cease, whereas love never fails and abides eternally
Because love requires no personal sacrifice
Because love was practiced only by the twelve apostles
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 13:8, 13 teaches that prophecies fail and tongues cease, but love never faileth, concluding: 'now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.'

qs.q: Why was Moses barred by God from leading Israel into the Promised Land of Canaan (Numbers 20)?
o: Because he lost the physical stone tablets of the Law
Because at Meribah he struck the rock twice in anger and spoke rashly instead of sanctifying God by speaking to it
Because he refused to appoint Joshua as his successor
Because he fell ill during the journey through Moab
qs.e: Numbers 20:11-12 records God telling Moses and Aaron that because they did not believe Him to sanctify Him in the eyes of Israel, they would not bring the assembly into Canaan.

qs.q: How did Nathan the prophet cleverly convict King David of his hidden guilt regarding Bathsheba and Uriah?
o: He brought eyewitnesses from Joab's army to testify against David
He told a parable about a rich man stealing a poor man's single beloved ewe lamb, making David condemn himself before saying 'Thou art the man!'
He posted a public indictment on the gates of Jerusalem
He threatened David with immediate military invasion by Syria
qs.e: 2 Samuel 12:1-7 details Nathan's parable of the ewe lamb, which aroused David's righteous anger against the rich man, whereupon Nathan declared 'Thou art the man!'.

qs.q: How did Elisha retrieve a borrowed iron axe head that had fallen into the Jordan River (2 Kings 6)?
o: He sent a skilled swimmer to dive for it
He cut off a stick, cast it into the water at the spot, and made the iron float to the surface
He commanded the Jordan River to stop flowing until it was recovered
He used a magnetic rod provided by Syrian blacksmiths
qs.e: 2 Kings 6:5-6 records that when the axe head fell in the water, Elisha cut down a stick, cast it in thither, and the iron did swim.

qs.q: How did Nehemiah resolve the severe economic crisis and internal oppression among returned exiles in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 5)?
o: He banished all wealthy nobles from Jerusalem
He rebuked the nobles for charging high interest (usury) on poor brethren, forcing them to restore mortgaged lands and forgive debts
He requested financial subsidies from the Roman empire
He commanded the poor to work as indentured servants in Persia
qs.e: Nehemiah 5:6-12 details Nehemiah confronting the nobles and rulers for usury, demanding complete restoration of lands, vineyards, and interest.

qs.q: What did Ezekiel's vision of the Valley of Dry Bones (Ezekiel 37) communicate to the scattered exiles of Israel?
o: That physical resurrection would occur only for levitical priests
That God would sovereignly breathe life into the hopeless, scattered nation of Israel and restore them to their land
That the Babylonian army would be buried in that valley
That the exiles should build a permanent necropolis in Babylon
qs.e: Ezekiel 37:11-14 explains the vision: the dry bones represent the whole house of Israel saying 'Our hope is lost', whom God promises to raise up and bring back to Israel.

qs.q: What fundamental principle of faith is articulated in Habakkuk 2:4 in contrast to the proud soul?
o: The wealthy shall rule by their gold
Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him: but the just shall live by his faith
Victory belongs solely to those with large armies
Righteousness is attained through public ceremonial fasting
qs.e: Habakkuk 2:4 states: 'Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him: but the just shall live by his faith', a key verse quoted in Romans, Galatians, and Hebrews.

qs.q: In Matthew 5:38-42, how does Jesus redefine the traditional law of retaliation ('an eye for an eye')?
o: By demanding double legal punishment for all physical injuries
By teaching non-retaliation and active love: turn the other cheek, give your cloak, and go the extra mile
By encouraging disciples to appeal to Roman courts for every conflict
By restricting forgiveness strictly to family members
qs.e: Matthew 5:38-42 transforms retribution into radical grace: 'resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.'

qs.q: In the Parable of the Wheat and Tares (Matthew 13), why did the householder forbid his servants from pulling up the tares immediately?
o: The tares were valuable crops used for animal feed
Lest while gathering up the tares, they root up also the wheat with them; both must grow together until harvest
The servants lacked proper harvesting sickles
The householder wanted to sell the tares to neighboring towns
qs.e: Matthew 13:28-30 explains that pulling tares early risks uprooting wheat, symbolizing God allowing righteous and wicked to co-exist until the final judgment.

qs.q: What controversy arose among the Pharisees when Jesus healed a man born blind on the Sabbath day (John 9)?
o: They accused the man of faking his blindness
Some declared Jesus was not from God because He kept not the Sabbath, while others asked how a sinner could do such miracles
They demanded that Jesus pay a fine to the temple treasury
They praised Jesus for fulfilling Isaiah's prophecy
qs.e: John 9:16 records the division among the Pharisees: 'This man is not of God, because he keepeth not the sabbath day. Others said, How can a man that is a sinner do such miracles?'

qs.q: Why were the believers in Berea praised in Acts 17:11 in comparison to those in Thessalonica?
o: They built larger church buildings in Greece
They received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily whether those things were so
They raised large funds for Paul's journey to Rome
They refused to engage in discussions with Greek philosophers
qs.e: Acts 17:11 states: 'These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.'

qs.q: In James 2:14-26, how does James explain the necessary relationship between genuine faith and works?
o: Works can save a person without any need for faith in Christ
Faith without works is dead, being alone; true faith is demonstrated and perfected through practical deeds of love
Faith and works are completely unrelated in Christian living
Works are required only for levitical priests and apostles
qs.e: James 2:17, 26 emphasizes that faith if it hath not works is dead, being alone, using Abraham and Rahab as examples of faith expressed through action.

qs.q: In Genesis 22, how does Abraham's obedience on Mount Moriah establish both a supreme test of covenant faith and a profound redemptive typology?
o: By proving that human sacrifice was required for covenant blessings in Israel
By demonstrating total faith in God's power to raise Isaac from the dead, while prefiguring God providing His only Son as the ultimate substitutionary sacrifice
By showing that Abraham cared more for his reputation than his son
By establishing Mount Moriah as the political capital of the Philistines
qs.e: Hebrews 11:17-19 and Genesis 22 show Abraham trusting God to raise Isaac, while the ram provided by God (Jehovah Jireh) prefigured the divine substitutionary atonement.

qs.q: How does 1 Samuel 16:7 redefine the spiritual evaluation of leadership during the anointing of David over his older brothers?
o: It asserts that physical height and military experience are the primary qualifications for kingship
It contrasts human reliance on outward physical appearance with God's evaluation of the inner heart attitude and moral character
It establishes that only the eldest son in a family can be anointed king
It proves that Samuel made a mistake by selecting David
qs.e: 1 Samuel 16:7 records God correcting Samuel: 'Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature... for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart.'

qs.q: What theological resolution is achieved in Job 38-42 when God answers Job out of the whirlwind?
o: God gives a detailed explanation of Satan's role in Job's suffering
God reveals His unsearchable wisdom and sovereign majesty in creation, leading Job to repent of arrogant questioning and trust God's sovereign governance without demanding full explanation
God admits that Job's suffering was an accidental oversight
God commands Job's friends to offer human sacrifices to appease His wrath
qs.e: Job 42:1-6 shows Job acknowledging God's omnipotence and his own ignorance: 'I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee. Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.'

qs.q: In Isaiah 6:1-8, how does the vision of God's transcendent holiness transform Isaiah's self-awareness and prophetic mission?
o: It makes Isaiah feel spiritually superior to the priests in Jerusalem
The revelation of God's absolute holiness confronts Isaiah with his own sinful ruin ('Woe is me!'), leading to divine cleansing with a live coal and voluntary surrender to be sent
It causes Isaiah to abandon his prophetic calling in fear
It instructs Isaiah to build a physical sanctuary in Assyria
qs.e: Isaiah 6:5-8 shows that encountering divine holiness produces conviction of sin, followed by hot-coal purification from the altar, enabling Isaiah to answer 'Here am I; send me.'

qs.q: In Romans 8:14-39, how does Paul synthesize the Christian's present suffering with future glory and ultimate security?
o: By promising that believers will never experience physical persecution or trials on earth
By explaining that present sufferings are not worthy to be compared with future glory, while the Spirit intercedes for us and nothing can separate us from God's love in Christ
By asserting that only levitical martyrs are entitled to divine inheritance
By teaching that Christian security depends strictly on maintaining personal sinless perfection
qs.e: Romans 8:18, 26, 38-39 affirms that present suffering is outweighed by glory, the Spirit groans in intercession, and nothing in creation shall separate us from the love of God.

qs.q: What responsibility did God assign to man upon placing him in the Garden of Eden (Genesis 2:15)?
o: To build stone altars and towers
To dress it and to keep it
To dig gold and silver mines
To name all rivers in the region
qs.e: Genesis 2:15 states: 'And the LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.'

qs.q: When God brought Abram outside at night in Genesis 15, what cosmic image did He use to illustrate Abram's future offspring?
o: Grains of corn in a basket
The number of stars in the sky
The pebbles in the Jordan River
qs.e: Genesis 15:5 records God bringing Abram forth abroad and saying: 'Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them... So shall thy seed be.'

qs.q: What miracle permitted the Israelites to cross the Red Sea safely while escaping Pharaoh's army?
o: An angel built a floating wooden pontoon
The Lord caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind, dividing the waters so Israel walked on dry ground
A severe drought dried up the sea completely for three months
The Israelites swam across guided by dolphins
qs.e: Exodus 14:21-22 describes the Lord dividing the sea with a strong east wind, making the sea dry land for the children of Israel.

qs.q: What title did John the Baptist proclaim upon seeing Jesus coming toward him at the Jordan River (John 1:29)?
o: Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world
qs.e: John 1:29 records John the Baptist declaring: 'Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.'

qs.q: In the Beatitudes (Matthew 5:6), what promise is given to those who hunger and thirst after righteousness?
qs.e: Matthew 5:6 promises: 'Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.'

qs.q: What was the very first miracle (sign) performed by Jesus at the wedding feast in Cana of Galilee?
qs.e: John 2:11 notes that turning water into wine at Cana was the beginning of miracles Jesus did to manifest His glory.

qs.q: On which day after His crucifixion did Jesus Christ rise from the dead, according to the Scriptures?
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 15:4 states that Christ was buried and rose again the third day according to the Scriptures.

qs.q: How did Jacob react when Joseph's brothers presented him with Joseph's coat dipped in goat's blood?
o: He immediately suspected his sons had lied
He rent his clothes, put sackcloth on his loins, and mourned many days believing an evil beast devoured Joseph
He sent a search team to Egypt
He offered a calf as a sacrifice at Bethel
qs.e: Genesis 37:33-34 records Jacob recognizing the coat and saying, 'It is my son's coat; an evil beast hath devoured him... and Jacob rent his clothes.'

qs.q: How did God visibly guide the children of Israel during their wilderness journeys (Exodus 13)?
o: By a flying eagle during the day and a glowing star at night
By a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night
By a trumpet sound every morning and evening
By a visible levitical guard marching ahead
qs.e: Exodus 13:21-22 states the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of cloud to lead the way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light.

qs.q: How did Gideon reduce his army from ten thousand down to three hundred men at the spring of Harod (Judges 7)?
o: He selected those who brought swords and shields
He chose only those who lapped water with their hands to their mouths like a dog, setting aside those who bowed on knees to drink
He selected the youngest soldiers in the camp
He chose men from the tribe of Judah only
qs.e: Judges 7:5-7 records God instructing Gideon to separate those who lapped water bringing hand to mouth (300 men) to deliver Israel.

qs.q: How did King David demonstrate covenant loyalty to his deceased friend Jonathan regarding Mephibosheth (2 Samuel 9)?
o: He appointed Mephibosheth as general over Joab's army
He restored all the land of Saul to lame Mephibosheth and granted him a permanent seat at the royal table
He sent Mephibosheth to live in luxury in Moab
He exempted Mephibosheth from paying city taxes
qs.e: 2 Samuel 9:7 records David assuring Mephibosheth: 'Fear not: for I will surely shew thee kindness for Jonathan thy father's sake, and will restore thee all the land of Saul... thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.'

qs.q: What judgment did Elijah pronounce against King Ahab when they met in Naboth's vineyard (1 Kings 21)?
o: Ahab would be captured alive by the king of Syria
In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth shall dogs lick thy blood, even thine
Ahab's palace in Samaria would be burned by fire
Ahab's kingdom would immediately be divided into four
qs.e: 1 Kings 21:19 records Elijah's direct prophecy: 'In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth shall dogs lick thy blood, even thine.'

qs.q: What glorious messianic titles are prophesied for the divine child in Isaiah 9:6?
o: King of Kings, High Priest, Commander of Assyria
Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace
Lion of Judah, Prophet of Horeb, Deliverer of Samaria
Son of David, Scribe of the Law, Ruler of Babylon
qs.e: Isaiah 9:6 declares: 'and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.'

qs.q: In the Parable of the Pearl of Great Price (Matthew 13), what action did the merchant take upon finding one precious pearl?
o: He borrowed money from friends to pay half the cost
He went and sold all that he had and bought it
He negotiated a lower price with the owner
He hid the pearl in the ground until harvest
qs.e: Matthew 13:45-46 describes the merchant finding one pearl of great price, going and selling all that he had, and purchasing it.

qs.q: What happened to the herd of about two thousand swine when Jesus permitted the legion of demons to enter them (Mark 5)?
o: The swine scattered peacefully into the wilderness
The herd ran violently down a steep place into the sea and were choked in the waters
The swine turned on their owners in anger
The herd fell sick for seven days and recovered
qs.e: Mark 5:13 records the unclean spirits entering the swine, whereupon the herd ran violently down a steep bank into the sea and drowned.

qs.q: What confession was made by the Roman centurion standing guard at the cross of Jesus (Matthew 27:54)?
o: This man was a dangerous political rebel!
Truly this was the Son of God
The governor made a mistake in executing this man
This man possessed great sorcery skills
qs.e: Matthew 27:54 records that when the centurion saw the earthquake and events, he feared greatly, saying, 'Truly this was the Son of God.'

qs.q: Why did Paul publicly confront Peter (Cephas) at Antioch according to Galatians 2:11-14?
o: Peter was teaching false doctrines regarding resurrection
Peter hypocritically withdrew from eating with Gentile believers when Jewish emissaries from James arrived
Peter refused to travel to Rome with Paul
Peter insisted on collecting money for himself
qs.e: Galatians 2:11-14 records Paul withstanding Peter to the face because he walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel by segregating from Gentiles.

qs.q: What spiritual character qualities led the church at Jerusalem to select Stephen as one of the seven deacons (Acts 6)?
o: He was wealthy and belonged to the Sanhedrin
He was a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit
He was a trained Roman lawyer
He was a priest from the line of Zadok
qs.e: Acts 6:5 highlights Stephen as 'a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost', chosen alongside six others to serve.

qs.q: What threefold concise instruction for daily Christian living is given in 1 Thessalonians 5:16-18?
o: Fast weekly, give alms, attend temple feasts
Rejoice evermore, pray without ceasing, in every thing give thanks
Avoid foreign trade, keep strict vows, judge neighbors
Seek wealth, defend rights, avoid social gathering
qs.e: 1 Thessalonians 5:16-18 commands: 'Rejoice evermore. Pray without ceasing. In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.'

qs.q: How did Isaac respond when the Philistines of Gerar repeatedly strove over the water wells dug by Abraham's servants (Genesis 26)?
o: He waged war against King Abimelech immediately
He peacefully moved away and dug other wells (Esek, Sitnah, Rehoboth) until there was no strife
He poisoned the contested wells to punish Gerar
He abandoned farming and returned to Mesopotamia
qs.e: Genesis 26:17-22 shows Isaac choosing peace, opening old wells, moving when contested, until at Rehoboth he said 'For now the LORD hath made room for us.'

qs.q: Why did Moses put a veil over his face when speaking to the children of Israel after coming down from Mount Sinai (Exodus 34)?
o: To hide a physical disfigurement received on the mountain
Because the skin of his face shone brightly from talking with God, making the people afraid to come near him
To observe Egyptian ritual custom for holy leaders
To shield his eyes from the desert sandstorm
qs.e: Exodus 34:29-35 explains that Moses' face shone after speaking with Yahweh, so he put a veil on his face when speaking to Israel after delivering God's words.

qs.q: How was Saul confirmed as king before the entire assembly of Israel at Mizpah (1 Samuel 10)?
o: He was chosen by democratic voting among tribal leaders
Samuel brought the tribes forward and Saul was selected by divine lot, then found hiding among the baggage
He defeated the Philistine champion in single combat before the crowd
He was crowned by the high priest in Shiloh
qs.e: 1 Samuel 10:20-24 details the selection by lot at Mizpah, pointing out Saul standing head and shoulders taller than the rest.

qs.q: Why did the prophet Shemaiah intervene when Rehoboam assembled 180,000 troops to fight against the northern tribes (1 Kings 12)?
o: Judah lacked weapons to fight northern forces
Shemaiah delivered God's word commanding them not to fight their brethren, for the kingdom division was from the Lord
Persia had ordered a cease-fire in the region
The priests refused to carry the Ark into battle
qs.e: 1 Kings 12:22-24 records Shemaiah telling Rehoboam: 'Thus saith the LORD, Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren... for this thing is from me.'

qs.q: Why did Ezra proclaim a fast at the river Ahava prior to leading the second group of exiles back to Jerusalem (Ezra 8)?
o: To mourn the destruction of Babylon
To humbly seek God's protection for their journey and children, being ashamed to ask the Persian king for a military escort
To observe the national day of Atonement
To prepare for levitical priesthood examinations
qs.e: Ezra 8:21-23 records Ezra proclaiming a fast to afflict themselves before God, because he was ashamed to require a band of soldiers since he had declared God protects those who seek Him.

qs.q: What wisdom regarding interpersonal speech is taught in Proverbs 15:1?
o: A sharp retort silences an opponent quickly
A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger
Silence is always understood as agreement in arguments
Loud shouting demonstrates conviction in debate
qs.e: Proverbs 15:1 states: 'A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.'

qs.q: In Isaiah 58, how does God define the acceptable fast that pleases Him in contrast to mere self-affliction?
o: Fasting seven days without drinking water while wearing sackcloth
Loosening the bands of wickedness, sharing bread with the hungry, housing the poor, and clothing the naked
Offering double animal sacrifices at the temple altar
Refraining from speaking foreign languages on fast days
qs.e: Isaiah 58:6-7 describes true fasting: 'Is not this the fast that I have chosen? to loose the bands of wickedness... to deal thy bread to the hungry...'

qs.q: What Pentecostal prophecy in Joel 2:28-29 was quoted by Peter in Acts 2 to explain the Holy Spirit's outpouring?
o: The temple shall be rebuilt in three days
I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy
The stars shall fall from heaven upon Samaria
All foreign nations shall pay tribute to Jerusalem
qs.e: Joel 2:28-29 and Acts 2:17-18 promise the universal outpouring of God's Spirit upon all flesh, sons, daughters, young men, and old men.

qs.q: What was the core evangelical message preached by John the Baptist in the wilderness of Judea (Matthew 3)?
o: Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand
Keep the oral traditions of the Pharisees strictly
qs.e: Matthew 3:1-2 states that John the Baptist came preaching in the wilderness of Judea, saying, 'Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.'

qs.q: How does Jesus address anxiety over daily physical needs like food and clothing in Matthew 6:25-34?
o: By encouraging disciples to accumulate vast storehouses of grain
By pointing to how God feeds the birds and clothes the lilies, exhorting 'Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness'
By instructing disciples to work continuously without sleeping
By promising that believers will never face economic scarcity
qs.e: Matthew 6:31-33 directs disciples away from anxious worry toward divine trust: 'Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.'

qs.q: What lesson on gratitude and faith was demonstrated when Jesus healed ten lepers in Luke 17?
o: All ten lepers returned to offer sacrifices at the temple
Only one, a Samaritan stranger, returned to fall at Jesus' feet giving thanks, receiving spiritual wholeness
Jesus rebuked the Samaritan for returning instead of going to the priests
The nine Jewish lepers were struck with leprosy again for unthankfulness
qs.e: Luke 17:17-19 shows Jesus asking 'Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?', praising the Samaritan stranger whose faith made him whole.

qs.q: During Jesus' trial before the Sanhedrin (Matthew 26), what declaration caused High Priest Caiaphas to tear his clothes and accuse Him of blasphemy?
o: Jesus declared He would destroy the Roman empire in three days
Jesus affirmed He was the Christ, the Son of God, and foretold seeing the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power
Jesus claimed to be greater than King Solomon
Jesus refused to answer any questions
qs.e: Matthew 26:63-65 records Jesus affirming His messianic identity and divine enthronement, whereupon the high priest rent his clothes shouting 'He hath spoken blasphemy!'.

qs.q: How did Barnabas (Joseph, a Levite of Cyprus) demonstrate exemplary sacrificial generosity in the early church (Acts 4)?
o: He funded the building of the first church in Antioch
Having land, he sold it, brought the money, and laid it at the apostles' feet for distribution to the needy
He donated a fleet of fishing ships to Galilean believers
He paid the bail for Peter and John's release from prison
qs.e: Acts 4:36-37 records Barnabas selling his land and laying the money at the apostles' feet, earning his name 'Son of Consolation'.

qs.q: What accusation was leveled against Paul and Silas by hostile mobs in Thessalonica (Acts 17)?
o: They were stealing silver vessels from local temples
These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also, acting contrary to Caesar's decrees
They were Roman spies planning a tax boycott
They were preaching against Greek athletic games
qs.e: Acts 17:6-7 records the mob dragging Jason and brethren, crying: 'These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also; Whom Jason hath received...'

qs.q: How does Paul describe the Christian's armor piece called 'the helmet of salvation' in Ephesians 6?
o: A physical helmet worn during street evangelism
Spiritual protection for the mind and thoughts grounded in the assurance of divine salvation
A ceremonial crown given to levitical elders
A symbol of political protection from Roman authorities
qs.e: Ephesians 6:17 and 1 Thessalonians 5:8 describe taking the helmet of salvation (the hope of salvation) to guard the believer's mind against spiritual attacks.

qs.q: What recurring four-stage cycle defines the overarching narrative structure of the book of Judges?
o: Prophecy, anointed king, victory, tribute payment
Apostasy (sin), divine oppression, groaning/repentance, and divine deliverance through a raised judge
Temple building, animal sacrifice, exile, return
Famine, flight to Egypt, prosperity, return to Canaan
qs.e: Judges 2:11-19 outlines the repetitive cycle: Israel forsakes God, falls to enemies, groans under oppression, repents, and God raises a judge to deliver them.

qs.q: What startling prophecy was delivered by the unnamed man of God from Judah against Jeroboam's altar at Bethel (1 Kings 13)?
o: That the altar would be taken to Babylon within three years
That a child named Josiah would be born to the house of David who would burn the bones of false priests upon that altar
That Jeroboam would rule over both Judah and Israel
That fire from heaven would consume Dan and Bethel immediately
qs.e: 1 Kings 13:1-2 explicitly predicts King Josiah by name 300 years before his birth: 'Behold, a child shall be born unto the house of David, Josiah by name; and upon thee shall he offer the priests...'

qs.q: How did Nehemiah organize the physical reconstruction of Jerusalem's walls to foster maximum personal commitment and speed (Nehemiah 3)?
o: He hired foreign contractors from Tyre to build the entire wall
He assigned families, priests, and trade guilds to repair the specific sections directly opposite their own homes
He forced all residents to work in a single centralized construction team
He assigned wall building exclusively to levitical priests
qs.e: Nehemiah 3 details the strategic organization where individuals and families repaired the wall 'over against his house', creating personal ownership and efficient division of labor.

qs.q: What theological view of human existence under the sun is presented in Ecclesiastes 3:1-8 ('To every thing there is a season')?
o: Human events occur in chaotic, random fashion without divine oversight
All human activities and life events are subject to God's sovereign timing and appointed purpose
Human beings have complete power to control all natural seasons
Time is an illusion and earthly actions have no moral consequences
qs.e: Ecclesiastes 3:1-8 emphasizes divine providence over human life, asserting that God has set a season and time for every purpose under heaven.

qs.q: What divine truth was illustrated when Jeremiah visited the potter's house in Jeremiah 18?
o: That clay vessels are superior to metallic urns for temple use
Just as the potter has power to reshape a spoiled clay vessel, God has sovereign authority to reshape or judge nations based on their repentance or persistence in evil
That Israel would forever remain broken without possibility of reshaping
That levitical priests must learn pottery trades
qs.e: Jeremiah 18:1-10 shows God explaining: 'O house of Israel, cannot I do with you as this potter? saith the LORD. Behold, as the clay is in the potter's hand, so are ye in mine hand.'

qs.q: What distinguishes the five wise virgins from the five foolish virgins in the Parable of the Ten Virgins (Matthew 25)?
o: The wise virgins bought expensive gold lamps while the foolish had clay lamps
The wise virgins took reserve oil in vessels with their lamps, ensuring readiness when the bridegroom was delayed
The wise virgins stayed awake all night while the foolish slept
The wise virgins refused to attend the wedding feast
qs.e: Matthew 25:1-13 notes that the foolish took lamps without oil reserves, whereas the wise took oil in their vessels, symbolizing spiritual preparation for Christ's return.

qs.q: What supreme mandate is expressed in the Great Commission given by the risen Christ in Matthew 28:18-20?
o: To establish a earthly political kingdom headquartered in Jerusalem
To go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, and teaching them obedience
To enforce Mosaic dietary laws across Gentile territories
To build physical cathedrals throughout the Roman empire
qs.e: Matthew 28:18-20 records Jesus claiming all authority and sending disciples: 'Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them... Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you.'

qs.q: How did Peter justify his decision to preach to and baptize the Gentile household of Cornelius before the Jerusalem church (Acts 11)?
o: He argued that Cornelius paid a large sum to the church treasury
He recounted his divine vision at Joppa and noted that the Holy Spirit fell upon the Gentiles just as upon Jewish believers at Pentecost, asking 'what was I, that I could withstand God?'
He claimed that Roman authorities forced him to perform the baptism
He asserted that Gentile baptism was allowed only during wartime
qs.e: Acts 11:15-17 shows Peter explaining how the Holy Spirit fell on Cornelius' house, convincing the Jerusalem brethren who glorified God saying 'Then hath God also to the Gentiles granted repentance unto life.'

qs.q: In Romans 6:1-14, how does Paul explain the spiritual significance of Christian baptism?
o: As a mere outward bath requiring no inner transformation
As a spiritual identification with Christ's death and burial, so that being dead to sin, believers rise to walk in newness of life
As a ritual replacing the requirement for moral obedience
As a guarantee against earthly physical suffering
qs.e: Romans 6:3-4 teaches: 'Know ye not, that so many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into his death? Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised up from the dead... even so we also should walk in newness of life.'

qs.q: What strict practical principle regarding work ethic does Paul lay down in 2 Thessalonians 3:10?
o: Wealthy believers must support all idle members indefinitely
If any would not work, neither should he eat
Manual labor is beneath spiritual leaders and apostles
Churches should collect taxes for Roman authorities
qs.e: 2 Thessalonians 3:10 explicitly commands: 'For even when we were with you, this we commanded you, that if any would not work, neither should he eat.'

qs.q: How does 1 Peter 2:9-10 describe the collective identity and missional purpose of the Christian church?
o: As a political faction seeking dominion over pagan governments
As a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people called to show forth the praises of Him who called them out of darkness into light
As an elite secret society guarded by temple Levites
As a temporary Jewish movement bound to Jerusalem
qs.e: 1 Peter 2:9 declares: 'But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light.'

qs.q: How does the Sinai Covenant preamble in Exodus 19:4-6 ('I bare you on eagles' wings, and brought you unto myself') establish the biblical relationship between grace and law?
o: It proves that keeping the Law was the prerequisite earning mechanism for deliverance from Egypt
It shows that divine redemption from slavery was an unmerited act of grace, while the Law was given as the covenant response for a redeemed kingdom of priests
It demonstrates that the Law was intended to apply only to Levites rather than all Israel
It establishes that animal sacrifices were forbidden prior to entering Canaan
qs.e: Exodus 19:4-6 shows God reminding Israel of His gracious deliverance before presenting the Law, revealing that obedience is the response of a redeemed people rather than a means to earn salvation.

qs.q: What moral and theological lesson is communicated by the tragic death of the unnamed prophet from Judah in 1 Kings 13?
o: That old prophets in Bethel held greater authority than young prophets from Judah
That divine commands are absolute, and trusting a misleading human claim—even from another prophet—in direct contradiction to God's word results in fatal judgment
That lions in the wilderness act without divine control
That eating bread in Bethel was permitted if offered by an elder
qs.e: 1 Kings 13 shows the prophet disobeying God's explicit instruction because he believed an old prophet's lie, demonstrating that no human or angelic word can override a direct divine command.

qs.q: How does Isaiah 55:8-11 contrast human limitations with the sovereign efficacy of God's word?
o: By asserting that human thoughts are superior to divine revelations in practical matters
By declaring 'For my thoughts are not your thoughts', affirming that God's word shall not return void but shall infallibly accomplish His redemptive purpose as rain waters the earth
By proving that prophetic words require human political power to take effect
By showing that divine promises expire after three generations
qs.e: Isaiah 55:8-11 contrasts human and divine ways, affirming: 'So shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please.'

qs.q: In Galatians 2:15-21, how does Paul summarize the radical reality of union with Christ regarding law-works and justification?
o: Believers achieve justification by combining legal ritual performance with faith in Christ
Knowing that man is not justified by the works of the law but by faith in Jesus Christ, Paul declares 'I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me'
The Mosaic Law remains the sole instrument for attaining righteousness before God
Justification applies exclusively to Abraham's physical biological descendants
qs.e: Galatians 2:16, 20 affirms that justification comes solely through faith in Christ, resulting in being crucified with Christ and living by the faith of the Son of God.

qs.q: How does 1 Peter 2:4-10 reframe Old Testament tabernacle and temple priesthood concepts for the New Testament church?
o: By restricting priestly duties exclusively to ordained ministers in Jerusalem
By portraying Christ as the chief cornerstone and believers as living stones built into a spiritual house and holy priesthood to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God
By commanding Christians to rebuild the physical Temple in Jerusalem with precious stones
By abolishing all worship and sacrificial concepts completely
qs.e: 1 Peter 2:4-5 describes believers coming to Christ as living stones, built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God by Jesus Christ.

qs.q: Before joining Paul's second missionary journey, Timothy was circumcised by Paul (Acts 16). What chiefly explains this decision?
o: Paul yielded where no gospel truth was at stake, so the mission to unreached Jews would not be needlessly hindered
Circumcision was required for salvation under the new covenant
Paul wanted Timothy to appear superior to Gentile converts
The Jerusalem council had ordered all converts to be circumcised
qs.e: Paul consistently refused circumcision as a condition of salvation (Galatians 2), yet here no doctrine was at stake: circumcising Timothy removed an offence that would have blocked their witness in Jewish synagogues. It shows wise flexibility for the gospel's advance, not compromise of its truth.

qs.q: After Jesus visited his house, Zacchaeus promised to give half his goods to the poor and restore fourfold anything he had wrongly taken. What does his response chiefly demonstrate?
o: Genuine repentance expresses itself in concrete restitution and generosity
Salvation is earned by generous giving
Public figures must resign on becoming Christians
Wealth makes a person a sinner regardless of conduct
qs.e: Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector, turned from extortion to restitution far beyond the law's requirement (Exodus 22 required restoring the principal plus one fifth; fourfold echoed the sheep-stealing penalty in 2 Samuel 12:6). Jesus declared salvation had come to his house, showing that true repentance produces visible change, not that giving itself earns salvation.

qs.q: A tech startup in Yaba, Lagos, conducts monthly feedback sessions with smartphone users to refine its app features based on customer preferences rather than engineering preference. Which marketing management philosophy is the startup practicing?
qs.e: The marketing concept focuses on determining the needs and wants of target markets and delivering the desired satisfaction more effectively than competitors.

qs.q: An entrepreneur operating a cassava processing plant in Nsukka upgrades waste-water treatment facilities to ensure local streams remain unpolluted, prioritizing community health alongside factory profit. This operational approach represents the
qs.e: The societal marketing concept holds that a company should make marketing decisions considering consumers' wants, company requirements, and long-term societal interests.

qs.q: A boutique hotel in Victoria Island, Lagos, calculates that acquiring a new corporate guest costs N45,000 in digital marketing, whereas retaining an existing corporate client yields N350,000 in net profit over three years. This calculation highlights the strategic value of
qs.e: Customer lifetime value (CLV) quantifies the total net profit a business can expect to earn from a single customer over the entire duration of their relationship.

qs.q: A fitness club owner in Abuja charges a monthly membership fee of N25,000. On average, members stay subscribed for 24 months. If the club's variable cost per member is N7,000 monthly, what is the customer lifetime value (CLV) in profit contribution per member?
qs.e: Monthly profit per member = N25,000 - N7,000 = N18,000. Customer lifetime value = N18,000 x 24 months = N432,000.

qs.q: A commercial bank in Kano trains its branch cashiers and customer care officers on interpersonal courtesy and product knowledge before launching a new high-yield savings product to the public. In holistic marketing, this internal alignment is known as
qs.e: Internal marketing involves hiring, training, and motivating able employees who want to serve customers well, ensuring all staff support marketing goals.

qs.q: When a fast-moving consumer goods firm in Agbara reduces its powdered milk sachet weight from 30g to 26g while keeping the retail price at N100 to offset rising raw material costs, which element of the marketing mix is being adjusted primarily alongside product content?
qs.e: Maintaining the nominal price point while downsizing package content (downsizing) is a strategic price adjustment mechanism to protect profit margins under inflation.

qs.q: In transitioning from the seller-oriented 4 Ps framework to the buyer-oriented 4 Cs model, the 'Place' element corresponds directly to
qs.e: In the 4 Cs framework, Product becomes Customer solution, Price becomes Cost, Place becomes Convenience, and Promotion becomes Communication.

qs.q: A quick-service restaurant chain in Port Harcourt standardizes its kitchen assembly line to reduce customer wait time from 15 minutes to 3 minutes. In the extended marketing mix for services (7 Ps), this improvement represents
qs.e: Process refers to the procedures, mechanisms, and flow of activities by which a service is delivered to the customer efficiently.

qs.q: A logistics and courier company operating in Onitsha equips its delivery drivers with branded uniforms, clean vans, and digital track-and-trace display screens. In service marketing, these tangible touchpoints represent
qs.e: Physical evidence includes the environment in which the service is delivered and any tangible goods that facilitate performance or communication of the service.

qs.q: An edtech firm in Ikeja offers an online video tutoring subscription for N12,000 quarterly. If it spends N3,000 per subscriber on platform server hosting (variable cost) and incurs N1,800,000 in fixed overheads quarterly, how many subscribers are required to achieve break-even in the marketing mix pricing model?
qs.e: Contribution margin per subscriber = N12,000 - N3,000 = N9,000. Break-even subscribers = Fixed Costs / CM = N1,800,000 / N9,000 = 200 subscribers.

qs.q: Sachet drinking water purchased daily by commuters at bus stops in Lagos without prior planning or comparison represents which category of consumer goods?
qs.e: Convenience goods are consumer products that customers purchase frequently, immediately, and with minimal buying effort and store comparison.

qs.q: A hospital in Ibadan purchases an emergency backup 100kVA diesel generator to guarantee uninterrupted power during surgical operations. For the hospital, this generator is classified as
qs.e: Capital items are industrial products that aid in the buyer's production or operations, including installations and major accessory equipment.

qs.q: A conglomerate in Aba manufactures laundry detergents, toilet soaps, dishwashing liquids, and body lotions. The total number of different product lines offered by the company defines its product mix
qs.e: Product mix width (or breadth) refers to the number of different product lines carried by a company.

qs.q: A fruit juice processing firm in Benin City currently sells 1-liter cartons of orange juice and pineapple juice. It introduces a new 250ml sachet variant of orange juice targeted at primary school lunchboxes. This addition is an example of
qs.e: Line extension occurs when a company extends existing brand names to new forms, sizes, or flavors of an existing product category.

qs.q: A solar inverter manufacturer in Asaba offers a basic 3kVA inverter unit for N350,000. For an additional N100,000, it adds a 3-year warranty, free remote mobile monitoring, and annual maintenance visits. These additional features represent which product level?
qs.e: The augmented product includes additional services and benefits built around the core benefit and actual product, such as warranty and after-sales service.

qs.q: A major retail supermarket chain in Abuja sells packaged long-grain rice under its own store name at a price 15% lower than national brands. This packaging strategy is known as a
qs.e: A private label (or store brand) is a brand created and owned by a reseller of a product or service.

qs.q: A conglomerate in Nigeria markets its cement, sugar, salt, and fertilizer under a single corporate name, Dangote. This branding strategy is referred to as
qs.e: Family umbrella branding involves using a single corporate brand name for two or more related or unrelated products in a portfolio.

qs.q: A well-known instant noodle brand in Nigeria leverages its high brand recognition to launch a new line of seasoned potato chips under the exact same brand name. This strategy is an example of
qs.e: Brand extension uses an established brand name to launch a product in a completely new product category.

qs.q: A shopper in Kano enters a provision shop asking specifically for a particular brand of malt drink. When told it is out of stock, the shopper walks past three alternative brands to find another store that stocks their preferred drink. The customer has reached which stage of brand loyalty?
qs.e: Brand insistence is the highest level of brand loyalty where consumers refuse substitutes and will exert substantial effort to buy that specific brand.

qs.q: A premium smartphone manufacturer sells its flagship model for N600,000, while a unbranded generic phone with identical hardware specifications sells for N400,000. The N200,000 price premium consumers are willing to pay solely due to the brand name quantifies the brand's
qs.e: Brand equity is the commercial value derived from consumer perception of the brand name rather than from the product itself, often reflected in premium pricing.

qs.q: The plastic bottle directly holding liquid herbal tea sold in a pharmacy in Jos represents which level of packaging?
qs.e: Primary packaging is the material that directly touches and holds the product, containing it for immediate consumer use.

qs.q: A cardboard box holding 24 individual 1-liter juice cartons for ease of shelf stocking in a supermarket represents
qs.e: Secondary packaging holds multiple primary packages together for protection, display, and handling at the retail store level.

qs.q: Wooden pallets and shrink-wrapped heavy corrugated crates used to transport yam flour across state boundaries from Benue to Lagos are classified as
qs.e: Tertiary (or transit) packaging is designed to protect bulk quantities of goods during bulk shipping, warehousing, and transportation.

qs.q: A seasoning manufacturer in Ogun State package powdered spice into 5g single-use sachets priced at N20 each, enabling low-income rural households to buy exact cooking quantities. This packaging strategy capitalizes primarily on
qs.e: Sachetization breaks bulk into ultra-small affordable units, matching consumer cash flow and expanding market penetration in emerging markets.

qs.q: A cosmetics firm in Lagos redesigns its cream container from a round glass jar to a stackable rectangular plastic tub, reducing master carton shipping volume by 20%. If original freight cost was N500 per unit, what is the new freight cost per unit, assuming freight cost scales linearly with volume?
qs.e: A 20% reduction in volume lowers freight cost by 20%: N500 - (0.20 x N500) = N500 - N100 = N400 per unit.

qs.q: A trader in Ariaria Market, Aba, buys leather shoes for N4,000 per pair and applies a 25% markup on cost. What is the selling price of the shoes?
qs.e: Selling price = Cost + (Cost x Markup %) = N4,000 + (N4,000 x 0.25) = N4,000 + N1,000 = N5,000.

qs.q: If a boutique owner in Ikeja sells a designer dress for N20,000 and earns a profit of N5,000, what is the profit margin percentage on selling price?
qs.e: Profit margin on selling price = (Profit / Selling Price) x 100 = (N5,000 / N20,000) x 100 = 25%.

qs.q: A manufacturer sells goods to a wholesaler with a list price of N50,000, subject to a trade discount of 20% and a cash discount of 5% for payment within 10 days. If the wholesaler pays within 10 days, what is the net amount paid?
qs.e: Price after trade discount = N50,000 x (1 - 0.20) = N40,000. Cash discount = N40,000 x 0.05 = N2,000. Net payment = N40,000 - N2,000 = N38,000.

qs.q: A printing press in Kaduna incurs annual fixed costs of N2,400,000. It prints custom journals sold at N2,000 per unit, with a variable cost of N800 per unit. What is the break-even volume in units?
qs.e: Contribution margin per unit = N2,000 - N800 = N1,200. Break-even quantity = Fixed Costs / CM = N2,400,000 / N1,200 = 2,000 units.

qs.q: A solar home system provider in Enugu faces fixed costs of N3,600,000 annually. Each system sells for N150,000 with variable costs of N90,000 per unit. If the company targets an annual profit of N1,800,000, how many units must be sold?
qs.e: CM per unit = N150,000 - N90,000 = N60,000. Required units = (Fixed Costs + Target Profit) / CM = (N3,600,000 + N1,800,000) / N60,000 = N5,400,000 / N60,000 = 90 units.

qs.q: A poultry farmer in Epe sells fresh eggs directly to consumers at the farm gate without using any middlemen. This distribution network represents a
qs.e: A zero-level channel (direct marketing channel) consists of a manufacturer selling directly to the final consumer without intermediaries.

qs.q: A soft drink manufacturer distributes its products through thousands of roadside kiosks, open market vendors, supermarkets, and street hawkers across Nigeria. This distribution coverage strategy is known as
qs.e: Intensive distribution aims to stock products in as many outlets as possible, essential for convenience items like soft drinks.

qs.q: A luxury Italian suit brand appoints only one authorized retail showroom in Victoria Island, Lagos, to sell its apparel in Nigeria. This distribution coverage is termed
qs.e: Exclusive distribution grants severe limitations on the number of intermediaries, giving one dealer exclusive rights to distribute the brand in a territory.

qs.q: A dispute arising between a soft drink manufacturer and its appointed regional wholesalers over direct factory sales to major retail supermarkets in their territory is an example of
qs.e: Vertical channel conflict occurs between different levels within the same distribution channel (e.g. manufacturer vs wholesaler).

qs.q: A cement factory in Gboko ships cement to Lagos via rail freight at N12,000 per ton (transit time 5 days) or via road haulage at N18,000 per ton (transit time 2 days). If holding cost of inventory in transit is N1,000 per ton per day, which mode yields lower total distribution cost per ton and by how much?
o: Rail freight is cheaper by N3,000
Road haulage is cheaper by N2,000
Rail freight is cheaper by N6,000
Both modes cost exactly the same
qs.e: Rail total cost = Freight N12,000 + Transit inventory (5 days x N1,000 = N5,000) = N17,000. Road total cost = Freight N18,000 + Transit inventory (2 days x N1,000 = N2,000) = N20,000. Rail is cheaper by N20,000 - N17,000 = N3,000.

qs.q: An agricultural chemical firm offers trade allowances and extra free cartons to agro-dealers in Ibadan to persuade them to stock and push its new herbicide to farmers. This promotional strategy is classified as a
qs.e: A push strategy uses the sales force and trade promotion to push the product through marketing channels to final consumers.

qs.q: A soft drink company launches a national radio contest urging consumers to buy bottled drinks, collect caps, and demand prizes from their local provision shops. This strategy is a
qs.e: A pull strategy spends heavily on consumer advertising and promotion to induce final consumers to buy the product, pulling it through channels.

qs.q: A financial services firm in Lagos coordinates its TV commercials, billboard messaging, radio jingles, and social media posts so that all channels communicate a single unified brand message. This strategic approach is called
qs.e: Integrated Marketing Communications (IMC) carefully integrates and coordinates company communication channels to deliver a clear, consistent message.

qs.q: In the AIDA model of promotional communication, what does the second letter 'I' represent?
qs.e: The AIDA model stands for Attention, Interest, Desire, and Action.

qs.q: A consumer goods company sets its annual promotional budget at exactly 5% of its projected annual gross sales revenue of N800,000,000. What is the allocated promotional budget?
An advertising campaign launched by a solar inverter firm in Enugu aims primarily to educate rural off-grid shopkeepers on how solar power operates. This campaign is categorized as
qs.e: Informative advertising is heavily used when introducing a new product category to build primary demand and educate consumers.

qs.q: A radio station in Ibadan charges N150,000 for a 30-second advert spot during peak morning commute hours, reaching an estimated audience of 500,000 listeners. What is the Cost Per Thousand (CPM) for this radio advert?
qs.e: CPM = (Cost of Advert / Total Audience) x 1,000 = (N150,000 / 500,000) x 1,000 = N0.30 x 1,000 = N300.

qs.q: An established malt drink brand runs commercials during festive seasons simply displaying cold bottles with cheerful holiday music without mentioning product features. This form of advertising is
qs.e: Reminder advertising is important for mature products to keep consumers thinking about the product.

qs.q: A media buyer evaluates two radio stations in Lagos: Station A charges N400,000 per advert spot with 1,600,000 listeners; Station B charges N250,000 per spot with 800,000 listeners. Which station offers the lower CPM and by how much?
o: Station A is cheaper by N62.50
Station B is cheaper by N50.00
Station A is cheaper by N125.00
Both stations have the same CPM

qs.q: The statutory body in Nigeria responsible for regulating advertising practice, controlling advert contents, and conducting pre-exposure vetting of advertisements is the
qs.e: ARCON (Advertising Regulatory Council of Nigeria, formerly APCON) regulates advertising practice and advertisement vetting in Nigeria.

qs.q: In the personal selling process, a sales representative who researches a prospective corporate client's financial background and executive structure before making initial contact is engaged in
qs.e: Pre-approach is the step in which the salesperson learns as much as possible about a prospective customer before making a sales call.

qs.q: When a prospective buyer in Kano says 'Your solar inverter is too expensive,' and the salesperson replies 'While the initial cost is higher, it eliminates generator fuel costs and pays for itself within 12 months,' the salesperson is executing which selling step?
qs.e: Handling objections is the step in which the salesperson seeks out, clarifies, and overcomes customer objections to buying.

qs.q: A commercial sales representative in Lagos receives a monthly base salary of N100,000 plus a 5% commission on total sales exceeding N2,000,000. If the representative generates N4,500,000 in sales in a month, what is their total monthly earnings?
qs.e: Eligible sales for commission = N4,500,000 - N2,000,000 = N2,500,000. Commission = 5% of N2,500,000 = N125,000. Total earnings = N100,000 base + N125,000 commission = N200,000.

qs.q: A firm assigns its sales representatives exclusive geographical territories across Southwestern Nigeria, expecting each representative to sell the firm's entire product line to all customers in that territory. This organizational design is a
qs.e: A territorial sales force structure assigns each salesperson an exclusive geographic territory in which that salesperson sells the company's full line.

qs.q: An industrial machinery supplier in Port Harcourt estimates that it has 400 key accounts requiring 15 sales visits per year each. If a full-time sales representative can complete 300 client visits per year, how many sales representatives are needed under the workload method?
qs.e: Total annual calls required = 400 accounts x 15 visits = 6,000 calls. Sales force size = Total calls / Calls per rep = 6,000 / 300 = 20 representatives.

qs.q: A supermarket in Lekki, Lagos, attaches a free plastic mixing bowl to every 2kg bag of cake flour purchased. This sales promotion technique is classified as a
qs.e: A premium is a good offered either free or at low cost as an incentive to buy a product.

qs.q: An instant noodle company prints unique scratch codes inside promo wrappers, allowing buyers to text codes and win instant cash prizes or cars. This promotional scheme is a
qs.e: Contests and sweepstakes offer consumers the chance to win something such as cash, trips, or goods by luck or extra effort.

qs.q: A soft drink manufacturer offers retail shop owners in Onitsha 1 extra free carton for every 10 cartons purchased in cash during a holiday promotion. This trade incentive is known as
qs.e: Free goods are offers of extra cases of merchandise to intermediaries who buy certain quantities or who feature a certain flavor or size.

qs.q: An electronics brand pays retail sales assistants in computer stores N1,000 cash for every unit of its premium laptop sold during a quarter. In trade promotion, this cash incentive is called
qs.e: Push money (or a spiff) is cash or gifts given to dealers or their sales force to push the manufacturer's goods.

qs.q: A retail store sells 500 units of a beverage per month at N1,000 each (gross margin 30%). During a 1-month promotion, it slashes the price by 10% to N900, causing volume to increase to 800 units. If unit cost remains N700, did total gross profit increase or decrease and by how much?
qs.e: Pre-promo gross profit = 500 units x (N1,000 - N700) = 500 x N300 = N150,000. Promo gross profit = 800 units x (N900 - N700) = 800 x N200 = N160,000. Profit increased by N160,000 - N150,000 = N10,000.

qs.q: An oil processing company in Port Harcourt builds modern community health centers and sinks borehole wells in host villages to foster goodwill and peaceful operating relations. This activity represents
qs.e: Corporate social responsibility (CSR) and community relations build positive goodwill with external stakeholders and local communities.

qs.q: Following a rumor on social media regarding product contamination, a beverage firm holds an immediate press conference with regulatory officials and releases laboratory certificates proving safety. This action exemplifies
qs.e: Crisis management involves swift, transparent public relations handling to mitigate damage to brand reputation during negative events.

qs.q: A commercial bank sponsors the annual Lagos City Marathon, placing its logo on runner bibs, banners, and national TV broadcasts. This promotional investment is an example of
qs.e: Event sponsorship builds brand exposure and positive public relations by linking the company to popular sporting or cultural events.

qs.q: The primary strategic advantage of public relations and publicity over paid television advertising is its
qs.e: Publicity carries higher message credibility because news stories and features seem more authentic and believable to readers than paid ads.

qs.q: A bottled water company pledges to donate N5 from every 75cl bottle sold during the dry season to fund rural borehole drilling in arid northern communities. This strategy is known as
qs.e: Cause-related marketing directly links product sales to raising funds for a specific charitable or social cause.

qs.q: A cosmetic brand in Lagos formulates distinct product lines specifically for teenagers, working professional women, and elderly consumers based on age brackets. This market segmentation basis is
qs.e: Demographic segmentation divides the market into groups based on variables such as age, gender, family size, income, occupation, and education.

qs.q: An energy drink manufacturer targets long-distance commercial drivers, night-shift factory workers, and university students studying for exams based on product usage occasions and lifestyle. This segmentation is
qs.e: Psychographic segmentation divides buyers based on social class, lifestyle, or personality; behavioral segmentation divides based on occasions or usage.

qs.q: A boutique footwear producer in Aba focuses exclusively on custom hand-crafted leather boots for men with shoe sizes 46 and above. This target marketing strategy represents
qs.e: Concentrated (or niche) marketing targets a large share of one or a few smaller segments or niches.

qs.q: A salt refining company packages a single standard grade of iodized salt in identical 500g plastic bags sold nationwide without variation in price or marketing message. This approach is
qs.e: Undifferentiated (mass) marketing targets the whole market with one offer, ignoring segment differences.

qs.q: To be effective and actionable for a business, a market segment must fulfill five key criteria. When a segment is rejected because it contains too few consumers to generate sufficient profit, it fails which criterion?
qs.e: Substantiality requires that market segments are large or profitable enough to serve.

qs.q: What is the first step in the consumer buying decision process when a householder notices that their cooking gas cylinder is completely empty?
qs.e: The buying process starts with problem or need recognition, where the buyer senses a difference between their actual state and desired state.

qs.q: A consumer experiences psychological discomfort, anxiety, and second-guessing shortly after making an expensive purchase of a N450,000 solar generator. In consumer behavior, this state is called
qs.e: Cognitive dissonance is buyer discomfort caused by post-purchase conflict, where the buyer doubts whether they made the correct choice.

qs.q: When buying household table salt at a local neighborhood store, a shopper picks whichever brand is on the counter without comparing ingredients or price. This buying behavior is classified as
qs.e: Habitual buying behavior occurs under conditions of low consumer involvement and little significant brand difference.

qs.q: A teenager in Ibadan insists on purchasing a specific brand of basketball sneakers primarily because their favorite musical artist and school friends wear them. In consumer behavior, the musician and peer group act as a
qs.e: A reference group serves as a direct or indirect point of comparison or reference in forming a person's attitudes or behavior.

qs.q: According to Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs, purchasing a home security alarm system and emergency backup battery in a residential estate fulfills primarily which level of human needs?
qs.e: Safety needs encompass security, protection, stability, and freedom from fear or threat.

qs.q: Before embarking on expensive field surveys, a marketing research officer in Lagos collects population census figures, CBN economic bulletins, and published trade reports. These data sources are classified as
qs.e: Secondary data consists of information that already exists somewhere, having been collected for another purpose.

qs.q: A research team invites 8 mothers in Kano to a conference room to discuss their perceptions, preferences, and feeding habits regarding infant cereals under the guidance of a trained moderator. This research method is a
qs.e: A focus group interview involves personal interviewing of 6 to 10 people for a few hours with a trained moderator to talk about a product or service.

qs.q: A supermarket researcher in Ibadan counts the exact number of shoppers who stop by the dairy display case and records how many pick up a specific brand without speaking to the shoppers. This data collection technique is
qs.e: Observational research gathers primary data by observing relevant people, actions, and situations.

qs.q: A field researcher selects every 10th shopper entering a shopping mall in Enugu from a starting random point until 100 interviews are completed. This sampling method is known as
qs.e: Systematic sampling selects sample members from a target population according to a random starting point and a fixed, periodic interval.

qs.q: An e-commerce firm in Yaba tests two different landing page layouts (Version A with a red buy button, Version B with a green buy button) by randomly directing 5,000 visitors to each version and comparing purchase rates. This research methodology is an
qs.e: Experimental research gathers primary data by selecting matched groups of subjects, giving them different treatments, controlling factors, and checking differences in group responses.

qs.q: An empty seat on an early morning flight from Abuja to Lagos cannot be stored in inventory for resale on the evening flight if it goes unsold. This service characteristic is known as
qs.e: Perishability means that services cannot be stored for later sale or use.

qs.q: A patient cannot inspect, touch, or test a physician's medical consultation before paying for and receiving the clinical checkup. This service characteristic represents
qs.e: Intangibility means services cannot be seen, tasted, felt, heard, or smelled before they are bought.

qs.q: A barber cutting a client's hair in a salon in Kaduna performs the service while the client simultaneously consumes it. This characteristic is termed
qs.e: Inseparability means services are produced and consumed at the same time and cannot be separated from their providers.

qs.q: The quality of service delivered at a hotel front desk in Calabar varies depending on which receptionist is on duty and their energy level during the shift. This service characteristic is
qs.e: Variability (heterogeneity) means that the quality of services depends on who provides them, as well as when, where, and how they are provided.

qs.q: In the SERVQUAL framework for assessing service quality, when a customer rates a logistics firm highly because it delivers shipments accurately on the promised date without errors, which dimension is being demonstrated?
qs.e: Reliability refers to the ability to perform the promised service dependably and accurately.

qs.q: An online shoe store in Lagos spends N200,000 on social media ads, generating 10,000 ad clicks that result in 250 completed shoe purchases. What is the e-commerce conversion rate?
qs.e: Conversion rate = (Number of conversions / Total clicks) x 100 = (250 / 10,000) x 100 = 2.5%.

qs.q: A digital agency runs a search engine campaign for a real estate firm in Abuja, spending N600,000 in total. The campaign yields 30 qualified property buyer leads. What is the Cost Per Acquisition (CPA) per lead?
qs.e: Cost Per Acquisition = Total Ad Spend / Total Conversions = N600,000 / 30 = N20,000.

qs.q: Optimizing website text, mobile responsiveness, and page loading speed so a company ranks at the top of unpaid organic search engine results is called
qs.e: Search Engine Optimization (SEO) improves website traffic quality and volume from organic (unpaid) search results.

qs.q: An online clothing retailer pays a fashion influencer a 10% commission on every sale tracked through a unique promotional link shared on the influencer's social media profile. This digital marketing strategy is
qs.e: Affiliate marketing pays third-party publishers (affiliates) a commission to generate traffic or leads to the company's products.

qs.q: An online marketplace where individual consumers list and sell used personal items directly to other consumers, such as Jiji or eBay, operates under which e-commerce business model?
qs.e: Consumer-to-Consumer (C2C) e-commerce involves commercial transactions between private individuals.

qs.q: A newly introduced electric vehicle brand in Nigeria experiences high promotional expenses, negative net profits, and slow sales growth while educating early adopters. The brand is in which stage of the product lifecycle?
qs.e: The introduction stage is characterized by slow sales growth, high launch costs, and non-existent or negative profits.

qs.q: A fintech mobile payment solution experiences rapid market acceptance, surging sales revenues, rising profits, and the emergence of several new competitive copycat apps. This product is in the
qs.e: The growth stage features rapid market acceptance, escalating sales volume, increasing profits, and new competitors entering the market.

qs.q: The sachet water industry in Nigeria exhibits saturated consumer demand, intense price competition among hundreds of local producers, stable sales volume, and squeezed profit margins. This product category is in the
qs.e: The maturity stage is marked by slowdown in sales growth, saturation of market demand, fierce price competition, and industry consolidation.

qs.q: Demand for standalone DVD players in Nigeria drops drastically as consumers switch to internet streaming and flash drives. Manufacturers scale back ad budgets and harvest remaining sales. DVD players are in the
qs.e: The decline stage occurs when sales drop significantly due to technological shifts, consumer taste changes, or increased competition.

qs.q: To extend the lifecycle of a mature malt drink brand experiencing flat sales, the manufacturer formulates a low-sugar variant and launches an export campaign to neighboring ECOWAS countries. This strategy is known as
qs.e: Modifying the product (new features/variants) and modifying the market (new geographic segments) are classic techniques to extend the PLC during maturity.

qs.q: Demand for industrial corrugated packaging boxes in Aba surges sharply because consumer market demand for packaged biscuits and soaps increases. In industrial marketing, this phenomenon is called
qs.e: Derived demand is business demand that ultimately comes from (derives from) the demand for consumer goods.

qs.q: An administrative receptionist at a corporate head office in Lagos routinely screens phone calls and blocks sales representatives from scheduling meetings with the Chief Procurement Officer. In the organizational buying center, the receptionist acts as a
qs.e: Gatekeepers control the flow of information to others in the organizational buying center.

qs.q: A manufacturing plant manager in Ibadan reorders 100 reams of A4 printing paper from an existing supplier under pre-negotiated price and delivery terms without modifications. This organizational buying situation is a
qs.e: A straight rebuy is a business buying situation in which the buyer routinely reorders something without any modifications.

qs.q: A private university in Abuja decides to replace its desktop computer labs with laptops, inviting quotes from 4 vendors to revise specifications, pricing, and warranty terms. This purchase is a
qs.e: A modified rebuy occurs when a business buyer wants to modify product specifications, prices, terms, or suppliers.

qs.q: A commercial flour mill in Kano agrees to purchase all its grain transport trucks from an auto assembly plant in Kaduna, provided the assembly plant purchases all its staff canteen baked bread flour from the Kano mill. This B2B purchasing arrangement is
qs.e: Reciprocal buying involves two organizations agreeing to buy each other's products and services.

qs.q: A Nigerian fast-food company expands into Ghana by granting a local Accra entrepreneur the legal right to use its brand name, recipes, and operating systems in exchange for an upfront fee and ongoing royalties. This market entry mode is
qs.e: Franchising is a contractual association between a franchisor and an independent franchisee who buys the right to own and operate units in the franchise system.

qs.q: A footwear manufacturer in Aba partners with a distribution firm in Togo to build a shared warehouse and retail chain in Lome, sharing equity capital, operational control, and financial risks equally. This market entry mode is a
qs.e: A joint venture is a commercial enterprise undertaken jointly by two or more businesses which otherwise retain their distinct identities, sharing capital and risks.

qs.q: A global fast-food brand entering Nigeria adjusts its menu by replacing pork items with halal beef and introducing spicy jollof rice options to match local cultural preferences. This strategy is known as
qs.e: Product adaptation involves altering a product to meet local conditions, cultural preferences, or legal requirements in international markets.

qs.q: The regional trade agreement that enables goods originating within ECOWAS member states to move duty-free across West African borders without import tariffs is the
qs.e: The ECOWAS Trade Liberalization Scheme (ETLS) is the main regional trade instrument aimed at encouraging free movement of goods originating in West Africa.

qs.q: A Nigerian importer orders N40,000,000 worth of electrical appliances from a supplier in Europe invoiced in Euros. If the Naira depreciates by 15% against the Euro before payment is settled, how much additional Naira must the importer pay to clear the invoice?
qs.e: Additional Naira cost due to 15% currency depreciation = 15% of N40,000,000 = 0.15 x N40,000,000 = N6,000,000.

qs.q: A motor spare parts manufacturer in Nnewi invests heavily in expanding foundry production capacity to 50,000 units per month, assuming that producing at maximum volume and lowest cost will automatically guarantee sales. The manufacturer is demonstrating the
qs.e: The production concept holds that consumers favor products that are available and highly affordable, leading management to focus on production efficiency.

qs.q: A cosmetics company in Ikeja sells a luxury skin cream for N15,000 per jar. The total manufacturing and packaging cost is N6,000. If the customer perceives total tangible and intangible benefits worth N20,000, what is the customer perceived value (net value benefit)?
qs.e: Customer perceived value = Total perceived benefit - Total customer cost (price paid) = N20,000 - N15,000 = N5,000.

qs.q: A railway corporation in Enugu defines its business strictly as 'running train tracks and engines' rather than 'providing passenger and freight transportation solutions'. When bus fleets and airline shuttles capture its market share, the railway suffers from
qs.e: Marketing myopia is short-sighted inward management focus on products rather than on broader customer needs and solutions.

qs.q: An electricity distribution company (DisCo) in Abuja launches a public campaign urging consumers to turn off air conditioners and water heaters during peak evening hours to prevent power grid overload. This strategic effort to reduce demand temporarily is known as
qs.e: Demarketing aims to reduce demand temporarily or permanently, not to destroy demand but only to reduce or shift it.

qs.q: A state ministry of health in Kano runs aggressive radio adverts and billboard campaigns highlighting the organ damage caused by unprescribed cough syrup abuse to eradicate its consumption completely. This approach represents
qs.e: Counter-marketing seeks to destroy unwholesome or harmful demand completely (such as for dangerous drugs, tobacco, or alcohol).

qs.q: A soft drink bottling plant in Ibadan increases its 35cl bottle retail price from N150 to N200. As a result, weekly sales drop from 10,000 cases to 8,000 cases. What is the price elasticity of demand coefficient for the soft drink?
qs.e: Percentage change in price = (200 - 150) / 150 = +33.33%. Percentage change in quantity = (8,000 - 10,000) / 10,000 = -20.0%. Elasticity = -20% / 33.33% = -0.60.

qs.q: An e-commerce mobile application platform operating in Yaba redesigned its user checkout workflow, reducing payment button taps from 6 clicks to 2 clicks. In the customer-centric 4 Cs framework, this improvement enhances customer
qs.e: Convenience in the 4 Cs framework corresponds to Place in the 4 Ps, focusing on ease of acquiring and transacting.

qs.q: A high-end private medical clinic in Abuja installs marble flooring, soft acoustic lighting, plush leather recliners, and complimentary refreshments in its waiting lounge. In the 7 Ps services mix, these physical elements constitute
qs.e: Physical evidence includes the physical environment where the service is provided and tangible touchpoints that reinforce service quality perceptions.
