qs.q: A commercial air conditioning installer in Port Harcourt bundles a 2-year free servicing contract and free electrical cabling with every unit purchased for N400,000. How does this service addition modify the product offering in the marketing mix?
qs.e: Free servicing and installation accessories build around the basic product to create an augmented product offering superior value.

qs.q: A manufacturer of fruit juices sells 50,000 cartons monthly at N4,000 per carton. If variable production cost is N2,500 per carton and monthly fixed marketing expenses are N45,000,000, what is the net monthly operating profit?
qs.e: Total contribution margin = 50,000 cartons x (N4,000 - N2,500) = 50,000 x N1,500 = N75,000,000. Net profit = Total CM - Fixed Expenses = N75,000,000 - N45,000,000 = N30,000,000.

qs.q: A civil engineering contractor in Abuja purchases bulk cement bags, steel rebar rods, and gravel for bridge construction. In industrial product classification, these materials are
qs.e: Materials and parts are industrial goods that enter the manufacturer's product completely, including raw materials and fabricated parts.

qs.q: A furniture manufacturer in Benin City introduces a new modular office desk series with 6 color options and 4 drawer configurations under its existing executive desk line. This expansion increases the product line's
qs.e: Product line depth refers to the number of versions or variants offered of each product in the line.

qs.q: A pharmaceutical manufacturer in Onitsha reformulates its pediatric syrup by removing artificial colorings and adding a child-resistant safety cap. This action represents
qs.e: Product modification involves changing one or more characteristics of a product (quality, functional, or aesthetic features).

qs.q: An FMCG firm in Ogun State launches a low-priced sachet variant of its popular tin milk. Within six months, 40% of sachet milk buyers are existing buyers who stopped purchasing the higher-margin tin milk. This phenomenon is known as
qs.e: Product cannibalization occurs when a new product eats into the sales volume and market share of an existing product from the same company.

qs.q: A consumer buys a 55-inch smart television in Jos primarily to watch football matches in high definition. The basic core need fulfilled by this purchase is classified as the
qs.e: The core benefit is the fundamental service or need that the consumer is truly buying (e.g. entertainment/viewing experience).

qs.q: A multinational company markets Ariel detergent, Pampers diapers, and Always sanitary pads in Nigeria without prominently displaying its corporate parent name on the front packages. This branding strategy is
qs.e: Individual branding uses distinct brand names for each product in a company's portfolio, protecting the corporate reputation if one product fails.

qs.q: A commercial bank and an international airline collaborate to issue a joint credit card that earns frequent flyer miles whenever spent. This partnership is an example of
qs.e: Co-branding occurs when two established brand names of different companies are used on the same product.

qs.q: A major commercial bank in Nigeria changes its corporate logo, changes its branch interior colors, and adopts the tagline 'Empowering Your Future' to refresh its market image among young tech workers. This strategic action is
qs.e: Rebranding is the creation of a new name, term, symbol, design, or combination for an established brand to develop a new identity.

qs.q: A luxury leather shoe maker in Aba decides to put its brand name on low-cost plastic flip-flops sold for N500 at roadside stalls. Existing customers perceive the brand as less exclusive, resulting in
qs.e: Brand dilution occurs when a brand extension adversely affects consumer perceptions about the attributes or quality of the core brand.

qs.q: In a market survey conducted in Computer Village, Ikeja, 85 out of 100 shoppers correctly identify a mobile phone brand's logo without seeing the brand name. This percentage measures
qs.e: Brand recognition is the ability of consumers to confirm prior exposure to the brand when given the brand as a cue.

qs.q: A tamper-evident metallic foil seal placed across the mouth of a plastic medicine bottle in a pharmacy serves primarily which packaging function?
qs.e: Tamper-evident seals provide protection, preventing contamination and assuring consumers of safety and product integrity.

qs.q: A food processing firm prints nutritional facts, NAFDAC registration numbers, batch codes, and expiry dates on the back of its packaged oats. This fulfills which function of packaging?
qs.e: Labeling provides crucial consumer information regarding ingredients, usage, and legal compliance required by regulatory agencies like NAFDAC.

qs.q: A biscuit manufacturer designs an ornate metal tin container for its holiday cookies so that consumers will reuse the tin as a household storage box after eating the cookies. This packaging design is known as
qs.e: Dual-use (or reusable) packaging is designed to be repurposed by consumers for other household uses after the original contents are consumed.

qs.q: In a self-service supermarket in Port Harcourt, a brightly colored product package with bold typography acts as a 'silent salesman'. Which primary function of packaging does this illustrate?
qs.e: Packaging acts as a silent salesman on self-service supermarket shelves by attracting attention, describing the product, and making the sale.

qs.q: A cooking oil refiner in Kano replaces heavy glass bottles with lightweight PET plastic bottles, reducing package tare weight per case from 2.5kg to 0.5kg. If a delivery truck transports 1,000 cases, how many total kilograms of dead weight are saved during transport?
qs.e: Tare weight saved per case = 2.5kg - 0.5kg = 2.0kg. Total dead weight saved = 1,000 cases x 2.0kg = 2,000 kg.

qs.q: A boutique owner buys a handbag for N12,000 and wants to achieve a 20% profit margin on the selling price. What must be the selling price of the handbag?
qs.e: Selling price S = Cost / (1 - Margin %) = N12,000 / (1 - 0.20) = N12,000 / 0.80 = N15,000. Profit = N3,000 (which is 20% of N15,000).

qs.q: A tech firm introducing a revolutionary foldable smartphone sets an initial price of N1,200,000 to maximize short-term revenue from tech enthusiasts before lowering price over time. This pricing strategy is
qs.e: Market-skimming pricing sets a high initial price for a new product to skim maximum revenues layer by layer from segments willing to pay.

qs.q: A supermarket in Ibadan prices boxed chocolates at N4,999 instead of N5,000. This pricing tactic relies on which psychological principle?
qs.e: Odd pricing uses prices ending in odd numbers (like .99 or 9) to make the price seem significantly lower than it is.

qs.q: A printer manufacturer sells desktop laser printers at a break-even price of N35,000 but sets a high profit margin on replacement toner cartridges. This strategy is
qs.e: Captive product pricing sets a low price for the main product and a high markup on goods that must be used with the main product.

qs.q: A cinema in Ikeja charges N2,500 for adult evening tickets and N1,500 for student afternoon tickets for the exact same movie screening. This pricing practice is known as
qs.e: Segmented pricing (price discrimination) sells a product or service at two or more prices, where the difference in prices is not based on differences in costs.

qs.q: A fashion designer in Lagos sells bespoke dresses exclusively through an e-commerce website and social media messaging directly to individual buyers. This distribution network is a
qs.e: Direct distribution channels sell products directly from the producer to final consumers without independent intermediaries.

qs.q: A major wholesaler in Bodija Market, Ibadan, purchases 5,000 bags of rice from processing mills, stores them in central warehouses, and sells 10-bag bundles to small neighbourhood retailers. Which key channel function is the wholesaler performing?
qs.e: Wholesalers perform bulk breaking by purchasing large quantities and breaking them down into smaller lots for retailers.

qs.q: A corporate food company in Lagos bypasses independent regional wholesalers and begins selling directly to major supermarket chains. The elimination of wholesalers from the distribution chain is called
qs.e: Disintermediation is the cutting out of marketing channel intermediaries by product or service producers or the displacement of traditional resellers.

qs.q: A petroleum refining company transports refined PMS fuel from Port Harcourt to Kaduna via an underground pipeline rather than road tankers. The primary operational advantage of pipeline transport is
o: Fastest delivery speed for small lots
qs.e: Pipelines provide continuous, automated, high-volume physical transport for liquid petroleum products at very low variable costs per unit.

qs.q: A distributor in Onitsha holds N50,000,000 in average inventory. Annual inventory holding cost rate is 18%. By implementing a just-in-time (JIT) replenishment system, average inventory is reduced to N30,000,000. How much annual inventory holding cost is saved?
qs.e: Inventory reduction = N50,000,000 - N30,000,000 = N20,000,000. Annual holding cost savings = 18% of N20,000,000 = 0.18 x N20,000,000 = N3,600,000.

qs.q: A new solar home kit company runs heavy television ads and sponsors radio talk shows to build brand awareness among suburban homeowners in Ogun State. Which element of the promotional mix is primarily utilized?
qs.e: Advertising is any paid form of non-personal presentation and promotion of ideas, goods, or services by an identified sponsor.

qs.q: A telecommunications company sends targeted SMS text messages with personalized recharge discount offers directly to registered subscribers. This strategy is an example of
qs.e: Direct marketing involves engaging directly with carefully targeted individual consumers to obtain an immediate response and cultivate lasting relationships.

qs.q: When setting promotional budgets, a company that allocates marketing funds to match the estimated promotional expenditures of its main industry competitors is using the
qs.e: The competitive-parity method sets promotion budgets to match competitors' outlays.

qs.q: The most thorough and logically defensive method for establishing a marketing promotion budget, which defines specific campaign objectives, identifies required tasks, and estimates associated costs, is the
qs.e: The objective-and-task method develops promotion budgets by defining specific objectives, determining tasks required, and estimating costs.

qs.q: In communication theory applied to advertising, when a radio listener in Enugu misinterprets a promotional tagline due to localized language dialect differences, which element of the communication process has failed?
qs.e: Decoding is the process by which the receiver assigns meaning to the symbols encoded by the sender; misinterpretation represents a decoding error.

qs.q: An oil marketing company sponsors an educational television documentary on environmental conservation without promoting any specific fuel brand. This advert is categorized as
qs.e: Institutional (corporate) advertising promotes the corporate image, reputation, or social contributions rather than a specific product.

qs.q: A billboard advert for an insect repellent shows a mother smiling peacefully while her sleeping baby is protected under a net, appealing to maternal protective instincts. This advertisement uses an
qs.e: Emotional appeals attempt to stir up negative or positive emotions (such as love, safety, fear, or pride) to motivate purchase.

qs.q: A media planner schedules television commercials to run at steady, continuous levels every week throughout the year. This media scheduling pattern is known as
qs.e: Continuous scheduling runs advertising at an even, continuous schedule over a given period.

qs.q: An ad agency charges N1,200,000 to produce a 30-second video ad and N800,000 to air it on regional TV reaching 2,500,000 viewers. What is the total CPM including production and media costs?
In an advertising agency, the professional responsible for negotiating and purchasing billboard slots, television airtime, and radio ad schedules is the
qs.e: The media buyer negotiates and purchases advertising time and space across various media channels.

qs.q: A sales representative calling on a commercial bakery in Ibadan presents cost comparison charts showing how switching to their commercial baking oven saves N80,000 monthly in gas. This step in personal selling is the
qs.e: Presentation and demonstration is the personal selling step where the salesperson tells the 'value story' to the buyer, showing how the offer solves problems.

qs.q: After delivering a comprehensive presentation on industrial solar panels, a salesperson asks: 'Would you prefer installation to begin this Monday or next Thursday?' This sales technique is an example of an
qs.e: An assumptive close assumes the customer has already decided to buy and asks for secondary choices like delivery dates.

qs.q: Two weeks after installing a commercial generator at a hotel in Enugu, the sales representative visits the hotel engineer to verify performance and answer questions. This personal selling step is
qs.e: Follow-up is the last step in the selling process in which the salesperson follows up after the sale to ensure customer satisfaction and repeat business.

qs.q: A B2B sales team is organized such that dedicated sales representatives sell exclusively to agricultural clients, while another set sells exclusively to educational institutions. This structure is a
qs.e: A customer (or market) sales force structure organizes salespeople along customer or industry lines.

qs.q: A field salesperson receives a fixed salary of N150,000 plus a commission of 4% on all sales generated. If the salesperson achieves N6,000,000 in monthly sales, what percentage of their total earnings comes from commissions?
qs.e: Commission = 4% of N6,000,000 = N240,000. Total earnings = N150,000 + N240,000 = N390,000. Percentage from commission = (N240,000 / N390,000) x 100 = 61.54% ~ 61.5%.

qs.q: A manufacturer of dishwashing liquid places a N100 instant discount sticker on the front of its 1-liter bottle in supermarkets across Abuja. This promotional tactic is a
qs.e: Price-off deals (cents-off/naira-off) offer consumers savings off the regular price directly marked on the label or package.

qs.q: A coffee shop chain in Victoria Island issues loyalty stamp cards where customers receive a free coffee after buying 9 cups. This promotional mechanism is designed primarily to promote
qs.e: Frequency / loyalty programs reward customers who buy frequently or in large amounts to encourage repeat purchase behavior.

qs.q: A trade exhibition held annually at the Lagos International Trade Fair Complex allows B2B heavy machinery suppliers to demonstrate tractors to agricultural cooperative representatives. This event functions as a
qs.e: Trade shows and conventions are business promotional events where firms exhibit products to industry buyers and build B2B relationships.

qs.q: A beverage firm agrees to reimburse 50% of the cost of local newspaper advertisements placed by independent retail distributors featuring its fruit juice brand. This financial support is called
qs.e: Cooperative advertising allowances are trade incentives where a manufacturer pays a percentage of the retailer's local advertising costs.

qs.q: A consumer products firm spending N20,000,000 on a sales promotion generates N50,000,000 in incremental sales volume. If unit gross profit margin is 35%, what is the net return on investment (ROI) percentage of the sales promotion campaign?
A major corporate bank publishes a quarterly employee magazine and hosts monthly town hall meetings with staff to build internal culture and alignment. These activities fall under
qs.e: Internal PR focuses on building positive relationships, communication channels, and shared values among company employees.

qs.q: An association of local poultry farmers in Nigeria engages policy consultants to meet with federal legislators to advocate against reducing tariffs on imported frozen chicken. This activity is
qs.e: Lobbying involves dealing with legislators and government officials to promote or defeat regulation and legislation.

qs.q: A public relations officer prepares a written news announcement regarding the commissioning of a new factory line in Sagamu and emails it to national newspaper editors. This document is a
qs.e: A press (or news) release is a brief, written summary sent to media outlets to announce news events or developments.

qs.q: A tech corporation donates 500 refurbished laptops to public secondary schools in Kano State. Journalists cover the handover ceremony on national news. The resulting media coverage is classified as
qs.e: Earned media (publicity) is news coverage or editorial mention gained through promotional efforts rather than paid advertising.

qs.q: When evaluating the financial equivalent value of public relations coverage, PR managers calculate the cost of purchasing equivalent advertising space for news articles. This metric is known as
qs.e: Advertising Value Equivalency (AVE) measures the benefit to a client from media coverage by calculating what that coverage would cost as paid advertising.

qs.q: A clothing manufacturer produces heavy wool coats for customers in cold mountain regions like Jos and light cotton shirts for humid coastal cities like Lagos. This segmentation approach is
qs.e: Geographic segmentation divides the market into different geographical units such as nations, regions, states, cities, or climate zones.

qs.q: A toothpaste brand offers four versions: one for tooth whitening, one for sensitive gums, one for fresh breath, and one for decay protection. This market segmentation is based on
qs.e: Benefit segmentation divides buyers according to the different benefits that they seek from the product.

qs.q: An airline categorizes its passenger database into 'Frequent Flyers' (heavy users who generate 70% of revenue) and 'Occasional Holiday Travelers' (light users). This breakdown is an example of
qs.e: Usage rate segmentation classifies buyers into light, medium, and heavy product users.

qs.q: A commercial bank designs distinct financial packages: 'SME Commercial Current Account' for business owners, 'Campus Student Account' for undergraduates, and 'Private Wealth Account' for high-net-worth individuals. This target marketing strategy is
qs.e: Differentiated (segmented) marketing targets several market segments and designs separate offers for each.

qs.q: Plotting consumer perceptions of rival mobile phone brands on a two-dimensional grid representing 'Price' on one axis and 'Battery Performance' on the other axis creates a
qs.e: A perceptual (or positioning) map visually displays consumer perceptions of competing brands along key purchasing dimensions.

qs.q: A buyer evaluating three competing refrigerator brands in an appliance store in Aba weighs cooling speed, power consumption, and warranty duration before making a final choice. The buyer is in which decision stage?
qs.e: In the evaluation of alternatives stage, consumers evaluate different brand choices based on specific product criteria and attributes.

qs.q: A shopper in a supermarket notices that a candy bar's net weight was reduced from 50g to 48g without altering the package size, but fails to notice the change. In sensory psychology applied to marketing, the 2g difference was below the consumer's
qs.e: The Just Noticeable Difference (JND) or differential threshold is the minimal difference that can be detected between two similar stimuli.

qs.q: When a consumer hears a television advert for a product they dislike, they unconsciously re-interpret the spokesperson's words to fit their pre-existing negative bias. This perceptual process is called
qs.e: Selective distortion describes the tendency of people to interpret information in a way that supports what they already believe.

qs.q: A household buying decision for a new family car involves the teenage daughter suggesting an SUV model, the father reviewing financing options, and the mother making the final brand decision. In buying roles, the mother is the
qs.e: The decider is the person who ultimately makes the buying decision or any part of it (whether to buy, what to buy, how to buy, or where to buy).

qs.q: A consumer switches from buying Brand A biscuits to Brand B biscuits not because Brand A was bad, but simply out of curiosity to try a new taste. This purchase behavior is
qs.e: Variety-seeking buying behavior occurs in situations characterized by low consumer involvement but significant perceived brand differences, leading to frequent brand switching for novelty.

qs.q: A market research agency in Lagos collects field survey data specifically to answer a client's question regarding customer satisfaction with a new telco data plan. This freshly gathered data is classified as
qs.e: Primary data consists of information collected for the specific purpose at hand.

qs.q: Dividing a city's population into distinct income subgroups (Low, Middle, High income) and randomly selecting 50 households from each subgroup ensures balanced representation. This sampling technique is
qs.e: Stratified random sampling divides the population into mutually exclusive groups (strata) and draws random samples from each stratum.

qs.q: A questionnaire item that asks: 'Do you agree that our product is cheap and reliable?' violates proper survey design principles because it is a
qs.e: A double-barreled question asks about two different issues in a single statement, confusing respondents and distorting results.

qs.q: A research student interviews 30 shoppers waiting at a bus stop simply because they are easy to reach and willing to answer questions quickly. This non-probability sampling method is
qs.e: Convenience sampling selects population members from whom it is easiest to obtain information.

qs.q: Testing a draft questionnaire on 25 respondents before deploying it to 2,000 respondents nationwide to detect confusing questions and timing issues is called
qs.e: Pre-testing (or pilot testing) involves administering a survey instrument to a small sub-sample to refine question wording and design.

qs.q: A fast-food restaurant in Abuja serves a customer cold fried chicken. When the customer complains, the manager replaces the meal immediately with a hot portion and provides a free drink coupon. This process of resolving service failure is
qs.e: Service recovery refers to the actions taken by a service provider in response to a service failure to restore customer satisfaction.

qs.q: A customer rates a commercial bank high on the SERVQUAL dimension of 'Empathy' when branch staff display
o: Caring, individualized attention to the customer's specific problems
qs.e: Empathy in SERVQUAL represents caring, individualized attention provided to customers.

qs.q: Mapping out step-by-step customer actions, visible front-stage employee interactions, and invisible back-stage support activities for a hotel check-in process creates a
qs.e: A service blueprint is a operational tool that visualizes the service delivery process across front-stage and back-stage touchpoints.

qs.q: A cinema management in Port Harcourt reduces ticket prices by 50% for Tuesday afternoon shows to fill empty seats during low-demand hours. This capacity management technique manages service
qs.e: Differential pricing during off-peak hours shifts consumer demand to match fixed capacity, overcoming service perishability.

qs.q: Commercial banks installing Automated Teller Machines (ATMs) and mobile banking applications to enable self-service cash withdrawals represent the deployment of
qs.e: Self-service technologies (SSTs) allow customers to produce a service independent of direct involvement by service firm employees.

qs.q: A commercial blog charges advertisers N50 per click whenever a reader clicks on an advert banner embedded in its blog articles. This digital pricing model is known as
o: Cost Per Click (CPC) / Pay Per Click (PPC)
qs.e: Cost Per Click (CPC) is an online advertising pricing model where the advertiser pays the publisher only when the ad is clicked.

qs.q: An online retail store tracks that 40 out of 100 website visitors leave the website immediately after viewing only the homepage without clicking any links. The homepage has a
qs.e: Bounce rate represents the percentage of visitors who enter the site and then leave ('bounce') rather than continuing to view other pages.

qs.q: A fashion brand sends customized email promotions containing discount coupon codes to users who added items to their digital shopping cart but closed the browser before paying. This technique is
qs.e: Cart abandonment retargeting reaches out to prospective buyers who left items in an online cart to encourage them to complete the purchase.

qs.q: A wholesale spare parts dealer in Lagos creates a private online portal allowing registered motor mechanics across Nigeria to check stock levels, view trade prices, and place bulk orders. This operates under which business model?
qs.e: Business-to-Business (B2B) e-commerce involves digital commercial transactions between companies.

qs.q: An online business spends N500,000 on digital ads, attracting 20,000 clicks. From those clicks, 400 purchases are completed. What is the Cost Per Click (CPC) and the Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC)?
qs.e: CPC = Total Spend / Total Clicks = N500,000 / 20,000 = N25. CAC = Total Spend / Total Purchases = N500,000 / 400 = N1,250.

qs.q: During which stage of the product lifecycle are industry profits at their peak level, attracting numerous competitor entry into the market?
qs.e: Profits peak in the late growth / early maturity stage as volume expanded rapidly while unit production costs declined due to economies of scale.

qs.q: A firm marketing a mature product in Nigeria decides to cut all promotional expenditures to minimum maintenance levels to maximize short-term cash flow while sales gradually drop. This strategy is
qs.e: Harvesting involves reducing costs (R&D, ad spend, maintenance) to increase short-term cash flows despite declining sales.

qs.q: Early adopters of a newly launched high-tech agricultural drone in Nigeria are characterized as being
o: Opinion leaders who adopt new ideas early but carefully
Skeptical consumers who adopt only after majority adoption
qs.e: Early adopters are opinion leaders who embrace new technologies early and guide mainstream buyer perceptions.

qs.q: A fashion item experiences an immediate, sudden spike in sales volume due to viral social media trend status, followed by an equally rapid collapse in sales within three months. The lifecycle curve of this item is a
qs.e: A fad is a temporary period of unusually high sales driven by consumer enthusiasm and immediate product or brand popularity.

qs.q: When a pharmaceutical company finds that its mature anti-malarial drug can also be marketed as a preventative treatment for travelers, it extends the product lifecycle through
o: Finding new product uses / Market modification
qs.e: Finding new product uses or new user segments expands the target market and extends the product lifecycle.

qs.q: In an industrial purchasing department, the senior engineering specialist who reviews technical blueprints and sets chemical purity standards for raw materials acts as an
qs.e: Influencers affect the buying decision by helping define specifications and providing technical information for evaluating alternatives.

qs.q: A manufacturing company buying a complex multi-million Naira automated bottling plant for the first time faces high risk and extensive technical evaluation. This organizational purchase situation is a
qs.e: A new task buy is a business buying situation in which the buyer purchases a product or service for the first time.

qs.q: Assigning dedicated senior key account managers to maintain direct personal relationships with a commercial bank's top 20 corporate accounts is an example of
qs.e: Key Account Management (KAM) focuses resources on building long-term strategic relationships with the company's most important business accounts.

qs.q: A software company maintains a central Customer Relationship Management (CRM) database recording purchase history, complaint logs, and renewal dates for all enterprise clients. The primary objective of CRM is to
o: Maximize customer retention and lifetime customer value
qs.e: Customer Relationship Management (CRM) manages detailed information about individual customers to maximize customer loyalty and lifetime value.

qs.q: Organized business buyers tend to differ from final individual consumers because organizational buyers typically feature
o: Fewer but much larger buyers with professional purchasing procedures
More numerous small buyers who buy impulsively
Geographically scattered buyers making small purchases
qs.e: Business markets usually contain far fewer but much larger buyers who follow formal procurement processes.

qs.q: A firm in Ibadan sells surplus agricultural machinery to a trading export merchant in Lagos, who then resells the machinery to buyers in Benin Republic without the Ibadan firm dealing directly with foreign buyers. This mode is
qs.e: Indirect exporting involves selling to domestic intermediaries who then export the product overseas.

qs.q: A multinational firm builds a wholly owned manufacturing factory in Ogun State, Nigeria, retaining 100% equity ownership and operational control. This international entry strategy is
qs.e: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) involves direct ownership of foreign-based manufacturing or assembly facilities.

qs.q: A country imposes a maximum statutory limit of 10,000 metric tons on the total quantity of foreign cement that can be imported into its territory per year. This trade barrier is an import
qs.e: An import quota is a limit placed on the amount of a product that can be imported into a country.

qs.q: A mobile phone manufacturer sells the exact same phone model with identical packaging and advertising worldwide without any regional alterations. This strategy is international product
qs.e: Product standardization markets the same product using the same marketing strategy worldwide.

qs.q: A shoes manufacturer in Aba exports leather boots to Ghana with a C.I.F. value of N20,000 per pair. If Ghana imposes a 20% import tariff duty, what is the landed cost per pair before local dealer margins?
qs.e: Landed cost = C.I.F value + Tariff duty = N20,000 + (20% of N20,000) = N20,000 + N4,000 = N24,000.

qs.q: A financial technology startup in Lagos develops a micro-investment mobile application based on extensive survey data showing young professionals want automated spare-change savings. By aligning product design directly with expressed user needs, the startup demonstrates the
qs.e: The marketing concept focuses on identifying customer needs first and designing products to satisfy those needs efficiently.

qs.q: A cement manufacturer in Ibese updates its kiln technology to reduce carbon emissions by 40% while donating solar streetlights to surrounding villages. Balancing company profitability, customer satisfaction, and long-term environmental protection embodies the
qs.e: The societal marketing concept balances company profits, consumer wants, and long-term public welfare.

qs.q: A fast-moving consumer goods company in Agbara restructures its distribution by replacing large central warehouses with regional fulfillment centers, reducing delivery transit time to retailers from 4 days to 24 hours. In the 4 Cs framework, this improves
qs.e: Convenience in the 4 Cs framework represents place and distribution efficiency, making products easily accessible to buyers.

qs.q: A private hospital in Abuja upgrades its reception ambiance, installs digital patient queue monitors, and provides branded comfort kits to admitted patients. In service marketing, these tangible elements represent
qs.e: Physical evidence includes tangible facilities, equipment, and visual elements that communicate service quality.

qs.q: A beverage producer in Benin City sells bottled natural spring water. To expand its portfolio, it introduces sparkling flavored water in 330ml aluminum cans. This new offering within the beverage category is a
qs.e: Line extension involves introducing new variants (flavors, packaging, sizes) within an existing product line.

qs.q: An industrial manufacturing plant in Kano purchases heavy hydraulic press machinery valued at N85,000,000 for its metal stamping operations. In industrial product classification, this machinery is a
qs.e: Capital items include major installations and machinery that aid in long-term manufacturing operations.

qs.q: A supermarket chain in Ibadan packages cassava flour under its own retail store brand, selling it at a lower price than national packaged flour brands. This product is a
qs.e: Private label (store) brands are owned and sold exclusively by a retailer or wholesaler.

qs.q: A famous biscuit brand in Nigeria uses its established brand name to launch a new line of breakfast cornflakes. This branding move is an example of
qs.e: Brand extension applies an existing brand name to enter a completely new product category.

qs.q: A milk powder manufacturer packages powdered milk into single-serve 12g sachets priced at N50, making high-quality milk accessible to low-income households daily. This packaging innovation utilizes
qs.e: Sachetization breaks bulk products into affordable micro-units tailored to daily consumer cash flows.

qs.q: A cosmetics manufacturer in Ogun State uses corrugated fiberboard master boxes to pack 48 individual shampoo bottles for truck transport to regional distributors. These master boxes represent
qs.e: Secondary packaging groups primary packages together for storage, retail handling, and shelf display.

qs.q: A trader in Alaba International Market, Lagos, purchases home theater systems for N40,000 each and applies a 30% markup on cost. What is the retail selling price?
qs.e: Selling price = Cost + (Cost x Markup %) = N40,000 + (N40,000 x 0.30) = N40,000 + N12,000 = N52,000.

qs.q: A retailer sells an electronic gadget for N25,000, achieving a profit of N5,000. What is the profit margin percentage on selling price, and what is the equivalent markup percentage on cost?
qs.e: Margin = Profit / Selling Price = N5,000 / N25,000 = 20%. Cost = N20,000. Markup = Profit / Cost = N5,000 / N20,000 = 25%.

qs.q: A manufacturing firm in Kaduna has fixed costs of N3,000,000 annually. It sells product X for N5,000 per unit with variable production costs of N2,000 per unit. What is the break-even sales volume in units and in Naira revenue?
qs.e: Contribution margin = N5,000 - N2,000 = N3,000. BEP units = N3,000,000 / N3,000 = 1,000 units. BEP revenue = 1,000 x N5,000 = N5,000,000.

qs.q: A publisher sells textbooks with a list price of N10,000, subject to a trade discount of 25% to booksellers and a 4% cash discount for payment within 14 days. If a bookseller pays within 14 days, what is the net price per book?
qs.e: Price after trade discount = N10,000 x 0.75 = N7,500. Cash discount = 4% of N7,500 = N300. Net price = N7,500 - N300 = N7,200.

qs.q: A solar energy firm in Enugu incurs fixed costs of N4,000,000 annually. Its solar home kit sells for N200,000 with variable costs of N120,000 per unit. To earn a target annual net profit of N2,000,000, how many units must be sold?
qs.e: CM per unit = N200,000 - N120,000 = N80,000. Required units = (Fixed Costs + Target Profit) / CM = (N4,000,000 + N2,000,000) / N80,000 = N6,000,000 / N80,000 = 75 units.

qs.q: A soft drink bottling company in Port Harcourt distributes through exclusive regional master distributors, who sell to sub-wholesalers, who then supply local retail kiosks. How many levels of intermediaries are in this distribution channel?
qs.e: The channel includes Master Distributor -> Sub-wholesaler -> Retail Kiosk, which equals three levels of intermediaries.

qs.q: A manufacturer of high-end luxury wristwatches appoints only two exclusive retail outlets in Lagos State to represent the brand. This distribution strategy is
qs.e: Exclusive distribution limits distribution to very few dealers with exclusive rights in specific territories.

qs.q: A conflict occurring between two authorized regional distributors of the same beer brand over selling into each other's allocated territories is categorized as
qs.e: Horizontal channel conflict occurs among firms at the same level of the channel (e.g. distributor vs distributor).

qs.q: A pharmaceutical manufacturer offers trade discounts and promotional displays to community pharmacy owners to encourage them to stock and recommend its new multivitamin brand. This strategy is a
qs.e: A push strategy directs marketing efforts at channel members to induce them to carry and push the product to end users.

qs.q: A company running a nationwide promotion spend allocation sets its budget by allocating 6% of its forecasted sales revenue of N1,500,000,000. What is the total promotional budget?
A radio advert broadcast in Kano costs N180,000 per 30-second slot and reaches an estimated audience of 600,000 listeners. What is the Cost Per Thousand (CPM) of this radio ad?
qs.e: CPM = (Ad Cost / Total Audience) x 1,000 = (N180,000 / 600,000) x 1,000 = N300.

qs.q: An established detergent brand runs short TV commercials showing clean white shirts with its catchy jingle without detailed product explanations. This represents
qs.e: Reminder advertising keeps the product top-of-mind for mature brands.

qs.q: A sales representative in Lagos earns a base salary of N120,000 plus a 6% commission on sales exceeding a monthly threshold of N3,000,000. If total monthly sales are N5,500,000, what is the total earnings?
qs.e: Commissionable sales = N5,500,000 - N3,000,000 = N2,500,000. Commission = 6% of N2,500,000 = N150,000. Total earnings = N120,000 + N150,000 = N270,000.

qs.q: A salesperson handling prospective industrial clients in Enugu researches company executive backgrounds and past equipment purchases prior to initiating contact. This stage in selling is
qs.e: Pre-approach involves conducting background research on prospective buyers before meeting them.

qs.q: A fast-food chain in Abuja attaches a scratch card to every meal deal, giving customers a chance to instantly win free drinks or cinema tickets. This promotional technique is a
qs.e: Contests and sweepstakes give consumers a chance to win prizes based on chance or skill.

qs.q: A detergent maker offers retail shopkeepers in Onitsha 2 extra free cartons for every 20 cartons purchased in a single order. This trade promotion is known as
qs.e: Free goods allowances provide extra product units at no charge to trade buyers meeting specific volume targets.

qs.q: An oil company operating in the Niger Delta builds schools, equips computer laboratories, and provides university scholarships for youths in its host communities. This program exemplifies
qs.e: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) builds long-term community goodwill and positive public relations.

qs.q: Following media reports about a minor batch defect, a food processing company voluntarily recalls the affected batch, issues a press statement, and opens a 24-hour helpline. This swift response is
qs.e: Crisis communications management handles emergency situations transparently to safeguard brand trust.

qs.q: A financial institution divides its consumer market into 'Recent University Graduates', 'Middle-Aged Executives', and 'Retirees' to offer customized pension and investment plans. This segmentation basis is
qs.e: Demographic lifecycle segmentation divides markets based on age cohorts and life stages.

qs.q: An athletic shoe brand designs distinct shoes for marathon runners, basketball players, and casual weekend walkers based on activity lifestyle. This market division relies on
qs.e: Psychographic (lifestyle) and behavioral (product usage) criteria segment consumers according to activities and specific benefit needs.

qs.q: A consumer experiences intense regret after purchasing a luxury car, questioning whether they spent too much money. This psychological state is known as
qs.e: Cognitive dissonance is post-purchase anxiety or doubt regarding a major buying decision.

qs.q: When purchasing cooking salt at a local store, a buyer picks the first package available without comparing brands or prices. This decision process exemplifies
qs.e: Habitual buying behavior involves low involvement and minimal brand differentiation.

qs.q: A market research team in Lagos gathers existing company sales reports, central bank economic bulletins, and published industry whitepapers prior to conducting field interviews. This data is classified as
qs.e: Secondary data is pre-existing data gathered previously for another purpose.

qs.q: A research group conducts structured discussions with 8 selected mothers in Kano led by a moderator to explore opinions on a new infant food formulation. This research method is a
qs.e: Focus group interviews gather qualitative insights from small groups guided by a moderator.

qs.q: An unsold seat on a commercial flight from Abuja to Lagos cannot be saved in inventory for sale on the following day's flight. This illustrates service
qs.e: Perishability means services cannot be stored for future sale.

qs.q: A patient receiving a medical consultation cannot physically touch or inspect the doctor's diagnosis prior to the service encounter. This characteristic is service
qs.e: Intangibility means services cannot be perceived by physical senses before purchase.

qs.q: An e-commerce business in Yaba spends N300,000 on digital ad banners, generating 15,000 ad clicks that result in 300 completed sales orders. What is the conversion rate and the Cost Per Click (CPC)?
Optimizing website code, keyword structure, and loading speed so a company ranks naturally at the top of Google organic search results is called
qs.e: Search Engine Optimization (SEO) improves organic, unpaid search engine visibility.

qs.q: A newly launched solar air-conditioner brand in Nigeria experiences high initial promotional costs, negative net operating profits, and slow initial sales growth. The product is in the
qs.e: The introduction stage features high launch expenditures, low initial sales volume, and negative profits.

qs.q: A digital streaming platform experiences rapid customer adoption, expanding sales revenues, rising operating profits, and entry of new market competitors. The product is in the
qs.e: The growth stage exhibits rapid sales expansion, profit growth, and competitive entry.

qs.q: Demand for industrial cocoa processing machinery in Ondo depends directly on consumer demand for packaged chocolate and cocoa beverages. In business marketing, this is
qs.e: Derived demand in B2B markets originates from ultimate consumer demand for end products.

qs.q: An administrative executive in a corporate purchasing department screens sales phone calls and prevents vendors from directly contacting the Procurement Manager. In buying center roles, the executive acts as a
qs.e: Gatekeepers control access to decision makers and manage the flow of information in a buying center.

qs.q: A Nigerian restaurant brand expands into Kenya by licensing a local operator in Nairobi to use its trade name, brand identity, and proprietary recipes in return for royalties. This entry mode is
qs.e: Franchising grants an independent operator the right to run a business under the franchisor's brand and system.

qs.q: A shoe manufacturer in Aba partners with a Ghanaian distribution company to co-establish a footwear factory in Accra, sharing equity investment and risks. This market entry mode is a
qs.e: A joint venture is a partnership where two firms create a jointly owned commercial entity, sharing equity and management.

qs.q: A global beverage corporation modifies its product line in West Africa by introducing a local hibiscus (zobo) flavor variant while maintaining its global brand umbrella. This strategy represents
qs.e: Glocalization (product adaptation) adapts global product strategies to local cultural preferences and market conditions.

qs.q: A manufacturer exports industrial water pumps to Cote d'Ivoire at a C.I.F. price of N50,000 per unit. If Cote d'Ivoire levies a 15% import tariff duty, what is the duty-inclusive landed cost per pump?
qs.e: Landed cost = C.I.F price + Tariff duty = N50,000 + (15% of N50,000) = N50,000 + N7,500 = N57,500.

qs.q: An industrial paper processing mill in Lagos faces fixed costs of N5,000,000 annually. Variable costs per ton of paper are N150,000 and selling price is N250,000 per ton. How many tons must be sold to break even?
qs.e: Contribution margin per ton = N250,000 - N150,000 = N100,000. BEP in tons = Fixed Costs / CM = N5,000,000 / N100,000 = 50 tons.

qs.q: A digital ad campaign spent N400,000 to generate 10,000 visits and 200 online purchases. Calculate the Cost Per Acquisition (CAC) and the website conversion rate.
qs.e: CAC = Total Spend / Purchases = N400,000 / 200 = N2,000. Conversion Rate = (200 / 10,000) x 100 = 2.0%.

qs.q: A manufacturing plant has annual fixed expenses of N6,000,000, variable costs of N12,000 per unit, and sells its product for N20,000 per unit. If annual sales volume is 1,200 units, what is the net margin percentage on total revenue?
qs.e: Total Revenue = 1,200 x N20,000 = N24,000,000. Total Variable Cost = 1,200 x N12,000 = N14,400,000. Contribution Margin = N9,600,000. Net Profit = CM - Fixed Expenses = N9,600,000 - N6,000,000 = N3,600,000. Net Margin = (N3,600,000 / N24,000,000) x 100 = 15.0%.

qs.q: A retail supermarket in Port Harcourt buys canned soup for N600 per can and sets a selling price of N800. What is the markup percentage on cost and the margin percentage on selling price?
qs.e: Profit = N800 - N600 = N200. Markup on cost = N200 / N600 = 33.33%. Margin on selling price = N200 / N800 = 25.0%.

qs.q: A bread baker in Ibadan shifts focus from merely maximizing daily oven output to producing low-sugar, whole-grain loaves after observing increased health awareness among middle-aged civil servants. Which marketing philosophy is the baker demonstrating?
qs.e: The marketing concept focuses on determining the needs and wants of target markets and delivering satisfaction more effectively than competitors. Here, the baker adapted production based on customer health preferences rather than pushing existing factory output.

qs.q: An entrepreneur operating a palm oil processing mill in Enugu invests in effluent treatment facilities to prevent local stream pollution, arguing that business profitability should not compromise community environmental health. This management orientation represents the
qs.e: The societal marketing concept holds that a company should make marketing decisions by considering consumers' wants, the company's requirements, and society's long-term interests (such as environmental preservation and public health).

qs.q: A consumer purchases a solar home system for N250,000 because it eliminates monthly generator fuel expenses of N45,000 and provides silent night electricity. The difference between the total benefits perceived by the buyer and the total costs incurred is known as customer
qs.e: Customer perceived value is the customer's evaluation of the difference between all the benefits and all the costs of a marketing offer relative to competing alternatives.

qs.q: A shoe manufacturer in Aba focuses exclusively on building highly automated machinery to churn out 10,000 pairs of basic sandals daily at the lowest unit cost, assuming consumers will buy anything cheap and widely available. This approach exemplifies the
qs.e: The production concept assumes that consumers will favor products that are widely available and highly affordable, leading management to concentrate on high production efficiency and mass distribution.

qs.q: For a pure transaction to take place in a free market exchange between a tomato farmer and a processor in Kano, which of the following condition sets MUST be present?
o: A written legal contract witnessed by a government agent
An equal financial net worth between both trading entities
A minimum credit line granted by a commercial bank
At least two parties, each with something of value, able to communicate and deliver, and free to accept or reject
qs.e: For an exchange to occur, five basic conditions must be met: (1) at least two parties, (2) each party has something of value to the other, (3) each party can communicate and deliver, (4) each party is free to accept or reject the offer, and (5) each party believes it is desirable to deal with the other.

qs.q: A boutique hotel in Abuja introduces free airport shuttle services, complimentary high-speed Wi-Fi, and a customized greeting by front desk personnel to enhance its core accommodation offering. In the extended marketing mix for services, these enhancements represent
qs.e: The hotel enhances the augmented product (shuttle service, Wi-Fi) and physical evidence/people aspects to create service value. In service marketing mix terms, complimentary services form part of the augmented product, while front desk greetings involve people and physical evidence.

qs.q: When a fast-moving consumer goods company adjusts its sachet detergent pack size, lowers prices by N50, expands sales into rural village kiosks, and runs radio ads in local languages, it is manipulating the
qs.e: The marketing mix consists of the controllable tactical tools—Product (pack size), Price (N50 drop), Place (rural kiosks), and Promotion (local radio ads)—that the firm blends to produce the desired response in the target market.

qs.q: In transitioning from traditional marketing mix (4 Ps) to customer-centric framework (4 Cs), 'Place' corresponds directly to
qs.e: In Lauterborn's 4 Cs framework, Product becomes Customer solution, Price becomes Cost, Place becomes Convenience, and Promotion becomes Communication.

qs.q: A soft drink bottling firm in Lagos experiences sudden sales drops due to new government sugar tax regulations and rising inflation. These external non-controllable factors belong to the firm's
qs.e: Government tax policy (PESTLE political/legal factor) and inflation (economic factor) are broad macro-environmental forces beyond the direct control of an individual company.

qs.q: A Fintech startup designs an instant loan app. To ensure seamless adoption, it ensures 2-minute loan processing (Process), clean user interface (Physical evidence), and prompt customer support agents (People). These elements represent the additional 3 Ps applicable to
qs.e: The extended 7 Ps framework adds People, Process, and Physical Evidence to the traditional 4 Ps specifically to address the unique characteristics of services marketing.

qs.q: When a consumer purchases an expensive smartphone primarily for social prestige and executive status rather than basic communication, which product level is fulfilling that psychological desire?
qs.e: The core benefit is the fundamental service or benefit the customer is really buying—in this case, status and prestige. The physical phone hardware forms the actual product.

qs.q: A cosmetics firm in Onitsha sells facial cleansers, body lotions, anti-aging serums, and hair shampoos. The total number of distinct product lines offered by this firm represents its product mix
qs.e: Product mix width (or breadth) refers to the number of different product lines the company carries. Depth refers to the number of versions offered of each product in the line.

qs.q: A motor spare parts trader carries 8 different brands and sizes of brake pads under his automotive braking product line. This number of items within a single line indicates the line's
qs.e: Product line depth refers to the number of total items or variants offered within a specific product line.

qs.q: Products like life insurance policies, pre-planned funeral services, and emergency fire extinguishers, which consumers typically do not think of buying until a pressing need arises, are classified as
qs.e: Unsought goods are consumer products that the consumer either does not know about or knows about but does not normally consider buying under normal circumstances.

qs.q: A computer buyer spends 3 weeks comparing prices, technical specifications, warranty terms, and battery life across HP, Dell, and Lenovo laptops before making a purchase. In consumer product classification, laptops are
qs.e: Shopping goods are less frequently purchased consumer products and services that customers compare carefully on suitability, quality, price, and style before buying.

qs.q: A famous dairy brand in Nigeria uses its established corporate brand name 'Peak' to launch a new product line of instant chocolate powder mix called 'Peak Chocolate'. This strategy is known as
qs.e: Brand extension involves using an established brand name on new or modified products in a new product category.

qs.q: Supermarket chain Shoprite contracts a local flour mill to package cassava flour under Shoprite's own store label 'Ritebrand' rather than the mill's name. This is an example of a
qs.e: A private label brand (or store brand) is a brand created and owned by a reseller (wholesaler or retailer) of a product or service.

qs.q: When two well-known brands like Nike and Apple join forces to create the 'Nike+Apple' fitness tracking ecosystem, combining both brand names on one product, they are utilizing
qs.e: Co-branding is the practice of using the established brand names of two different companies on the same product.

qs.q: The commercial value that a company derives from consumer perception of the brand name of a particular product or service, rather than from the product or service itself, is defined as brand
qs.e: Brand equity is the differential effect that knowing the brand name has on customer response to the product or its marketing.

qs.q: A consumer who enters a pharmacy requesting specifically for 'Panadol' and refuses to buy any generic paracetamol substitute even when Panadol is temporarily out of stock has reached the brand loyalty stage of brand
qs.e: Brand insistence is the ultimate stage of brand loyalty where consumers refuse to accept alternatives and will search until they find that specific brand.

qs.q: A toothpaste tube containing the paste itself is placed inside a printed cardboard box, which is then packed into a corrugated master carton containing 48 boxes for transport. In packaging hierarchy, the printed cardboard box represents
qs.e: Primary packaging directly holds the product (the tube). Secondary packaging protects/holds the primary package (the printed box). Tertiary/transit packaging holds multiple secondary units for shipping (the master corrugated carton).

qs.q: In Nigeria, NAFDAC regulatory requirements compel food manufacturers to display manufacturing dates, expiry dates, batch numbers, and NAFDAC registration numbers on product labels. This function of packaging and labelling is primarily
qs.e: Displaying mandatory dates, ingredients, and regulatory numbers fulfills legal and customer safety requirements imposed by regulatory agencies like NAFDAC.

qs.q: A seasoning powder manufacturer redesigns its packaging into reusable plastic storage jars instead of disposable foil sachets to give consumers post-purchase utility. This strategy is called
qs.e: Reusable (or dual-use) packaging provides consumers with a container that serves another purpose after the original product is consumed, creating added value.

qs.q: A pharmaceutical firm wraps glass syrup bottles in thick expanded polystyrene casing before packing them into wooden crates for long-distance haulage across bumpy roads. The primary function of this packaging layer is
qs.e: The primary role of transit/protective packaging is to safeguard contents against physical damage, breakage, and environmental degradation during transportation and handling.

qs.q: Which of the following packaging decisions directly supports environmental sustainability by reducing plastic waste in urban drainage systems?
o: Switching from single-use plastics to biodegradable cassava-starch film
Adding glossy metallic lamination on paper boxes
qs.e: Switching to biodegradable packaging materials reduces plastic pollution and aligns with green marketing and environmental sustainability goals.

qs.q: A leather bag artisan in Kaduna incurs a total unit cost of N8,000 to make a luxury briefcase. If she desires a 25% markup on cost, what will be the selling price of the briefcase?
qs.e: Selling Price = Unit Cost + (Markup % * Unit Cost) = N8,000 + (0.25 * N8,000) = N8,000 + N2,000 = N10,000.

qs.q: A merchant sells a solar lantern for N20,000. If the merchant's gross profit margin on selling price is 30%, what was the cost price of the solar lantern to the merchant?
qs.e: Gross Profit Margin = (Price - Cost) / Price = 0.30. Profit = 0.30 * N20,000 = N6,000. Cost = Selling Price - Profit = N20,000 - N6,000 = N14,000.

qs.q: A producer of fruit juice incurs fixed operating costs of N1,500,000 per month. Each carton of juice sells for N5,000 and has variable manufacturing costs of N2,000. How many cartons must the producer sell per month to achieve a target monthly profit of N900,000?
qs.e: Contribution Margin per unit = Selling Price - Variable Cost = N5,000 - N2,000 = N3,000. Target Sales Volume = (Fixed Costs + Target Profit) / Contribution Margin = (N1,500,000 + N900,000) / N3,000 = N2,400,000 / N3,000 = 800 cartons.

qs.q: A book publisher lists a textbook at N4,000. Booksellers are given a 20% trade discount. If a bookseller pays promptly within 7 days, an additional 5% cash discount is granted on the net invoice price. How much will a bookseller pay for 10 books paid within 7 days?
qs.e: List Price for 10 books = 10 * N4,000 = N40,000. Trade discount of 20% = 0.20 * N40,000 = N8,000. Net invoice price = N40,000 - N8,000 = N32,000. Cash discount of 5% on net invoice = 0.05 * N32,000 = N1,600. Amount paid = N32,000 - N1,600 = N30,400.

qs.q: A smartphone brand enters the market pricing its premium flagship device at N850,000 to capture high-income early adopters willing to pay top value, planning to gradually lower prices over time. This pricing strategy is known as market
qs.e: Market-skimming pricing involves setting a high initial price to skim maximum revenues layer by layer from segments willing to pay the high price before lowering prices later.

qs.q: A poultry farmer in Ogun State sells fresh eggs directly to household consumers from a farm store at the gate without using intermediaries. What channel level is being operated?
qs.e: A zero-level channel (also called direct marketing channel) consists of a manufacturer selling directly to consumers without any intermediary.

qs.q: A soft drink producer distributes its beverage through every available supermarket, neighborhood kiosk, street vendor, and gas station in Lagos to ensure maximum exposure. Which intensity of distribution is being practiced?
qs.e: Intensive distribution stocks the product in as many outlets as possible to ensure maximum market coverage and availability for convenience items.

qs.q: Conflict arising between an authorized regional distributor of electronic goods in Kano and a retail dealer in the same city over price cutting and territory infringement is classified as
qs.e: Vertical channel conflict occurs between different levels of the same distribution channel (e.g., between a wholesaler/distributor and a retailer). Horizontal conflict occurs between firms at the same channel level.

qs.q: A manufacturer of luxury Swiss wristwatches grants selling rights exclusively to one flagship store in all of West Africa. This distribution strategy is called
qs.e: Exclusive distribution gives a limited number of dealers the exclusive right to distribute the company's products in their trade territories, typical for luxury items.

qs.q: A manufacturer sells product X to a wholesaler at N1,000 per unit after adding a 25% markup on manufacturing cost. The wholesaler then sells to a retailer at a 20% markup on wholesale cost. The retailer adds a 30% markup on retail cost to set the final consumer price. What is the final price paid by the consumer?
qs.e: Wholesaler cost = N1,000. Wholesaler price to retailer = N1,000 * (1 + 0.20) = N1,200. Retailer price to consumer = N1,200 * (1 + 0.30) = N1,560.

qs.q: A new beverage company offers free trial mini-cans at motor parks while simultaneously offering retail trade allowances to supermarket managers who stock 50 crates. The company is using a combination of
qs.e: Offering trade allowances to retailers pushes product into channels, while giving free samples to end-consumers pulls consumer demand through the channel. Combining both creates a push-pull promotional strategy.

qs.q: In the classic AIDA model of promotional response, what does the letter 'D' stand for?
qs.e: AIDA stands for Attention, Interest, Desire, and Action—representing the stages a consumer goes through when responding to marketing communications.

qs.q: Carefully integrating and coordinating the company's many communications channels to deliver a clear, consistent, and compelling message about the organization and its products is known as
qs.e: Integrated Marketing Communications (IMC) integrates all promotional tools so that they work together in harmony to deliver a unified brand message.

qs.q: A manufacturer of farm tractors relies heavily on sales representatives visiting commercial farm owners individually to demonstrate machinery rather than placing mass television ads. This reliance indicates a primary reliance on a
qs.e: A push strategy involves using the sales force and trade promotion to push the product through channels to final consumers, essential in high-value B2B capital equipment sales.

qs.q: Which promotional budget setting method calculates marketing expenditure as a fixed percentage of current or forecasted revenue?
qs.e: The percentage-of-sales method sets the promotion budget at a specified percentage of current or forecasted sales, or as a percentage of the unit sales price.

qs.q: An advert placed by a newly launched telecommunications network comparing its internet speed side-by-side with an established competitor's speed benchmark is known as
qs.e: Comparative (or persuasive) advertising directly or indirectly compares one brand with one or more other brands to demonstrate superiority.

qs.q: An advertising campaign during the festive season featuring a familiar soft drink brand with the tag line 'Refresh Your Celebration' aims primarily to perform which advertising objective?
qs.e: Reminder advertising is used for mature products to keep consumers thinking about the product, maintaining top-of-mind brand awareness during peak consumption periods.

qs.q: In advertising media planning, the total percentage of target audience members exposed to an advertisement at least once during a given time period is defined as
qs.e: Reach is a measure of the percentage of people in the target market who are exposed to the ad campaign during a given period of time.

qs.q: If a radio ad costs N150,000 and reaches an estimated audience of 500,000 listeners, what is the Cost Per Thousand (CPM) impressions for this advertisement?
A company sponsors a billboard campaign aimed solely at improving public goodwill and promoting corporate commitment to renewable energy, without focusing on selling any specific product. This is
qs.e: Institutional (or corporate) advertising promotes the image, reputation, or ideas of an organization rather than specific goods or services.

qs.q: During a B2B sales meeting for industrial generators, the prospect states: 'Your machinery is good, but your maintenance contract fee is too steep.' The sales representative responds by breaking down the daily maintenance savings against downtime losses. Which step of the personal selling process is taking place?
qs.e: Handling objections is the step in the personal selling process in which the salesperson seeks out, clarifies, and overcomes customer objections to buying.

qs.q: A medical sales representative researches a consultant doctor's clinic hours, research publications, and current drug prescription preferences before making an introductory visit. This step is known as
qs.e: The pre-approach step involves learning as much as possible about a prospective customer before making a sales call.

qs.q: A sales rep earns a monthly base salary of N120,000 plus a 4% commission on all sales volume generated above a monthly quota of N2,000,000. If the rep achieves N5,500,000 in total sales for October, total monthly earnings will be
qs.e: Commissionable sales = N5,500,000 - N2,000,000 = N3,500,000. Commission earned = 4% of N3,500,000 = 0.04 * 3,500,000 = N140,000. Total earnings = Base salary (N120,000) + Commission (N140,000) = N260,000.

qs.q: The final stage in the personal selling process that ensures customer satisfaction, reduces post-purchase anxiety, and builds long-term business relationship is
qs.e: Follow-up is the last step in the personal selling process in which the salesperson follows up after the sale to ensure customer satisfaction and repeat business.

qs.q: A real estate representative asking a prospective homebuyer: 'Would you prefer taking possession of the duplex in November or early December?' is employing which closing technique?
qs.e: The alternative-choice close presents the buyer with two positive choices (e.g. November or December possession), assuming the purchase decision has already been made.

qs.q: A detergent company attaches a plastic measuring cup to every 1kg bag of washing powder at no extra charge to encourage immediate customer trial and repeat purchases. This sales promotion tool is an example of a
qs.e: A premium is an item offered for free or at a low cost as a bonus to purchase a product, providing an immediate incentive to buyers.

qs.q: To clear seasonal inventory before restocking, an apparel store in Port Harcourt offers 'Buy One T-Shirt, Get One Free' for two weeks. This promotional tactic is classified as a
qs.e: Consumer sales promotions are short-term incentives directed at end consumers to encourage purchase or sale of a product or service.

qs.q: A food processing firm spends N500,000 on a scratch-and-win sales promotion campaign, which yields N2,500,000 in total promotional sales volume. If the firm operates at a 30% gross profit margin on sales, what is the net return on marketing investment (ROMI) percentage for this campaign?
qs.e: Gross profit generated = 30% of N2,500,000 = N750,000. Net profit from promotion = N750,000 - N500,000 (campaign cost) = N250,000. ROMI = (Net profit / Campaign cost) * 100 = (N250,000 / N500,000) * 100 = 50%.

qs.q: A manufacturer offers wholesalers a N500 allowance for every case of soft drinks purchased during the month of November, provided the wholesaler features the product in local newspaper flyers. This trade incentive is known as a
qs.e: A promotional allowance is a payment or price reduction given by manufacturers to channel members to reward them for advertising or supporting the product.

qs.q: Which of the following describes a major disadvantage of relying excessively on frequent sales promotions and price discounting?
o: It severely delays short-term sales volume
It trains consumers to wait for discounts and erodes brand margins
qs.e: Excessive discounting conditions consumers to become price sensitive and wait for deals, eroding brand prestige and squeezing profit margins.

qs.q: Following a social media rumor regarding contamination in its sachet water product, a beverage firm holds an urgent press briefing, presents NAFDAC lab clearance certificates, and invites journalists to inspect its plant. This activity falls under
qs.e: Crisis public relations involves management of company communications to handle negative news, restore trust, and protect corporate reputation during an emergency.

qs.q: A commercial bank funds the complete renovation of a public library in Benin City and sponsors local youth football tournaments. These actions are designed to enhance corporate image through
qs.e: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiatives build favorable public relations and goodwill by demonstrating commitment to community development and societal welfare.

qs.q: Unlike paid advertising, publicity generated through media coverage of a new scientific discovery by a pharmaceutical firm is generally perceived by consumers as having higher
qs.e: Publicity carries higher credibility than advertising because the news message comes from an independent third party (journalists/media) rather than a paid commercial sponsor.

qs.q: A firm releases a written news announcement to major national dailies describing its upcoming merger with a telecommunications provider. This written communication document is called a
qs.e: A press release (or news release) is an official statement distributed to news media members to provide information, announce events, or make official statements.

qs.q: A major petroleum refinery sponsors the annual Nigerian National Science Olympiad competition for secondary schools. In public relations terms, this strategic activity is classified as corporate
qs.e: Sponsorship is a PR technique where a company provides financial or resource support for an event or cause in exchange for public association and goodwill.

qs.q: A cosmetics company divides its market into segments based on consumer income levels (under N100,000, N100,000-N300,000, and above N300,000 monthly). Which base of market segmentation is being utilized?
qs.e: Demographic segmentation divides the market based on variables such as age, gender, income, occupation, education, and family size.

qs.q: A fitness studio targets urban professionals who value active lifestyle, health consciousness, and luxury wellness experiences. This segmentation is based on
qs.e: Psychographic segmentation divides buyers into different segments based on social class, lifestyle, attitude, or personality characteristics.

qs.q: An automobile manufacturer produces luxury sedans for high-net-worth executives, rugged pickup trucks for agricultural enterprises, and compact hatchbacks for university students. This targeting strategy is known as
qs.e: Differentiated (segmented) marketing targets several market segments and designs separate, distinct offers for each segment.

qs.q: A small artisanal bakery in Calabar focuses 100% of its resources on producing gluten-free, sugar-free pastries exclusively for diabetic customers. This target marketing approach is
qs.e: Concentrated (niche) marketing focuses resources on capturing a large share of one small, specific sub-market or niche with specialized requirements.

qs.q: To evaluate whether a potential market segment is viable for targeted entry, marketers require that the segment be measurable, substantial, accessible, actionable, and
qs.e: According to Kotler, effective market segments must be Measurable, Substantial, Accessible, Differentiable (conceptually distinguishable and responding differently to mix elements), and Actionable.

qs.q: After buying a brand-new car for N18,000,000, a customer feels anxious, wondering whether a competing SUV model would have been a better choice. The buyer seeks reassuring reviews from friends to relieve this mental discomfort. This psychological state is called
qs.e: Cognitive dissonance is buyer discomfort caused by post-purchase conflict or doubt about whether the right purchase decision was made.

qs.q: In Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs, a consumer buying a security alarm system and house insurance is satisfying which level of needs?
qs.e: Safety needs include physical protection, security, stability, law, order, and freedom from fear.

qs.q: Which step in the consumer buying decision process immediately follows 'Problem or Need Recognition'?
qs.e: The 5-stage consumer decision process is: 1. Problem recognition -> 2. Information search -> 3. Evaluation of alternatives -> 4. Purchase decision -> 5. Post-purchase behavior.

qs.q: A consumer tends to screen out most commercial advertisements seen daily on social media feed, paying attention only to ads displaying discount footwear because he currently needs new shoes. This perceptual tendency is termed
qs.e: Selective attention is the tendency for people to screen out most of the information to which they are exposed, filtering in only messages relevant to current needs.

qs.q: A university student choices to buy a specific brand of sneakers because his campus peer group and popular music influencers wear them. In consumer behavior, these peer groups act as a
qs.e: A reference group serves as a direct or indirect point of comparison or reference in forming a person's attitudes or behavior.

qs.q: A market researcher gathers census figures published by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) to estimate the population density of potential retail store sites. The NBS data collected by the researcher is
qs.e: Secondary data consists of information that already exists somewhere, having been collected previously for another purpose by another agency or research study.

qs.q: A beverage manufacturer gathers 8 consumers in a comfortable room guided by a trained moderator to discuss their feelings, reactions, and taste preferences regarding a new herbal drink concept. This research method is a
qs.e: A focus group discussion involves gathering 6 to 10 people with a trained moderator to talk about a product, service, or organization in depth.

qs.q: A retail supermarket chain tests two different aisle shelf layouts in 10 store branches to measure which layout yields higher sales revenue per visitor. This type of research design is
qs.e: Causal (experimental) research tests hypotheses about cause-and-effect relationships by manipulating one or more independent variables (shelf layout) and measuring dependent effects (sales).

qs.q: A survey researcher divides a city into 5 geographical zones, then randomly selects 100 households from each zone to ensure proportionate spatial representation. This sampling technique is
qs.e: Stratified random sampling divides the population into mutually exclusive groups (strata like geographic zones) and draws random samples from each stratum.

qs.q: A market research project budgeted N2,000,000. Field enumerator costs account for N800,000, questionnaire printing N200,000, data analysis software N400,000, and respondent incentives N200,000. What percentage of the total research budget remains unspent as contingency buffer?

An airline flight departing with 20 empty seats cannot sell those unused seat positions after takeoff, resulting in permanent revenue loss. This scenario illustrates which unique service characteristic?
qs.e: Perishability means that services cannot be stored for later sale or use; unpurchased service capacity is lost forever.

qs.q: A haircut service is created and consumed at the exact moment the barber cuts the client's hair. The barber cannot produce the haircut without the client being present. This reflects service
qs.e: Inseparability means services are produced and consumed at the same time and cannot be separated from their providers.

qs.q: A passenger's experience on a commercial bus voyage varies depending on whether the driver is attentive or tired and whether the vehicle AC functions smoothly. This fluctuation in service quality highlights service
qs.e: Variability (heterogeneity) means that the quality of services depends on who provides them, as well as when, where, and how they are provided.

qs.q: In Parasuraman's SERVQUAL model, which dimension measures the willingness of service employees to help customers and provide prompt service?
qs.e: Responsiveness in SERVQUAL refers to the willingness to help customers and provide prompt, attentive service.

qs.q: When a bank branch installs comfortable air-conditioned waiting lounges, digital queue monitors, and clean executive desks, it is strengthening which element of the extended service marketing mix?
qs.e: Physical evidence includes the environment in which the service is delivered and where the firm and customer interact, as well as any tangible components that facilitate service delivery.

qs.q: An online clothing store runs a digital ad campaign that records 50,000 ad impressions and generates 2,500 link clicks. What is the Click-Through Rate (CTR) of this campaign?
qs.e: CTR = (Total Clicks / Total Impressions) * 100 = (2,500 / 50,000) * 100 = 0.05 * 100 = 5.0%.

qs.q: An e-commerce business spent N200,000 on social media advertising. The campaign resulted in 4,000 web visits and 80 completed customer purchases. What is the Cost Per Acquisition (CPA) per purchase?
qs.e: Cost Per Acquisition (CPA) = Total Ad Spend / Total Conversions (Purchases) = N200,000 / 80 = N2,500.

qs.q: Optimizing website code, publishing keyword-rich content, and building authoritative external backlinks to improve non-paid search engine ranking is known as
qs.e: Search Engine Optimization (SEO) is the process of maximizing the number of visitors to a website by ensuring that the site appears high on the list of organic (unpaid) search results.

qs.q: A popular fashion blogger promotes an online shoe brand on her Instagram page using a custom discount link. For every buyer who purchases shoes using her link, she earns a 10% commission. This digital marketing model is
qs.e: Affiliate marketing is a performance-based marketing arrangement where a business rewards affiliates for each visitor or customer brought by the affiliate's own marketing efforts.

qs.q: Which digital marketing metric measures the percentage of website visitors who leave the site after viewing only a single landing page without taking any further action?
qs.e: Bounce rate represents the percentage of visitors who enter the site and then leave ('bounce') rather than continuing to view other pages within the same site.

qs.q: A newly invented green hydrogen generator enters the market. Sales growth is slow, production costs are high, and profits are negative due to heavy initial R&D and promotional expenditures. Which stage of the Product Life Cycle (PLC) is this product in?
qs.e: The Introduction stage of the PLC is characterized by slow sales growth, high unit costs, negative or low profits, and heavy promotional expenses to build primary demand.

qs.q: During which stage of the Product Life Cycle do competitors enter the market in large numbers, sales rise rapidly, and unit manufacturing costs fall due to economies of scale?
qs.e: The Growth stage features rapid market acceptance, rising sales, new competitors entering, and declining unit production costs.

qs.q: Sales of DVD media players have steadily plummeted over recent years as streaming platforms dominate consumer entertainment. Management decides to harvest remaining profits without further ad spending. DVD players are in the PLC stage of
qs.e: The Decline stage is marked by falling sales and profits over a prolonged period due to technological advances or shifts in consumer tastes.

qs.q: A soft drink brand experiencing flat sales in a mature market modifies its beverage formula, introduces sugar-free variants, and repositions the brand for fitness enthusiasts. This strategic effort is called PLC
