qs.e: Product lifecycle extension strategies are techniques used to prolong the maturity stage of a product and prevent it from entering the decline stage.

qs.q: At which stage of the Product Life Cycle is industry profit per unit at its peak, even though total industry sales volume reaches its peak later in the next stage?
qs.e: Profit per unit peaks during the Growth stage as economies of scale are achieved and price competition has not yet reached the aggressive levels seen in Maturity.

qs.q: In an industrial manufacturing plant purchasing raw steel, the chief engineer who specifies technical specifications and grade tolerances acts in the buying center as a
qs.e: In the organizational buying center, influencers affect the buying decision by helping define specifications and providing information for evaluating alternatives.

qs.q: The corporate purchasing officer who negotiates final payment terms, executes contract paperwork, and issues purchase orders to chosen suppliers fulfills the buying center role of
qs.e: The buyer in an organizational buying center has formal authority to select the supplier and arrange terms of purchase.

qs.q: A corporate executive's administrative secretary who controls access to executive phone lines and blocks uninvited sales reps from delivering sales literature performs the buying center role of a
qs.e: Gatekeepers control the flow of information to other members of the buying center (e.g., receptionists, secretaries, technical advisors).

qs.q: An organization reorders office printing paper from its regular vendor without modifying product specifications or pricing terms. In industrial buying scenarios, this transaction type is a
qs.e: A straight rebuy is a business buying situation in which the buyer routinely reorders something without any modifications.

qs.q: A commercial truck fleet operator orders 20 heavy-duty trucks, but requests upgraded diesel engines and customized extended maintenance warranties from the truck dealer. This purchasing situation is a
qs.e: A modified rebuy is a business buying situation in which the buyer wants to modify product specifications, prices, terms, or suppliers.

qs.q: A Nigerian agricultural firm exports processed cocoa butter directly to European chocolate makers without establishing physical production plants abroad. This market entry mode is known as
qs.e: Exporting involves producing goods in one country and selling them to buyers in another country, representing the simplest international entry strategy.

qs.q: A fast-food chain headquartered in South Africa allows an investor in Lagos to operate restaurants using its brand name, recipes, and operational systems in exchange for royalty fees. This international entry strategy is
qs.e: Franchising is a form of licensing where a franchisor grants a franchisee the right to use its complete business system and trademark in exchange for fees and royalties.

qs.q: A foreign multinational company partners with a local Nigerian engineering firm to form a newly incorporated third company, sharing capital investment, risks, and profits. This entry method is a
qs.e: A joint venture occurs when a firm enters a foreign market by joining with foreign investors to create a local business in which they share ownership and control.

qs.q: When a global fast-food brand modifies its international menu by excluding pork products in Middle Eastern markets and adding spicy jollof rice options in Nigeria, it is practicing product
qs.e: Product adaptation (or glocalisation) involves altering a product or marketing mix strategy to meet local consumer preferences, cultural norms, or legal requirements in foreign markets.

qs.q: A manufacturing enterprise sets up a wholly-owned factory in Ghana, acquiring land, machinery, and hiring staff locally. In international market entry strategies, this represents
qs.e: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) involves direct ownership of foreign-based manufacturing or assembly facilities, offering complete control but carrying highest financial risk.

qs.q: A commercial cassava starch mill in Makurdi designs its entire operations around customer feedback, continuously assessing market demand for food-grade vs industrial-grade starch. This organization operates under the principle of
qs.e: Customer orientation is the core element of the marketing concept where all business activities are directed toward identifying and satisfying customer needs.

qs.q: An aggressive solar panel vendor uses high-pressure telemarketing and cold calls to persuade homeowners to buy batteries, regardless of whether the home's electrical wiring can safely handle the load. This business approach is rooted in the
qs.e: The selling concept holds that consumers will not buy enough of the firm's products unless it undertakes a large-scale selling and promotion effort, often focusing on short-term sales over long-term customer satisfaction.

qs.q: Which of the following best describes the difference between a consumer's 'need' and a 'want' in marketing theory?
o: A need requires financial purchasing power, whereas a want is purely imaginary
A need is a basic state of felt deprivation, whereas a want is that need shaped by culture and individual personality
A need applies only to industrial buyers, whereas a want applies to retail buyers
A need is created by television advertising, whereas a want is biological
qs.e: Human needs are states of felt deprivation (food, clothing, safety). Wants are the form human needs take as they are shaped by culture and individual personality (e.g., needing food but wanting a plate of amala).

qs.q: When a motorcycle manufacturer aligns its engineering, sales, customer support, human resources, and finance departments to work together to deliver superior value to dispatch riders, it is practicing
qs.e: Internal marketing is the task of hiring, training, and motivating able employees who want to serve customers well, ensuring that all internal departments work together to support marketing goals.

qs.q: A consumer utility evaluation shows that a subscriber values unlimited monthly mobile data at N15,000, while the telecommunications network incurs N4,000 in network bandwidth operating cost per subscriber. If the monthly subscription fee is set at N10,000, what is the customer surplus (net customer value)?
qs.e: Customer surplus (net customer value) = Perceived total value - Price paid = N15,000 - N10,000 = N5,000.

qs.q: A fruit juice maker changes its container from a glass bottle to an eco-friendly pouch, lowers the retail price from N600 to N450, and shifts advertising from print magazines to TikTok video ads. Which element of the marketing mix was NOT modified in this strategy?
qs.e: The firm altered Product (pouch packaging), Price (N600 to N450), and Promotion (TikTok ads). The Place (distribution channels) remained unchanged.

qs.q: In marketing mix planning for a capital-intensive business, why must decisions regarding Product, Price, Place, and Promotion be coordinated interdependently rather than in isolation?
o: Because consumers buy products only when all 4 Ps are priced identically
Because government regulators enforce identical spending across all four elements
Because an inconsistency in one element can neutralize the effectiveness of the other three
Because advertising agencies control distribution decisions
qs.e: The marketing mix elements must be harmonized; for example, setting a premium price for a luxury product while distributing it through low-end discount stalls creates brand inconsistency and ruins sales performance.

qs.q: A commercial air conditioning servicing company establishes standardized 45-minute response times for repair calls and issues tablet checklists to technicians. In the services marketing mix, this initiative improves
qs.e: Process refers to the actual procedures, mechanisms, and flow of activities by which the service is delivered.

qs.q: When a luxury perfume brand limits distribution exclusively to high-end department stores in major capital cities, it is using 'Place' strategy directly to reinforce its brand's
qs.e: Exclusive, high-end channel distribution aligns with luxury branding, reinforcing customer perception of exclusivity and high quality.

qs.q: A fast-food chain in Nigeria bundles a burger, french fries, and a soft drink for N3,500, whereas buying each item individually costs N4,200 in total. This marketing mix tactic combines elements of
qs.e: Bundling multiple products together at a discounted total price is a product-bundling packaging and promotional pricing tactic designed to increase average basket size.

qs.q: A consumer buys a generator for N350,000. The seller includes a 2-year free repair warranty, free home delivery, and a complimentary oil filter. These added services form the product's
qs.e: The augmented product consists of additional services, warranties, and benefits built around the core benefit and actual product to create extra value.

qs.q: An industrial manufacturing firm purchases raw palm kernel oil to process into industrial soap noodles. For the manufacturing firm, the palm kernel oil is classified as
qs.e: Raw materials are industrial goods that become part of another physical product through processing or manufacturing.

qs.q: A biscuit manufacturing company adds a new low-sugar digestive variant and a chocolate-coated variant to its existing biscuits line. This strategic product decision is known as product line
qs.e: Product line filling involves adding more items within the present range of the product line.

qs.q: An automaker that previously produced only mid-range family sedans launches a new luxury executive SUV priced at N65,000,000 to enter higher-margin market tiers. This action represents product line
qs.e: Upward stretching occurs when a company operating in the middle or lower end of the market introduces higher-end, higher-priced products.

qs.q: Which product innovation strategy involves introducing a completely new-to-the-world technology that creates an entirely new market category?
qs.e: Disruptive (or radical) innovation introduces breakthrough technology or business models that create a new market value network, displacing established market leaders.

qs.q: When consumers immediately recognize the yellow color, distinctive double-curve logo, and signature ringtone of MTN without seeing the company name written out, they are demonstrating high brand
qs.e: Brand recognition and recall measure the ability of consumers to identify or retrieve a brand from memory using visual cues, logos, or slogans.

qs.q: A company markets distinct detergent brands such as 'Omo', 'Surf', and 'Sunlight' independently without highlighting the parent corporate brand Unilever on the front label. This brand architecture is a
qs.e: An individual branding strategy assigns distinct, separate brand names to different products in the company's portfolio, preventing negative spillover across products.

qs.q: Which term describes the psychological associations, emotional connections, and personality traits that consumers attribute to a brand name in their minds?
qs.e: Brand image is the consumer's perception and set of beliefs held about a specific brand based on experience and marketing communication.

qs.q: A pharmaceutical manufacturer grants an international biotechnology firm legal permission to produce and sell its patented vaccine formulation in exchange for a 6% royalty fee on global sales. This is brand
qs.e: Brand licensing is a contractual arrangement where a brand owner permits another company to use its brand name, patent, or logo for a fee or royalty.

qs.q: A brand extension risk where launching a cheaper, lower-grade product under the same prestigious brand name damages the premium standing and sales of the original luxury product is known as brand
qs.e: Brand dilution occurs when a brand extension weakens or damages consumer perception of the core brand's high status, while cannibalization steals sales from the original product.

qs.q: Why do manufacturers of liquid pharmaceuticals use amber-colored glass bottles instead of clear glass for packaging oral syrups?
o: To comply with trade discount regulations
To protect light-sensitive active ingredients from chemical degradation
qs.e: Amber glass blocks ultraviolet light, protecting light-sensitive active chemical compounds in medication from degrading during storage.

qs.q: A cereal company prints a nutrition facts panel listing calories, sugar content, and allergen warnings on the side of its packaging. This packaging function is
qs.e: Nutritional facts, allergen notices, and ingredient lists fulfill informational and regulatory compliance functions on packaging.

qs.q: Which packaging component forms the outermost shipping container that protects multiple unit boxes during sea freight container transport?
qs.e: Tertiary (or transit) packaging protects goods during bulk handling, warehousing, and long-distance transport.

qs.q: A cosmetic brand designs a perfume bottle with an ergonomic, anti-slip grip spray pump. This packaging innovation primarily enhances product
qs.e: Ergonomic packaging design improves ease of handling, comfort, and functional utility for the consumer during use.

qs.q: An agribusiness enterprise replaces traditional wooden crates with recyclable ventilated plastic crates for transporting tomatoes from Jos to Lagos, reducing transit spoilage losses from 35% down to 8%. If a truckload carries 500 crates valued at N10,000 each, what is the monetary value of tomato savings per truckload?
qs.e: Total truckload value = 500 * N10,000 = N5,000,000. Spoilage reduction = 35% - 8% = 27%. Value saved = 27% of N5,000,000 = 0.27 * 5,000,000 = N1,350,000.

qs.q: A boutique owner buys a designer dress for N24,000 and sells it for N32,000. What is the gross profit margin percentage achieved on the selling price?
qs.e: Gross Profit = Selling Price - Cost = N32,000 - N24,000 = N8,000. Gross Profit Margin % = (Profit / Selling Price) * 100 = (N8,000 / N32,000) * 100 = 25%.

qs.q: An electronics retailer prices a television set at N199,999 instead of N200,000 to make the item appear significantly cheaper to price-sensitive shoppers. This tactic is
qs.e: Psychological pricing (odd-even pricing) uses prices that end in odd numbers (like .99 or N199,999) to create a perception that the product is cheaper than it actually is.

qs.q: A supermarket owner marks down old stock of canned beans below purchase cost to draw shoppers into the store, anticipating that customers will buy profitable items while inside. The reduced-price canned beans act as a
qs.e: A loss leader is a product sold at a financial loss or near-zero margin to attract customers into a store, where they buy other profitable goods.

qs.q: A printer manufacturer sells desktop printers at a cheap unit price of N25,000, but charges high prices for the replacement ink cartridges required to operate the printer. This pricing practice is known as
qs.e: Captive-product pricing sets a low price on the main core product (printer) and high markups on the necessary consumable accessory (ink cartridges).

qs.q: A manufacturing firm produces 10,000 electric fans annually with total fixed costs of N40,000,000 and variable costs of N6,000 per fan. If the company seeks a 20% target return on an invested capital of N100,000,000, at what price per fan must it sell all 10,000 units?
qs.e: Unit fixed cost = N40,000,000 / 10,000 = N4,000. Total unit cost = Variable cost (N6,000) + Fixed cost (N4,000) = N10,000. Target total return required = 20% of N100,000,000 = N20,000,000. Target profit per fan = N20,000,000 / 10,000 = N2,000. Required price per fan = Unit cost (N10,000) + Target profit (N2,000) = N12,000.

qs.q: An agricultural enterprise in Benue State sells fresh yam tubers to wholesale merchants in Mile 12 Market Lagos, who sell to neighborhood market women, who then retail to households. How many channel levels exist between producer and household consumer?
qs.e: The intermediaries between producer and final consumer are: (1) Wholesale merchants and (2) Retail market women. Therefore, this is a two-level channel.

qs.q: A commercial truck freight operator calculates logistics transport expenses across three alternative delivery routes to move 20 metric tons of fertilizer. Route A costs N800,000, Route B costs N950,000, and Route C costs N1,100,000. If choosing Route A reduces cargo damage risk by 10% relative to Route B, where potential damage loss on Route B is N200,000, which route minimizes total cost including expected damage risk?
o: Routes A and B have identical total cost
qs.e: Route A cost = N800,000. Expected damage on Route A = 10% less than Route B (N200,000 - N20,000 = N180,000 or lower). Total cost Route A = N800,000. Route B total cost = N950,000 + N200,000 damage = N1,150,000. Route A is clearly cheaper.

qs.q: When a company operates both physical retail outlets and an online e-commerce mobile application to reach different consumer preferences, it is utilizing a
qs.e: A multi-channel distribution system (or hybrid channel) occurs when a single firm sets up two or more marketing channels to reach one or more customer segments.

qs.q: An independent retailer who purchases inventory outright from manufacturers, takes legal title, holds warehouse stock, and sells to consumers is a
qs.e: Merchant middlemen take legal title to the goods they handle and buy/sell on their own financial account, unlike agents and brokers who do not take title.

qs.q: Which vertical marketing system (VMS) achieves channel coordination and leadership not through corporate ownership or contractual agreements, but through the sheer size and market power of one dominant channel member?
qs.e: An Administered VMS coordinates successive stages of production and distribution through the dominant size and power of one channel member (e.g. Walmart or Procter & Gamble).

qs.q: In designing promotional messages using the AIDA framework, securing customer interest occurs immediately AFTER achieving
qs.e: The sequential stages of the AIDA model are: Attention -> Interest -> Desire -> Action. Thus, interest comes immediately after capturing attention.

qs.q: A manufacturer of heavy industrial cranes uses trade shows, specialized technical brochures, and face-to-face sales demonstrations to convince engineering procurement directors. This promotional mix balance reflects an emphasis on
o: B2B personal selling and trade promotion
qs.e: B2B capital equipment promotional mix relies heavily on personal selling, technical demonstrations, and trade shows to reach specialized decision-makers.

qs.q: Which promotional budget method assesses competitor promotional spending across industry journals and matches the company's budget to industry average expenditure percentages?
qs.e: The competitive-parity method sets the promotion budget to match competitors' outlays or industry benchmark averages.

qs.q: Why is the objective-and-task method widely regarded as the most logical promotional budgeting approach by marketing theorists?
o: Because it guarantees the company will outspend competitors
Because it requires zero market research data
Because it automatically reduces promotion expense during financial downturns
Because it forces management to spell out specific objectives, define required tasks, and estimate associated costs
qs.e: The objective-and-task method is most logical because it defines specific promotion goals, outlines the tasks needed to accomplish them, and sums costs to determine budget.

qs.q: A consumer goods company spends N12,000,000 annually across promotional tools: 40% on TV advertising, 30% on sales promotion discounts, 20% on personal selling commissions, and 10% on PR sponsorships. How much money is allocated to personal selling commissions?
qs.e: Personal selling commission budget = 20% of N12,000,000 = 0.20 * N12,000,000 = N2,400,000.

qs.q: An ad campaign launched during an election year highlighting a company's anti-pollution filters and green manufacturing awards is aimed at building corporate reputation. This form of advertising is
qs.e: Institutional advertising promotes corporate image, corporate responsibility, and goodwill rather than specific commercial products.

qs.q: An advertiser spends N600,000 to air 4 radio jingles during peak morning commute hours on a station reaching 1,200,000 listeners per broadcast. What is the Cost Per Thousand (CPM) for a single broadcast airing costing N150,000?
qs.e: Cost per single broadcast = N150,000. Audience reached = 1,200,000 listeners. CPM = (N150,000 / 1,200,000) * 1,000 = 0.125 * 1,000 = N125.

qs.q: In advertising media scheduling, placing advertisements at steady, continuous levels throughout the entire year without seasonal fluctuation is known as a
qs.e: A continuous media pattern schedules ad placements at an even, constant level over a given time period.

qs.q: A media plan schedules heavy ad exposures during harvest season, zero ads during off-season, and moderate ads during festival months. This media timing pattern is known as
qs.e: Flighting involves scheduling ads for heavy periods followed by periods with no ads at all.

qs.q: An ad campaign achieves a reach of 60% of the target market of 2,000,000 households with an average frequency of 4 exposures per household. What is the total Gross Rating Points (GRP) score for this campaign?
qs.e: Gross Rating Points (GRP) = Reach (%) * Average Frequency = 60 * 4 = 240 GRPs.

qs.q: A pharmaceutical sales rep calls on hospital pharmacists to introduce a new antibiotic, presents clinical trial data, answers questions, and secures an initial trial purchase order. What type of sales personnel is this rep?
qs.e: An order getter is a salesperson who actively identifies prospects, presents solutions, overcomes objections, and closes sales through creative selling.

qs.q: A customer purchasing industrial paint remarks: 'Your delivery timeline of 14 days is too slow for our contract schedule.' The sales agent replies: 'If we expedite air freight shipping to deliver within 4 days at no extra fee, will you sign the contract today?' Which closing method is used?
qs.e: A concession (or special-offer) close offers an added incentive or compromise (free expedited shipping) in exchange for an immediate buying commitment.

qs.q: A medical device sales rep researches a surgeon's preferred surgical tools, hospital affiliations, and published articles prior to making initial contact. This personal selling phase is the
qs.e: The pre-approach stage involves gathering detailed intelligence about a qualified prospect before conducting the actual sales interview.

qs.q: In sales force territory design, assigning sales representatives based strictly on distinct geographical boundaries (e.g. Lagos West, Kano State, Rivers State) is known as a
qs.e: A territorial sales force structure assigns each salesperson an exclusive geographic territory in which that salesperson sells the company's full line.

qs.q: A sales rep receives a fixed base salary of N150,000 plus 5% commission on sales up to N3,000,000, and 8% commission on any sales volume exceeding N3,000,000. If total monthly sales achieved equal N5,000,000, what is the salesperson's total monthly pay?
qs.e: Base salary = N150,000. First tier commission (5% on N3,000,000) = 0.05 * N3,000,000 = N150,000. Second tier commission (8% on excess N2,000,000) = 0.08 * N2,000,000 = N160,000. Total pay = N150,000 + N150,000 + N160,000 = N410,000.

qs.q: A cement manufacturer offers building contractors one free bag of cement for every 20 bags purchased in cash. What is the effective percentage price discount granted to contractors through this sales promotion?
qs.e: The contractor receives 21 bags for the price of 20. Discount percentage = (Free units / Total units received) * 100 = (1 / 21) * 100 = 4.76%.

qs.q: An online retail platform gives first-time users a promotional voucher code granting N2,000 off any purchase exceeding N10,000. This consumer promotion strategy aims primarily at consumer
qs.e: Introductory discount vouchers lower the adoption barrier, encouraging first-time trial and acquiring new registered users.

qs.q: A fast-food restaurant prints collectible game cards under cup lids where customers who collect four matching symbols win a new motorcycle. This promotional tool is a
qs.e: Contests and sweepstakes give consumers the chance to win prizes through luck or extra effort, boosting brand engagement.

qs.q: A pharmaceutical company provides medical representatives with branded desk pens, prescription pads, and diagnostic penlights to hand out to consulting physicians. These items are
qs.e: Advertising specialties (or promotional products) are useful articles imprinted with an advertiser's name, logo, or message given as gifts to prospects.

qs.q: A retail supermarket chain conducts a 30-day promotional campaign costing N1,000,000. Daily baseline sales revenue before promotion was N500,000 at a 20% profit margin. During the promotion, daily sales rose to N800,000 at the same 20% margin. What was the net incremental profit generated over the 30-day campaign after deducting campaign costs?
qs.e: Daily baseline profit = 20% of N500,000 = N100,000. Daily promotional profit = 20% of N800,000 = N160,000. Daily incremental profit = N160,000 - N100,000 = N60,000. Total 30-day incremental profit = 30 * N60,000 = N1,800,000. Net incremental profit = N1,800,000 - N1,000,000 (campaign cost) = N800,000.

qs.q: When a chemical factory accident leads to gas leakage in an industrial zone, the firm's chief executive immediately visits affected residents, commits to covering medical bills, and establishes an open hotline. In public relations, this response represents effective
qs.e: Crisis management involves swift, transparent, and empathetic public relations communication to protect public safety and preserve corporate trust during an emergency.

qs.q: A multi-national mining company builds modern healthcare clinics and solar-powered boreholes in its host communities in Niger State. These corporate investments are examples of
qs.e: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) reflects a company's commitment to manage the social, environmental, and economic effects of its operations responsibly.

qs.q: An organization hires specialized representatives to meet regularly with government lawmakers and regulatory officials to influence pending environmental legislation affecting its industry. This PR practice is
qs.e: Lobbying involves building and maintaining relations with legislators and government officials to influence legislation and regulation.

qs.q: A major brewery organizes an annual cultural music festival, placing its brand banners across the venue and hosting key distributors in VIP lounges. The primary PR objective of this event is
qs.e: Event sponsorship connects the brand to favorable consumer experiences, building positive brand associations and corporate goodwill.

qs.q: A financial services institution publishes an annual integrated sustainability report detailing its carbon footprint reduction, gender diversity metrics, and community development loans. This publication serves primarily as a PR tool for
qs.e: Sustainability and corporate reports communicate non-financial performance and governance to investors, regulators, and societal stakeholders.

qs.q: A footwear company divides the market into heavy runners, casual walkers, and professional athletes based on purchase frequency and product usage rate. This segmentation strategy is
qs.e: Behavioral segmentation divides buyers into groups based on their knowledge, attitudes, uses, or responses to a product (e.g. usage rate, user status, loyalty status).

qs.q: A bank offers a basic savings account with zero minimum balance for university students, a high-yield investment account for working professionals, and a private wealth management package for retirees. The bank is segmenting based on
qs.e: Demographic life-stage segmentation categorizes consumers based on age and life-stage positions (students, young professionals, retirees).

qs.q: When a firm designs a single marketing mix offer and directs it at the entire mass market without differentiating between sub-groups, it is adopting an
qs.e: Undifferentiated (mass) marketing ignores market segment differences and targets the whole market with one offer.

qs.q: A local fashion brand customizes tailor-made formal suits specifically to individual customer measurements and fabric choices. This extreme form of target marketing is known as
qs.e: Micro-marketing (or individual marketing) tailors products and marketing programs to the needs and preferences of individual customers.

qs.q: A manufacturer of commercial air conditioners segments its market into banking halls, hospital surgical suites, and manufacturing plants based on industry sector and cooling precision requirements. In business-to-business marketing, this is
qs.e: B2B segmentation uses organizational demographics such as industry sector, company size, and operating requirements to segment business customers.

qs.q: A consumer evaluating television brands scores Samsung 9/10 on picture quality and 7/10 on price, Sony 10/10 on picture quality and 5/10 on price, and LG 8/10 on picture quality and 9/10 on price. If the buyer assigns a weight of 60% to picture quality and 40% to price, which brand yields the highest weighted evaluation score?
An individual who buys a luxury sports wristwatch primarily to signal financial success and achieve admiration among corporate peers is fulfilling which level in Maslow's hierarchy of needs?
qs.e: Esteem needs include self-esteem, status, recognition, respect, and prestige.

qs.q: A shopper notices a high price tag on a designer jacket, assuming that the high price automatically signifies superior craftsmanship and premium fabric quality. This cognitive rule of thumb is a
qs.e: A heuristic is a mental shortcut or rule of thumb; the price-quality heuristic leads consumers to equate higher prices with higher quality.

qs.q: A consumer who regularly buys the same brand of table salt without comparing alternatives or seeking information is exhibiting
qs.e: Habitual buying behavior occurs under conditions of low consumer involvement and little significant brand difference (e.g. buying table salt).

qs.q: When a household purchases a new family vehicle, the teenage son researches internet reviews and recommends an electric hybrid, the mother sets the financial budget limit, and the father signs the check. In family buying roles, the mother acts as the
qs.e: The mother sets financial boundaries and constraints, acting as a decider/gatekeeper in the family buying process.

qs.q: A retail supermarket installs foot-traffic sensors at store entrances and video cameras above aisles to track how long shoppers spend in front of cereal displays without asking questions directly. This data collection method is
qs.e: Observational research involves gathering primary data by observing relevant people, actions, and situations without direct questioning.

qs.q: A market researcher intercepts shoppers standing in front of a shopping mall entrance and interviews whoever agrees to talk. This sampling method is classified as
qs.e: Convenience sampling is a non-probability sampling technique where subjects are selected because of their convenient accessibility to the researcher.

qs.q: A questionnaire item that asks: 'How satisfied are you with our product quality and customer service?' violates sound questionnaire design principles because it is a
qs.e: A double-barreled question asks about two different issues in a single sentence (quality AND customer service), making it impossible for respondents to answer accurately if their feelings differ on the two.

qs.q: A market research company surveys 400 respondents out of a total target population of 100,000. If 240 respondents express preference for Brand X, what is the estimated population proportion preferring Brand X?
Which research approach is best suited for preliminary, qualitative exploration of an unfamiliar market problem when researchers have little prior knowledge?
qs.e: Exploratory research is used to gather preliminary information that will help define problems and suggest hypotheses.

qs.q: An accounting firm cannot inventory audit hours during slow summer months to use during busy tax seasons. This service constraint is due to service
qs.e: Service perishability prevents service capacity from being produced in advance and stored in inventory for future peak demand periods.

qs.q: A patient evaluates a dental clinic's quality based on the cleanliness of the waiting room, modern lighting, and crisp white uniforms worn by staff. In services marketing, these physical cues form the
qs.e: Physical evidence (servicescape) provides tangible signals that customers use to assess the quality of intangible services.

qs.q: In the Service-Profit Chain model, employee satisfaction leads directly to higher employee retention and productivity, which in turn drives higher
o: Internal service value and customer loyalty
qs.e: The Service-Profit Chain links internal service quality and satisfied employees to higher service value, customer satisfaction, customer loyalty, and ultimate corporate profitability.

qs.q: When a hotel experiences a service breakdown due to an overbooked room, front desk managers immediately upgrade the guest to a luxury suite with free dinner. This immediate corrective action is called
qs.e: Service recovery encompasses the actions taken by a service provider in response to a service failure to solve the problem and retain the customer.

qs.q: According to the Service Gaps Model, 'Gap 1' (Management Perception Gap) occurs when there is a discrepancy between
o: Service standards and actual service delivery
Customer expectations and management perception of those expectations
Management perception and service quality specifications
Service delivery and external communications to customers
qs.e: Gap 1 in the Parasuraman-Zeithaml-Berry Gap Model represents the difference between customer expectations and management's understanding of those customer expectations.

qs.q: A digital marketer allocates N500,000 to a pay-per-click campaign at a cost per click (CPC) of N250. The website achieves a 4% conversion rate from click traffic. How many customer purchases (conversions) will the campaign yield?
qs.e: Total Clicks = Total Spend / CPC = N500,000 / N250 = 2,000 clicks. Conversions = 4% of 2,000 clicks = 0.04 * 2,000 = 80 purchases.

qs.q: A software company sends automated educational emails, product guides, and webinar invitations over 6 weeks to prospective leads who downloaded an e-book. This digital marketing strategy is
qs.e: Lead nurturing uses targeted email communication sequences to build relationships with prospects at every stage of the sales funnel.

qs.q: Creating and sharing valuable, relevant free content (e.g. blog articles, how-to videos, infographics) to attract and retain a clearly defined target audience is known as
qs.e: Content marketing is a strategic marketing approach focused on creating and distributing valuable, relevant, and consistent content to attract and retain an audience.

qs.q: Which social media metric measures total user interactions (likes, shares, comments, retweets, saves) relative to total reach or impressions?
qs.e: Engagement rate measures the level of active interaction (likes, comments, shares) that audience members have with published content.

qs.q: Targeting online users with display ads based on their previous browsing history after they visit a website without making a purchase is called
qs.e: Retargeting (or remarketing) serves targeted ads to users who have already visited a website or mobile app as they browse elsewhere on the web.

qs.q: When electric vehicle sales plateau in domestic urban centers, an automotive manufacturer exports existing EV models to developing markets and introduces fleet leasing programs to corporate clients. These actions are PLC
qs.e: Market modification and product modification are classic PLC extension strategies deployed during maturity to sustain sales revenue.

qs.q: In which stage of the Product Life Cycle does aggressive price competition among surviving brands reach its highest intensity as market growth flattens?
qs.e: During the Maturity stage, market growth slows down or levels off, leading to intense competition for market share and aggressive price discounting.

qs.q: A consumer technology company decides to 'harvest' a declining product line. This means the company will
o: Increase retail price by 300% to turn it into a luxury good
Invest heavily in research and development to revamp the brand
Sell off the factory machinery immediately at auction
Reduce operational costs and advertising to maximize short-term cash flow before phasing out the product
qs.e: Harvesting involves reducing various costs (R&D, advertising, sales force) in hopes that sales will hold up, thereby maximizing short-term cash flow.

qs.q: A consumer brand introduces a new energy drink. In the first year, sales grow rapidly at 45% per quarter, unit production costs drop, and distribution expands across major supermarket chains. The product is in the
qs.e: Rapid sales expansion, expanding distribution networks, and falling unit costs characterize the Growth stage of the PLC.

qs.q: A smartphone manufacturer phases out production of 3G feature phones as market demand shifts completely to 4G and 5G smartphones. Phasing out obsolete products is the final step in managing the PLC stage of
qs.e: Phasing out or dropping products is the final management decision in the Decline stage of the product life cycle.

qs.q: An industrial manufacturing company invites 5 approved steel suppliers to submit formal competitive bids detailing price, delivery schedules, and metallurgical quality certifications. This stage in the business buying process is
qs.e: Proposal solicitation is the stage of the business buying process in which the buyer invites qualified suppliers to submit written proposals or tenders.

qs.q: In B2B organizational purchasing, a 'new-task' buying situation is characterized by
o: High decision risk, extensive information search, and involvement of multiple buying center members
Low unit cost and single-agent decision authority
Routine repeat ordering with zero evaluation
Short transaction cycles and minimal supplier negotiation
qs.e: A new-task buying situation involves purchasing a product or service for the first time, requiring extensive research, high investment, and multiple decision-makers.

qs.q: A commercial airline enters into a long-term strategic partnership with an aircraft engine manufacturer where both companies share maintenance data, co-develop fuel-efficient turbines, and integrate IT systems. This relationship is
qs.e: Collaborative relationship marketing in B2B involves long-term commitment, mutual trust, joint problem solving, and integrated business processes.

qs.q: A manufacturing plant manager notices that an assembly line machine breaks down frequently. The manager completes a formal internal requisition form requesting procurement to buy a replacement motor. In buying center roles, the plant manager is the
qs.e: The initiator is the person who first requests or suggests purchasing a product or service, often also acting as the user.

qs.q: A corporate purchasing department conducts an annual performance appraisal of its key raw material suppliers, rating them on on-time delivery percentage, defect rates, and invoice accuracy. This B2B purchasing phase is
qs.e: Performance review is the final stage of the business buying process in which the buyer rates supplier performance and decides whether to continue, modify, or drop the relationship.

qs.q: A pharmaceutical multinational manufactures active drug compounds in India and ships them in bulk to its subsidiary in Nigeria, where local staff package and bottle the syrup for West African distribution. This international strategy is
qs.e: Contract manufacturing or local assembly involves producing components abroad and performing final assembly/packaging locally to save freight and tariff costs.

qs.q: When a company charges a significantly lower price for its exported product in a foreign market than it charges in its domestic home market, often below production cost to drive out local competitors, it is practicing
qs.e: Dumping is the practice of selling exported goods in a foreign country at a price below home market prices or below cost of production.

qs.q: In international trade, a government imposed restriction that limits the physical quantity of a specific good that may be imported during a given timeframe is a
qs.e: An import quota is a government-imposed trade restriction that limits the physical quantity or value of a commodity allowed into a country during a specified period.

qs.q: A Nigerian oil company exchanges 500,000 barrels of crude oil directly with a foreign government in return for 50,000 metric tons of refined premium motor spirit without any currency exchange taking place. This trade transaction is
qs.e: Barter is a direct exchange of goods or services between two trading parties without money changing hands, a primary form of countertrade.

qs.q: A multinational firm entering a foreign country chooses to grant an independent local enterprise the right to use its patented production process and trademark in exchange for royalties. The entry mode is
qs.e: Licensing allows a foreign company to enter a market by granting a local firm rights to intellectual property, patents, or processes in exchange for royalty fees.

qs.q: A telecommunications company in Nigeria integrates its mobile money platform, data services, and entertainment streaming apps into a unified digital ecosystem where every customer touchpoint reinforces overall corporate value. This illustrates
qs.e: Holistic marketing recognizes that everything matters in marketing—from internal marketing and integrated communications to performance marketing and customer relationship management.

qs.q: An agricultural input distributor prioritizes long-term farmer retention by offering free soil testing and technical agronomy advice rather than pushing one-off seasonal fertilizer sales. The distributor is practicing
qs.e: Relationship marketing aims to build long-term, mutually satisfying relations with key parties (customers, suppliers, distributors) to earn and retain their long-term business.

qs.q: A consumer evaluates two competing solar generator brands. Brand A provides utility worth N300,000 at a price of N220,000. Brand B provides utility worth N400,000 at a price of N300,000. Which brand offers higher net customer value (customer surplus)?
o: Brand A because its absolute price is lower
qs.e: Net customer value (surplus) = Perceived total utility - Price paid. For Brand A: N300,000 - N220,000 = N80,000. For Brand B: N400,000 - N300,000 = N100,000. Brand B offers higher net customer value.

qs.q: A rideshare tech platform lowers peak-hour surge fares by 15% (Price) and launches in two new regional cities (Place) while expanding driver training programs (People). In marketing mix terminology, the firm is modifying both traditional 4 Ps and extended service 3 Ps to maximize
qs.e: Modifying price, distribution location, and service personnel addresses both physical product and service delivery dimensions to enhance market penetration and customer satisfaction.

qs.q: In the 4 Cs framework developed by Robert Lauterborn, the element that replaces the traditional 'Promotion' element is
qs.e: In the 4 Cs framework, Product becomes Customer solution, Price becomes Cost, Place becomes Convenience, and Promotion becomes Communication.

qs.q: A consumer goods company manufactures 4 distinct lines: Soaps (5 variants), Detergents (4 variants), Toothpastes (3 variants), and Shampoos (6 variants). What is the total length of the company's product portfolio?
qs.e: Product portfolio length is the total number of items across all product lines. Total length = 5 + 4 + 3 + 6 = 18 items.

qs.q: An individual buys a battery-powered lantern during power outages purely for immediate functional illumination. The functional illumination itself represents the product's
qs.e: The core benefit is the fundamental problem-solving service or benefit that the consumer is buying (illumination).

qs.q: A computer software company releases a basic version of its antivirus software for free, while charging a premium annual subscription for advanced firewall and ransomware protection features. This product strategy is known as
qs.e: The freemium business model offers basic software or web services free of charge while charging a premium for advanced proprietary features or functionality.

qs.q: When a luxury fashion house licenses its trademark name to an independent eyewear manufacturer to produce sunglasses bearing the fashion house logo, the fashion house earns revenue primarily through
qs.e: Brand licensing agreements compensate the brand owner (licensor) through contractually agreed royalty fees based on sales revenue.

qs.q: A electronics manufacturer launches a low-end smartphone under a completely new brand name 'Spark' rather than its flagship brand 'Apex' to avoid damaging 'Apex's' high-end prestige image. The manufacturer is avoiding
qs.e: Creating a separate brand name for lower-end products protects the core brand from brand dilution and loss of premium standing.

qs.q: A dairy firm packs fresh milk in vacuum-sealed Tetra Pak cartons that extend shelf life without refrigeration for 6 months. This packaging design directly addresses product
qs.e: Tetra Pak vacuum packaging preserves liquid food products against spoilage and microbial degradation, mitigating perishability.

qs.q: In consumer goods marketing, packaging that features vibrant colors, clear typography, and a prominent brand ambassador image on store shelves fulfills the primary role of
qs.e: In self-service retail environments, effective retail packaging acts as a 'silent salesperson', capturing shopper attention and projecting promotional appeal.

qs.q: A restaurant chain buys fresh chicken at N2,000 per kg. It applies a 60% markup on cost to establish the menu price per kg. If the restaurant later decides to grant a 10% promotional discount off this menu price during lunch hours, what is the discounted price per kg?
qs.e: Original Menu Price = N2,000 * (1 + 0.60) = N3,200. Promotional discount of 10% = 0.10 * N3,200 = N320. Discounted price = N3,200 - N320 = N2,880.

qs.q: An industrial machine manufacturer incurs fixed manufacturing overhead of N60,000,000 per year and variable costs of N400,000 per machine. If the selling price per machine is set at N1,000,000, how many machines must be produced and sold to achieve a net operating profit of N15,000,000?
qs.e: Contribution Margin per unit = Selling Price - Variable Cost = N1,000,000 - N400,000 = N600,000. Required Sales Volume = (Fixed Overhead + Target Profit) / Contribution Margin = (N60,000,000 + N15,000,000) / N600,000 = N75,000,000 / N600,000 = 125 machines.

qs.q: A gas station sets petrol prices dynamically based on real-time traffic volume, weather conditions, and nearby competitor queue lengths via an automated software algorithm. This pricing strategy is
qs.e: Dynamic pricing (also called surge or real-time pricing) continually adjusts prices in real-time based on fluctuating demand, supply, and competitor factors.

qs.q: A manufacturer of heavy industrial transformers distributes exclusively through 3 authorized engineering distributors across all of West Africa. This distribution strategy is
qs.e: Selective or exclusive distribution uses a limited number of specialized intermediaries to maintain close control over service, installation, and positioning.

qs.q: A textile manufacturer sells fabrics directly to garment factories (B2B) while simultaneously selling through regional wholesalers who supply retail fabric shops (B2C). Operating multiple distribution paths like this is known as a
qs.e: A hybrid or multi-channel distribution system uses two or more distinct marketing channels to reach different customer segments.

qs.q: A logistics enterprise manages physical inventory movement, warehousing, order processing, and intermodal freight transport for manufacturing clients. These integrated operational activities constitute
o: Supply chain physical distribution / logistics management
qs.e: Logistics (physical distribution) encompasses planning, implementing, and controlling the physical flow of materials, final goods, and related information from points of origin to points of consumption.

qs.q: A pharmaceutical firm uses medical representatives to visit doctors while simultaneously placing educational wellness ads in national health magazines. This promotional combination is
qs.e: Using sales reps (push) directed at prescribers combined with consumer wellness advertising (pull) creates an integrated push-pull promotional strategy.

qs.q: The promotional budget setting method that builds the budget from the ground up by identifying specific marketing goals, determining exact required tasks, and calculating task execution costs is the
qs.e: The objective-and-task method develops promotional budgets by defining specific objectives, determining tasks, and estimating costs of performing those tasks.

qs.q: A television ad campaign costing N3,000,000 airs 5 times during a prime-time broadcast viewed by an estimated 2,000,000 households per airing. What is the Cost Per Thousand (CPM) impressions for the entire multi-airing campaign (10,000,000 total household impressions)?
qs.e: Total Impressions = 5 airings * 2,000,000 households = 10,000,000 impressions. CPM = (Total Campaign Cost / Total Impressions) * 1,000 = (N3,000,000 / 10,000,000) * 1,000 = 0.30 * 1,000 = N300.

qs.q: An advert that emphasizes a brand's unique selling proposition (USP), highlights product benefits, and urges consumers to switch from competing brands fulfills which core advertising objective?
qs.e: Persuasive advertising aims to build selective brand demand and persuade consumers that a brand offers the best quality or value for their money.

qs.q: A sales rep in the B2B solar equipment industry identifies 20 prospective commercial clients, verifies that they have both financial authority and operational need for solar installations, and ranks them by order value potential. This sales process step is
qs.e: Prospecting and qualifying is the first step in personal selling where salespeople identify potential qualified customers with financial ability and authority to buy.

qs.q: A corporate equipment salesperson earns a base salary of N200,000 plus a 5% commission on total monthly sales. If she closes N6,000,000 in equipment contracts during the month, what is her total gross pay for that month?
qs.e: Commission earned = 5% of N6,000,000 = 0.05 * N6,000,000 = N300,000. Total gross pay = Base salary (N200,000) + Commission (N300,000) = N500,000.

qs.q: A cosmetics retailer places free sample sachets of face cream inside popular women's fashion magazines distributed across major urban centers. This sales promotion method focuses on driving
qs.e: Free sampling is the most effective sales promotion tool for inducing consumer trial of a new or modified product.

qs.q: A manufacturer provides a temporary price discount to retail store owners who build prominent end-cap aisle displays featuring the manufacturer's soft drink brand. This incentive is a
qs.e: A trade allowance (or merchandise allowance) compensates retailers for featuring or displaying manufacturer products in store.

qs.q: When a major airline experiences flight delays due to severe harmattan dust haze, its corporate communications team releases hourly social media updates explaining weather safety protocols and arranging hotel accommodations. This action demonstrates proactive
qs.e: Proactive PR communication during operational disruptions protects corporate image, maintains customer trust, and manages brand reputation.

qs.q: An oil exploration firm establishes a university scholarship endowment for geology students in its operating region. In public relations, this initiative is an example of community-focused
qs.e: Educational scholarships sponsored by corporate entities represent CSR initiatives aimed at community empowerment and positive stakeholder relations.

qs.q: A commercial bank divides its retail market into low-income micro-savers, middle-income salary earners, and high-net-worth investors based on monthly income deposit tiers. This segmentation uses
qs.e: Segmenting buyers based on income, wealth, or deposit levels is a demographic segmentation approach.

qs.q: A car manufacturer targets eco-conscious consumers who prioritize environmental sustainability and zero-carbon transportation in their personal lifestyle choices. This segmentation strategy is
qs.e: Psychographic segmentation groups consumers according to shared values, attitudes, interests, and lifestyle choices.

qs.q: An online education startup designs specialized professional certification courses targeting software developers seeking promotion to senior cloud architects. This target strategy focuses on a highly specific
qs.e: Focusing on a narrowly defined customer group with specific, specialized skill upgrade requirements represents niche marketing.

qs.q: A buyer purchases a home security camera system after seeing news reports about neighborhood burglaries. In the consumer decision process, the news reports triggered
qs.e: Problem (need) recognition is the first stage in the buying process where the consumer recognizes a problem or need triggered by internal or external stimuli.

qs.q: A consumer who always purchases the same brand of toothpaste without evaluating alternative brands or seeking new information exhibits
qs.e: Habitual buying behavior is characterized by low consumer involvement and minimal perceived brand differences.

qs.q: A prospective home buyer compares three housing estates based on location, price, security, and infrastructure amenities before selecting one. This phase of the buying process is
qs.e: Evaluation of alternatives is the stage of the buyer decision process in which the consumer uses information to evaluate alternative brands in the choice set.

qs.q: A research agency collects data from 500 respondents using standardized structured questionnaires administered via mobile phone interviews. This research design is primarily
qs.e: Quantitative descriptive research uses structured measurement tools (questionnaires) administered to representative samples to quantify market characteristics.

qs.q: A market researcher reviews past academic journal articles, government statistical bulletins, and industry trade association reports before designing a field study. The researcher is collecting
qs.e: Secondary data consists of existing published literature, government reports, and industry publications collected previously for another purpose.

qs.q: A beverage company tests two different packaging color schemes (Blue vs Green) across two isolated regional test markets for 3 months to determine which scheme yields higher sales volume. This is an example of
qs.e: Experimental (causal) research manipulates an independent variable (packaging color) under controlled conditions to observe effects on a dependent variable (sales).

qs.q: A hotel room that remains unoccupied on a Tuesday night cannot be stored and sold on Wednesday, resulting in unrecoverable revenue loss. This illustrates service
qs.e: Perishability means services cannot be stored for future sale or use.

qs.q: A customer receiving a haircut cannot separate the service delivery from the presence and skill of the barber performing the haircut. This reflects service
qs.e: Inseparability means services are produced and consumed simultaneously in the presence of the provider.

qs.q: A hospital designs comfortable patient waiting lounges, clear signage, and neat professional uniforms for nursing staff to project high clinical quality. These elements form the service
qs.e: Physical evidence includes tangible facilities, equipment, and staff appearance used to communicate service quality.

qs.q: An e-commerce mobile app tracks customer items left in shopping carts and automatically sends a push notification offering a 5% discount if the customer completes checkout within 2 hours. This automated digital tactic is
qs.e: Cart abandonment recovery sends targeted notifications or emails to users who added items to an e-commerce cart but left without buying.

qs.q: A firm spends N300,000 on digital banner ads. The campaign registers 100,000 ad impressions and generates 2,000 user clicks. What is the Click-Through Rate (CTR) of this campaign?
Building high-quality website content, structuring HTML metadata tags, and optimizing site loading speed to improve organic position on Google search result pages is
qs.e: Search Engine Optimization (SEO) improves unpaid organic visibility on search engine results pages.

qs.q: A technological product category experiences declining industry sales, shrinking profit margins, and mass departure of competitors. The product category is in the PLC stage of
qs.e: The Decline stage of the product life cycle is marked by sustained drops in sales volume and industry exiting by competitors.

qs.q: During the Growth stage of the Product Life Cycle, a pioneer company should primarily focus its marketing strategy on
o: Harvesting short-term cash flow before exiting
Building brand preference and expanding distribution market share
Informing early adopters about basic core utility
Drastically cutting research and development budgets
qs.e: During the growth stage, consumer awareness exists, so focus shifts from primary demand building to establishing brand preference and capturing market share against new entrants.

qs.q: In an industrial manufacturing company, the technical engineer who writes detailed specifications for raw material inputs serves in the buying center as an
qs.e: Influencers in organizational buying define specifications and provide technical information for evaluating alternative products.

qs.q: A hotel chain routinely reorders cleaning supplies from its existing contract supplier every Monday without altering product specs or terms. This organizational purchase is a
qs.e: A straight rebuy is a routine reorder without any modification to specifications or terms.

qs.q: An IT department manager tests 3 enterprise software solutions and makes the final technical choice on which database system the firm will acquire. In buying center terms, the manager is the
qs.e: Deciders have formal or informal power to select or approve final product suppliers and technical choices.

qs.q: A Nigerian agricultural exporter ships dried ginger directly to spice grinding companies in Europe without employing foreign sales intermediaries. This market entry mode is
qs.e: Direct exporting occurs when a producer sells products directly to buyers in foreign markets without using third-party export intermediaries.

qs.q: A global beverage multinational adapts its product sweetness levels and advertising slogans to match local cultural preferences in each foreign country it enters. This international strategy is
qs.e: Product adaptation (glocalisation) tailors marketing mix elements to local consumer tastes and cultural conditions in international markets.

qs.q: A company that focuses primarily on continuous product improvements without evaluating actual consumer preferences is practicing the
qs.e: The product concept assumes consumers will favor products that offer the most quality, performance, and innovative features. However, it risks marketing myopia if customer needs are ignored.

qs.q: Which component of a brand refers specifically to the symbol, design, or distinctive coloring that can be recognized visually but cannot be spoken?
qs.e: A brand mark is the visual element of a brand such as a logo, symbol, or distinct design that can be recognized visually but cannot be pronounced verbally.

qs.q: The immediate wrapper or container holding a single unit of sachet water is classified as
qs.e: Primary packaging is the immediate container that holds the product itself, such as the plastic sachet containing sachet water or a bottle holding a beverage.

qs.q: A farmer in Benue State who sells yam tubers directly to final consumers at a roadside stall is utilizing a distribution channel of level
qs.e: A zero-level channel (direct marketing channel) consists of a manufacturer selling directly to the final consumer without any intermediate resellers.

qs.q: Short-term incentives designed to encourage the immediate purchase or sale of a product or service are known as
qs.e: Sales promotion consists of short-term incentives like coupons, discounts, free samples, and contests aimed at encouraging immediate trial or buying.

qs.q: Dividing a consumer market into distinct groups based on variables such as age, gender, income, and educational level is termed
qs.e: Demographic segmentation classifies buyers based on measurable population characteristics such as age, gender, household income, occupation, and education.

qs.q: The use of social media channels, search engines, and email campaigns to promote products directly to online consumers is known as
qs.e: Digital marketing encompasses all marketing efforts that leverage electronic devices, the internet, and digital platforms to reach target audiences.

qs.q: When a soft drink manufacturer expands its warehouse and depot network across southwestern Nigeria to improve product availability, it is modifying which element of the marketing mix?
qs.e: Expanding warehouse and depot networks improves physical distribution and market reach, directly relating to the Place element of the marketing mix.

qs.q: Fast-moving consumer goods like laundry detergent sachets that consumers buy frequently, immediately, and with minimal comparison effort are classified as
qs.e: Convenience goods are inexpensive items bought regularly with minimal planning and search effort by consumers.

qs.q: A footwear trader in Aba buys a pair of leather shoes for N8,000 and applies a 25 percent markup on cost. What is the selling price of the shoes?
qs.e: Markup amount = N8,000 * 0.25 = N2,000. Selling price = Cost + Markup = N8,000 + N2,000 = N10,000.

qs.q: An informative advertising campaign is most appropriate during which stage of a product's lifecycle?
qs.e: Informative advertising builds primary demand and creates awareness about product features, usage, and benefits during the introduction stage.

qs.q: In personal selling, the initial step where a salesperson identifies potential customers who have both the need and financial capacity to purchase is called
qs.e: Prospecting is the first step in the personal selling process, involving identifying and qualifying prospective clients based on interest, need, and buying power.

qs.q: A major supermarket in Lagos places promotional displays and eye-level product banners directly at checkout counters. This technique is known as
qs.e: Point-of-purchase (POP) displays are sales promotion materials positioned directly where purchase decisions are made to stimulate impulse purchases.

qs.q: When a telecommunications firm holds an urgent press briefing to explain a network outage and announce compensation for affected users, it is performing
qs.e: Crisis public relations addresses unexpected negative events, seeking to preserve organizational reputation, communicate facts, and maintain public trust.

qs.q: The first step in the consumer buying decision process occurs when a buyer recognizes a difference between their actual state and a desired state, known as
qs.e: The buying decision process begins with problem or need recognition, triggered when internal or external stimuli highlight a gap between current state and desired state.

qs.q: A research team administering structured face-to-face questionnaire surveys directly to shoppers at Kantin Kwari market in Kano is collecting
qs.e: Primary data refers to original information collected specifically for the research project at hand through methods like surveys, interviews, or experiments.

qs.q: Because a haircut cannot be produced in advance and stored on a shelf for future sale, services exhibit the core characteristic of
qs.e: Perishability means service capacity cannot be saved, stored, resold, or returned for future use if left unconsumed when available.

qs.q: A product lifecycle stage characterized by rapid increase in sales, expanding market adoption, and entry of new market competitors is the
qs.e: The growth stage features rapid acceptance by consumers, surging sales revenue, economies of scale, and entry of competing brands.

qs.q: A commercial bank tracking client transaction histories and sending customized birthday goodwill messages alongside tailored loan offers is implementing
qs.e: Customer Relationship Management (CRM) uses detailed customer data to build long-term retention, customized communication, and customer loyalty.

qs.q: A sachet water producer has monthly fixed operational costs of N500,000. Each bag of sachet water costs N300 to produce and sells for N500. What is the break-even output volume in bags per month?
qs.e: Contribution margin per unit = Selling price - Variable cost = N500 - N300 = N200. Break-even units = Fixed costs / Contribution margin = N500,000 / N200 = 2,500 bags.

qs.q: A palm oil merchant buys a keg of unrefined palm oil for N12,000 and sells it for N15,000. What is the profit margin percentage based on the selling price?
qs.e: Profit amount = Selling price - Cost = N15,000 - N12,000 = N3,000. Margin on selling price = (N3,000 / N15,000) * 100% = 20%.

qs.q: Which distribution coverage strategy is most appropriate for a manufacturer selling low-cost consumer packaged goods like toilet soaps that require maximum retail exposure?
qs.e: Intensive distribution aims to place products in as many outlets as possible to maximize accessibility for high-frequency convenience items.

qs.q: Segmenting a market into groups based on consumer values, interests, social class, and lifestyle characteristics is known as
qs.e: Psychographic segmentation divides buyers into segments based on social class, lifestyle, attitudes, interests, and personality characteristics.

qs.q: A consumer who feels anxiety and doubt after purchasing an expensive generator in Computer Village, wondering if another brand was better, is experiencing
qs.e: Cognitive dissonance is post-purchase psychological discomfort caused by consumer doubts about whether they made the optimal purchasing decision.

qs.q: To ensure equal representation of traders across food, electronics, and textile sectors in Onitsha Main Market, a researcher should use
qs.e: Stratified random sampling divides the population into mutually exclusive subgroups (strata) based on relevant categories and samples randomly within each stratum.

qs.q: A hotel in Calabar cannot store unused guest room capacity from a low-season month to sell during the Carnival peak season. This illustrates service
qs.e: Perishability means service capacity is time-dependent and cannot be stored for future sale when current demand fluctuates.

qs.q: An online fashion store improving its website structure and content so that it ranks higher in organic search engine results is employing
qs.e: Search Engine Optimization (SEO) involves optimizing web pages to boost unpaid, organic visibility on search engine results pages.

qs.q: During the maturity stage of a product lifecycle, a firm seeking to sustain sales growth by attracting non-users and entering new geographic regions is applying
qs.e: Market modification strategies aim to expand sales volume by finding new user segments, increasing usage rates, or expanding into new sales territories.

qs.q: When an exporter sells goods in a foreign country at a price lower than their domestic production cost or local market price, the practice is called
qs.e: Dumping occurs when an exporting firm sets foreign prices below domestic prices or cost of production, often disrupting the host nation's local industries.

qs.q: A key advantage of long-term collaborative relationship marketing over traditional transactional marketing is that it
o: lowers customer acquisition costs through higher retention
focuses exclusively on single-sale volume maximization
eliminates the need for post-sale customer support
reduces the reliance on quality control standards
qs.e: Relationship marketing retains existing clients over time, significantly lowering expensive repeat acquisition costs and building customer lifetime value.

qs.q: A glass bottle designed with specialized shock-absorbing corrugated sleeves for shipping fruit juice across bad road networks performs primarily a
qs.e: The primary objective of structural packaging during transit is protection against physical damage, spillage, contamination, and environmental hazards.

qs.q: Which advertising media evaluation metric measures the total estimated number of distinct households exposed to an ad message at least once during a given period?
qs.e: Reach measures the total percentage or count of different target audience members exposed to a specific advertisement during a given timeframe.

qs.q: When a prospective business client raises concerns regarding the high upfront cost of new office software, the salesperson re-frames the cost in terms of daily operational savings. This sales technique is
qs.e: Handling objections is the stage in personal selling where the salesperson listens to consumer hesitations, addresses concerns, and reframes value.

qs.q: A manufacturer offering temporary price reductions to wholesalers to encourage them to buy larger quantities before a holiday season is using a
qs.e: Trade allowances are financial promotional incentives provided to channel intermediaries (wholesalers/retailers) to motivate bulk purchases or store display efforts.

qs.q: A distributor lists an electrical appliance at N20,000. Retailers receive a 15 percent trade discount. If a retailer pays within 10 days, an additional 5 percent cash discount is allowed on the net invoice price. How much does the retailer pay if paying within 10 days?
qs.e: Trade discount = 15% of N20,000 = N3,000. Net invoice price = N20,000 - N3,000 = N17,000. Cash discount = 5% of N17,000 = N850. Net payment = N17,000 - N850 = N16,150.

qs.q: A plastic manufacturing firm in Ogun State has annual fixed overhead costs of N1,200,000. Its plastic containers sell for N2,500 each, while variable production costs are N1,500 per unit. How many units must the firm produce and sell to achieve a target annual profit of N600,000?
qs.e: Unit contribution margin = N2,500 - N1,500 = N1,000. Required total contribution = Fixed costs + Target profit = N1,200,000 + N600,000 = N1,800,000. Required volume = N1,800,000 / N1,000 = 1,800 units.

qs.q: A distribution arrangement in which independent wholesale and retail firms integrate their operating programs under contract to achieve greater economies of scale than they could individually is a
qs.e: A contractual VMS consists of independent firms at different channel levels operating under formal contractual agreements (e.g., retail cooperatives or franchises).

qs.q: A mobile network operator segments its subscribers into heavy data streamers, moderate daily users, and emergency-only users based on subscription frequency and gigabytes consumed. This illustrates
qs.e: Behavioral segmentation divides buyers based on knowledge, attitude, use, or response. Categorizing consumers by heavy, medium, or light consumption uses usage rate criteria.

qs.q: High-status individuals whose buying choices, lifestyle habits, and product endorsements strongly influence the purchasing decisions of their followers act as
qs.e: Opinion leaders within reference groups exert social influence on others because of special skills, knowledge, personality, or social standing.

qs.q: To explore consumer underlying attitudes toward a proposed brand logo change prior to a quantitative survey, a market research firm conducts interactive, guided group discussions. This technique is a
qs.e: A focus group discussion is a qualitative research technique where a trained moderator leads a small group in an open-ended discussion to uncover deeper consumer perceptions.

qs.q: Because service delivery involves simultaneous production and consumption, service marketers rely heavily on physical evidence and ambient surroundings (servicescape) to mitigate consumer perception of
qs.e: Intangibility means services cannot be seen or felt before purchase. Marketers manage physical evidence (cleanliness, modern equipment, staff uniforms) to signal quality.

qs.q: An e-commerce mobile app recorded 10,000 unique visitor sessions in a month, resulting in 250 completed checkouts. What is the overall e-commerce conversion rate?
qs.e: Conversion rate = (Number of successful purchases / Total visitor sessions) * 100% = (250 / 10,000) * 100% = 2.5%.

qs.q: When a global fast-food brand adjusts its core menu items to suit local Nigerian palate preferences by introducing jollof rice options, it is pursuing a strategy of
qs.e: Product adaptation involves modifying a product's features, flavor, or formulation to meet local cultural preferences, tastes, or regulatory conditions in international markets.

qs.q: When a soft drink company introduces sugar-free, ginger-flavored, and zero-calorie variants under its main brand name to capture distinct consumer niches, it is executing a product line
qs.e: Product line extension occurs when a company introduces additional items in a given product category under the same brand name (such as new flavors, sizes, or formulas).

qs.q: A commercial firm partnering with a non-profit health organization to donate N50 from every pack of sanitary pads sold toward girl-child education in rural schools is engaged in
qs.e: Cause-related marketing ties product sales directly to raising funds or awareness for a specific charitable or social cause, enhancing brand equity while supporting society.

qs.q: A supermarket trader desires a target profit margin of 25 percent calculated on the selling price of packaged rice. What markup percentage on cost price must the trader apply to achieve this margin?
qs.e: Formula relating markup on cost (m) to margin on selling price (g): m = g / (1 - g). Given g = 0.25, m = 0.25 / (1 - 0.25) = 0.25 / 0.75 = 1/3 = 33.33%.

qs.q: Conflict that arises when a manufacturing brand establishes its own direct e-commerce portal selling goods to consumers at prices lower than those charged by its independent retail store distributors is classified as
qs.e: Vertical channel conflict occurs between different levels in the same channel, such as between a manufacturer and its authorized retailers over direct selling and price undercutting.

qs.q: Under the Assael buying behavior matrix, when a consumer displays high involvement in an expensive purchase with significant perceived differences between available brands, the consumer exhibits
qs.e: Complex buying behavior occurs when buyers are highly involved in a purchase and perceive significant differences among brands, requiring active information search.

qs.q: A beverage firm conducts experimental test marketing in two comparable cities (Ibadan and Benin), charging N250 per unit in one and N300 in the other while keeping promotion identical. This research design aims to determine
o: price elasticity of demand through causal research
consumer demographic profiles through exploratory research
qs.e: Causal research tests cause-and-effect relationships by manipulating independent variables (price) while controlling extraneous variables to measure impact on dependent variables (sales volume).

qs.q: A country enforcing strict government import quotas and administrative customs inspection delays on foreign textiles to protect domestic textile manufacturers is utilizing
qs.e: Non-tariff trade barriers include quotas, administrative procedures, embargoes, and bureaucratic delays that restrict international trade without imposing direct monetary import tariffs.

qs.q: A manufacturing philosophy emphasizing high production efficiency, mass volume, and low costs to make products widely available is the
qs.e: The production concept holds that consumers prefer products that are widely available and inexpensive, focusing management efforts on high production efficiency and wide distribution.

qs.q: The classic marketing mix consists of four core controllable decision variables commonly known as the Four Ps, which stand for
qs.e: The traditional marketing mix formulated by E. Jerome McCarthy comprises Product, Price, Place, and Promotion.

qs.q: Equipment, heavy machinery, and industrial raw materials purchased by commercial firms to produce other final products are categorized as
qs.e: Industrial goods are business-to-business products purchased by companies for further processing or for use in conducting industrial operations.

qs.q: Setting a low introductory price for a brand-new market offering to attract a large number of buyers quickly and secure dominant market share is called
qs.e: Penetration pricing sets an initially low price to penetrate the market deeply and quickly, capturing substantial sales volume and market share.

qs.q: Intermediaries who buy large quantities of merchandise from producers, store inventory, and resell in smaller quantities to retail outlets are called
qs.e: Wholesalers perform bulk-breaking by purchasing large volumes from manufacturers and selling smaller, convenient lots to retail businesses.

qs.q: Advertising intended to increase demand for an established brand by emphasizing its competitive superiority and unique features is classified as
qs.e: Persuasive advertising seeks to build selective brand demand by convincing consumers that a specific brand offers superior quality or value.

qs.q: The fundamental set of basic values, perceptions, wants, and behaviors learned by a member of society from family and key institutions is defined as
qs.e: Culture is the most basic cause of a person's wants and behavior, learned through socialization within family, religious, educational, and community institutions.

qs.q: A corrugated cardboard carton holding 24 individual plastic bottles of vegetable oil for safe transport and storage in a retail stockroom represents
qs.e: Secondary packaging protects primary containers during transport and storage and is usually discarded when the product is unpacked for use or retail display.

qs.q: Favorable consumer sentiment and favorable repeat purchasing behavior consistently directed toward a specific brand over competing options is termed
qs.e: Brand loyalty is a deeply held commitment to re-buy or re-patronize a preferred product or service consistently over time despite situational influences.

qs.q: A boutique owner in Kaduna purchases a designer jacket for N5,000 and applies a 40 percent markup on cost price. What is the final retail price?
qs.e: Markup amount = N5,000 * 0.40 = N2,000. Retail price = Cost + Markup = N5,000 + N2,000 = N7,000.

qs.q: The phase in the personal selling process where a sales representative asks the customer directly for an order is known as
